exceptions-api-restricted.name: ApiClassConstFetchRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Rule<Expr\ClassConstFetch>: flags `Foo::BAR` (and `Foo::class`) when `Foo` resolves to a class/interface inside the real PHPStan's own `PHPStan\` namespace (via ApiRuleHelper::isPhpStanCode) that is not tagged `@api` on its class doc-block (or, for `::class`, on any method's own doc-block) - i.e. BC-promise enforcement for extension authors touching PHPStan internals.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: This entire rule family only fires when analyzed PHP code references classes literally in the PHP PHPStan library's own `PHPStan\` namespace under a vendor/ directory (ApiRuleHelper::isPhpStanCode gates on exactly that). phpstan-rs is a Rust program with no equivalent PHP namespace/API surface that third-party analyzed PHP code could misuse this way, so there is no sensible port target - this is PHPStan-linting-PHPStan-extensions, not general PHP analysis.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: ApiClassExtendsRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Rule<Class_>: flags `class X extends Y` when `Y` is PHPStan-internal code (via ApiRuleHelper) and lacks an `@api` tag (special-cased to always allow extending MutatingScope).
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Same PHPStan-namespace/BC-promise self-protection mechanism as ApiClassConstFetchRule; no analog exists for phpstan-rs, a Rust binary with no PHP classes of its own to be extended by analyzed code.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: ApiClassImplementsRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Rule<Class_>: for each `implements` interface, flags it if PHPStan-internal and not `@api` (or marked `@api-do-not-implement`, which always flags even if also `@api`).
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Same PHPStan-own-namespace BC-promise mechanism; not applicable to phpstan-rs.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: ApiInstanceofRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Rule<Expr\Instanceof_>: flags `$x instanceof PhpStanInternalClass` unless `@api`-tagged; even for `@api` classes/interfaces it additionally flags the instanceof as a fragile 'assumption' unless the checked class is PHPStan's own Type interface/an interface, or the expression's static type already resolves the instanceof to a definite true/false or already narrows to a subtype of the checked class.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Purely about instanceof checks against PHPStan-internal PHP classes; phpstan-rs has no such namespace to protect for analyzed code.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: ApiInstanceofTypeRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Rule<Expr\Instanceof_>: flags `instanceof` against any PHPStan\Type class carrying the `#[InstanceofDeprecated]` attribute (read via a compiled attribute-collector map), suggesting the type's own `isX()`/`isSuperTypeOf()` method instead; skipped for AccessoryType checks and for code implementing TypeTraverserCallable or already inside a TypeTraverser-generated instanceof visitor.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Enforces PHPStan's own internal coding convention (never `instanceof SomeType`, use `Type::isX()`) against code that touches PHPStan's Type hierarchy specifically; phpstan-rs's own Rust `Type` enum in src/types.rs is a different, unrelated type system with no such deprecated-instanceof surface for analyzed PHP code to trip.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: ApiInstantiationRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Rule<Expr\New_>: flags `new PhpStanInternalClass(...)` unless the class's constructor doc-comment contains `@api` and is declared directly on that class (not inherited).
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Same PHPStan-own-namespace BC-promise mechanism; not applicable.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: ApiInterfaceExtendsRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Rule<Interface_>: for each `extends` on an interface declaration, flags PHPStan-internal parents lacking `@api` (or flagged `@api-do-not-implement`).
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Same mechanism as ApiClassImplementsRule for interface extends; not applicable to phpstan-rs.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: ApiMethodCallRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Rule<Expr\MethodCall>: resolves the called method via Scope::getMethodReflection, and if its declaring class is PHPStan-internal code, flags the call unless the declaring class is `@api`-tagged or the method's own doc-comment contains `@api`.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Same PHPStan-own-namespace BC-promise mechanism; not applicable - phpstan-rs's checker (src/checker/calls.rs) resolves method calls against user code's own classes, not against a PHP `PHPStan\` API surface.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: ApiRuleHelper
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Not a Rule itself - an `#[AutowiredService]` DI helper shared by the Api/* rules above. `isPhpStanName()` checks a namespace string starts with `PHPStan\` (excluding the vendored PhpDocParser/BetterReflection sub-namespaces). `isPhpStanCode()` additionally requires, when the calling scope is itself inside the `PHPStan\` namespace, that the referenced class's declaring file sits under a `vendor/` directory relative to the caller (i.e. true PHPStan-core code calling into a vendored copy of itself still counts, but internal same-package calls don't get flagged).
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Pure DI-wired helper class whose entire purpose is answering 'is this PHP code inside the real PHPStan library', consumed only by the other Api/* rules above; no equivalent concept exists for a Rust rewrite with no such PHP namespace to identify.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: ApiStaticCallRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Rule<Expr\StaticCall>: resolves `Foo::bar()` via the class's native method reflection and flags it if the declaring class is PHPStan-internal and not covered (class `@api`, unless the method is `__construct`, or the method doc-comment itself has `@api`).
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Same PHPStan-own-namespace BC-promise mechanism as ApiMethodCallRule but for static calls; not applicable.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: ApiTraitUseRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Rule<Stmt\TraitUse>: for each trait named in a `use TraitName;` statement, flags it if the trait is PHPStan-internal code (via ApiRuleHelper) - there is no `@api`-escape path at all here (any @api check is absent; every internal trait use is flagged).
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Same PHPStan-own-namespace BC-promise mechanism; not applicable to phpstan-rs, which has no PHP traits of its own.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: GetTemplateTypeRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Rule<Expr\MethodCall>: specifically detects calls to a method literally named `getTemplateType` (case-insensitive) declared on PHPStan's `Type` interface, and when both the class-name and template-type-name arguments are known string literals, flags the call if the named template type doesn't actually exist on that class's TemplateTypeMap - i.e. a typo-catcher for PHPStan extension authors calling PHPStan's own generics API.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Depends entirely on PHPStan's own `Type::getTemplateType(string $class, string $templateType)` runtime API and its TemplateTypeMap reflection; phpstan-rs's generics handling (src/checker/generics.rs) is an unrelated internal mechanism with no equivalent externally-callable method for analyzed PHP code to misuse.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: NodeConnectingVisitorAttributesRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Rule<Expr\MethodCall>: flags `$node->getAttribute('parent'|'previous'|'next')` calls (where `$node` is a nikic php-parser `Node`) when made from inside a class that implements a `PHPStan\`-namespaced interface, because those NodeConnectingVisitor-supplied attributes were removed/changed in newer PHPStan versions.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: A PHPStan-version-migration warning specific to writing PHPStan custom rules/collectors (classes implementing PHPStan's own Rule/Collector interfaces) that walk the nikic php-parser AST via getAttribute(); phpstan-rs's own parser/AST (src/parser/*, src/ast.rs) has no such attribute API for analyzed code to call, and phpstan-rs is not itself an extensible rule-authoring platform being linted here.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: OldPhpParser4ClassRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Rule<Name>: inside a class implementing a `PHPStan\`-namespaced interface, flags references to old nikic/php-parser v4 node class names (e.g. `PhpParser\Node\Scalar\LNumber`) that were renamed in php-parser v5 (e.g. to `Node\Scalar\Int_`), reporting the v5 replacement name.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: A nikic/php-parser v4-to-v5 migration aid for authors of PHPStan rules/collectors referencing php-parser's old class names; phpstan-rs uses its own hand-written parser/lexer (src/parser/*, src/lexer/*) rather than nikic/php-parser, so this specific class-rename table has no meaning for phpstan-rs or code it analyzes.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: PhpStanNamespaceIn3rdPartyPackageRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Rule<Stmt\Namespace_>: flags any `namespace PHPStan...` declaration found outside the real `phpstan/*` composer packages (walks up from the file to find the nearest composer.json and checks its `name` field), since third-party code declaring itself inside the reserved `PHPStan\` namespace is disallowed.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Protects the literal `PHPStan\` PHP namespace as reserved for PHPStan's own composer packages; phpstan-rs is a Rust crate with no PHP namespace of its own for third-party PHP packages to squat on, so there's nothing to protect.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: RuntimeReflectionFunctionRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Rule<Expr\FuncCall>: inside a class implementing a `PHPStan\`-namespaced interface, flags calls to `is_a()`, `is_subclass_of()`, `class_parents()`, `class_implements()`, `class_uses()` as runtime-reflection concepts unsafe under PHPStan's static/BetterReflection engine, suggesting `ReflectionProvider` instead.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Guidance specific to authors of PHPStan rules/extensions who must avoid PHP's live runtime-reflection functions in favor of PHPStan's own static ReflectionProvider; phpstan-rs is itself a static analyzer with no comparable 'live reflection API vs static ReflectionProvider' duality to warn analyzed extension code about.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: RuntimeReflectionInstantiationRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Rule<Expr\New_>: same as RuntimeReflectionFunctionRule but for `new Reflection*(...)` (ReflectionClass, ReflectionMethod, ReflectionProperty, ReflectionParameter, ReflectionFunction, ReflectionClassConstant, ReflectionObject, ReflectionGenerator, ReflectionExtension, ReflectionZendExtension, 'ReflectionEnum'/'ReflectionEnumBackedCase'/'ReflectionFiber'), gated the same way on being inside a class implementing a `PHPStan\` interface.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Same PHPStan-extension-authoring guidance as RuntimeReflectionFunctionRule; not applicable to phpstan-rs.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: CatchWithUnthrownExceptionRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Rule<CatchWithUnthrownExceptionNode> (level 4): reports a 'dead catch' - either 'X is already caught above' when a preceding catch clause already exhaustively covers this one's type (caught type narrows to NeverType), or 'X is never thrown in the try block' when nothing in the try body can actually throw the caught exception type, computed by NodeScopeResolver walking the try body to collect all statically-throwable exception types and intersecting with each catch's declared type; unchecked (unchecked-exception) dead catches are only reported when the `exceptions.reportUncheckedExceptionDeadCatch` config flag is on, via ExceptionTypeResolver::isCheckedException.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: phpstan-rs's try/catch handling (src/checker/stmt.rs StmtKind::Try, ~lines 472-559) does full control-flow merging of try/catch/finally branches and even validates each catch type implements Throwable (its own 'Finding 57'), but never computes what exception types the try body can actually throw and never cross-checks that set against each catch clause - there is no throw-type inference, no @throws resolution, and no checked/unchecked exception classification anywhere in src/ (confirmed via repo-wide grep for throws/ThrowType/exceptionType/CheckedException - no hits in src/checker or src/types.rs). Both diagnostic identifiers (catch.alreadyCaught, catch.neverThrown) are entirely unimplemented.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: CaughtExceptionExistenceRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Rule on Catch_ nodes: for each caught type, errors 'class.notFound' if the class doesn't exist (unless in an isInClassExists guard), errors 'catch.notThrowable' if the class exists but isn't an interface and doesn't implement Throwable, and additionally runs ClassNameCheck for case-sensitivity/deprecation on the class name.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: The 'not an exception' half is implemented: each catch type is resolved and checked via registry.is_subclass_of(class, "Throwable"), reporting 'cannot catch {class}: it does not implement Throwable' (finding 57). Missing: the 'class.notFound' branch entirely - phpstan-rs has no class-existence checking anywhere (resolve_name_expr always returns Type::Object regardless of whether the registry actually has the class), and no isInClassExists carve-out; also no ClassNameCheck equivalent (case-sensitivity/deprecated-class-usage checking) is run here or anywhere in the checker.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: DefaultExceptionTypeResolver
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Default ExceptionTypeResolver implementation: decides whether a given exception class name is a 'checked' exception by consulting configured unchecked/checked regex and class-name lists (exceptions.uncheckedExceptionRegexes/Classes, checkedExceptionRegexes/Classes), falling back to 'checked iff any checked-list config is non-empty' when no explicit match is found.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: phpstan-rs has no checked/unchecked exception classification, no equivalent config surface, and no @throws PHPDoc handling at all (grep for 'throws'/'@throws' in src/docblock.rs and src/checker/*.rs returns nothing) - this whole checked-exceptions subsystem (which DefaultExceptionTypeResolver is the config-driven default implementation of) is entirely absent.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: ExceptionTypeResolver
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Pure interface (isCheckedException(string $className, Scope $scope): bool) - the extension point third-party configs can implement to plug custom checked/unchecked exception logic into the analyser; not itself a rule or check.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: A DI extension-point interface with no logic of its own (the same category as PHPStan's other pluggable-extension interfaces) - phpstan-rs has no plugin/extension architecture, and since the underlying checked-exceptions feature this interface serves (see DefaultExceptionTypeResolver) is itself unimplemented, there is nothing for an equivalent interface to plug into.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: MethodThrowTypeCovarianceRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Rule on InClassMethodNode: compares a (non-constructor, non-private) method's @throws type against every parent/interface method it overrides, erroring 'throws.shouldBeVoid'/'throws.notCovariantWithImplicitVoid' if the parent declares @throws void (explicitly or implicitly) but the child throws something, or 'throws.notCovariant' if the child's throw type isn't a subtype of the parent's.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Depends entirely on @throws PHPDoc parsing and method throw-type reflection, neither of which exists in phpstan-rs (no docblock.rs @throws handling, no MethodReflection::getThrowType equivalent, and no ParentMethodHelper-style parent-method-collection walk for this purpose).

exceptions-api-restricted.name: MissingCheckedExceptionInFunctionThrowsRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Rule on FunctionReturnStatementsNode: delegates to MissingCheckedExceptionInThrowsCheck with the function's declared @throws type and its collected ThrowPoints, reporting 'missingType.checkedException' for each checked exception thrown in the body but absent from @throws.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Requires both @throws PHPDoc parsing (absent) and a ThrowPoint-collection pass across statement results (no analogous per-statement throw-point tracking exists in phpstan-rs's checker) - neither building block is present.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: MissingCheckedExceptionInMethodThrowsRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Method-level counterpart of MissingCheckedExceptionInFunctionThrowsRule: on MethodReturnStatementsNode, same delegation to MissingCheckedExceptionInThrowsCheck for the method's throw type vs. its ThrowPoints, same 'missingType.checkedException' diagnostic.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Same missing infrastructure as the function variant: no @throws PHPDoc support and no ThrowPoint collection in phpstan-rs.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: MissingCheckedExceptionInPropertyHookThrowsRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Property-hook counterpart: on PropertyHookReturnStatementsNode, delegates to the same check for a get/set property hook's @throws type vs. its ThrowPoints.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: PHP property hooks (8.4 asymmetric-visibility get/set hooks) have no equivalent construct in phpstan-rs's parser/AST at all (no PropertyHook node kind), and the underlying @throws-checked-exception machinery is also absent (see MissingCheckedExceptionInFunctionThrowsRule) - both the specific hook feature and the general mechanism are missing, but since property hooks themselves aren't modeled anywhere in this codebase this is scored not_applicable for the hook-specific surface rather than a duplicate 'missing' of the same underlying gap.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: MissingCheckedExceptionInThrowsCheck
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Shared helper (not a Rule) used by the three MissingCheckedExceptionIn*ThrowsRule classes: given a declared @throws Type and a list of ThrowPoints, flattens each explicit throw point's type, skips anything already covered by the declared throw type or that is exactly Throwable-supertype, and returns the ones whose object classes resolve to a 'checked' exception per ExceptionTypeResolver.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Pure helper for the checked-exceptions feature family; since @throws parsing, ThrowPoint collection, and ExceptionTypeResolver are all absent from phpstan-rs, there is no equivalent helper and nothing for one to compute.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: NoncapturingCatchRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Rule on Catch_ nodes: emits a nonignorable 'catch.nonCapturingNotSupported' error if a catch clause omits the captured variable (`catch (Foo)` instead of `catch (Foo $e)`) while the configured target PHP version predates 8.0, which is when non-capturing catch was introduced.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: phpstan-rs has no PhpVersion/target-version modeling anywhere in the codebase (confirmed via grep - no PhpVersion, php_version, or per-syntax-feature version gating exists), and its parser already accepts non-capturing catch unconditionally as valid modern syntax; a version-gated syntax-support rule has no sensible equivalent in a checker that only targets a single implicit modern PHP version.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: OverwrittenExitPointByFinallyRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Rule (level 4) on FinallyExitPointsNode: when both a try/catch block and its finally block contain an exit point (return/throw/continue/break) that would run, since the finally-block's exit point silently overwrites the try/catch's, it reports both locations with 'finally.exitPoint' - one error noting the original exit point is overwritten, one pointing at the overwriting one.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: phpstan-rs's Try handling in src/checker/stmt.rs (StmtKind::Try) does control-flow merging of try/catch/finally locals for narrowing purposes but performs no analysis of exit-point overwriting inside finally blocks - no FinallyExitPointsNode-equivalent collection or diagnostic exists.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: ThrowExprTypeRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Rule (level 3) on Node\Expr\Throw_: verifies the thrown expression's type is a subtype of Throwable via findTypeToCheck (which also flags throwing an object of unknown class), erroring 'throw.notThrowable' ('Invalid type %s to throw.') otherwise.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: The core Throwable-subtype check is implemented but only for the *statement* form (`throw expr;`, StmtKind::Throw), reporting 'cannot throw {class}: it does not implement Throwable' when the thrown value resolves to a concrete Type::Object non-Throwable class. The *expression* form (`ExprKind::Throw`, e.g. `$x ?? throw new Foo()`) in src/checker/expr.rs:652-655 only evaluates the inner expression and returns Type::Never - it never runs the Throwable check, so `$x ?? throw new StdClass()` would go unflagged. Also, unlike PHPStan, only a concrete Type::Object is checked; unions/unknown-class cases are silently skipped (matches project-wide leniency but no 'unknown class' companion diagnostic exists either).

exceptions-api-restricted.name: ThrowExpressionRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Rule (level 0) on Node\Expr\Throw_: emits a nonignorable 'throw.notSupported' error if a throw-as-expression (not the standalone-statement form, tracked via StandaloneThrowExprVisitor) is used while targeting a PHP version older than 8.0.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Same reasoning as NoncapturingCatchRule: phpstan-rs has no configurable target-PHP-version concept, and its parser already unconditionally supports throw-as-expression syntax (ExprKind::Throw in src/ast.rs and src/parser/postfix.rs) as ordinary modern PHP - there is no version-gate for this rule to have an equivalent of.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: ThrowsVoidFunctionWithExplicitThrowPointRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Rule (level 3) on FunctionReturnStatementsNode: when a function's PHPDoc declares '@throws void' but the body has an explicit throw point whose exception class isn't configured as unchecked, reports 'throws.void' - 'Function %s() throws exception %s but the PHPDoc contains @throws void.'
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Depends on @throws void PHPDoc parsing and ThrowPoint collection, both absent from phpstan-rs; no equivalent check exists.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: ThrowsVoidMethodWithExplicitThrowPointRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Method-level counterpart on MethodReturnStatementsNode: same '@throws void' contradiction check for methods, 'throws.void' error naming the declaring class and method.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Same missing @throws/ThrowPoint infrastructure as the function variant.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: ThrowsVoidPropertyHookWithExplicitThrowPointRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Property-hook counterpart on PropertyHookReturnStatementsNode: same '@throws void' contradiction check for a get/set property hook body.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: PHP property hooks are not modeled anywhere in phpstan-rs's parser/AST (no hook node kind exists), and the underlying @throws/ThrowPoint machinery is also absent - the hook-specific surface has no sensible Rust equivalent to point to.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: TooWideFunctionThrowTypeRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Rule on FunctionReturnStatementsNode: delegates to TooWideThrowTypeCheck (not in this chunk) with the function's declared @throws type and collected ThrowPoints, reporting 'throws.unusedType' for each declared throw class never actually thrown - 'Function %s() has %s in PHPDoc @throws tag but it's not thrown.'
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Same missing @throws-parsing and ThrowPoint-collection prerequisites as the other throws-family rules; TooWideThrowTypeCheck (the shared helper it calls) is likewise absent from phpstan-rs.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: TooWideMethodThrowTypeRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Method-level counterpart: on MethodReturnStatementsNode, applies the same 'declared @throws class never thrown' check but restricted to private methods, or non-private methods on final classes/final methods, or (if configured) any first-declaring public/protected method; when the @throws is only implicit (no PHPDoc) and 'tooWideImplicitThrows' config is off, suppresses the error; when explicit, adds a tip suggesting a narrower @throws.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Same missing prerequisites (no @throws PHPDoc, no ThrowPoint collection, no TooWideThrowTypeCheck helper, no method-finality/visibility-driven applicability gating for this feature).

exceptions-api-restricted.name: TooWidePropertyHookThrowTypeRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Property-hook counterpart: on PropertyHookReturnStatementsNode, same 'declared @throws class never thrown' check for get/set hooks, gated by hook/property visibility and finality similarly to the method variant.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Property hooks have no representation in phpstan-rs's AST/parser, and the underlying @throws/ThrowPoint/TooWideThrowTypeCheck machinery is absent project-wide - no sensible hook-specific equivalent exists to build against.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: TooWideThrowTypeCheck
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Shared Check (not a Rule itself) used by TooWideFunctionThrowTypeRule/TooWideMethodThrowTypeRule/TooWidePropertyHookThrowTypeRule: given a declared @throws type and the collected ThrowPoints seen in the body, unions the actual thrown types (respecting the implicitThrows config flag to ignore implicit throws) and returns, for each declared throw class not matched by any actual throw point, a string describing that too-wide class so the caller can emit 'is never thrown' errors.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: phpstan-rs has no @throws docblock tracking, no ThrowPoint collection, and no 'declared throw type is too wide' diagnostic anywhere in src/checker or src/docblock.rs (grepped for throws/ThrowPoint/TooWide - nothing beyond unrelated comments). This is a real, registered PHPStan capability (not playground-only), so it is a genuine gap, not not_applicable.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: RestrictedInternalClassConstantUsageExtension
exceptions-api-restricted.description: RestrictedClassConstantUsageExtension implementation: flags access to a class constant that is itself @internal, or whose declaring class is @internal, from outside the declaring class's root namespace (or from a namespace-less non-matching class), emitting classConstant.internal / classConstant.internal<ClassType> identifiers.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Confirmed actively registered in conf/config.level0.neon (constant variant) - not a playground-only rule. phpstan-rs has no @internal-tag tracking anywhere (grepped docblock.rs/registry.rs/checker/*.rs for isInternal/@internal - nothing), so there is no equivalent restricted-usage diagnostic for internal class constants.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: RestrictedInternalClassNameUsageExtension
exceptions-api-restricted.description: RestrictedClassNameUsageExtension implementation: flags any usage of an @internal class/interface/trait/enum name (instantiation, extends, catch, instanceof, type hints, etc., via ClassNameUsageLocation) from outside its root namespace, with special-case skips when the usage location is itself an already-internal static method/property/constant access on that class.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Registered in conf/config.level0.neon. No @internal-tag class usage restriction exists in phpstan-rs; oop.rs/resolve.rs have no isInternal concept for class references.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: RestrictedInternalFunctionUsageExtension
exceptions-api-restricted.description: RestrictedFunctionUsageExtension implementation: flags calls to an @internal-tagged function made from outside that function's root namespace, emitting a function.internal identifier.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Registered in conf/config.level0.neon. calls.rs has no @internal function-tag restriction; registry.rs's function table carries no internal flag.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: RestrictedInternalMethodUsageExtension
exceptions-api-restricted.description: RestrictedMethodUsageExtension implementation: flags calls to an @internal method, or any method on an @internal declaring class, made from outside the declaring class's root namespace, distinguishing static vs instance method in both the message and the method.internal/staticMethod.internal<ClassType> identifiers.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Registered in conf/config.level2.neon. No equivalent in calls.rs/oop.rs; method reflection in registry.rs has no isInternal flag to check against.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: RestrictedInternalPropertyUsageExtension
exceptions-api-restricted.description: RestrictedPropertyUsageExtension implementation: flags access to an @internal property, or any property on an @internal declaring class, from outside the declaring class's root namespace, distinguishing static vs instance property in message and identifier (property.internal / staticProperty.internal<ClassType>).
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Registered in conf/config.level2.neon. No equivalent property-access restriction based on @internal exists in phpstan-rs's property handling.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: RestrictedInternalUsageHelper
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Shared helper (not itself a Rule/extension) used by all five RestrictedInternal*UsageExtension classes: shouldClassBeReported()/shouldFunctionBeReported() decide whether the current scope's namespace/class already 'owns' the internal symbol (skip reporting if so, and always skip for anonymous classes), and getRootNamespace() extracts the first namespace segment used for the 'from outside its root namespace X' message text.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: No corresponding namespace-scoping helper exists because there is no @internal-tag feature at all in phpstan-rs to build this helper for.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: UsedNamesRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Level-0 Rule<FileNode> that walks each namespace block in a file and reports a nonIgnorable error when a class/interface/trait/enum declaration's name, or a `use`/group-use alias, collides (case-insensitively) with an already-declared name or import in the same namespace scope of that file (identifiers: class.nameInUse/interface.nameInUse/trait.nameInUse/enum.nameInUse/use.nameInUse); function/const imports are exempted from the alias-collision check.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: phpstan-rs's parser records `use` imports (src/ast.rs UseImport, consumed via add_uses in project.rs/registry.rs) purely to build the alias->FQN map for name resolution; there is no pass anywhere that checks for duplicate class-declaration names or duplicate use-aliases within a namespace block, and no class.nameInUse/use.nameInUse diagnostics exist in the checker.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: ExistingNamesInGroupUseRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Level-0 Rule<GroupUse> that, for each member of a `use Foo\{...}` group-use statement, verifies the imported constant exists (constant.notFound), function exists and has correct case (function.notFound/function.nameCase), or class/interface/trait exists (delegating to the shared ClassNameCheck, which is what emits class.notFound-style errors) - group members inherit TYPE_CONSTANT/TYPE_FUNCTION/TYPE_NORMAL from the item or the group prefix.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Registered at level 0 - this is core baseline PHPStan behavior, not optional. phpstan-rs's stmt.rs Use-statement handling (src/parser/stmt.rs, group-use parsing) only builds the alias table for name resolution (see project.rs/registry.rs add_uses); grepping for 'constant.notFound'/'function.notFound' across src/ found nothing, so no rule verifies group-use targets actually exist or checks function-name case.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: ExistingNamesInUseRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Level-0 Rule<Use_> that, for a plain `use X;`/`use function f;`/`use const C;` statement, checks the imported constant exists (constant.notFound), function exists with correct case (function.notFound/function.nameCase), or class exists via ClassNameCheck - the single-item counterpart to ExistingNamesInGroupUseRule.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Registered at level 0 (core baseline). Same gap as ExistingNamesInGroupUseRule: phpstan-rs only uses `use` statements to populate the name-resolution alias map, never validates that the imported function/const/class actually exists or that function name-casing matches; class-not-found is separately handled elsewhere for actual class *usages* but not specifically at the `use` import site with this identifier.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: ArrayDimCastRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Playground-only Rule<ArrayDimFetch>: warns when a constant scalar array-access key (e.g. a float or bool literal used as `$arr[1.5]`) will be silently cast by PHP's array-key coercion rules to a different key value, identifier phpstanPlayground.arrayDimFetchCast.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Confirmed via conf/*.neon greps that no Playground/* rule is wired into the normal phpstan analyse pipeline; they are registered only in vendor/phpstan-src/issue-bot/playground.neon, a separate standalone service (phpstan.org's playground/issue-bot) outside the CLI analyzer phpstan-rs targets. Not part of the ground-truth CLI rule set to port.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: FunctionNeverRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Playground-only Rule<FunctionReturnStatementsNode>: when a function has zero return statements, delegates to NeverRuleHelper to determine whether every execution path always throws or always terminates, and if so suggests the return type should be declared 'never' (identifier phpstanPlayground.never).
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Only registered in issue-bot/playground.neon, not in any conf/config.level*.neon used by the standard analyser - a phpstan.org playground/issue-bot-only suggestion rule, out of scope for a CLI-analyzer rewrite.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: LiteralArrayKeyCastRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Playground-only Rule<Array_>: for each array-literal item with a constant scalar key, warns if PHP's array-key coercion would cast that literal key to a different value (identifier phpstanPlayground.arrayKeyCast) - the array-literal counterpart to ArrayDimCastRule.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Only registered in issue-bot/playground.neon; not part of the standard CLI rule levels.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: MethodNeverRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Playground-only Rule<MethodReturnStatementsNode>: the method-level counterpart of FunctionNeverRule, using NeverRuleHelper to suggest a method with no returns and only throw/terminate exit paths should declare return type 'never'.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Only registered in issue-bot/playground.neon, not any standard analyser level config.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: NeverRuleHelper
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Shared helper (not a Rule) used by FunctionNeverRule/MethodNeverRule: given a ReturnStatementsNode and its declared return type, returns false if the return type is already an explicit NeverType or the function is a generator, otherwise collects all execution-end nodes that are always-terminating but not plain `throw` expressions (return list is empty when every terminating path is a throw, meaning 'always throws'; false is returned early if any execution end is not always-terminating).
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Exists solely to support the two playground-only Never rules above; no equivalent needed since those rules aren't in scope.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: NoPhpCodeRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Playground-only Rule<FileNode>: reports when an analysed file's entire AST is a single InlineHTML node (i.e. the sample has no <?php tag at all), identifier phpstanPlayground.noPhp - a playground UX guard against pasting non-PHP snippets.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Registered only in issue-bot/playground.neon; meaningless outside the phpstan.org playground UI where users paste arbitrary snippets - phpstan-rs analyzes real project files that are always valid PHP files by construction.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: NotAnalysedTraitRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Playground-only Rule<CollectedDataNode>: cross-references TraitDeclarationCollector and TraitUseCollector data to report traits that are declared but never `use`d anywhere in the analysed file set, identifier phpstanPlayground.traitUnused, since PHPStan does not analyse trait bodies except through the classes that use them.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Only registered in issue-bot/playground.neon; addresses a playground-specific pitfall (single-file snippets with an unused trait silently not analysed) rather than a general CLI-analyzer concern.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: PhpdocCommentRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Playground-only Rule<Node\Stmt>: on every statement's attached comments, flags a comment whose text contains an `@tag`-looking token (regex `(\s|^)@\w+(\s|$)`) but does not start with the `/**` PHPDoc-block prefix (nor `//`/`#` single-line prefixes it explicitly skips), identifier phpstanPlayground.phpDoc - catches malformed `/* @param ... */` blocks that PHP-Parser won't recognise as PHPDoc.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Only registered in issue-bot/playground.neon; a playground authoring-hint rule, not part of the standard rule levels phpstan-rs targets.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: PromoteParameterRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: A generic Rule wrapper used only by phpstan.org's Playground: given a configurable bool parameter, it either suppresses a wrapped rule's errors entirely or re-emits them tagged 'phpstanPlayground.configParameter' with a tip explaining which config flag would enable them (used to preview stricter settings in the web UI), also de-duplicating against another already-registered instance of the same rule class via the DI container.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Namespace Playground, identifier prefix 'phpstanPlayground.*'; not wired into any conf/*.neon level config (verified: no reference to PromoteParameterRule outside its own file, and 'playground' in config.neon/parametersSchema.neon refers only to unrelated sourceLocatorPlaygroundMode). It is registered exclusively by the closed-source phpstan.org Playground application to preview config toggles interactively. No sensible standalone-CLI equivalent to build.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: StaticVarWithoutTypeRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Playground-only Rule for `Node\Stmt\Static_`: requires every `static $var` declaration to carry an `@var` PHPDoc tag (either one shared tag for a single var, or one entry per variable name when multiple vars are declared in one statement), else emits 'phpstanPlayground.staticWithoutType'.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Same Playground namespace/mechanism as PromoteParameterRule - not wired into standard conf/*.neon levels, only used by phpstan.org's web playground to encourage typed static vars in submitted snippets. No standard-CLI parity target.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: RestrictedClassConstantUsageExtension
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Pure DI-tagged extension interface (`phpstan.restrictedClassConstantUsageExtension`) with a single method `isRestrictedClassConstantUsage(ClassConstantReflection, Scope): ?RestrictedUsage` that third-party extensions (or PHPStan's own InternalTag extensions) implement to flag a class constant fetch as restricted (e.g. @internal).
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Marker/contract interface for PHPStan's third-party plugin extension system, no logic of its own. phpstan-rs is a monolithic checker with no equivalent plugin-extension architecture; the concrete behavior it enables by default (flagging @internal class-constant access) is tracked as missing on RestrictedClassConstantUsageRule below.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: RestrictedClassConstantUsageRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Real dispatch Rule on `Node\Expr\ClassConstFetch`: resolves the referenced class(es) (via the literal `Foo::BAR` name, or via RuleLevelHelper::findTypeToCheck for `$obj::BAR`/dynamic expressions), looks up the constant reflection, and calls every registered RestrictedClassConstantUsageExtension, re-checking with a RewrittenDeclaringClassClassConstantReflection when the constant is inherited so extensions see the actual fetch-site class; builds a RuleError from each non-null RestrictedUsage returned.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Autowired by default (#[AutowiredService]) and, per conf/config.level0.neon, driven by the InternalTag extensions (feature-toggled) to report `Access to constant X of internal class/constant Y from outside its allowed namespace`. phpstan-rs has zero @internal-tag enforcement anywhere (confirmed by grep across src/checker and src/*.rs) so this diagnostic family is entirely absent, not merely consolidated elsewhere.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: RestrictedClassNameUsageExtension
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Pure DI-tagged extension interface (`phpstan.restrictedClassNameUsageExtension`) with `isRestrictedClassNameUsage(ClassReflection, Scope, ClassNameUsageLocation): ?RestrictedUsage`, letting extensions flag a bare class-name usage (e.g. `new Foo`, `Foo::class`, `instanceof Foo`, extends/implements) as restricted, informed by a ClassNameUsageLocation describing where/how the name was used.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Marker/plugin-extension interface only, no check logic; consumed by PHPStan's InternalTag extension for @internal class usage. No sensible Rust plugin-architecture equivalent to build standalone (unlike the sibling *_Extension interfaces, this one has no matching dispatcher Rule file in this chunk - the dispatcher is RestrictedClassNameUsageRule, which lives outside this file list).

exceptions-api-restricted.name: RestrictedFunctionCallableUsageRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Dispatch Rule on `FunctionCallableNode` (first-class callable syntax `strlen(...)`): resolves the function reflection and calls every registered RestrictedFunctionUsageExtension, converting any returned RestrictedUsage into a RuleError.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Covers the first-class-callable variant of the same @internal-function check as RestrictedFunctionUsageRule. phpstan-rs has no first-class-callable-specific restricted-usage handling and no @internal enforcement at all.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: RestrictedFunctionUsageExtension
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Pure DI-tagged extension interface (`phpstan.restrictedFunctionUsageExtension`) with `isRestrictedFunctionUsage(FunctionReflection, Scope): ?RestrictedUsage`, the plugin point used to flag calls to a given function as restricted (default consumer: @internal functions).
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Marker interface, no logic. No plugin-extension architecture exists in phpstan-rs to mirror; the actual @internal-function diagnostic is tracked as missing on the two dispatcher rules (RestrictedFunctionUsageRule, RestrictedFunctionCallableUsageRule).

exceptions-api-restricted.name: RestrictedFunctionUsageRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Dispatch Rule on `Node\Expr\FuncCall`: for a statically-named call (`Name` node, not a dynamic `$fn()`), resolves the FunctionReflection and asks every registered RestrictedFunctionUsageExtension whether the call is restricted, emitting a RuleError per non-null result.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Default-wired via conf/config.level0.neon's phpstan.restrictedFunctionUsageExtension tag driven by InternalTag; produces 'Call to function X() from outside its allowed namespace' for @internal functions. phpstan-rs has no equivalent check anywhere in src/checker.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: RestrictedMethodCallableUsageRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Dispatch Rule on `MethodCallableNode` (first-class callable syntax `$obj->method(...)`): gets the type of the call target, iterates its object class names, resolves the method reflection per class, and asks each registered RestrictedMethodUsageExtension for a RestrictedUsage.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: First-class-callable counterpart of RestrictedMethodUsageRule, same default @internal-method wiring. No equivalent logic in phpstan-rs.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: RestrictedMethodUsageExtension
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Pure DI-tagged extension interface (`phpstan.restrictedMethodUsageExtension`) with `isRestrictedMethodUsage(ExtendedMethodReflection, Scope): ?RestrictedUsage`, the plugin point consumed by four different call-shape rules (instance call, static call, and both first-class-callable variants) plus the deprecated-string-cast rule.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Marker interface, no logic of its own. The concrete @internal-method diagnostics it powers are tracked as missing on RestrictedMethodUsageRule, RestrictedMethodCallableUsageRule, RestrictedStaticMethodUsageRule, RestrictedStaticMethodCallableUsageRule, and RestrictedUsageOfDeprecatedStringCastRule.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: RestrictedMethodUsageRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Dispatch Rule on `Node\Expr\MethodCall` (`$obj->method()`): gets the type of `$obj`, iterates its possible object class names, resolves the method reflection on each, and reports a RuleError for every non-null RestrictedUsage any registered RestrictedMethodUsageExtension returns.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Default-wired via conf/config.level2.neon's phpstan.restrictedMethodUsageExtension tag driven by InternalTag; produces 'Call to method X() of internal class Y from outside its allowed namespace'. phpstan-rs has no @internal-tag or restricted-method-usage checking (grep across src/checker/*.rs confirms no such logic).

exceptions-api-restricted.name: RestrictedPropertyUsageExtension
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Pure DI-tagged extension interface (`phpstan.restrictedPropertyUsageExtension`) with `isRestrictedPropertyUsage(ExtendedPropertyReflection, Scope): ?RestrictedUsage`, the plugin point consumed by both the instance-property and static-property restricted-usage rules.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Marker interface, no logic. Concrete @internal-property diagnostics tracked as missing on RestrictedPropertyUsageRule and RestrictedStaticPropertyUsageRule.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: RestrictedPropertyUsageRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Dispatch Rule on `Node\Expr\PropertyFetch` (`$obj->prop`): gets the type of `$obj`, iterates its object class names, resolves the instance-property reflection on each, and reports a RuleError for every non-null RestrictedUsage any registered RestrictedPropertyUsageExtension returns.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Default-wired via conf/config.level2.neon, driven by InternalTag for @internal properties. No equivalent in phpstan-rs.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: RestrictedStaticMethodCallableUsageRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Dispatch Rule on `StaticMethodCallableNode` (first-class callable `Foo::bar(...)`): resolves the referenced class(es) either from a literal `Name` or via RuleLevelHelper::findTypeToCheck for a dynamic class expression, resolves the method reflection, re-checks with a RewrittenDeclaringClassMethodReflection when the method is inherited, and reports errors from registered RestrictedMethodUsageExtensions.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: First-class-callable counterpart of RestrictedStaticMethodUsageRule; same default @internal-method wiring. No equivalent in phpstan-rs.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: RestrictedStaticMethodUsageRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Dispatch Rule on `Node\Expr\StaticCall` (`Foo::bar()`): resolves the referenced class(es) (literal name or dynamic via RuleLevelHelper), resolves the method reflection, re-checks with RewrittenDeclaringClassMethodReflection for inherited methods so the extension sees the actual call-site class, and reports errors from registered RestrictedMethodUsageExtensions.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Default-wired, driven by InternalTag for @internal static methods. phpstan-rs has no equivalent restricted-usage/@internal checking for static calls.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: RestrictedStaticPropertyUsageRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Dispatch Rule on `Node\Expr\StaticPropertyFetch` (`Foo::$bar`): resolves the referenced class(es) (literal or dynamic via RuleLevelHelper), resolves the static-property reflection, re-checks with RewrittenDeclaringClassPropertyReflection for inherited properties, and reports errors from registered RestrictedPropertyUsageExtensions.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Default-wired, driven by InternalTag for @internal static properties. No equivalent logic exists in phpstan-rs.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: RestrictedUsage
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Trivial immutable value object (private constructor + static `create()` factory) holding just `errorMessage` and `identifier`, returned by every RestrictedUsage*Extension implementation and consumed by the dispatch rules to build a RuleError; contains no check logic itself.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Pure DTO with no behavior of its own - equivalent in a Rust rewrite would only be meaningful once the RestrictedUsage engine itself (dispatch rules + InternalTag extensions) is implemented, which it currently is not (see the sibling Rule files above, all 'missing').

exceptions-api-restricted.name: RestrictedUsageOfDeprecatedStringCastRule
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Dispatch Rule on `Cast\String_` (explicit `(string) $obj` casts): gets the type of the cast operand, iterates its object class names, and for each class that natively declares `__toString`, asks registered RestrictedMethodUsageExtensions whether that `__toString` method is restricted, reporting an error if so - catching implicit magic-method invocation that the plain MethodCall-based rule would miss.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Despite the filename mentioning 'Deprecated', this is about @internal `__toString()` methods triggered via implicit string casts (same InternalTag-driven mechanism as the other RestrictedUsage rules), not a general deprecated-cast check (that is DeprecatedCastRule, a different file). phpstan-rs performs no @internal enforcement and no special-casing of `(string)` casts invoking a restricted `__toString`.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: RewrittenDeclaringClassClassConstantReflection
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Pure decorator implementing ClassConstantReflection: wraps an inner ClassConstantReflection and delegates every method to it verbatim except getDeclaringClass(), which returns a caller-supplied ClassReflection instead of the wrapped constant's real declaring class.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Zero check/analysis logic of its own; it is plumbing instantiated only by RestrictedClassConstantUsageRule to present each ancestor class in turn to a RestrictedUsageExtension (a PHPStan plugin-extension interface for 'restrict where this constant may be used', per phpstan-src CLAUDE.md's extension-points list). phpstan-rs has no restricted-usage extension subsystem (grep for RestrictedUsage/RestrictedMethod/RestrictedProperty/RestrictedClassConstant in src/ returns nothing) and, being an architecturally closed rewrite rather than a plugin host, has no sensible equivalent to build for this specific decorator.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: RewrittenDeclaringClassMethodReflection
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Pure decorator implementing ExtendedMethodReflection: wraps an inner ExtendedMethodReflection and delegates every method (variants, asserts, purity, throw type, etc.) except getDeclaringClass(), which returns a caller-supplied ClassReflection.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Same delegate-everything-but-declaring-class pattern; used by RestrictedStaticMethodUsageRule, RestrictedStaticMethodCallableUsageRule, and Classes/InstantiationRule.php to feed a per-ancestor-scoped method reflection to RestrictedUsageExtension implementations while walking a class hierarchy. No independent check logic. phpstan-rs has no restricted-usage extension mechanism to plug this into (confirmed via grep of src/), so there is no rewrite equivalent for this plumbing class specifically.

exceptions-api-restricted.name: RewrittenDeclaringClassPropertyReflection
exceptions-api-restricted.description: Pure decorator implementing ExtendedPropertyReflection: wraps an inner ExtendedPropertyReflection and delegates every method (readable/writable type, hooks, visibility, deprecation, etc.) except getDeclaringClass(), which returns a caller-supplied ClassReflection.
exceptions-api-restricted.notes: Used only by RestrictedStaticPropertyUsageRule to hand a per-ancestor declaring-class-rewritten property reflection to a RestrictedUsageExtension when walking the static property's class hierarchy. No check logic of its own. phpstan-rs has no restricted-usage extension subsystem (grep of src/ confirms), so this decorator's supporting role has no sensible Rust equivalent to build.

arrays-cast-operators-regex.name: AllowedArrayKeysTypes
arrays-cast-operators-regex.description: Static helper (not a Rule): getType() builds the union of scalar types legal as an array key (int|string, plus bool/float/null unless reportNonIntStringArrayKey/PHP-version deprecation applies), and narrowOffsetKeyType() narrows a foreach/array key's type given the container's own type - used by InvalidKeyInArrayDimFetchRule, InvalidKeyInArrayItemRule and NonexistentOffsetInArrayDimFetchCheck.
arrays-cast-operators-regex.notes: No equivalent 'legal array key type' concept exists anywhere in src/types.rs or src/checker/*.rs - array keys are never validated against int|string|bool|float|null, so there is nothing this helper's output feeds into.

arrays-cast-operators-regex.name: ArrayDestructuringRule
arrays-cast-operators-regex.description: Rule on Assign nodes whose LHS is list(...)/[...]: flags destructuring on a non-array/non-ArrayAccess RHS ('Cannot use array destructuring on X'), and recursively checks each destructured key exists via NonexistentOffsetInArrayDimFetchCheck, including nested list() targets.
arrays-cast-operators-regex.notes: src/checker/assignment.rs's check_assignment_target/bind_assignment_target recurse through nested ArrayLiteral destructuring targets to bind element types (including via ArrayShape field lookup), but never validates that the RHS is actually array-like, and never checks that a destructured key exists on the RHS - no diagnostic is emitted for either case.

arrays-cast-operators-regex.name: ArrayUnpackingRule
arrays-cast-operators-regex.description: Rule on ArrayItem: on PHP versions that don't support string-keyed array unpacking (<8.1), flags '...$x' spread items whose iterable key type is (possibly) string with 'arrayUnpacking.stringOffset'.
arrays-cast-operators-regex.notes: src/checker/expr.rs's infer_spread_array_literal_type merges spread sources' key/value types for inference purposes only; it never checks the spread source's key type against string-ness or gates behavior on a target PHP version, and no diagnostic is emitted.

arrays-cast-operators-regex.name: DeadForeachRule
arrays-cast-operators-regex.description: Rule on Foreach_ statements: flags 'Empty array passed to foreach.' when the iterated expression's type is iterable but provably never iterates at least once (isIterableAtLeastOnce()->no() would already exclude it, i.e. this fires on definitely-empty arrays).
arrays-cast-operators-regex.notes: src/checker/stmt.rs's Foreach arm only computes the loop-variable element type via array_element_type() for inference/narrowing purposes; it never inspects whether the subject could be empty, and no diagnostic exists for it.

arrays-cast-operators-regex.name: DuplicateKeysInLiteralArraysRule
arrays-cast-operators-regex.description: Rule on LiteralArrayNode: tracks seen/auto-incrementing keys (including union-typed keys) across a literal array's items and reports 'array.duplicateKey' with all duplicate positions listed, when the same scalar key value appears more than once.
arrays-cast-operators-regex.notes: src/checker/expr.rs's infer_array_literal_type (around line 1845) explicitly implements only the PHP runtime semantics of 'a later duplicate key overwrites an earlier one' for type-inference purposes ('A later duplicate key overwrites an earlier one, matching real PHP's own array-literal semantics') - it never emits a diagnostic about the duplication itself.

arrays-cast-operators-regex.name: InvalidKeyInArrayDimFetchRule
arrays-cast-operators-regex.description: Rule on ArrayDimFetch: when the base is (possibly) an array, checks the dim expression's type against AllowedArrayKeysTypes and reports 'offsetAccess.invalidOffset' ('Invalid'/'Possibly invalid array key type X') when it isn't a legal array key type.
arrays-cast-operators-regex.notes: No key-type validation exists for $x[$key] reads/writes in src/checker/expr.rs or assignment.rs - only check_shape_key_access's narrow 'does this literal key exist in a known ArrayShape' check exists, which is a different concern (existence, not key-type legality).

arrays-cast-operators-regex.name: InvalidKeyInArrayItemRule
arrays-cast-operators-regex.description: Rule on ArrayItem (literal array key => value pairs): checks the key expression's type against AllowedArrayKeysTypes and reports 'array.invalidKey' when the key type isn't a legal array key (e.g. an object or resource key).
arrays-cast-operators-regex.notes: src/checker/expr.rs's infer_array_literal_type accepts any key expression kind (falling back to Type::Array(Mixed) degradation for non-literal keys) without ever validating that the key's type is a legal scalar array key.

arrays-cast-operators-regex.name: IterableInForeachRule
arrays-cast-operators-regex.description: Rule on InForeachNode: flags 'foreach.nonIterable' when the foreach subject's type is not iterable, and separately surfaces 'Iterating over an object of an unknown class %s.' via RuleLevelHelper when the class is unresolvable.
arrays-cast-operators-regex.notes: src/checker/stmt.rs's Foreach handling (and control_flow.rs's CFG-building counterpart) only reads the subject's type to compute the loop variable's element type; no check ever verifies the subject is actually iterable, so a foreach over e.g. an int or a non-iterable object is silently accepted.

arrays-cast-operators-regex.name: NonexistentOffsetInArrayDimFetchCheck
arrays-cast-operators-regex.description: Shared Check helper (not itself a Rule, injected into ArrayDestructuringRule and NonexistentOffsetInArrayDimFetchRule): given a base expr and a dim type, reports 'offsetAccess.notFound' when hasOffsetValueType() is definitely no (skipping cases already covered by InvalidKeyInArrayDimFetchRule), and optionally ('maybe' reporting flags) when it's only possibly missing, with separate config knobs for general vs. constant arrays.
arrays-cast-operators-regex.notes: src/checker/assignment.rs's check_shape_key_access is a narrow analog: it flags a literal string/int key with 'array{...} has no key X' but only when the base's inferred type is (a union entirely composed of) a fully-known Type::ArrayShape - it has no notion of general Type::Array offset existence, no reportMaybes/reportPossiblyNonexistent* configurability, and doesn't special-case optional shape fields the way the PHP version's 'maybe' path does.

arrays-cast-operators-regex.name: NonexistentOffsetInArrayDimFetchRule
arrays-cast-operators-regex.description: Rule on ArrayDimFetch: skips implicit array-creation ($x[...] on an as-yet-undefined $x), checks the base is offset-accessible ('offsetAccess.nonOffsetAccessible'), special-cases array_key_first/array_key_last/array_rand/count()-1 idioms as always-safe, then delegates the remaining existence check to NonexistentOffsetInArrayDimFetchCheck.
arrays-cast-operators-regex.notes: src/checker/expr.rs's Index arm (around line 802) calls check_shape_key_access for reads, giving the same narrow ArrayShape+literal-key coverage as the Check class above, but has none of this rule's own logic: no 'is the base even offset-accessible' check, no array_key_first/array_key_last/array_rand/count()-1 special-casing, and no isInExpressionAssign/isUndefinedExpressionAllowed exemptions.

arrays-cast-operators-regex.name: OffsetAccessAssignOpRule
arrays-cast-operators-regex.description: Rule on AssignOp (e.g. $x['k'] += 1) whose var is an ArrayDimFetch: computes what setOffsetValueType() would do with the container/dim types and reports 'offsetAssign.dimType' when the container can't accept a new/existing offset of that dim type at all.
arrays-cast-operators-regex.notes: write_index_into() in src/checker/assignment.rs (used by bind_assignment_target for the write side) always succeeds or silently no-ops (returns None, meaning 'don't guess') - it never distinguishes 'this container structurally cannot take this offset' and never emits a diagnostic; AssignOp isn't specially handled for ArrayDimFetch targets at all.

arrays-cast-operators-regex.name: OffsetAccessAssignmentRule
arrays-cast-operators-regex.description: Rule on ArrayDimFetch nodes that are themselves an assignment target (plain '=' form): same setOffsetValueType()-based check as OffsetAccessAssignOpRule, reporting 'offsetAssign.dimType' when the container rejects the new/existing offset's key type outright.
arrays-cast-operators-regex.notes: Same gap as OffsetAccessAssignOpRule - write_index_into never rejects a write based on the container's structural ability to hold a given key type; there is no notion of a container type that disallows a particular offset kind (e.g. writing a string key into a `list`).

arrays-cast-operators-regex.name: OffsetAccessValueAssignmentRule
arrays-cast-operators-regex.description: Rule on any Expr that is Assign/AssignOp/AssignRef with an ArrayDimFetch var whose own base is an *object* type: checks the assigned value's type against what the object's setOffsetValueType() (i.e. ArrayAccess::offsetSet's declared param type) would accept, reporting 'offsetAssign.valueType' on mismatch.
arrays-cast-operators-regex.notes: There is no modeling anywhere in src/checker of ArrayAccess-implementing objects supporting `$obj[$k] = $v` with offsetSet()-typed value checking; only plain array/ArrayShape containers are tracked for offset writes, and even those never validate the assigned value's type against a declared value type.

arrays-cast-operators-regex.name: OffsetAccessWithoutDimForReadingRule
arrays-cast-operators-regex.description: Rule on ArrayDimFetch: reports the non-ignorable 'offsetAccess.noDim' error 'Cannot use [] for reading.' whenever a dim-less `$x[]` appears outside of an assignment-target position.
arrays-cast-operators-regex.notes: src/checker/expr.rs's Index arm (idx: Option<Expr>) never special-cases a None dim used in read position - no diagnostic exists for `$x[]` used anywhere other than an assignment/foreach-value target.

arrays-cast-operators-regex.name: UnpackIterableInArrayRule
arrays-cast-operators-regex.description: Rule on LiteralArrayNode: for each unpacked ('...$x') array item, reports 'arrayUnpacking.nonIterable' ('Only iterables can be unpacked, X given.') when the spread expression's type isn't iterable.
arrays-cast-operators-regex.notes: src/checker/expr.rs's infer_spread_array_literal_type (around line 1881) treats any spread source it can't resolve into an ArrayShape as 'degraded' and falls back to array_element_type().unwrap_or(Mixed) purely for inference - it never checks or reports that the spread source is actually iterable.

arrays-cast-operators-regex.name: DeprecatedCastRule
arrays-cast-operators-regex.description: Rule on Cast nodes: on PHP 8.5+ (phpVersion->deprecatesNonStandardCasts()), flags the non-standard cast spellings (integer)/(boolean)/(double)/(binary) with 'cast.deprecated', recommending (int)/(bool)/(float)/(string) instead - distinguished via the parser's stored 'kind' attribute on each Cast node.
arrays-cast-operators-regex.notes: src/parser/expr.rs's try_parse_cast (around line 409-412) immediately normalizes every alias spelling ('integer'->'int', 'double'/'real'->'float', 'binary'->'string', 'boolean'->'bool') into one canonical ExprKind::Cast(ty, ...) string, discarding which spelling was actually used - the distinction this rule depends on isn't even representable in the current AST, and there's no PhpVersion-gated check anywhere.

arrays-cast-operators-regex.name: EchoRule
arrays-cast-operators-regex.description: Rule on Stmt\Echo_: for each echoed expression, reports 'echo.nonString' ('Parameter #N (X) of echo cannot be converted to string.') when the expression's type's toString() coercion would fail (e.g. an object without __toString, an array).
arrays-cast-operators-regex.notes: src/checker/stmt.rs's Echo arm (around line 130) only calls check_expr on each expression for its own side effects (undefined-variable checks etc.) - there is no toString()-coercion concept in src/types.rs and no diagnostic is ever produced for a non-stringable echo argument.

arrays-cast-operators-regex.name: InvalidCastRule
arrays-cast-operators-regex.description: Rule on Expr\Cast: dispatches to the source type's toInteger()/toBoolean()/toFloat()/toString() (matching the cast kind) and reports 'cast.int'/'cast.bool'/'cast.double'/'cast.string' ('Cannot cast X to Y.') when that coercion is impossible (e.g. casting an array to string, or certain objects to int/float).
arrays-cast-operators-regex.notes: src/checker/expr.rs's Cast arm (both check_expr around line 636 and infer_expr around line 1581) unconditionally maps the cast keyword to its target Type variant (Int/Float/String/Bool/Array/Object/Null) regardless of the source expression's actual type - there's no toInteger/toBoolean/toFloat/toString concept on Type at all, so an invalid cast (e.g. `(string) $someArray`) is never flagged.

arrays-cast-operators-regex.name: InvalidPartOfEncapsedStringRule
arrays-cast-operators-regex.description: Rule on InterpolatedString: for each non-literal part, uses RuleLevelHelper to find its type and reports 'encapsedStringPart.nonString' if that part's type's toString() is an ErrorType (i.e. the value cannot legally be cast to string, e.g. an array or a class without __toString).
arrays-cast-operators-regex.our_location: src/checker/expr.rs:1173 (ExprKind::Interpolated) checks each part's sub-expression via check_expr but never inspects whether the part's type is string-castable
arrays-cast-operators-regex.notes: phpstan-rs has no concept of a Type::toString()/ErrorType coercion check anywhere (no per-Type castability model, no object __toString tracking for string coercion). No diagnostic is ever raised for interpolating a non-stringable value (array, bare object) inside a double-quoted string.

arrays-cast-operators-regex.name: PrintRule
arrays-cast-operators-regex.description: Rule on Print_ expression: reports 'print.nonString' if the printed expression's type cannot be cast to string (same ErrorType-from-toString() check as InvalidPartOfEncapsedStringRule).
arrays-cast-operators-regex.our_location: src/parser/postfix.rs:446-451 (print parsed as a synthetic call to name "print"); src/checker/calls.rs:453 ("print" merely whitelisted as a language construct so it isn't flagged as an undefined function call)
arrays-cast-operators-regex.notes: print's argument is never type-checked for string-castability; the same missing string-coercion-validity primitive as InvalidPartOfEncapsedStringRule is the root cause.

arrays-cast-operators-regex.name: UnsetCastRule
arrays-cast-operators-regex.description: Rule on Cast\Unset_: if the configured PhpVersion no longer supports the (unset) cast (removed in PHP 8.0), reports non-ignorable error 'cast.unset'.
arrays-cast-operators-regex.our_location: src/parser/expr.rs:395-429 (try_parse_cast accepts "unset" as a normalized cast kind); src/checker/expr.rs:636-648 (Cast typing maps "unset" -> Type::Null, no diagnostic)
arrays-cast-operators-regex.notes: phpstan-rs has no PhpVersion/target-version configuration concept anywhere in the codebase, so no version-gated cast rule (unset/void/backtick/inc-dec deprecations) can fire. The (unset) cast is silently accepted and typed as null with zero diagnostics, even though it is a PHP 8.0+ fatal-adjacent removed feature.

arrays-cast-operators-regex.name: VoidCastRule
arrays-cast-operators-regex.description: Rule on Cast\Void_: reports 'cast.voidNotSupported' if PhpVersion doesn't support it (only PHP 8.5+), and independently (version-agnostically) reports non-ignorable 'cast.void' whenever the (void) cast appears anywhere other than a first-level statement (i.e. used within a larger expression).
arrays-cast-operators-regex.our_location: src/parser/expr.rs:395-429 ("void" accepted as a cast kind); src/checker/expr.rs:636-648 (Cast typing, "void" falls into the default Type::Mixed arm)
arrays-cast-operators-regex.notes: Both halves are absent: no PhpVersion gating (see UnsetCastRule note) and no notion of "first-level statement" context is tracked on Scope/Checker to detect a (void) cast used mid-expression, so 'cast.void' can never be emitted either.

arrays-cast-operators-regex.name: BacktickRule
arrays-cast-operators-regex.description: Rule on ShellExec (backtick operator): if PhpVersion deprecates the backtick operator (PHP 8.5+), reports 'backtick.deprecated' with an auto-fix that rewrites the backtick expression into an equivalent shell_exec() call.
arrays-cast-operators-regex.our_location: src/parser/postfix.rs:584-596 (Token::ShellExec is parsed and immediately desugared into a call to shell_exec() during parsing itself, discarding the fact it was written with backticks)
arrays-cast-operators-regex.notes: No PhpVersion gating exists (see UnsetCastRule), and phpstan-rs has no autofix/Fixable mechanism at all. Additionally the parser's own desugaring erases the backtick-vs-function-call distinction before the checker ever sees the AST, so even a version-agnostic "backtick used" diagnostic could not be added without first preserving that distinction in the AST.

arrays-cast-operators-regex.name: InvalidAssignVarRule
arrays-cast-operators-regex.description: Rule on any Expr that is Assign/AssignOp/AssignRef: reports non-ignorable 'nullsafe.assign' if the LHS contains a nullsafe (?->) access, 'nullsafe.byRef' if an AssignRef's RHS contains a nullsafe access, and 'assign.invalidExpr' if the LHS (recursing through List_ destructuring) is anything other than a Variable/PropertyFetch/ArrayDimFetch/StaticPropertyFetch.
arrays-cast-operators-regex.notes: check_assignment_target recurses through ArrayLiteral/PropertyAccess/Index targets and falls back to a plain check_expr for anything else, but never flags a genuinely non-assignable LHS (e.g. assigning to a function-call result or a literal) nor checks for nullsafe operators appearing on an assignment target/by-ref source.

arrays-cast-operators-regex.name: InvalidBinaryOperationRule
arrays-cast-operators-regex.description: Rule on Expr (BinaryOp or AssignOp): synthesizes a TypeExpr-substituted copy of the operation using the narrowed operand types and asks the scope to re-evaluate its resulting type; if that result is an ErrorType, reports '<binaryOp|assignOp>.invalid' describing the illegal combination (e.g. array + object, string - int).
arrays-cast-operators-regex.our_location: src/checker/expr.rs (infer_binary, e.g. BinOp::Add at ~2377, BinOp::Sub/Mul/Pow at ~2399, BinOp::Concat at ~2349)
arrays-cast-operators-regex.notes: infer_binary always produces a best-effort result type for every operand-type combination (falling back to permissive types like Union([Int,Float]) or Mixed) and never treats any operand pairing as an outright type error, so no diagnostic is ever raised for operations PHP would actually fatal on (e.g. array + object).

arrays-cast-operators-regex.name: InvalidComparisonOperationRule
arrays-cast-operators-regex.description: Rule on BinaryOp (==, !=, <, <=, >, >=, <=>): flags a comparison as invalid ('<op>.invalid') when exactly one side is a definite number and the other is a possibly-nullable object or possibly-nullable array (a comparison PHP itself errors on), consulting OperatorTypeSpecifyingExtensionRegistry first for custom-object overrides.
arrays-cast-operators-regex.our_location: src/checker/expr.rs:2362-2372 (Eq/Identical/NotEq/.../Lt/Gt/LtEq/GtEq all just return Type::Bool unconditionally)
arrays-cast-operators-regex.notes: No operand-type validation of any kind is performed for comparison operators; a comparison between, say, an int and an array/object is typed as plain bool with no error.

arrays-cast-operators-regex.name: InvalidIncDecOperationRule
arrays-cast-operators-regex.description: Rule on PreInc/PostInc/PreDec/PostDec: reports '<preInc|postInc|preDec|postDec>.expr' if the operand isn't a Variable/ArrayDimFetch/PropertyFetch/StaticPropertyFetch, and '<...>.type' if the operand's type isn't one of float/int/(numeric-)string/SimpleXMLElement/GMP/BcMath\Number/null/bool (version-gated), with tips about PHP-version deprecations for non-numeric-string/null/bool operands.
arrays-cast-operators-regex.notes: This arm only updates the tracked variable type (e.g. null -> int on increment) and infers the resulting type; it never validates that the operand is a legal lvalue-like target or that its type actually supports ++/--, and there is no PhpVersion concept to drive the deprecation tips.

arrays-cast-operators-regex.name: InvalidUnaryOperationRule
arrays-cast-operators-regex.description: Rule on Expr (UnaryPlus/UnaryMinus/BitwiseNot): synthesizes a TypeExpr-substituted copy of the unary op and re-evaluates it via the scope; reports 'unaryOp.invalid' if the result is an ErrorType (e.g. ~ on an array/object, or +/- on a non-numeric value).
arrays-cast-operators-regex.our_location: src/checker/expr.rs:619-634 (ExprKind::Unary Not/Neg/Plus and the generic Unary/Grouping fallback)
arrays-cast-operators-regex.notes: Unary minus/plus coerce string operands to Int and otherwise pass the operand type through unchanged; BitwiseNot isn't special-cased at all (falls into the generic passthrough arm at line 633). No case is ever treated as a type error, so applying ~ or unary -/+ to an array or object produces no diagnostic.

arrays-cast-operators-regex.name: PipeOperatorRule
arrays-cast-operators-regex.description: Rule on BinaryOp\Pipe (PHP 8.5 |> operator): if the right-hand callable's first parameter is passed by reference, reports 'pipe.byRef' since a pipe's implicit temporary value can't be passed by reference.
arrays-cast-operators-regex.our_location: src/lexer.rs:1295-1296 (Token::PipeGt lexed for |>); src/parser/expr.rs:259-262 (parsed into BinOp::Pipe); src/checker/expr.rs:2436-2440 (BinOp::Pipe typed as Type::Mixed unconditionally)
arrays-cast-operators-regex.notes: The |> operator itself is correctly lexed, parsed, and distinguished from bitwise-or (Token::Pipe is a separate token from Token::PipeGt), so operator-level parity is good, but the checker never inspects the right-hand callable's parameter list, so a by-reference first parameter on the piped-to callable is never flagged.

arrays-cast-operators-regex.name: RegularExpressionPatternRule
arrays-cast-operators-regex.description: Rule on FuncCall: for any preg_* function, extracts every statically-known pattern string argument (including array-of-patterns forms for preg_replace/preg_filter/preg_replace_callback and its _array variant, and simple concatenation via RegexExpressionHelper) and validates each with Nette\Utils\Strings::match(), reporting 'regexp.pattern' with the underlying PCRE error message if the pattern is malformed.
arrays-cast-operators-regex.our_location: src/regex_groups.rs (parse_capture_groups and its supporting hand-rolled regex-atom scanner)
arrays-cast-operators-regex.notes: regex_groups.rs implements its own PCRE-subset parser, but purely to infer named/numbered capture groups for preg_match()'s $matches output shape; on anything it can't confidently parse it just returns None silently (no diagnostic path exists) rather than validating pattern well-formedness and reporting a syntax error back to the user.

arrays-cast-operators-regex.name: RegularExpressionQuotingRule
arrays-cast-operators-regex.description: Rule on FuncCall: for preg_match/preg_match_all/preg_filter/preg_grep/preg_replace/preg_replace_callback/preg_split calls whose pattern argument is a string concatenation, recursively finds preg_quote() sub-calls used to build the pattern and validates that preg_quote()'s optional delimiter argument matches the pattern's own actual delimiter character(s) (accounting for characters PCRE always escapes regardless), reporting 'argument.invalidPregQuote' for a missing or mismatched delimiter argument.
arrays-cast-operators-regex.notes: No equivalent logic exists anywhere in src/ - no delimiter-extraction helper, no preg_quote-argument cross-checking. This is a narrow but real correctness check (catching the classic preg_quote($x) forgetting its delimiter, or being passed the wrong one) with nothing analogous in phpstan-rs's call-checking (src/checker/calls.rs).

standalone-checks.name: AttributesCheck
standalone-checks.description: A shared Check class (not a Rule itself) that class/function/property/param attribute rules delegate to: validates each #[Attribute(...)] use — the named class exists, is actually an Attribute class, isn't abstract, has the required target flag, isn't a non-repeatable duplicate, isn't deprecated, and that its constructor is public and invoked with valid arguments (via FunctionCallParametersCheck) — plus case-sensitivity of the attribute class name.
standalone-checks.notes: phpstan-rs's lexer.rs only skips PHP attribute syntax while parsing stub files (skip_stub_availability_attribute etc.); there is no AST attribute-group node processed by the checker and no semantic validation of attribute classes anywhere in src/checker/*. Nothing to point to as even a partial equivalent.

standalone-checks.name: ClassCaseSensitivityCheck
standalone-checks.description: Check class comparing a referenced class/interface/trait/enum name's as-written case against its canonical declared case (skipping built-ins unless configured, use-alias imports, and class_alias renames), emitting a '<type>.nameCase' diagnostic on mismatch.
standalone-checks.notes: No case-sensitivity comparison of referenced vs. declared class names exists in src/; grepping for nameCase/case-sensitivity logic across the checker and registry turns up nothing.

standalone-checks.name: ClassForbiddenNameCheck
standalone-checks.description: Check class flagging class names that carry PHP-Scoper/Rector/PHPUnit/Box/PHPStan internal prefixing (plus prefixes contributed by ForbiddenClassNameExtension) as accidental leaked-prefix references, with a nonignorable 'class.prefixed' diagnostic and a tip suggesting the unprefixed name.
