standalone-checks.notes: No prefix-scanning logic for internal PHAR-scoping artifacts exists in src/. This is a fairly self-contained string check independent of full class resolution, so it would be easy to add, but nothing implements it today.

standalone-checks.name: ClassNameCheck
standalone-checks.description: Check class that is the single dispatcher every class-name-referencing rule calls: runs ClassCaseSensitivityCheck, ClassForbiddenNameCheck, and any RestrictedClassNameUsageExtension against a batch of (className, AST node) pairs for a given usage location.
standalone-checks.notes: Since neither of the two checks it aggregates (case sensitivity, forbidden name) exists in phpstan-rs, and there is no extension-point equivalent for restricted-class-name-usage, the orchestrator itself has no counterpart.

standalone-checks.name: DateIntervalInstantiationRule
standalone-checks.description: A real Rule<New_> that, for `new DateInterval($literal)` calls, actually constructs a native DateInterval with the literal string and reports a 'new.dateInterval' error if PHP itself throws (invalid ISO-8601 duration format).
standalone-checks.notes: grep for DateInterval anywhere in src/checker/*.rs and src/registry* returns nothing; phpstan-rs has no constant-string-literal runtime-probing rule for DateInterval construction.

standalone-checks.name: DateTimeInstantiationRule
standalone-checks.description: A real Rule<New_> (registered at level 5) that, for `new DateTime($literal)`/`new DateTimeImmutable($literal)`, constructs a native DateTime with the literal and inspects DateTime::getLastErrors() to report each parse warning/error as 'new.dateTime'/'new.dateTimeImmutable'.
standalone-checks.notes: Same situation as DateIntervalInstantiationRule — no DateTime-string-literal validation exists anywhere in src/.

standalone-checks.name: FunctionCallParametersCheck
standalone-checks.description: The large shared Check class every call-site rule (function/method/static-method/constructor/attribute calls) delegates to: normalizes positional/named/unpacked arguments, checks arity against min/max parameter counts, validates named-argument ordering and support, checks argument types against parameter types (with template-type resolution and unresolvable-type diagnostics), validates by-reference argument targets (readonly properties, nullsafe chains, non-reference-returning calls), checks allowed-constant/exclusive-group/bitmask constraints on constant arguments, and flags an unused void-returning call result.
standalone-checks.notes: src/checker/calls.rs `check_args` (around line 262) implements the core of this: too-few/too-many positional-argument-count errors and a per-argument type-compatibility check against the resolved parameter type (with a Mixed-argument short-circuit). It has no equivalent for named-argument-specific diagnostics (unknown parameter, duplicate/already-passed, positional-after-named), unpacked-argument iterable validation, unresolvable-template-type reporting, allowed-constant/exclusive-group/bitmask checks, or the 'void-returning call used as a value' diagnostic. By-ref handling (same file, ~line 60-140) only recognizes plain `Variable` arguments for inferring the post-call type and never rejects an invalid by-ref target (readonly property, nullsafe chain, non-ref-returning call) the way NullsafeCheck/FunctionCallParametersCheck jointly do.

standalone-checks.name: FunctionDefinitionCheck
standalone-checks.description: Check class validating function/method/anonymous-function declarations: every class referenced in a parameter or return type (native+PHPDoc) must exist and must not be a trait; flags unresolvable pure-intersection native types; deprecation diagnostics for implicitly-nullable parameter types, unsupported union types pre-PHP-8, and required-parameter-after-optional; validates @template types are actually used in a parameter; validates method @self-out types; and flags #[NoDiscard] misuse on void/never returns.
standalone-checks.notes: phpstan-rs performs no 'referenced class does not exist' diagnostic anywhere — grepping every checker file for self.report(...) calls involving class-existence turns up zero hits, and none of FunctionDefinitionCheck's deprecation-era messages (implicitly nullable, union-type support, required-after-optional, self-out, NoDiscard) appear. src/checker/generics.rs does check template-variance misuse (covariant-in-input-position etc., ~line 218) but not the 'template type unused in any parameter' diagnostic this file emits.

standalone-checks.name: FunctionReturnTypeCheck
standalone-checks.description: Check class validating a `return` statement (or generator's implicit TReturn) against the function's declared return type: reports explicit-`never`-type violations, empty-`return;` inside a non-void function, a returned value inside a void function, and general return-value/return-type mismatches, resolving late-bound types first.
standalone-checks.notes: src/checker/stmt.rs's Return handling (Stmt::Return(Some) around line 80 and Stmt::Return(None) around line 100) covers general return-type-mismatch and 'bare return; inside a function whose declared type doesn't accept null' (generator-aware, skipping the getReturn()-only case), reported at severity level 3. It has no dedicated diagnostic for an explicit `never`-typed function actually reaching a return statement, and no distinct 'value returned from a void function' message — a value-returning return against a Void-declared type just falls through the same generic is_assignable mismatch path (or possibly none at all, since Type::Void has no special-cased is_assignable branch found in types.rs/checker.rs).

standalone-checks.name: IssetCheck
standalone-checks.description: Check class that renders human-readable diagnostics from the engine's already-resolved IssetabilityResolution chain for isset()/empty()/??: 'variable is never defined', 'offset does not exist', 'always exists and is not falsy/is not null', and 'nullsafe access is unnecessary, use -> instead', walking variable/offset/property links.
standalone-checks.notes: phpstan-rs explicitly does not check isset()/empty() targets: src/checker/expr.rs (~line 195-224) computes `is_existence_probe` for isset/empty calls specifically to route their arguments through `check_expr_quiet_root`, a deliberate design choice (per its own comment) to never flag 'offset doesn't exist'-style diagnostics for these constructs. No 'always exists' / 'never defined' / 'redundant nullsafe' diagnostics exist anywhere in the checker.

standalone-checks.name: MissingTypehintCheck
standalone-checks.description: Check class (helper) that walks a resolved Type looking for: iterable types missing an explicit value type (bare `array`/`iterable`), non-generic ObjectType instances of a class that is itself generic (missing template arguments), and Closure/callable types with no declared signature — feeding the higher rule-level 'missing typehint' diagnostics.
standalone-checks.notes: No equivalent type-tree traversal for 'iterable value type missing' or 'generic class used without template args' or 'callable with no signature' exists in types.rs or the checker; grepping for related terms (missingType, noValueType, iterableValue-as-diagnostic) returns nothing tied to a diagnostic.

standalone-checks.name: NullsafeCheck
standalone-checks.description: Tiny recursive helper: walks an expression's access chain (property fetch, array-dim fetch, method call, static call/property, list()) to determine whether it contains a nullsafe operator (`?->`) anywhere, used solely to gate the 'cannot pass by reference' diagnostic in FunctionCallParametersCheck.
standalone-checks.notes: phpstan-rs does track nullsafe for type-nullability propagation (e.g. src/checker/expr.rs lines ~382,526,1089,1154 widen the result to nullable), but nowhere reuses that to reject a nullsafe chain passed as a by-reference argument — calls.rs's by-ref handling (~line 60-140) only special-cases plain `Variable` args and has no 'contains nullsafe anywhere in this expression' check at all.

standalone-checks.name: ParameterCastableToStringCheck
standalone-checks.description: Check class helper (used by implode/join, sort-comparator, and castable-to-number rules) that verifies every element type of an array argument can be cast via a supplied cast function (e.g. toString/toNumber) without producing ErrorType, reporting a formatted 'argument.type' diagnostic otherwise.
standalone-checks.notes: No equivalent element-castability validation exists for implode/join or similar array-consuming string functions in src/checker/calls.rs or elsewhere; these functions aren't specially modeled for this concern.

standalone-checks.name: UnusedFunctionParametersCheck
standalone-checks.description: Check class computing the set of variable names actually referenced in a function/closure body (recursively, with special handling for func_get_args()/get_defined_vars()/compact()/dynamic-name variables which force treating all defined variables as used) to report each unused constructor-promoted parameter or unused closure `use (...)` variable.
standalone-checks.notes: grep for 'unused' anywhere in non-test src/ returns zero hits — phpstan-rs implements no unused-parameter or unused-closure-use detection at all, consistent with it having no dead-code-analysis category in general.

classes-traits.name: AccessPrivateConstantThroughStaticRule
classes-traits.description: Rule flagging `static::CONST` access to a private constant as unsafe (late static binding could resolve to a subclass without that constant), unless the enclosing class is final.
classes-traits.notes: phpstan-rs's registry.lookup_const (src/registry.rs:741) returns only a bare Type for a class constant, with no visibility field tracked at all, so there is no data to build this check from yet. StaticAccess constant-fetch handling (src/checker/expr.rs:1013-1083, :1701-1729) never inspects visibility.

classes-traits.name: AllowedSubTypesRule
classes-traits.description: Rule enforcing sealed-hierarchy restrictions declared via the pluggable AllowedSubTypesClassReflectionExtension: a class/interface may restrict which classes are allowed to be its subtype, and this rule reports any subclass/implementor not on that allow-list.
classes-traits.notes: No equivalent extension point or sealed-hierarchy concept exists anywhere in src/registry.rs or src/checker/*. In stock PHPStan this rule is inert unless a third-party extension registers allowed subtypes, so it is low priority, but it is a real generic mechanism (not DI-only plumbing) and thus not not_applicable.

classes-traits.name: ClassAttributesRule
classes-traits.description: Rule checking a class's PHP attributes: forbids the `#[Deprecated]` attribute on a class declaration and forbids `#[AllowDynamicProperties]` on readonly classes/enums/interfaces, plus delegates general attribute-target validation to AttributesCheck.
classes-traits.notes: phpstan-rs's lexer discards `#[...]` attribute syntax entirely at lex time (src/lexer.rs:524-529, only special-cased for a couple of stub-only attributes it needs for signature gating) and there is no AST node or AttributesCheck-equivalent anywhere in src/ast.rs or src/checker/*. No infrastructure exists to build this on.

classes-traits.name: ClassConstantAttributesRule
classes-traits.description: Rule delegating to AttributesCheck to validate that attributes attached to a class constant declaration target TARGET_CLASS_CONSTANT correctly.
classes-traits.notes: Same root cause as ClassAttributesRule: attributes are never parsed into the AST, so there is no attribute list on ClassConst nodes to check.

classes-traits.name: ClassConstantRule
classes-traits.description: Large Rule covering `Foo::BAR` class-constant-fetch correctness: unknown class on the left side, self/static/parent-outside-class errors, accessing a constant on a trait, undefined constant on a known class, private/protected constant access-scope violations, `::class` on an expression (PHP-version and dynamic-string restrictions), and dynamic (non-Identifier) constant-name-must-be-string checks.
classes-traits.notes: Only the 'undefined constant on an otherwise-resolved class' half is implemented, via src/checker/expr.rs:1071-1082 ('access to undefined constant {class}::{member}'). Everything else -- unknown-class-on-LHS, self/static/parent-outside-class, onTrait, private/protected visibility (registry has no const visibility, see AccessPrivateConstantThroughStaticRule), ::class dynamic-expression rules, and dynamic-name-must-be-string -- is missing.

classes-traits.name: ConsistentConstructorHelper
classes-traits.description: Pure helper (no diagnostics of its own) that walks up a class's parent chain to find the nearest ancestor whose constructor is marked with the `@consistent-constructor` PHPDoc tag, used by other rules to validate `new static()` safety.
classes-traits.notes: grep for 'consistent' anywhere in src/docblock.rs or src/registry.rs finds nothing -- the `@consistent-constructor` PHPDoc tag isn't recognized/parsed at all, so there is no data this helper's Rust equivalent could operate on.

classes-traits.name: DuplicateClassDeclarationRule
classes-traits.description: Rule using BetterReflection's global reflector to detect the same class/interface/trait/enum name declared (at different start lines) in more than one file across the whole analysed project, and reports every duplicate location.
classes-traits.notes: phpstan-rs's registry is a single global name->ClassInfo map with no support for tracking multiple distinct declarations under one name; checker.rs's own doc comment (around line 98) explicitly documents that real-project class-name collisions across vendor/ are treated as an accepted simplification going the opposite direction (silently picking one), not flagged.

classes-traits.name: DuplicateDeclarationHelper
classes-traits.description: Helper (no diagnostics interface itself) implementing the actual within-one-class-body scan for redeclared enum cases, class constants, properties (including constructor-promoted ones), and methods, shared by DuplicateDeclarationRule and DuplicateTraitDeclarationRule.
classes-traits.notes: No equivalent scan exists in src/checker/* or src/registry.rs; grep for 'Cannot redeclare'/'redeclare property'/'redeclare method' across src/ returns nothing.

classes-traits.name: DuplicateDeclarationRule
classes-traits.description: Thin Rule wrapper invoking DuplicateDeclarationHelper::checkClassLike for classes, interfaces, and enums.
classes-traits.notes: Depends entirely on the missing DuplicateDeclarationHelper logic; no equivalent exists.

classes-traits.name: DuplicateTraitDeclarationRule
classes-traits.description: Thin Rule wrapper invoking DuplicateDeclarationHelper::checkClassLike for traits specifically (traits get their own InTraitNode rule since InClassNode doesn't cover trait bodies).
classes-traits.notes: Same underlying gap as DuplicateDeclarationRule/Helper.

classes-traits.name: EnumSanityRule
classes-traits.description: Rule enforcing enum-specific invariants: no constructor/destructor/other magic methods (only __call/__callStatic/__invoke allowed), can't redeclare native cases()/from()/tryFrom(), backing type must be int or string, can't implement Serializable, non-backed enum case can't have a value, backed enum case must have a value, case value must match the declared backing type, and no two cases may share the same backing value.
classes-traits.notes: Only the last item (duplicate backing values across cases) is implemented, in src/checker/oop.rs check_enum_case_values (lines 94-121), and even that only compares cases whose value is a literal int/string AST node (documented simplification). All other checks -- constructor/destructor/magic-method bans, native-method redeclaration, backing-type validity, Serializable ban, value-presence-consistency, and case-value-type-match -- are missing (grep for 'enum.constructor'/'enum.backingType'/etc across src/checker/* finds nothing).

classes-traits.name: ExistingClassInClassExtendsRule
classes-traits.description: Rule validating a class's `extends` clause: unknown parent class, extending an interface/trait/enum instead of a class, extending a final (by keyword or @final) class, and readonly-class/non-readonly-class mismatch between parent and child.
classes-traits.notes: check_final_class_extension (src/checker/oop.rs:16-34) implements only the final-class-extension half using data already in the registry (extends/is_final), but the 'unknown class', kind-mismatch (interface/trait/enum), and readonly-mismatch checks are absent -- grep for 'extends unknown'/'extends interface'/'extends trait'/'extends enum'/'readonly class' across src/checker/* finds nothing. ClassKind is tracked (src/ast.rs:213-218) so the data needed to build these checks already exists.

classes-traits.name: ExistingClassInInstanceOfRule
classes-traits.description: Rule validating the class-name side of `$x instanceof Foo`: unknown class, case-sensitivity mismatch, and `instanceof` against a trait (always false).
classes-traits.notes: instanceof is heavily used for type *narrowing* (src/checker/narrowing.rs) but that is flow-sensitive typing, not a class-name-existence check; no 'class not found'/'instanceof.trait' diagnostic exists anywhere in src/checker/*.

classes-traits.name: ExistingClassInTraitUseRule
classes-traits.description: Rule validating a `use Trait;` statement: unknown trait, interface illegally using a trait, and using a class/interface/enum where a trait was expected.
classes-traits.notes: check_trait_conflicts (src/checker/oop.rs:45-92) checks a different thing entirely -- property/method signature conflicts between two traits actually used together -- not whether the named 'trait' resolves, is the right kind, or whether an interface illegally uses traits. No such check exists.

classes-traits.name: ExistingClassesInClassImplementsRule
classes-traits.description: Rule validating each name in a class's `implements` clause: unknown interface, or implementing a class/trait/enum instead of an interface.
classes-traits.notes: No equivalent check found; grep for 'implements unknown'/'implements class'/'implements trait' across src/ returns nothing.

classes-traits.name: ExistingClassesInEnumImplementsRule
classes-traits.description: Same family as ExistingClassesInClassImplementsRule but for an enum's `implements` clause.
classes-traits.notes: No equivalent check found anywhere in src/checker/*.

classes-traits.name: ExistingClassesInInterfaceExtendsRule
classes-traits.description: Rule validating each name in an interface's `extends` clause: unknown interface, or extending a class/trait/enum instead of an interface.
classes-traits.notes: No equivalent check found anywhere in src/checker/*.

classes-traits.name: ImpossibleInstanceOfRule
classes-traits.description: Rule reporting `instanceof` expressions whose result is statically known: an error when the right side isn't a class-string/object (dynamic case), and always-true/always-false diagnostics when type analysis proves the outcome, honoring last-condition and PHPDoc-vs-native-type configuration toggles.
classes-traits.notes: grep for 'alwaysTrue'/'alwaysFalse'/'always evaluate to' across src/checker/* returns nothing -- instanceof is used only for narrowing locals (src/checker/narrowing.rs:954 narrow_instanceof_true and friends), never for emitting an impossible-condition diagnostic.

classes-traits.name: InstantiationCallableRule
classes-traits.description: Rule (level 0) on PHPStan's own InstantiationCallableNode (produced when the parser sees `new Foo(...)` first-class-callable syntax on a constructor) that unconditionally reports 'Cannot create callable from the new operator.' as a nonIgnorable error, since PHP has no such construct.
classes-traits.notes: The Rust parser explicitly recognizes `new Foo(...)` (comment at postfix.rs:389 notes the syntax doesn't exist in PHP) but just drops the ellipsis flag and parses it as a normal zero/whatever-arg `new`, rather than producing a distinct node and emitting a diagnostic. No 'callable.notSupported' error is ever raised.

classes-traits.name: InstantiationRule
classes-traits.description: Large level-0 rule on `new` expressions: resolves the class name (Name node, class-string type, `static`/`self`/`parent`, dynamic expr type), then checks class-name-expr type (new on non-object), unknown class, trait/enum/interface/abstract instantiation, private/protected constructor visibility, RestrictedMethodUsageExtension checks, and full constructor-argument-count/type checking via FunctionCallParametersCheck.
classes-traits.notes: Implemented: interface-instantiation error, abstract-class error, class-not-found error, and constructor argument checking via check_args (mirrors FunctionCallParametersCheck for arity/types). Missing: trait instantiation error, enum instantiation error, private/protected constructor visibility error, 'no constructor + args given' error, self/parent/static out-of-class and no-parent-class errors (self/parent/static resolution silently falls back via resolve_pseudo instead of erroring), class-name case-sensitivity check, and RestrictedMethodUsageExtension hook (phpstan-rs has no such extension concept).

classes-traits.name: InvalidPromotedPropertiesRule
classes-traits.description: Level-0 rule on any FunctionLike: flags constructor-property-promotion usage that's invalid - promoted properties outside PHP 8.0, promoted properties outside a constructor (or in an abstract/interface constructor with no body), a variadic promoted parameter, and (PHP 8.5+) final-promoted-property version gating.
classes-traits.notes: The parser records promoted_visibility/promoted_readonly/hooks per-parameter, but nothing in src/checker validates their placement (constructor-only), variadic-ness, or PHP-version gating. phpstan-rs also has no PhpVersion abstraction at all, so any version-gated check is structurally absent.

classes-traits.name: LocalTypeAliasesCheck
classes-traits.description: Shared Check (not a Rule itself) invoked by LocalTypeAliasesRule/LocalTypeTraitAliasesRule/LocalTypeTraitUseAliasesRule: validates `@phpstan-type`/`@phpstan-import-type` tags on a class/trait - duplicate alias names (vs class names, global aliases, imported aliases), invalid alias names, unknown imported-from class/alias, circular/invalid type-alias resolution, missing typehints inside the aliased type, unknown/trait classes referenced by the alias, generic-object-type checks, and unresolvable-type checks.
classes-traits.notes: src/docblock.rs has no parsing of `@phpstan-type` or `@phpstan-import-type` tags at all (only @param/@return/@var/@template/@extends/@implements-family tags are handled), so there is no data structure for this check to operate on. This is a genuine unbuilt feature area, not not_applicable.

classes-traits.name: LocalTypeAliasesRule
classes-traits.description: Level-0 Rule on InClassNode that simply delegates to LocalTypeAliasesCheck::check() for class/interface/enum declarations (not traits).
classes-traits.notes: Thin dispatcher for the missing LocalTypeAliasesCheck functionality; no equivalent exists since `@phpstan-type` tags aren't parsed.

classes-traits.name: LocalTypeTraitAliasesRule
classes-traits.description: Level-0 Rule on Trait_ nodes that resolves the trait's own ClassReflection and delegates to LocalTypeAliasesCheck::checkInTraitDefinitionContext() to validate `@phpstan-type` tags declared directly on the trait.
classes-traits.notes: Same underlying feature (type-alias tags) is entirely unbuilt; trait handling generally exists in the registry (trait method folding) but not for phpdoc type aliases.

classes-traits.name: LocalTypeTraitUseAliasesRule
classes-traits.description: Level-0 Rule on InTraitNode (a trait as used/folded into a specific implementing class) that delegates to LocalTypeAliasesCheck::checkInTraitUseContext() to re-validate the trait's type aliases against the resolving/using class's context (e.g. class-name checks relative to the use site).
classes-traits.notes: Depends on the same unbuilt `@phpstan-type` tag machinery; phpstan-rs does fold trait methods/properties into the using class in registry.rs, but has no analogous phpdoc-tag-in-trait-use-context re-validation.

classes-traits.name: MethodTagCheck
classes-traits.description: Shared Check invoked by MethodTagRule/MethodTagTraitRule/MethodTagTraitUseRule: validates `@method` tags on a class - for each declared virtual method's parameter and return types, checks missing typehints (iterable value type, generic class args, callable signature), unknown/trait classes referenced, generic-object-type validity, and unresolvable types, both in trait-definition and trait-use context.
classes-traits.notes: `@method` tags are not parsed in src/docblock.rs at all, so magic/virtual methods declared via phpdoc are neither registered as callable methods nor validated. This is a real gap: PHPStan uses @method tags to add virtual methods to a class's method table, which phpstan-rs's registry does not do.

classes-traits.name: MethodTagRule
classes-traits.description: Level-2 Rule on InClassNode delegating to MethodTagCheck::check() for classes/interfaces/enums.
classes-traits.notes: Depends on unbuilt @method tag parsing/registration.

classes-traits.name: MethodTagTraitRule
classes-traits.description: Level-2 Rule on Trait_ nodes delegating to MethodTagCheck::checkInTraitDefinitionContext() for @method tags declared directly on a trait.
classes-traits.notes: Same unbuilt feature; no trait-level @method validation exists.

classes-traits.name: MethodTagTraitUseRule
classes-traits.description: Level-2 Rule on InTraitNode delegating to MethodTagCheck::checkInTraitUseContext() to re-validate a trait's @method tags in the context of each class using the trait.
classes-traits.notes: Same unbuilt feature area as MethodTagCheck.

classes-traits.name: MixinCheck
classes-traits.description: Shared Check invoked by MixinRule/MixinTraitRule/MixinTraitUseRule: validates `@mixin` tags - the tagged type must be able to call methods/access properties (else 'non-object' error), missing typehints inside it, unknown/trait classes it references, generic-object-type validity, and unresolvable types, in both trait-definition and trait-use contexts.
classes-traits.notes: `@mixin` tags are not parsed anywhere in phpstan-rs; a class with `@mixin OtherClass` gets none of OtherClass's methods/properties folded in and no validation of the tag itself. Real, unbuilt PHPStan-parity feature.

classes-traits.name: MixinRule
classes-traits.description: Level-2 Rule on InClassNode delegating to MixinCheck::check() for a class's own @mixin tags.
classes-traits.notes: Depends on unbuilt @mixin tag support.

classes-traits.name: MixinTraitRule
classes-traits.description: Level-2 Rule on Trait_ nodes delegating to MixinCheck::checkInTraitDefinitionContext() for @mixin tags declared directly on a trait.
classes-traits.notes: Same unbuilt feature area.

classes-traits.name: MixinTraitUseRule
classes-traits.description: Level-2 Rule on InTraitNode delegating to MixinCheck::checkInTraitUseContext() to re-validate a trait's @mixin tags per using-class context.
classes-traits.notes: Same unbuilt feature area as MixinCheck.

classes-traits.name: NewStaticInAbstractClassStaticMethodRule
classes-traits.description: Un-tagged (not #[RegisteredRule]-annotated in this snippet, but a standard Rule<New_>) rule flagging `new static()` inside a static method of an abstract class, since a direct call would crash (abstract class can't be instantiated) - identifier 'new.staticInAbstractClassStaticMethod'.
classes-traits.notes: phpstan-rs resolves `new static()`'s type via resolve_pseudo for inference purposes but never inspects whether the enclosing class is abstract and the enclosing method is static to raise this specific diagnostic. No PhpMethodFromParserNodeReflection-equivalent static-method-context check exists.

classes-traits.name: NewStaticRule
classes-traits.description: Level-0 rule flagging 'Unsafe usage of new static().' generally (identifier 'new.static') unless the class is final, has a findConsistentConstructor()-detected consistent constructor, has no constructor, the constructor is declared on an interface/is final/is abstract-in-prototype, an implemented interface itself declares a constructor, or (PHP 8.1+ abstract trait methods) the enclosing trait's constructor is abstract.
classes-traits.notes: phpstan-rs resolves `new static()` type-wise (via Type::StaticRef / resolve_pseudo) but never emits an 'unsafe new static()' diagnostic. There's also no ConsistentConstructorHelper / '@consistent-constructor' tag concept in the codebase at all.

classes-traits.name: NonClassAttributeClassRule
classes-traits.description: Level-0 rule on InClassNode: if the declared class/interface/trait/enum carries an `#[Attribute]` attribute, verifies it is actually a class (not interface/trait/enum - 'attribute.<kind>' error), is not abstract ('attribute.abstract'), and its constructor (if any) is public ('attribute.constructorNotPublic').
classes-traits.our_location: src/parser/classes.rs (attribute groups parsed into AST, unused by checker)
classes-traits.notes: Attribute groups (`#[...]`) are parsed into the AST (grep confirms attr_groups/AttrGroup exist in parser/classes.rs and ast.rs) but nothing in src/checker/*.rs inspects them - no rule checks whether an #[Attribute]-annotated declaration is a valid class, non-abstract, or has a public constructor.

classes-traits.name: PropertyTagCheck
classes-traits.description: Shared validation logic (not a Rule itself) for @property/@property-read/@property-write tags: checks each referenced type for missing generic type args, missing iterable value types, missing callable signatures (in trait-definition context), and for unknown classes, trait-as-type, unresolvable types, class-name-case, and generic-object-type conformance (in trait-use/class context).
classes-traits.notes: phpstan-rs parses @property/@property-read/@property-write tags and uses them to synthesize magic properties for type inference (registry/class_info.rs), but performs none of PropertyTagCheck's own diagnostics - no unknown-class check, no trait-as-invalid-type check, no missing-generics/iterable-value/callable-signature checks, no unresolvable-type check, no generic-object-type-conformance check for these tags specifically.

classes-traits.name: PropertyTagRule
classes-traits.description: Registered Rule (level 2) that runs PropertyTagCheck::check() on every class, combining both the trait-definition-context and trait-use-context checks for @property tags declared directly on the class.
classes-traits.notes: No corresponding diagnostic is emitted; only the type-inference side-effect of @property tags exists (see PropertyTagCheck notes).

classes-traits.name: PropertyTagTraitRule
classes-traits.description: Registered Rule (level 2) that runs PropertyTagCheck::checkInTraitDefinitionContext() on Trait_ nodes directly (missing-generics/iterable-value/callable-signature checks only, no class-existence checks since template types may be unresolved in trait-definition context).
classes-traits.notes: Traits are not modeled as a separately-analysed node type in phpstan-rs at all - registry.rs's flatten_traits merges a trait's members into using classes rather than keeping trait declarations as their own analysis unit, so there is no place this check could run.

classes-traits.name: PropertyTagTraitUseRule
classes-traits.description: Registered Rule (level 2) that runs PropertyTagCheck::checkInTraitUseContext() on InTraitNode (a trait as composed into a specific using class), re-resolving the trait's PHPDoc against that implementing class's template arguments and checking full class-existence/generic-conformance rules.
classes-traits.notes: Same architectural gap as PropertyTagTraitRule - no per-(trait, using-class) resolved-PHPDoc context exists in phpstan-rs; traits are flattened once into the registry rather than re-analysed per use site.

classes-traits.name: ReadOnlyClassRule
classes-traits.description: Registered Rule (level 0) flagging a `readonly class`/`readonly` anonymous class when the configured PHP version target doesn't support it (readonly classes need 8.2+, readonly anonymous classes need 8.3+).
classes-traits.notes: phpstan-rs has no PhpVersion/target-version concept anywhere in the codebase (grep for PhpVersion/php_version in src/ is empty), so no version-gated diagnostics of this kind can exist yet; readonly is otherwise tracked structurally (ast.rs ClassDecl/Property is_readonly, parser/classes.rs, and assignment.rs's readonly-write-once check), just not this PHP-version-support check.

classes-traits.name: RequireExtendsRule
classes-traits.description: Registered Rule (level 2) verifying that a class implementing an interface (or using a trait) carrying a `@phpstan-require-extends` tag actually extends the required class.
classes-traits.notes: docblock.rs has no parsing at all for @require-extends/@require-implements tags (grep confirms), and no template/require-tag machinery references them; entirely unimplemented from the docblock layer up.

classes-traits.name: RequireImplementsRule
classes-traits.description: Registered Rule (level 2) verifying that a class using a trait carrying a `@phpstan-require-implements` tag actually implements the required interface.
classes-traits.notes: Same gap as RequireExtendsRule - @require-implements is not parsed by docblock.rs at all.

classes-traits.name: TraitAttributeClassRule
classes-traits.description: Registered Rule (level 0) on Trait_ nodes forbidding a trait from carrying the #[Attribute] PHP attribute (traits cannot be attribute classes).
classes-traits.notes: PHP attributes (#[...]) are lexed and skipped as raw tokens (see src/lexer.rs skip_stub_availability_attribute/skip_language_level_type_aware_attribute) rather than parsed into structured AST data available to the checker, so no rule can inspect attribute names on a declaration; also traits aren't a distinct analysed node type at all.

classes-traits.name: UnusedConstructorParametersRule
classes-traits.description: Registered Rule (level 1) flagging constructor parameters (non-promoted, i.e. flags===0) that are never referenced in the constructor body, skipping attribute classes and classes whose interface already declares the constructor.
classes-traits.notes: grep for 'unused' across src/checker/*.rs returns nothing - phpstan-rs has no unused-parameter detection at all (for constructors or ordinary functions/methods), i.e. no UnusedFunctionParametersCheck equivalent exists anywhere.

classes-traits.name: ConflictingTraitConstantsRule
classes-traits.description: Registered Rule (level 0) on ClassConst nodes checking that a class constant overriding a same-named constant inherited (directly or recursively) from a used trait keeps compatible visibility (must not widen/narrow below the trait's), matches its final-ness, matches its native type (or absence), and (for immediate trait constants) keeps the same value.
classes-traits.notes: Class constants aren't tracked in the registry at all (grep for 'constants'/'class_const' in registry.rs and class_info.rs returns nothing), so there is no place to compare a class's own constant against a trait-inherited one; this rule's entire data dependency (ReflectionClassConstant, trait constant values/visibility/finality/native types) is absent from phpstan-rs.

classes-traits.name: ConstantsInTraitsRule
classes-traits.description: Registered Rule (level 0) on ClassConst nodes flagging a constant declared inside a trait body when the target PHP version predates 8.2 (which added trait constant support).
classes-traits.notes: No PhpVersion/target-version concept exists in phpstan-rs (same gap as ReadOnlyClassRule), and traits aren't walked as their own scope (isInTrait() equivalent) since they're flattened into using classes at registry build time.

classes-traits.name: NotAnalysedTraitRule
classes-traits.description: Registered Rule (level 4) on the aggregated CollectedDataNode: cross-references TraitDeclarationCollector and TraitUseCollector data project-wide to report every declared trait that is never `use`d anywhere and therefore never gets its own semantic analysis pass.
classes-traits.notes: phpstan-rs has no collector infrastructure/cross-file aggregation phase analogous to PHPStan's Collectors, and traits aren't analysed as standalone units in the first place (flatten_traits merges them into using classes), so there is neither the data-gathering machinery nor the concept of 'a trait not itself directly analysed' that this rule depends on.

classes-traits.name: TraitAttributesRule
classes-traits.description: Registered Rule (level 0) on InTraitNode validating attributes placed on a trait declaration: runs the generic AttributesCheck against TARGET_CLASS, flags #[Deprecated] on a trait when the PHP version predates 8.5, and flags #[AllowDynamicProperties] as never allowed on a trait.
classes-traits.notes: PHP attributes aren't parsed into structured AST nodes (see TraitAttributeClassRule notes) and traits aren't a distinct analysed node, and there is no PhpVersion concept - all three of this rule's prerequisites are absent.

classes-traits.name: TraitDeclarationCollector
classes-traits.description: Collector (level 4) gathering every named trait declaration's [name, line] across all analysed files, for later aggregation by NotAnalysedTraitRule.
classes-traits.notes: phpstan-rs has no Collector abstraction/cross-file aggregation mechanism at all; this is pure plumbing that only exists to feed NotAnalysedTraitRule, which itself is missing.

classes-traits.name: TraitUseCollector
classes-traits.description: Collector (level 4) gathering the list of trait names referenced by every `use Trait1, Trait2;` statement across all analysed files, for later aggregation by NotAnalysedTraitRule.
classes-traits.notes: Same as TraitDeclarationCollector - no Collector mechanism exists in phpstan-rs, and this data is consumed only by NotAnalysedTraitRule which is itself unimplemented; note phpstan-rs does read `use` trait lists elsewhere (registry.rs's own per-class `uses` field, consumed by flatten_traits) but not for this cross-file unused-trait purpose.

standalone-infra.name: ClassNameNodePair
standalone-infra.description: Pure immutable DTO pairing a class-name string with the AST Node it was referenced from; carries no check logic itself and exists purely as input to class-existence/case-sensitivity checking helpers (e.g. ClassNameCheck, ClassCaseSensitivityCheck) that batch-process many referenced class names per rule.
standalone-infra.notes: phpstan-rs has no unified 'collect (className, node) usage sites, then case/existence-check them' mechanism this DTO exists to feed. Instead, unknown-class checks are done ad hoc, one-off, per call site (e.g. src/checker/expr.rs:902 'instantiated class {class} not found', src/checker/stmt.rs:515/574 catch/throw Throwable checks) with no shared pairing/collection abstraction, and there is no class-name case-sensitivity checking anywhere in src/.

standalone-infra.name: ClassNameUsageLocation
standalone-infra.description: Value-object enum of ~27 'where was this class name used' kinds (traitUse, staticProperty, assert tag, attribute, catch, classConstant, implements/extends variants, instanceof, property/parameter/return type, selfOut, var tag, new, typeAlias, method/mixin/property/requireExtends/requireImplements/sealed tags, staticMethod, template bound/default) whose createMessage()/createIdentifier() are the single source of truth for the exact diagnostic wording and error-identifier PHPStan emits for an unknown-class reference at each of those sites.
standalone-infra.notes: phpstan-rs's Diagnostic struct (src/checker.rs:71) has no `identifier` field at all, and message text for unknown-class-style errors is hand-written per call site (format!() strings) rather than centralized through a location taxonomy. Most of the listed locations (assert-tag, template-bound/default, sealed, mixin, requireExtends/requireImplements, type alias, self-out) have no class-existence checking counterpart in src/ at all.

standalone-infra.name: DirectRegistry
standalone-infra.description: Simple in-memory implementation of Registry: indexes an injected Rule[] array by getNodeType() at construction, and getRules($nodeType) walks class_parents()+class_implements() (with a cache) to also return rules registered for any ancestor/interface of the requested node type. Used mainly by RuleTestCase to run a single rule under test without the full DI container.
standalone-infra.notes: This is dispatch infrastructure for a runtime collection of independently pluggable Rule objects keyed by AST node class, needed because PHPStan supports arbitrary third-party rules registered via DI/config at runtime. phpstan-rs's checker is a single monolithic Checker (src/checker.rs) whose traversal functions (src/checker/stmt.rs, expr.rs, etc.) dispatch directly via Rust match arms on the AST node kind, compiled in rather than resolved at runtime from a registry - there is no pluggable-rule-object concept to register or look up, so a runtime Registry has no sensible from-scratch counterpart.

standalone-infra.name: FoundTypeResult
standalone-infra.description: Value object returned by RuleLevelHelper::findTypeToCheck(): bundles the resolved Type to check, the list of referencedClasses found on it, any unknownClassErrors already built for missing classes among them, and an optional human-readable tip (e.g. suggesting ->getArgs() over ->args).
standalone-infra.notes: This is purely the return-type carrier for RuleLevelHelper::findTypeToCheck's algorithm (see RuleLevelHelper below), which has no counterpart in phpstan-rs - no per-union-member class-existence splitting, no accumulation of unknownClassErrors as a side list, and no tip mechanism anywhere in the checker.

standalone-infra.name: LazyRegistry
standalone-infra.description: The production Registry implementation, autowired as the 'registry' DI service: pulls all Rule instances tagged phpstan.rules.rule from an ExtensionsCollection, indexes them by getNodeType() lazily on first use, and resolves a requested node type's full applicable rule set via ExtensionClassHelper's runtime-reflection class-hierarchy walk, caching the result per node type.
standalone-infra.notes: Same reasoning as DirectRegistry: this is the DI-container-driven half of PHPStan's pluggable-rule extension architecture (service tags, ExtensionsCollection, runtime class-hierarchy resolution for arbitrary third-party Rule classes). phpstan-rs has no service container and no plugin/extension model - every check is a hardcoded function/match arm inside src/checker/*.rs, so there is no 'resolve rules for this node type from a container' step to reimplement.

standalone-infra.name: Registry
standalone-infra.description: The one-method interface (getRules(string $nodeType): array<Rule>) that both DirectRegistry and LazyRegistry implement; the abstraction NodeScopeResolver programs against to fetch the applicable Rule objects for the AST node it is currently visiting.
standalone-infra.notes: Pure interface for the pluggable-rule dispatch mechanism described above. phpstan-rs's Checker (src/checker.rs) calls its own check functions directly from src/checker/stmt.rs and src/checker/expr.rs rather than querying an abstract rule registry, so there is no seam this interface would need to fill in a monolithic, non-plugin-based Rust checker.

standalone-infra.name: Rule
standalone-infra.description: The @api, #[ExtensionInterface]-tagged generic interface every custom or built-in PHPStan rule implements: getNodeType() declares which AST node class to be invoked for, processNode(Node, Scope) returns the list<IdentifierRuleError> found at that node. This is the third-party plugin contract documented at phpstan.org/developing-extensions/rules.
standalone-infra.notes: This is explicitly PHPStan's public third-party extension point for authoring custom rules outside PHPStan's own codebase (registered via the phpstan.rules.rule service tag). phpstan-rs is a closed, from-scratch reimplementation with no plugin/extension-authoring story or DI container; its equivalent checks live as ordinary Rust functions called directly from the traversal in src/checker/*.rs, not as implementations of a public Rule trait resolved at runtime, so there is no sensible 1:1 Rust trait to build here.

standalone-infra.name: RuleErrorBuilder
standalone-infra.description: Fluent builder used by virtually every PHPStan rule to construct a RuleError: chains ->line()/->file()/->tip()/->addTip()/->identifier()/->metadata()/->nonIgnorable()/->fixNode() to progressively OR a type bitmask, then ->build() instantiates the matching dynamically-named RuleError<bitmask> class and copies the accumulated properties onto it (plus several canned tip helpers like discoveringSymbolsTip/treatPhpDocTypesAsCertainTip/possiblyImpureTip).
standalone-infra.notes: phpstan-rs's Diagnostic is a plain 4-field struct { location, message, span, level } built via struct literal / format!() calls scattered through src/checker/*.rs - covering only the rough equivalent of message+line/location. There is no builder pattern, no `identifier` field (so no per-error-identifier system at all, and nothing like phpstan.org/error-identifiers), no `tip` field or canned-tip helpers, no `metadata`, no `nonIgnorable` flag, and no fixNode/Patcher auto-fix support.

standalone-infra.name: RuleLevelHelper
standalone-infra.description: Autowired service used across most 'access to property/method/constant on X' rules: isThis() detects the $this expression; accepts() does a configurable type-acceptance check (transforming CallableType/ClosureType inner return types, optionally stripping null per checkNullables, optionally converting BenevolentUnionType per checkBenevolentUnionTypes, and gating explicit/implicit mixed per checkExplicitMixed/checkImplicitMixed) returning a RuleLevelHelperAcceptsResult; findTypeToCheck()/findTypeToCheckImplementation() is the core algorithm that, given a scope+expression, resolves its type while splitting unions/intersections member-by-member, filtering by checkThisOnly/checkUnionTypes settings, collecting per-class 'class.notFound' errors (respecting class_exists() guards), and producing the Arg/VariadicPlaceholder ->args tip.
standalone-infra.notes: Only a narrow slice of `accepts()`'s job is covered: is_assignable(sub, sup) -> bool does a simple, unconditional class-hierarchy-aware compatibility check with no configurable checkNullables/checkUnionTypes/checkExplicitMixed/checkImplicitMixed/checkBenevolentUnionTypes toggles (there is no rule-level-gating concept for these dimensions at all), no CallableType/ClosureType return-type transform, and returns a bare bool rather than reasons. There is no isThis() helper and no findTypeToCheck-equivalent: no per-union-member class-existence splitting with accumulated unknownClassErrors, no class_exists()-guard exemption, and no tip production.

standalone-infra.name: RuleLevelHelperAcceptsResult
standalone-infra.description: Small @api value object {result: bool, reasons: list<string>} returned by RuleLevelHelper::accepts(), with and() to combine two accept-checks (ANDing results, merging reason lists) and decorateReasons() to map a formatting callback over the reasons - used when a rule checks several candidate types/overloads and needs to report why each one was rejected.
standalone-infra.notes: src/registry.rs's is_assignable returns a plain bool with no accompanying reasons list and no combinator for merging multiple accept-checks' rejection reasons; phpstan-rs's diagnostic messages for type-mismatch errors are built as flat format!() strings rather than composed from a structured, combinable reasons result.

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: BooleanAndConstantConditionRule
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: Level-4 Rule<BooleanAndNode> that reports when the left operand, right operand, or overall result of a `&&`/`and` expression is a compile-time-constant boolean (`booleanAnd.leftAlwaysX`/`rightAlwaysX`/`alwaysX`, or `logicalAnd.*` for the `and` spelling), respecting the 'last condition in a chain, always-true not interesting' exemption via LastConditionVisitor and deferring to FunctionCallConstantConditionHelper/ConstantConditionInTraitHelper for dedup when the operand is itself a call or the code is in a trait.
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: phpstan-rs's If/While/DoWhile handling (src/checker/stmt.rs) only uses conditions to drive apply_narrowing (src/checker/narrowing.rs); nothing inspects a `&&` expression's inferred operand/result type for constant-boolean reporting, and no 'booleanAnd.*'-style diagnostic exists anywhere in src/.

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: BooleanNotConstantConditionRule
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: Level-4 Rule<Node\Expr\BooleanNot> reporting `!$expr` when `$expr`'s type is a constant boolean (`booleanNot.alwaysTrue`/`alwaysFalse`), with the same LastConditionVisitor exemption and function-call/trait dedup deferral as the And/Or rules.
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: No equivalent check; BooleanNot is only used for narrowing (apply_narrowing negates the wrapped condition) in src/checker/narrowing.rs, never diagnosed for a statically-known result.

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: BooleanOrConstantConditionRule
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: Level-4 Rule<BooleanOrNode>, the `||`/`or` mirror of BooleanAndConstantConditionRule: reports constant-boolean left/right/result operands with the same identifiers (`booleanOr.*`/`logicalOr.*`), last-condition exemption, and call/trait dedup deferral.
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: Same gap as BooleanAndConstantConditionRule; `||`/`or` conditions in src/checker/stmt.rs and narrowing.rs are only consumed for narrowing, never for constant-result diagnostics. Note stmt.rs *does* use a right-side-never-returns idiom (`$cond || die();`) for narrowing purposes, which is unrelated to this rule's constant-boolean check.

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: CollectedConstantConditionError
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: Pure static utility with one method, `transformPaths()`, that rewrites file paths embedded in an `Error` (or its JSON-decoded form after crossing a parallel-worker process boundary) for the result-cache's path-transform pass; carries no check/diagnostic logic itself.
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: Exists solely because PHPStan collector data can cross a parallel worker's process boundary (serialized to JSON) and later needs path rewriting for the on-disk result cache. phpstan-rs is a single-process, no-result-cache-serialization-boundary analyzer (per project.rs/registry.rs), so this specific plumbing has no sensible target; the actual detection logic it supports lives in the Rule/Helper classes below, which are assessed separately as missing.

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: ConstantConditionInTraitCollector
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: A CollectorWithPaths whose getNodeType()/processNode() both throw ShouldNotHappenException (it is never invoked by the AST walker; data is pushed into it manually via Scope::emitCollectedData from ConstantConditionInTraitHelper) - it exists purely as a typed data channel plus a transformCollectedDataPaths() hook that forwards to CollectedConstantConditionError for path rewriting.
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: This is the data-carrier half of the trait constant-condition dedup feature (see ConstantConditionInTraitHelper/Rule): when a trait's method is used by multiple classes, the same constant-condition error would otherwise be reported once per using class; this collects all occurrences project-wide so the consuming Rule can report it once, in the trait itself. phpstan-rs has neither this collector shape nor any trait-usage-context dedup at all - and since none of the underlying constant-condition rules (If/BooleanAnd/etc.) exist either, this whole feature is absent.

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: ConstantConditionInTraitHelper
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: DI service used by every Comparison constant-condition rule: `emitNoError()`/`emitError()` push a (rule, trait name, printed-expr:line key, value, transformed error) tuple into ConstantConditionInTraitCollector only when `$scope->isInTrait()`, so a later cross-file Rule can decide, per trait+expr+value, whether to report once in the trait or once per using-class context.
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: No equivalent in phpstan-rs: traits are analyzed per-file/per-class without any mechanism to defer or merge diagnostics across multiple usages of the same trait, and none of the consumer rules (BooleanAnd/Or/Not, If, ElseIf, DoWhile, ConstantLooseComparison, ImpossibleCheckType*) exist to call it.

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: ConstantConditionInTraitRule
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: Level-0 Rule<CollectedDataNode> that runs once after all files are analyzed: groups ConstantConditionInTraitCollector entries by (rule, trait, expr-key), and if every recorded occurrence for that key agrees on the same constant value, reports the error once (directly in the trait if the message was identical everywhere, otherwise once per distinct context) instead of once per using-class.
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: phpstan-rs's diagnostic pipeline (registry.rs/project.rs) has no cross-file collected-data aggregation pass comparable to CollectedDataNode rules, and nothing to consume ConstantConditionInTraitCollector output (which itself doesn't exist).

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: ConstantConditionRuleHelper
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: DI service providing `getBooleanType()`/`getNativeBooleanType()`: converts an expression's type (PHPDoc-aware or native-only) to a BooleanType via `->toBoolean()`, but first returns a plain non-constant `BooleanType` for expression kinds already covered by other, more specific rules (`==`, `!=`, `===`, `!==`, `instanceof`, `!`, `&&`, `||`, ternary, `isset`, `empty`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`) to avoid duplicate reporting.
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: phpstan-rs's Type enum does have literal `Type::True`/`Type::False` constant-boolean variants, so the underlying type-system primitive exists, but there is no `toBoolean()`-style coercion helper nor any skip-list used to feed a constant-condition rule - because no such rule exists to consume it.

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: ConstantLooseComparisonRule
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: Level-4 Rule<Node\Expr\BinaryOp> restricted to `==`/`!=`: when the comparison's own inferred type is a constant `true` or `false` (with the same PHPDoc-vs-native-type tip logic and last-condition exemption as the other rules here), reports `equal.alwaysTrue/False` or `notEqual.alwaysTrue/False` naming both operand types.
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: src/checker/expr.rs infers the result type of `BinOp::Eq`/loose comparisons (for downstream type propagation) but nothing checks whether that result is statically true/false and reports it; grep for loose-comparison diagnostics in src/ turns up nothing.

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: DoWhileLoopConstantConditionRule
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: Level-4 Rule<DoWhileLoopConditionNode> reporting a do-while's condition as constant true/false (`doWhile.alwaysTrue/False`), with special-case suppression: an always-true condition is not reported if the loop body yields, or if every exit point is either a `continue` (with level <=1) or something other than a plain break/continue jump out; an always-false condition is not reported if the body contains a `break`.
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: src/checker/stmt.rs's `StmtKind::DoWhile` arm (starting line 199) only uses the condition for narrowing/loop-state tracking; the `is_truthy_literal()` helper in control_flow.rs is used solely for loop-termination reachability analysis (e.g. treating `while (true)` as non-exiting for dead-code purposes), not for emitting a diagnostic about the condition's constancy.

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: ElseIfConstantConditionRule
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: Level-4 Rule<Node\Stmt\ElseIf_> reporting `elseif.alwaysTrue/False` when an `elseif` condition's type is a constant boolean, same tip/last-condition/dedup-deferral machinery as IfConstantConditionRule.
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: phpstan-rs's parser/checker represent `elseif` as a nested `If` inside the `else` branch (StmtKind::If handling in src/checker/stmt.rs), and that handling only narrows locals - it never checks whether the (elseif) condition is a compile-time-constant boolean.

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: FunctionCallConstantConditionCollector
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: CollectorWithPaths (getNodeType/processNode both throw ShouldNotHappenException; fed manually via emitCollectedData) that carries deferred constant-condition results for function/method/static-call conditions, plus transformCollectedDataPaths() delegating to CollectedConstantConditionError for parallel-worker path rewriting.
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: Data-carrier half of the mechanism that lets the generic constant-condition rules (If/BooleanAnd/etc.) defer to the more specific ImpossibleCheckType* rules when a condition is itself a function/method call, so the same call site isn't reported twice with different messages. No such deferral/dedup machinery exists in phpstan-rs, and none of the rules that would populate it exist either.

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: FunctionCallConstantConditionHelper
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: DI service with `isTypeCheckCandidate()` (true for a non-first-class-callable FuncCall/MethodCall/StaticCall), `emitFunctionCallNoError()`/`emitFunctionCallError()` (push deferred results into FunctionCallConstantConditionCollector, keyed by rule+trait+expr string), and `emitImpossibleCheckReported()` (marks a call site as already owned by ImpossibleCheckTypeFunctionCallRule/ImpossibleCheckTypeMethodCallRule via a separate collector) so the generic constant-condition rules and the impossible-check-type rules don't double-report the same call.
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: No equivalent glue exists; this only matters once both the generic constant-condition rules and the ImpossibleCheckType* rules exist, and phpstan-rs has neither family.

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: FunctionCallConstantConditionRule
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: Level-4 Rule<CollectedDataNode> run once at the end of analysis: reads all FunctionCallConstantConditionCollector entries plus all ImpossibleCheckTypeReportedCollector 'owned call site' markers, suppresses any call-site error already owned by an ImpossibleCheckType* rule, then applies the same per-file (non-trait) or project-wide (trait) dedup/merge logic as ConstantConditionInTraitRule before emitting the final TransformedRuleError list.
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: Depends entirely on collector infrastructure and sibling rules that don't exist in phpstan-rs (no CollectedDataNode-style final aggregation pass, no ImpossibleCheckTypeReportedCollector, no FunctionCallConstantConditionCollector).

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: IfConstantConditionRule
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: Level-4 Rule<Node\Stmt\If_> - the most basic/common member of this family: reports `if.alwaysTrue`/`if.alwaysFalse` when the `if` condition's type (PHPDoc-aware or native) is a constant boolean, with the PHPDoc-vs-native 'tip' logic and deferral to the function-call/trait helpers.
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: src/checker/stmt.rs's `StmtKind::If` arm only calls check_expr + apply_narrowing on the condition for both branches; it never inspects whether the condition's own inferred type is a constant `true`/`false` to flag dead code like `if (true) {...}` or a condition proven impossible by prior narrowing. This is likely the single highest-value missing rule in the category given how common such patterns are.

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: ImpossibleCheckTypeFunctionCallRule
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: Level-4 Rule<FunctionCallExpressionNode> that runs ImpossibleCheckTypeHelper::findSpecifiedType() against a function call used as a condition (e.g. `is_string($x)` where `$x` is already known to be non-string, or already known to be exactly string) and reports `function.impossibleType` (always false) or `function.alreadyNarrowedType` (always true, subject to the last-condition exemption), describing the actual argument types in the message.
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: phpstan-rs narrows on `is_string()`/`is_int()`/etc. calls (apply_narrowing in src/checker/narrowing.rs, used to update local types in the true/false branches) but never checks whether that narrowing target already fully subsumes or is disjoint from the argument's current type, so it never reports the call itself as redundant/impossible.

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: ImpossibleCheckTypeHelper
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: 555-line DI service, the analytic core behind both ImpossibleCheckType*Rule classes. `findSpecifiedType()`/`getSpecifiedType()` special-case `assert()`, `function_exists()`, `count()`/`sizeof()`, `defined()`, `array_search()`, `in_array()` (including a strict-vs-loose in_array analysis over ConstantArrayType haystacks, enum needles, and array-shape guaranteed-value reasoning), and `method_exists()` (constant-string class/method lookups against ReflectionProvider, including a check that base-class-declared methods can't be ruled out for narrower final-class reasoning), then falls back to running the general TypeSpecifier::specifyTypesInCondition() and comparing each 'sure type'/'sure not type' entry's target type against the argument's current type via isSuperTypeOf() to decide true/false/inconclusive, plus `getArgumentsDescription()` for message formatting and `doNotTreatPhpDocTypesAsCertain()` for computing the native-only comparison used for tips.
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: This is the single biggest logic gap in the category. phpstan-rs's narrowing.rs has real per-condition-shape narrowing (instanceof, is_*, preg_match, in_array target inference at line 349, and-or chains) but purely to *update* local variable types on the two branches - there is no companion step anywhere that compares the narrowing target against the argument's pre-existing type to decide the check is impossible/redundant and emit a diagnostic. The assert()/method_exists()/in_array() special-casing and the reflection-based method_exists() analysis have no Rust counterpart at all.

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: ImpossibleCheckTypeMethodCallRule
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: Level-4 Rule<MethodCallExpressionNode>, the method-call mirror of ImpossibleCheckTypeFunctionCallRule: resolves the called MethodReflection via the receiver's type and reports `method.impossibleType`/`method.alreadyNarrowedType` using the same ImpossibleCheckTypeHelper::findSpecifiedType() analysis.
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: Same root cause as ImpossibleCheckTypeFunctionCallRule/ImpossibleCheckTypeHelper - no narrowing-target-vs-current-type impossibility comparison exists in phpstan-rs, and this rule additionally needs the MethodReflection lookup path (`scope->getMethodReflection`) purely to format the error message, which is otherwise unused here for behavior.

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: ImpossibleCheckTypeReportedCollector
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: A pure marker Collector (26 lines) whose getNodeType()/processNode() both throw ShouldNotHappenException - it is never traversed normally; it exists only so CollectedDataEmitter/CollectedDataNode can tag and later query 'an impossible-check-type error was already reported for this node' entries under a typed collector key, letting sibling rules (StrictComparisonOfDifferentTypesRule, MatchExpressionRule, etc.) deduplicate against ImpossibleCheckTypeFunctionCallRule/StaticMethodCallRule without double-reporting the same constant condition.
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: Pure DI/collector-architecture plumbing with no logic of its own (both methods throw). phpstan-rs's checker is single-pass and emits Diagnostics eagerly with no Collector/CollectedDataNode two-phase architecture and no cross-rule dedup-by-marker mechanism, so there is nothing sensible to port for this bookkeeping class itself. The underlying feature it supports (avoiding duplicate 'impossible check' errors across rules) is moot since that whole rule family is itself missing (see ImpossibleCheckTypeStaticMethodCallRule, StrictComparisonOfDifferentTypesRule, etc. below).

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: ImpossibleCheckTypeStaticMethodCallRule
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: Level-4 Rule on StaticMethodCallExpressionNode: uses ImpossibleCheckTypeHelper to determine whether a static method call that behaves like a type check (e.g. Assert::isInstanceOf) always evaluates to true or false given the argument's known type, emitting 'Call to static method X::Y() will always evaluate to false/true' (identifiers staticMethod.impossibleType / staticMethod.alreadyNarrowedType), gated by treatPhpDocTypesAsCertain/reportAlwaysTrueInLastCondition and deduplicated via ConstantConditionInTraitHelper/FunctionCallConstantConditionHelper.
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: No equivalent in src/checker/*.rs. grep for 'impossibleType'/'alreadyNarrowedType'/'ImpossibleCheckType' in src/ returns nothing; static method calls are resolved for type/argument checking (checker/calls.rs, oop.rs) but never analyzed for constant-truthiness of a type-check-style call.

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: ImpossibleInArrayHaystackFiniteTypesRule
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: Rule on FuncCall for in_array()/array_search()/array_keys(): compares the needle's type against each finite-typed value in a constant-array haystack (via InitializerExprTypeResolver's resolveIdenticalType/resolveEqualType, respecting the 3rd strict-mode arg) and reports 'Value X in the haystack ... can never be equal/identical to the needle type Y' (identifier function.impossibleHaystackValue) for haystack entries that can never match, while carefully not flagging entries that are merely 'another value of the needle's own type' when some other entry can match.
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: src/checker/narrowing.rs uses in_array() only to build TYPE NARROWING facts (in_array_target_type, line ~349) for use as a condition in if/match, not to emit a diagnostic about individual dead haystack values. array_search()/array_keys() have no special handling in narrowing.rs or expr.rs at all for this purpose.

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: LogicalXorConstantConditionRule
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: Level-4 Rule on `xor` (LogicalXor): independently evaluates the boolean type of the left and right operands via ConstantConditionRuleHelper; when either side's type is a ConstantBooleanType, reports 'Left/right side of xor is always true/false' (identifiers logicalXor.leftAlwaysTrue/False, rightAlwaysTrue/False), with the same tip/last-condition/in-trait machinery as the other constant-condition rules.
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: src/ast.rs and src/checker/expr.rs only model `xor` (BinOp::LogicalXor) for its resulting Type::Bool (checker/expr.rs:2372); there is no evaluation of whether an operand is itself a constant-boolean type nor any diagnostic emitted for it.

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: MatchExpressionRule
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: Level-4 Rule on MatchExpressionNode: for each arm condition, builds an implicit `$subject === $armCondition` comparison and reports 'Match arm comparison ... is always false' (dead arm, match.alwaysFalse) or 'is always true' (match.alwaysTrue, with a 'remove remaining cases' tip, unless it's the actually-last arm) using per-arm narrowed scopes; separately, when there is no `default` arm and the match's own scope-computed remaining type (after subtracting all handled enum cases/values) is not `never` and no `UnhandledMatchError` is caught or declared via `@throws`, reports 'Match expression does not handle remaining value(s): ...' (match.unhandled).
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: src/checker/expr.rs's ExprKind::Match handling (lines ~1179-1266 and ~1510-1550) computes the match's result type and applies narrowing between arms for downstream inference, but never compares an arm's condition equality for constant-truthiness nor checks match exhaustiveness against enum cases / emits any diagnostic - it purely returns a type.

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: NumberComparisonOperatorsConstantConditionRule
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: Level-4 Rule on BinaryOp restricted to Greater/GreaterOrEqual/Smaller/SmallerOrEqual: if the whole comparison's inferred type is a ConstantBooleanType, reports 'Comparison operation "X" between A and B is always true/false' with per-operator identifiers (greater.alwaysTrue, smallerOrEqual.alwaysFalse, etc.), gated by treatPhpDocTypesAsCertain and with the usual possibly-impure tip / in-trait dedup machinery.
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: checker/expr.rs computes Type::Bool for these operators (same switch arm as other comparisons, line ~2363-2372) purely for type-inference purposes; no code checks whether that boolean result is itself a compile-time-constant true/false or emits a diagnostic for it.

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: PossiblyImpureTipHelper
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: A small DI-autowired helper (not a Rule) used by every constant-condition rule: given a Scope and the condition expression, calls MutatingScope::findPossiblyImpureCallDescriptions() and, if the `tips.possiblyImpure` config flag is on and any impure call descriptions are found, appends a 'possiblyImpureTip' note onto the RuleErrorBuilder explaining the constant result may depend on a side-effecting call.
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: src/checker.rs's Diagnostic struct (line 71) has only {location, message, span, level} - no identifier/tip fields at all, so there is no diagnostic-decoration mechanism to port. This helper is purely in service of the (also missing) constant-condition rule family and the (also missing) call-purity tracking (no 'pure'/'impure' concept exists anywhere in src/, confirmed via grep).

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: StrictComparisonOfDifferentTypesRule
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: Level-4 Rule on BinaryOp restricted to Identical/NotIdentical: uses RicherScopeGetTypeHelper's getIdenticalResult/getNotIdenticalResult (which carry human-readable 'reasons') to determine if the `===`/`!==` comparison is a compile-time-constant true/false given the operand types, and reports 'Strict comparison using === between A and B will always evaluate to false/true' (identifiers identical.alwaysFalse/True, notIdentical.alwaysFalse/True); special-cases lowercase/uppercase-string ambiguity for message verbosity, and adds a 'Use match expression instead' tip when comparing two different enum values outside of a match.
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: src/checker/narrowing.rs uses BinOp::Identical/NotIdentical (lines ~113-114, 780-783) purely to drive type-narrowing on `===`/`!==` conditions (e.g. `if ($x === null)`); src/checker/expr.rs (line ~2363-2365) computes only the resulting Type::Bool. No code anywhere evaluates whether the comparison result is itself a known constant or emits any 'always true/false' diagnostic for it.

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: SwitchConditionRule
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: Rule on SwitchConditionNode: walks switch arms tracking narrowed/native narrowed dead-arm state (mirroring MatchExpressionRule's arm-by-arm logic but for `switch`'s loose `==` semantics), reports duplicate `case` labels among finite-typed case values (switch.duplicateCase, comparing via type equality and PHP's loose-comparison table via looseCompare()), and reports 'Switch condition comparison ... is always false/true' (switch.alwaysFalse/True) with a 'remove remaining cases' tip for non-final always-true cases.
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: src/checker/stmt.rs's StmtKind::Switch handling (lines ~366-470) tracks narrowed_locals/running/exit_states purely for control-flow narrowing and reachability merging (documented at length in the comment block there); it never compares two case values for duplication nor evaluates a case's dispatch comparison for constant truthiness, so no switch.alwaysFalse/True/duplicateCase diagnostics exist.

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: TernaryOperatorConstantConditionRule
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: Level-4 Rule on Ternary: evaluates the condition's boolean type via ConstantConditionRuleHelper and, if constant, reports 'Ternary operator condition is always true/false' (ternary.alwaysTrue/False), deduplicating with the type-check-call rules and ConstantConditionInTraitHelper as usual.
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: Ternary expressions are type-checked/narrowed in checker/expr.rs for their result type but there is no check of whether the condition itself is a compile-time-constant boolean, and no ternary.always* diagnostic exists anywhere in src/.

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: UsageOfVoidMatchExpressionRule
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: Small level-2 Rule on Match_: when a match expression is used somewhere other than as a first-level statement (i.e. its result is actually consumed) and its 'keep-void' result type is void (all arms are void-typed calls), reports 'Result of match expression (void) is used.' (match.void).
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: src/checker/expr.rs's Match handling computes a real result type (never returning a special void-marker distinct from ordinary Type::Void) but never checks whether the match is used in a value-consuming context vs. a bare statement, and emits no diagnostic for void-in-expression-position for match specifically.

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: WhileLoopAlwaysFalseConditionRule
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: Level-4 Rule on While_: evaluates the loop condition's boolean type via ConstantConditionRuleHelper and, if it is definitely false, reports 'While loop condition is always false.' (while.alwaysFalse) with the usual tip/dedup machinery - flags a while-loop body that can never execute.
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: src/checker/control_flow.rs and stmt.rs handle StmtKind::While only for control-flow/termination purposes (e.g. is_truthy_literal(cond) at control_flow.rs:90 feeds always_terminates for while(true) loops) - a constant-false condition is never specifically detected or reported; a while(false) body is simply treated like any ordinary conditionally-executed block.

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: WhileLoopAlwaysTrueConditionRule
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: Level-4 Rule on BreaklessWhileLoopNode (a while loop verified to contain no break, or only continue N>1/continue with no matching break): if the condition's boolean type is constantly true, and the loop isn't a generator (hasYield) or inside a never-returning function, reports 'While loop condition is always true.' (while.alwaysTrue) - flags infinite loops that were presumably meant to be conditional.
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: control_flow.rs's is_truthy_literal(cond) + stmt_contains_break(body) combination (line 90) is used only to decide that a while(true){...} loop with no break always_terminates the function (for dead-code-after-loop / definite-return analysis) - it is never surfaced as its own diagnostic; there's no while.alwaysTrue equivalent.

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: CallToConstructorStatementWithoutImpurePointsRule
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: Level-4 Rule on CollectedDataNode: cross-references PossiblyPureNewCollector (every `new Foo();` used as a standalone statement) against ConstructorWithoutImpurePointsCollector (every class whose constructor was proven to have no impure points) filtered through PossiblyPureCallTransitivePurityResolver's whole-program transitive purity graph, and reports 'Call to new X() on a separate line has no effect.' (new.resultUnused) for constructors confirmed pure across the whole analyzed codebase.
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: Depends entirely on the Collector/CollectedDataNode whole-program pass and a purity-graph resolver, neither of which exist in phpstan-rs (grep for 'pure'/'Pure'/'impure' across src/ turns up only unrelated English-word hits like 'purely'/'purpose'; grep for 'resultUnused'/'no effect'/'separate line' is empty). No dead-code-from-unused-pure-constructor-call check exists at all.

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: CallToFunctionStatementWithoutImpurePointsRule
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: Level-4 Rule on CollectedDataNode: same pattern as the constructor variant but for plain function calls - cross-references PossiblyPureFuncCallCollector (standalone-statement function calls) against FunctionWithoutImpurePointsCollector filtered by the transitive purity resolver, reporting 'Call to function X() on a separate line has no effect.' (function.resultUnused).
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: Same missing infrastructure as CallToConstructorStatementWithoutImpurePointsRule - no purity tracking, no collector pass, no such diagnostic exists in phpstan-rs's checker (which does not flag unused function-call-statements even syntactically, let alone gated by proven purity).

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: CallToMethodStatementWithoutImpurePointsRule
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: Level-4 Rule on CollectedDataNode: instance-method variant - cross-references PossiblyPureMethodCallCollector (standalone-statement `$obj->method();` calls, matched against every possible class in the call's class-name list) against MethodWithoutImpurePointsCollector filtered by the transitive purity resolver, reporting 'Call to method X::Y() on a separate line has no effect.' (method.resultUnused).
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: Same missing purity/collector infrastructure; method calls are checked in src/checker/calls.rs and oop.rs for argument/return-type correctness but never for whether their unused result reflects dead code given proven purity.

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: CallToStaticMethodStatementWithoutImpurePointsRule
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: Level-4 Rule on CollectedDataNode: static-method variant - cross-references PossiblyPureStaticCallCollector against MethodWithoutImpurePointsCollector filtered by the transitive purity resolver, reporting 'Call to X::Y() on a separate line has no effect.' (staticMethod.resultUnused).
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: Same missing purity/collector infrastructure as the other three WithoutImpurePoints rules; no equivalent check exists for static method call statements in src/checker/*.rs.

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: ConstructorWithoutImpurePointsCollector
