comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: Level-4 Collector on MethodReturnStatementsNode: for constructors only, returns [declaringClassName, dependencies] when the method is possibly pure (not definitely impure), has no by-reference parameters that create new variables, declares no @phpstan-assert tags, has a void-or-absent @throws type, and PossiblyPureCallTransitivePurityResolver::resolveDependencies() can resolve its impure points/throw points into a concrete dependency list - feeding CallToConstructorStatementWithoutImpurePointsRule.
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: Pure whole-program purity-graph collection logic; phpstan-rs has neither a purity/impure-points model for constructors (or any method) nor a Collector architecture to aggregate it. No equivalent exists in src/registry.rs or src/checker/oop.rs (which handle constructor resolution/argument checking but never purity).

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: FunctionWithoutImpurePointsCollector
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: Level-4 Collector (not a Rule) that, for a function whose reflection says isPure()/hasSideEffects() are 'maybe', records the function's name plus the list of callable keys its impure points transitively depend on, skipping functions with by-ref params that create new variables, custom @phpstan-assert asserts, or an explicit throw type - feeding PossiblyPureCallTransitivePurityResolver's fixpoint closure.
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: phpstan-rs has no purity/impurity concept anywhere (FunctionReflection/FunctionSig carries no isPure/hasSideEffects/impure-points fields), confirmed by ROADMAP.md's explicit 'No purity/impurity tracking anywhere' limitation (tracked as future Phase 41, prerequisite to the DeadCode catalog in Phase 15). Grepped src/ for isPure/purity/ImpurePoint - no hits.

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: MethodWithoutImpurePointsCollector
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: Method-reflection analogue of FunctionWithoutImpurePointsCollector: a level-4 Collector recording, for a possibly-pure non-constructor method, its declaring class, name, display name, and its dependency keys (skipped if it has creates-new-variable by-ref params, asserts, or a non-void throw type).
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: Same root cause as the function variant - no purity tracking, no MethodReflection.isPure/hasSideEffects, no impure-point/collector infrastructure in src/checker or src/registry.rs.

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: NoopRule
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: Level-4 Rule on NoopExpressionNode that reports 'Unused result of ...' for a standalone-statement xor/logical-and/logical-or/boolean-and/boolean-or/ternary expression, and a generic 'Expression "..." on a separate line does not do anything.' for any other side-effect-free bare expression statement (skipping assigns, closures, and calls/news already covered by the *WithoutSideEffectsRule family).
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: Grepped src/ for resultUnused/'does not do anything'/logicalAnd/booleanAnd-style diagnostics - none exist. No expr-statement-noop detection anywhere in src/checker/stmt.rs or expr.rs; not mentioned in ROADMAP's Phase 15 DeadCode bullet list either (only unreachable code, always-true/false conditions, unused private members are named there), so this specific check isn't even explicitly tracked yet.

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: PossiblyPureCallTransitivePurityResolver
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: Autowired helper service (not a Rule/Collector itself) shared by the CallTo*StatementWithoutImpurePointsRule family: resolveDependencies() turns a declaration's impure/throw points into a list of callable dependency keys (or null if it can never be pure), resolveCall() resolves a func/method/static-call/new expression to the declaration(s) it targets (bailing on overridable non-final methods), and getPureCallableKeys() computes the fixpoint closure of transitively-pure declarations across all collected function/method/constructor data.
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: Pure algorithmic support class for the impure-points collector family; since none of that family (impure-points collectors, possibly-pure-call collectors, or the *WithoutSideEffectsRule consumers) exists in phpstan-rs and there is no purity model at all, this resolver has no counterpart to build on.

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: PossiblyPureFuncCallCollector
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: Level-4 Collector on Stmt\Expression that, for a bare function-call statement (unwrapping a pipe-operator RHS or first-class-callable pipe) whose target function reflection is possibly-pure with possibly-no-side-effects, records the function name and line for the later CallToFunctionStatementWithoutSideEffectsRule to flag.
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: No collector infrastructure or purity model exists; grep for PossiblyPure*/WithoutSideEffects across src/ is empty.

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: PossiblyPureMethodCallCollector
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: Method-call analogue of PossiblyPureFuncCallCollector: a level-4 Collector on Stmt\Expression that, for a bare method/nullsafe-method-call statement, checks every possible object class reflection has the method (private, final, or on a final class/declaring class), is possibly-pure with possibly-no-side-effects, then records the declaring class names, method name, and line.
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: Same gap - no purity model, no collector framework, no method-call-statement dead-code checking of any kind in src/checker.

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: PossiblyPureNewCollector
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: Level-4 Collector on Stmt\Expression that, for a bare `new ClassName(...)` statement whose class has a real (non-aliased) __construct that's possibly-pure, records the declaring class name and line for CallToConstructorStatementWithoutSideEffectsRule.
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: Same purity/collector gap; no equivalent 'statement is a pure-looking `new` with a discarded result' detection anywhere in src/checker.

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: PossiblyPureStaticCallCollector
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: Static-call analogue of the func-call collector: a level-4 Collector on Stmt\Expression that resolves a bare static-call statement's method reflection and, if possibly-pure with possibly-no-side-effects, records declaring class, method name, and line.
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: Same purity/collector gap as the other three PossiblyPure*Collector files; no equivalent in src/.

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: UnreachableStatementRule
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: Trivial level-4 Rule on the virtual UnreachableStatementNode (produced upstream by NodeScopeResolver once it sees a statement after one that always terminates) that unconditionally emits 'Unreachable statement - code above always terminates.' with identifier deadCode.unreachable.
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: phpstan-rs has real always_terminates()-style control-flow groundwork (src/checker/control_flow.rs, used from src/checker/stmt.rs) that already knows whether if/switch/try/match branches always terminate - but that machinery is used only to merge/narrow local-variable state across branches, never to flag a subsequent statement as unreachable and emit a diagnostic. ROADMAP.md explicitly lists 'unreachable code past an always-terminating statement' as open work under Phase 15. So: underlying analysis primitive exists, but the diagnostic-emitting rule itself does not - classified missing rather than partial since there is zero unreachable-statement reporting today.

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: UnusedPrivateConstantRule
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: Level-4 Rule on the virtual ClassConstantsNode that collects every private class constant not covered by an AlwaysUsedClassConstantsExtension, walks all ::CONST fetch sites across the class-and-its-usages, unsets any constant actually fetched (or bails to 'assume used' when the fetch target's name/class isn't statically known), and reports 'Constant X::Y is unused.' (identifier classConstant.unused) for what remains.
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: grep for classConstant.unused / 'is unused' / private-constant-usage tracking across src/ is empty; no class-level aggregation of const-fetch sites exists (no ClassConstantsNode equivalent). Matches ROADMAP's 'unused private methods/constants' bullet under the open Phase 15 DeadCode catalog.

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: UnusedPrivateMethodRule
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: Level-4 Rule on the virtual ClassMethodsNode: collects every non-trait private method (except the constructor and __clone) not always-used per AlwaysUsedMethodExtension, then walks every method-call site in the class (method/static calls with dynamic-name subtraction handling, plus a second pass over array-callable literals like [$this,'foo']) to unset methods actually invoked from outside their own recursive-self-call, reporting 'Method/Static method X::Y() is unused.' for the rest.
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: No aggregate class-method-call-site collection or private-method-usage tracking exists anywhere in src/checker/oop.rs or elsewhere; grep for method.unused is empty. Explicitly named in ROADMAP's open Phase 15 DeadCode list.

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: UnusedPrivatePropertyRule
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: Level-4 Rule on the virtual ClassPropertiesNode: the most elaborate of the three unused-private-member rules. Tracks per-property read/written state (seeded from readable/writable flags, @phpstan-always-read/-written phpdoc tags, ReadWritePropertiesExtension, and whether it has a default), walks every property-fetch usage site (including a dedicated exemption for a promoted-constructor-param's own self-write and for property-hook bodies), and emits five distinct messages depending on read/written combination: property.unused, property.neverRead, property.onlyWritten, property.neverWritten, property.onlyRead (also consulting an uninitialized-properties check).
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: No equivalent read/write/usage tracking for private properties across a class exists in src/checker/oop.rs or assignment.rs; grep across the five identifier strings is empty. Same open Phase 15 DeadCode gap.

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: TooWideArrowFunctionReturnTypehintRule
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: Level-4 Rule on InArrowFunctionNode: if the arrow function has an explicit return type that resolves to a UnionType, and its single expression isn't itself a yield, delegates to TooWideTypeCheck::checkAnonymousFunction() to compare the expression's inferred type against the declared union and flag unused union members as a too-wide typehint.
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: phpstan-rs has no declared-vs-actual-narrowest-type comparison utility at all (no TooWideTypeCheck analogue). ROADMAP.md names this entire family explicitly: 'No declared-vs-actual-narrowest-type inference (TooWideTypehints)', tracked as future Phase 45, describing the exact same union-member-narrowing mechanism this rule uses.

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: TooWideClosureReturnTypehintRule
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: Level-4 Rule on ClosureReturnStatementsNode: skips closures with no return type, closures whose body yields, or closures with zero return statements; otherwise unions the inferred types of every return statement and delegates to the same TooWideTypeCheck::checkAnonymousFunction() as the arrow-function rule.
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: Same missing TooWideTypeCheck infrastructure; ROADMAP Phase 45 covers this closure variant identically to the arrow-function one.

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: TooWideFunctionParameterOutTypeRule
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: Level-4 Rule on FunctionReturnStatementsNode delegating to TooWideParameterOutTypeCheck::check() with the function's execution-end points, return statements, and by-ref parameters, to flag a declared @param-out type (for a by-ref out-parameter) that is wider than what the function body ever actually assigns to that parameter.
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: phpstan-rs has no @param-out / parameter-out-type concept at all - grepped docblock.rs and registry.rs for param-out/ParamOut/passedByReference/by_ref with no hits, so there is no declared out-type to even compare against. Falls under the same Phase 45 too-wide-typehints gap, compounded by the missing @param-out phpdoc feature itself (not separately tracked in ROADMAP, but a clear prerequisite).

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: TooWideFunctionReturnTypehintRule
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: Level-4 Rule on FunctionReturnStatementsNode delegating to TooWideTypeCheck::checkFunctionReturnType() with the function's native return type, PHPDoc return type, and display name, to flag a declared function return type wider than the union of what the body actually returns.
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: Core case of the missing TooWideTypeCheck machinery; directly the subject of ROADMAP's open Phase 45.

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: TooWideMethodParameterOutTypeRule
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: Method analogue of TooWideFunctionParameterOutTypeRule: skips non-private methods unless checkTooWideParameterOutInProtectedAndPublicMethods is configured on, otherwise delegates to the same TooWideParameterOutTypeCheck::check() for the method's by-ref @param-out parameters.
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: Same missing @param-out concept and TooWideParameterOutTypeCheck as the function variant; no visibility-gated too-wide-out-type checking exists for methods either.

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: TooWideMethodReturnTypehintRule
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: Method analogue of TooWideFunctionReturnTypehintRule: skips trait context, gates non-private/non-final methods behind checkTooWideReturnTypesInProtectedAndPublicMethods and 'is this the first declaration in the hierarchy', then delegates to TooWideTypeCheck::checkFunctionReturnType() with an isSubclass hint (!$isFirstDeclaration && !$method->isPrivate()) for prototype-aware phrasing.
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: Same missing TooWideTypeCheck as the plain function-return-type rule, plus method-hierarchy-aware gating (first-declaration/override checks) that also doesn't exist. Falls under ROADMAP Phase 45.

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: TooWideParameterOutTypeCheck
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: Autowired helper (not a Rule itself) that, given a function/method's execution-end and return-statement scopes plus its by-ref/@param-out parameters, merges the final scopes, computes each by-ref parameter's actual assigned type, and delegates to TooWideTypeCheck::checkParameterOutType to report when the declared @param-out type (or plain by-ref parameter type) is wider than what is ever actually assigned to it.
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: No 'too wide' diagnostics of any kind exist in phpstan-rs. src/checker has no logic that inspects by-ref parameter assignments across a function body to compare against a declared @param-out/by-ref type; grepped for tooWide/paramOut/parameterByRef/nestedUnusedType identifiers across src/ with zero hits. Would require tracking execution-end/return scopes per function (control_flow.rs) plus a merge-and-compare pass, none of which currently exists.

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: TooWidePropertyTypeRule
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: A real Rule<ClassPropertiesNode> (registered at level 4) that iterates a class's private, non-trait, non-promoted properties, skips any the ReadWritePropertiesExtension marks as always-read/always-written/initialized-elsewhere, and for the rest calls TooWideTypeCheck::checkProperty with all in-class property assignments plus the property's native/PHPDoc/default types to flag a declared property type wider than everything ever assigned to it.
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: No equivalent rule exists in phpstan-rs. There is no per-class aggregation of all `$this->prop = ...` assignment sites analogous to ClassPropertiesNode/PropertyAssign, no ReadWritePropertiesExtension-style allow-list, and no property-type-narrowing diagnostic (searched src/checker/*.rs and src/registry.rs for property assign collection and 'tooWide'/'unusedType' identifiers — none found).

comparison-deadcode-toowide.name: TooWideTypeCheck
comparison-deadcode-toowide.description: The shared autowired engine behind all three too-wide-typehint rules: checkProperty(), checkFunctionReturnType(), checkParameterOutType() and checkAnonymousFunction() each union the actually-observed types (property assigns, return statements, or the actual by-ref variable type) and call private narrowType() to drop declared union members never actually produced, or (when reportTooWideBool is on) narrow a plain bool typehint down to true/false; also supports a 'nested too wide type' mode (reportNestedTooWideType) using SimultaneousTypeTraverser to find narrowable sub-types inside composite declared types, emitting return.unusedType/return.tooWideBool/property.unusedType/property.tooWideBool/paramOut.*/parameterByRef.*/return.nestedUnusedType/property.nestedUnusedType identifiers.
comparison-deadcode-toowide.notes: This is the core comparison logic (declared type vs. union of actually-produced types, including the bool->true/false narrowing and the nested-type traversal via SimultaneousTypeTraverser) and none of it exists in phpstan-rs: no return-type-narrowing-from-observed-returns check, no bool-to-true/false-if-only-one-branch-observed logic, and no SimultaneousTypeTraverser-equivalent nested narrowing pass. types.rs has no analogous 'narrow declared union against observed union' helper, and no callers of such a helper exist in src/checker/*.rs.

generics-variables-constants.name: AlwaysUsedClassConstantsExtension
generics-variables-constants.description: Pure DI extension-point interface (tag phpstan.constants.alwaysUsedClassConstantsExtension): third-party extensions implement isAlwaysUsed(ClassConstantReflection) to suppress PHPStan's unused-private-class-constant dead-code diagnostic for specific constants. No check logic of its own.
generics-variables-constants.notes: Marker/extension interface with zero logic - just a registration point for plugins. phpstan-rs also has no unused-class-constant / dead-code detection pass at all (grep for unused-constant logic found nothing), so there is no host feature this could even extend.

generics-variables-constants.name: ClassAsClassConstantRule
generics-variables-constants.description: Rule (level 0) on Stmt\ClassConst: flags any class constant literally named 'class' (case-insensitive) with a non-ignorable classConstant.class error, since 'class' is reserved for ::class fetching.
generics-variables-constants.notes: src/ast.rs's ClassConst node stores only {name, value, doc_comment, span} with no reserved-name validation anywhere in parser/classes.rs or the checker; declaring `const class = ...` is silently accepted.

generics-variables-constants.name: ConstantAttributesRule
generics-variables-constants.description: Rule (level 0) on Stmt\Const_ (global constants): validates any #[Attribute] groups via AttributesCheck against Attribute::TARGET_CONSTANT, and separately reports attributes-on-global-constants as PHP-8.5-only via a PhpVersion capability check.
generics-variables-constants.notes: phpstan-rs has no attribute-checking infrastructure at all - attributes are lexed (src/lexer.rs) but never modeled into the AST as attrGroups or validated for target/args - and no PhpVersion abstraction to gate PHP-8.5-only syntax.

generics-variables-constants.name: ConstantRule
generics-variables-constants.description: Rule (level 1) on Expr\ConstFetch: reports 'Constant %s not found.' (constant.notFound) when Scope::hasConstant() is false for the referenced global constant name, optionally with a discovering-symbols tip.
generics-variables-constants.notes: src/checker/expr.rs line ~1480 types any bare ExprKind::Name (which is how a constant fetch like MY_CONST is represented, since there is no distinct ConstFetch node) as Type::Mixed unconditionally - there is no known-constants table and no undefined-constant diagnostic.

generics-variables-constants.name: DynamicClassConstantFetchRule
generics-variables-constants.description: Rule (level 0) on ClassConstFetch where the constant name is itself an expression (Foo::{$expr}): reports PHP-8.3-version-gate error, then requires the name expression's type to be a string (classConstant.nameType otherwise).
generics-variables-constants.notes: src/ast.rs models class-constant/static access as StaticAccess(String, String) - both class and member are plain compile-time strings, so a dynamic (expression) class-constant-fetch node cannot even be parsed/represented in this AST. Fixing this would require a parser/AST redesign, not a checker addition; flagged missing rather than partial since there is no partial behavior to point to.

generics-variables-constants.name: FinalConstantRule
generics-variables-constants.description: Rule (level 0) on Stmt\ClassConst: if the constant is declared `final`, reports classConstant.finalNotSupported unless PhpVersion::supportsFinalConstants() (PHP 8.1+).
generics-variables-constants.notes: ClassConst in src/ast.rs has no is_final field at all (only name/value/doc_comment/span), and phpstan-rs has no PhpVersion/target-version abstraction anywhere to gate syntax by PHP version.

generics-variables-constants.name: FinalPrivateConstantRule
generics-variables-constants.description: Rule (level 0) on Stmt\ClassConst: for a constant that is both `final` and `private`, reports classConstant.finalPrivate ('cannot be final as it is never overridden by other classes') since a private constant can't be overridden anyway.
generics-variables-constants.notes: Same root cause as FinalConstantRule/OverridingConstantRule: ClassConst carries no visibility or final flags in the AST, and registry ClassInfo.consts is just HashMap<String, Type> with no per-constant reflection (visibility/final) to check.

generics-variables-constants.name: MagicConstantContextRule
generics-variables-constants.description: Rule (level 0) on Scalar\MagicConst: flags __CLASS__ outside a class, __TRAIT__ outside a trait, __FUNCTION__/__METHOD__ outside a function/closure, and __NAMESPACE__ in the global namespace, since each is always empty-string in that context.
generics-variables-constants.notes: phpstan-rs has no distinct MagicConst AST node - magic constants like __CLASS__/__LINE__/__FUNCTION__ parse as plain ExprKind::Name identifiers (only __DIR__ gets narrow special-case handling, in src/composer.rs for package-root resolution, unrelated to this rule) - so there is no context-sensitivity check for any of them.

generics-variables-constants.name: MissingClassConstantTypehintRule
generics-variables-constants.description: Rule (level 6) on Stmt\ClassConst: for each constant with a PHPDoc @var type, delegates to MissingTypehintCheck to flag iterable-with-no-value-type, non-generic-class-used-generically, and callable-with-no-signature within that type (missingType.iterableValue / missingType.generics / missingType.callable).
generics-variables-constants.notes: No MissingTypehintCheck-equivalent exists anywhere in phpstan-rs (grepped for its message identifiers project-wide with no hits) - this whole family of 'missing generic/iterable/callable specificity' diagnostics is unimplemented, not just for constants but for params/returns/properties too.

generics-variables-constants.name: NativeTypedClassConstantRule
generics-variables-constants.description: Rule (level 0) on Stmt\ClassConst: if the constant has a native type declaration (`const int X = 1;`), reports classConstant.nativeTypeNotSupported unless PhpVersion::supportsNativeTypesInClassConstants() (PHP 8.3+).
generics-variables-constants.notes: ClassConst in src/ast.rs has no native `type` field to even carry a declared type, and there is no PhpVersion gating mechanism in phpstan-rs.

generics-variables-constants.name: OverridingConstantRule
generics-variables-constants.description: Rule (level 0) on Stmt\ClassConst: finds the nearest overridden constant prototype (immediate interfaces first, then parent class), and reports if the override widens a final constant (classConstant.final), narrows visibility (classConstant.visibility), narrows the native type (classConstant.nativeType) or omits a native type the parent has (classConstant.missingNativeType), or narrows the PHPDoc value type (classConstant.type).
generics-variables-constants.notes: Registry's ClassInfo.consts is a flat HashMap<String, Type> (last-declaration-wins, no per-class-in-hierarchy prototype tracking, no visibility/final/native-vs-phpdoc distinction), and there is no override-compatibility check for constants anywhere in src/checker/oop.rs (which does implement the analogous method-override checks, so this is a real, comparably-sized gap, not an oversight of a whole feature family).

generics-variables-constants.name: ValueAssignedToClassConstantRule
generics-variables-constants.description: Rule (level 2) on Stmt\ClassConst: checks the assigned value's inferred type against, in priority order, the constant's native type (classConstant.value), its PHPDoc @var type (classConstant.phpDocType), or (if neither exists) an optionally-configured per-class-constant type from featureToggles.checkDynamicConstantNameValues.
generics-variables-constants.notes: No accepts()-style value-vs-declared-type check exists for class constants anywhere in the checker; registry stores only a single resolved Type per constant name with no native/phpdoc distinction to check the assigned literal against.

generics-variables-constants.name: ValueAssignedToDefineRule
generics-variables-constants.description: Rule on FuncCall: for calls to define('NAME', value), looks up a user-configured type for NAME via ConstantResolver::getConfiguredGlobalConstantType() and reports constant.defineValue if the assigned value doesn't fit it.
generics-variables-constants.notes: No define()-specific handling exists in src/checker/calls.rs, and phpstan-rs has no 'configured constant types' feature (a phpstan.neon-style user config mapping constant names to types) for this to even consult.

generics-variables-constants.name: ValueAssignedToGlobalConstantRule
generics-variables-constants.description: Rule on Stmt\Const_ (the `const NAME = value;` global-constant form): same configured-type check as ValueAssignedToDefineRule, reporting constant.value when the value doesn't fit a configured type for that constant name.
generics-variables-constants.notes: StmtKind::GlobalConst is parsed but only consumed for yield-detection in src/checker/control_flow.rs:200 - no value-type checking, and (as above) no configured-constant-type feature exists to check against.

generics-variables-constants.name: ClassAncestorsRule
generics-variables-constants.description: Rule (level 2) on InClassNode for Stmt\Class_: runs GenericAncestorsCheck twice (against @extends and @implements PHPDoc tags) to validate ~13 distinct conditions (unresolvable type, tag without real extends/implements, tag/actual mismatch, non-generic-target, wrong arg count, bound violation, disallowed call-site variance, missing type args on a generic ancestor), then folds in CrossCheckInterfacesHelper's diamond-interface conflict check.
generics-variables-constants.notes: src/checker/generics.rs's check_class_generic_bounds (called from checker.rs:324) does apply real bound-violation checking to a class's resolved extends_args/implements_args - the one condition out of GenericAncestorsCheck's ~13 that phpstan-rs implements - but arg-count mismatches, unresolvable/non-generic-target errors, tag-vs-actual-ancestor mismatches, disallowed call-site variance, and CrossCheckInterfacesHelper's interface-conflict check are all absent.

generics-variables-constants.name: ClassTemplateTypeRule
generics-variables-constants.description: Rule (level 2) on InClassNode for real classes: via TemplateTypeCheck, validates each @template tag's own declaration - name doesn't collide with an existing class or type alias, bound type is valid/supported, default type is valid and is a subtype of the bound, and no required @template follows one with a default.
generics-variables-constants.notes: registry/class_info.rs stores template_bounds: HashMap<String, Type> purely for later usage-site bound enforcement (check_generic_bounds); there is no declaration-site validation of template names, bound validity, or default-type ordering/subtyping anywhere in phpstan-rs.

generics-variables-constants.name: CrossCheckInterfacesHelper
generics-variables-constants.description: AutowiredService helper (not a Rule itself) used by ClassAncestorsRule/EnumAncestorsRule: walks a class's full interface/parent graph and reports generics.interfaceConflict when the same generic interface is reached twice via different paths (diamond inheritance) with incompatible template-type-map bindings.
generics-variables-constants.notes: No equivalent diamond-interface template-conflict detection exists in phpstan-rs; check_class_generic_bounds only validates bounds on a class's own direct extends/implements arguments, never cross-checks two different inheritance paths reaching the same generic interface with different bindings.

generics-variables-constants.name: EnumAncestorsRule
generics-variables-constants.description: Rule (level 2) on InClassNode for Stmt\Enum_: enum-flavored twin of ClassAncestorsRule - @extends is always flagged as invalid for enums (enums can't extend), @implements is validated the same way as ClassAncestorsRule's implements half, plus the same CrossCheckInterfacesHelper diamond check.
generics-variables-constants.notes: checker.rs's StmtKind::EnumDecl arm (line 337) never calls check_class_generic_bounds (that call is gated to ClassDecl only, at line 324) - enums get zero generic-ancestor checking of any kind in phpstan-rs, not even the partial bound-checking that classes get via ClassAncestorsRule's overlap.

generics-variables-constants.name: EnumTemplateTypeRule
generics-variables-constants.description: Level-2 Rule on InClassNode: if the class is an enum and has any PHPDoc @template tags, reports 'enum.generic' since enums cannot be generic.
generics-variables-constants.notes: phpstan-rs's docblock.rs parses @template tags uniformly for any class-like (including enums) into template_bounds/templates, but no check anywhere (generics.rs, checker.rs) rejects an enum carrying them - grep for 'enum.generic'/'cannot be generic' finds nothing.

generics-variables-constants.name: FunctionSignatureVarianceRule
generics-variables-constants.description: Level-2 Rule on InFunctionNode: delegates to VarianceCheck::checkParametersAcceptor for a top-level function's signature (params contravariant, return covariant, plus flags a function-scoped @template that carries a variance annotation at all, which is invalid outside classes/interfaces).
generics-variables-constants.notes: Checker::check_variance (generics.rs:190) is only invoked from src/checker.rs's check_function when class_name is Some (line 592-594) - never for plain top-level functions. There's also no tracking of variance annotations on function-scoped @template tags (FunctionSig has no covariant/contravariant fields), so the 'variance annotation only allowed for class/interface type params' half has no equivalent either.

generics-variables-constants.name: FunctionTemplateTypeRule
generics-variables-constants.description: Level-2 Rule on Node\Stmt\Function_: resolves the function's own PHPDoc and runs its @template tags through TemplateTypeCheck::check (name-collision, bound validity/support, default-type validity, required-after-optional).
generics-variables-constants.notes: No Rust equivalent of TemplateTypeCheck exists (see that entry); template_bounds parsed in docblock.rs are only ever used later for bound-substitution/violation via check_generic_bounds, never validated at declaration time for existing-class-name collisions, unsupported bound kinds, or default-type-vs-bound subtyping.

generics-variables-constants.name: GenericAncestorsCheck
generics-variables-constants.description: Shared AutowiredService used by InterfaceAncestorsRule/UsedTraitsRule (and ClassAncestorsRule elsewhere) to validate a list of @extends/@implements/@use tag types against the actual extended/implemented/used names: incompatible-type, unresolvable-type, no-names, wrong-name, delegates to GenericObjectTypeCheck for count/subtype, trait-as-bound, call-site-variance-not-allowed, and (when checkMissingTypehints) flags a generic ancestor referenced with no type args at all.
generics-variables-constants.notes: Checker::check_class_generic_bounds (generics.rs:125, called from checker.rs:324 for every ClassDecl) re-pairs extends/implements args into Object types and runs check_generic_bounds against them, covering the bound-subtype-violation core. It does not check argument-count mismatches (not enough/extra types), unresolvable types, 'has @extends but doesn't extend anything', trait-used-as-generic-arg, call-site variance, or the missing-typehints-for-bare-generic-ancestor diagnostic - none of those identifiers exist in the Rust source.

generics-variables-constants.name: GenericObjectTypeCheck
generics-variables-constants.description: Shared AutowiredService: walks a PHPDoc type for every GenericObjectType/GenericStaticType it contains and validates each against the referenced class's own template list - not-generic, too-few/too-many type args, call-site-variance-redundant/conflicting, and type-arg-not-subtype-of-bound (with template-to-template propagation via inferTemplateTypes for later positions).
generics-variables-constants.notes: Checker::check_generic_bounds (generics.rs:32) implements the core 'argument not a subtype of the corresponding @template bound' check, recursing through Object/Array/ClassString/Union/Intersection/ArrayShape - matching this class's main subtyping concern. It has no equivalent for the class-not-generic check, the too-few/too-many-type-args count checks, or call-site variance redundancy/conflict (call-site variance syntax like `Collection<covariant T>` isn't even parsed by phpstan-rs's docblock/type parser).

generics-variables-constants.name: InterfaceAncestorsRule
generics-variables-constants.description: Level-2 Rule on InClassNode, active only for Node\Stmt\Interface_: runs GenericAncestorsCheck against the interface's @extends tags (against its real `extends` list) and @implements tags (which must always error, since interfaces can't implement), plus CrossCheckInterfacesHelper for reachability-cycle-style cross-checks between multiple extended interfaces.
generics-variables-constants.notes: src/ast.rs's ClassKind::Interface goes through the same StmtKind::ClassDecl path as classes, so Checker::check_class_generic_bounds (called unconditionally per class-like in checker.rs:324) applies the same bound-subtype checking to an interface's extends/implements args. There is no equivalent of CrossCheckInterfacesHelper, no '@implements tag on an interface is always wrong' check, and no count-mismatch/unresolvable checks (same gaps as GenericAncestorsCheck).

generics-variables-constants.name: InterfaceTemplateTypeRule
generics-variables-constants.description: Level-2 Rule on InClassNode, active only for interfaces: runs the interface's own @template tags through TemplateTypeCheck::check.
generics-variables-constants.notes: Same underlying gap as FunctionTemplateTypeRule - no TemplateTypeCheck equivalent exists to validate @template declarations themselves (name collisions, unsupported bound, default-type subtyping, required-after-optional) on any class-like, interfaces included.

generics-variables-constants.name: MethodSignatureVarianceRule
generics-variables-constants.description: Level-2 Rule on InClassMethodNode: delegates to VarianceCheck::checkParametersAcceptor for a method's signature, contravariant on params, covariant on param-out types and return type, skipped entirely for private methods and __construct.
generics-variables-constants.notes: Checker::check_variance (generics.rs:190) is invoked from checker.rs:592-594 for every method with a known class, covering param-contravariant/return-covariant checking against the class's covariant_templates/contravariant_templates. Gaps: it is skipped only for __construct, not for private methods generally (real rule also exempts isPrivate()); there is no param-out type tracking at all (no @param-out support in docblock.rs), so that half of the check is entirely absent; and the function-scoped-template-with-variance-annotation loop from VarianceCheck isn't ported either.

generics-variables-constants.name: MethodTagTemplateTypeCheck
generics-variables-constants.description: Shared AutowiredService used by MethodTagTemplateTypeRule/MethodTagTemplateTypeTraitRule: resolves a class/trait's own @method tags, runs each tag's own @template sub-tags through TemplateTypeCheck, and additionally flags a @method template name that shadows a class-level @template name ('methodTag.shadowTemplate').
generics-variables-constants.notes: phpstan-rs's docblock.rs has no @method tag parsing at all (grep for MethodTag/method_tags/"@method" finds nothing) - magic-method-via-PHPDoc support and any templates nested inside such tags are entirely unimplemented.

generics-variables-constants.name: MethodTagTemplateTypeRule
generics-variables-constants.description: Level-2 Rule on InClassNode: reads the class's own doc-comment and forwards to MethodTagTemplateTypeCheck::check.
generics-variables-constants.notes: Depends entirely on @method tag parsing/MethodTagTemplateTypeCheck, neither of which exists in phpstan-rs.

generics-variables-constants.name: MethodTagTemplateTypeTraitRule
generics-variables-constants.description: Level-2 Rule on Node\Stmt\Trait_: same as MethodTagTemplateTypeRule but for a trait's own @method tags.
generics-variables-constants.notes: Same underlying gap - no @method tag support in docblock.rs/registry.rs at all.

generics-variables-constants.name: MethodTemplateTypeRule
generics-variables-constants.description: Level-2 Rule on Node\Stmt\ClassMethod: resolves the method's own PHPDoc, runs its @template tags through TemplateTypeCheck, and separately flags a method @template name that shadows the enclosing class's own @template name ('method.shadowTemplate').
generics-variables-constants.notes: No TemplateTypeCheck equivalent (see that entry) and no method-template-vs-class-template shadowing check anywhere in checker/*.rs (grep for 'shadow' only turns up an unrelated comment in narrowing.rs).

generics-variables-constants.name: PropertyVarianceRule
generics-variables-constants.description: Level-2 Rule on ClassPropertyNode: for a non-private native property, checks its readable type against VarianceCheck with covariant variance if the property has restricted write access (readonly, private(set), or a hook-set-less property-hook), otherwise invariant - catching e.g. a plain mutable public property typed with a class's own @template-covariant T.
generics-variables-constants.notes: Checker::check_variance (generics.rs) is only ever called for method signatures (checker.rs:593); there is no call site that runs property types through it, and phpstan-rs's property model has no readonly/private(set)/property-hook distinction feeding into a variance decision at all.

generics-variables-constants.name: TemplateTypeCheck
generics-variables-constants.description: Shared AutowiredService invoked by every *TemplateTypeRule (Function/Interface/Method/Trait): for each @template tag, checks the tag name doesn't collide with an existing class or type alias, validates the bound type's referenced classes exist and aren't traits, restricts the bound to a fixed allow-list of supported Type subclasses, runs GenericObjectTypeCheck on both bound and default type, and validates the default type is a subtype of the bound plus 'default type after a tag with no default' ordering.
generics-variables-constants.notes: phpstan-rs parses @template/@template-covariant/@template-contravariant tags (docblock.rs) into template_bounds/templates/covariant_templates/contravariant_templates purely for later substitution and bound-violation-at-usage-site checking (check_generic_bounds); none of TemplateTypeCheck's declaration-time validations (existing-class-name collision, type-alias collision - phpstan-rs has no @phpstan-type support either, unsupported-bound-kind, default-type-vs-bound subtyping, required-after-optional ordering) exist anywhere in the Rust source.

generics-variables-constants.name: TraitTemplateTypeRule
generics-variables-constants.description: Level-2 Rule on Node\Stmt\Trait_: resolves the trait's own PHPDoc and runs its @template tags through TemplateTypeCheck.
generics-variables-constants.notes: Same TemplateTypeCheck absence as Function/Interface/MethodTemplateTypeRule, applied to traits.

generics-variables-constants.name: UsedTraitsRule
generics-variables-constants.description: Level-2 Rule on Node\Stmt\TraitUse: resolves the enclosing class/trait's @use tags (generic trait instantiation, e.g. `@use Collection<int>`) and runs them through GenericAncestorsCheck against the real `use` statement's trait names.
generics-variables-constants.notes: docblock.rs has no @use tag parsing at all (grep for UsesTag/"@use" finds nothing), and registry.rs's ClassInfo.uses is a plain list of trait names with no per-use generic type-argument tracking - a generic trait used without or with mismatched type arguments is never flagged.

generics-variables-constants.name: VarianceCheck
generics-variables-constants.description: Shared AutowiredService with two entry points: checkParametersAcceptor (drives Function/MethodSignatureVarianceRule - flags function-scoped templates with a variance annotation, then checks params/param-out/return against contravariant/covariant position) and check (the core: walks a type's getReferencedTemplateTypes(positionVariance) and reports any class/interface template whose declared variance doesn't validPosition() the position it's used in).
generics-variables-constants.notes: Checker::check_variance (generics.rs:190-233) reimplements a simplified version of the core idea directly against phpstan-rs's own model: collect_template_params gathers TemplateParam names from param types (input position) and return type (output position) and flags any name in covariant_templates found on input or contravariant_templates found on output. As its own doc comment documents, this is deliberately conservative versus the real algorithm - it doesn't do real positional variance composition through a nested generic argument (a T found inside another class's own Collection<T> is treated as a direct occurrence rather than re-derived through that class's own variance), doesn't cover properties or param-out types, and the function-scoped-variance-annotation-is-invalid loop isn't ported at all.

generics-variables-constants.name: AssignToByRefExprFromForeachRule
generics-variables-constants.description: Rule on NodeAbstract, matching only VariableAssignNode/PropertyAssignNode: if the assigned variable/property still carries scope's synthetic ForeachValueByRefExpr type (meaning it was last bound as a `foreach (... as &$x)` by-ref value that was never unset), reports that a plain assignment to it now overwrites the source array's last element.
generics-variables-constants.notes: phpstan-rs's Foreach handling in src/checker/stmt.rs (~line 282) binds the loop value's element type via bind_assignment_target but has no synthetic 'last foreach by-ref value' expression-type marker and no later assignment-time check for it; grep for ForeachValueByRefExpr-equivalent tracking or a 'byRefForeachExpr'-style diagnostic in assignment.rs/stmt.rs/expr.rs finds nothing. This is a fairly niche, PHP-idiom-specific footgun rule with no Rust counterpart at all.

generics-variables-constants.name: CompactVariablesRule
generics-variables-constants.description: Level-0 Rule on FuncCall: for calls to compact(), extracts constant-string variable names from the arguments (including through constant arrays) and reports variable.undefined when a named variable is definitely or (if checkMaybeUndefinedVariables) possibly not defined in scope.
generics-variables-constants.notes: grep for 'compact' across src/ finds no handling at all - compact() is just an ordinary unresolved/unknown call to the checker, so undefined variables named inside it are never flagged. No equivalent logic in src/checker/calls.rs or expr.rs.

generics-variables-constants.name: DefinedVariableRule
generics-variables-constants.description: Level-0 Rule on Node\Expr\Variable: reports 'Undefined variable: $x' (variable.undefined) when a variable is never defined in scope, or 'Variable $x might not be defined.' when checkMaybeUndefinedVariables is on and it's only possibly defined; special-cases $argc/$argv in main scope and variable-variables via constant-string resolution.
generics-variables-constants.our_location: src/checker/expr.rs (Variable arm producing 'undefined variable $name' diagnostics) and src/checker/calls.rs (superglobal/definite-assignment tracking via Locals)
generics-variables-constants.notes: Core 'undefined variable $x' diagnostic is present and exercised across many tests (src/checker/tests/control_flow.rs, misc_and_regressions.rs). Possibly-undefined ('might not be defined') branch-merge tracking also exists via merge_scopes/Locals. Variable-variable ($$name) constant-string resolution and the argc/argv main-scope exemption were not confirmed as separately modeled, but the primary diagnostic class is solidly implemented.

generics-variables-constants.name: EmptyRule
generics-variables-constants.description: Level-1 Rule on EmptyExpressionNode: runs IssetCheck on empty()'s argument with a closure classifying the argument's type as 'is always falsy' / 'is not falsy' / 'is always null' / 'is not nullable' / 'is not falsy', suppressing undefined-variable/offset diagnostics for the probed expression itself; also routes through ConstantConditionInTraitHelper for trait-context deduplication.
generics-variables-constants.notes: Only the 'suppress undefined-variable/property checks on empty()'s own argument' half of IssetCheck's behavior is implemented (via check_expr_quiet_root). The actual diagnostic-emitting half - reporting when empty()'s argument is always/never falsy or always/never null (IssetCheck's message logic) - has no equivalent; no 'is always falsy'/'is not nullable' style messages exist anywhere in src/checker. Trait-context deduplication (ConstantConditionInTraitHelper) is also absent.

generics-variables-constants.name: InvalidVariableAssignRule
generics-variables-constants.description: Level-0 Rule on VariableAssignNode: reports non-ignorable assign.this ('Cannot re-assign $this.') when code assigns to $this, unless the enclosing class implements ArrayAccess.
generics-variables-constants.notes: check_assignment_target treats every bare Variable target, including 'this', as a no-op definition site with no special-casing; grep for 'assign.this'/'re-assign' across src/ finds nothing. `$this = ...;` would pass through the Rust checker silently.

generics-variables-constants.name: IssetRule
generics-variables-constants.description: Level-1 Rule on IssetExpressionNode: for each variable result inside isset(), runs IssetCheck reporting 'is always null' / 'is not nullable' when the checked value's nullability is statically known, deduplicating per trait via ConstantConditionInTraitHelper.
generics-variables-constants.notes: Same situation as EmptyRule: only the undefined-variable/property suppression for isset()'s own argument chain is implemented; the actual 'isset() on an always-null or never-null expression' diagnostic (IssetCheck's message-building) does not exist in src/checker. No 'is always null'/'is not nullable' messages found anywhere.

generics-variables-constants.name: NullCoalesceRule
generics-variables-constants.description: Level-1 Rule on CoalesceExpressionNode: runs IssetCheck on the ?? / ??= left side (same 'is always null'/'is not nullable' messages) and, when the unnecessaryNullCoalesce feature toggle is on, separately reports nullCoalesce.unnecessary when the right side is statically null and the left side is always set (making the whole ?? redundant).
generics-variables-constants.our_location: src/checker/expr.rs (ExprKind::Binary(BinOp::Coalesce, ...) arm, check_expr_quiet_root) and src/checker/narrowing.rs (Coalesce narrowing at lines 559/679)
generics-variables-constants.notes: ?? is recognized specially for type inference (widening/narrowing the result type) and its left side gets the same quiet-root undefined-variable suppression as isset/empty, but neither IssetCheck's 'always null'/'not nullable' diagnostic nor the unnecessaryNullCoalesce redundant-coalesce check exist - no 'nullCoalesce.unnecessary'-equivalent message anywhere in src/.

generics-variables-constants.name: ParameterOutAssignedTypeRule
generics-variables-constants.description: Level-3 Rule on VariableAssignNode: when the assigned variable is a by-ref parameter that creates a new variable, checks the assigned expression's type against the parameter's @param-out type (or its declared type if no @param-out) via ParameterOutTypeCheck, reporting paramOut.type/parameterByRef.type on mismatch.
generics-variables-constants.notes: grep for 'param-out'/'param_out'/'ParamOut' across src/ (including src/docblock.rs) returns nothing - @param-out is not parsed at all, so there is no data for this rule to act on, and no equivalent by-ref-assignment type check exists.

generics-variables-constants.name: ParameterOutExecutionEndTypeRule
generics-variables-constants.description: Level-3 Rule on ExecutionEndNode: at each point execution can end in a function/method, checks every by-ref parameter that has an @param-out type against the variable's current type there (skipped if the parameter's original by-ref value was never touched, or the end point is an explicit never-typed expression), via ParameterOutTypeCheck.
generics-variables-constants.notes: Depends entirely on @param-out parsing (absent, see ParameterOutAssignedTypeRule) and on an ExecutionEndNode-equivalent end-of-function-flow concept; neither exists in src/checker.

generics-variables-constants.name: ParameterOutTypeCheck
generics-variables-constants.description: Shared internal helper (not itself a Rule) used by the two ParameterOut*Rule classes above: given a checked expression, the promised out-type (declared @param-out or the parameter's own type), and whether it's an explicit @param-out, builds the paramOut.type/parameterByRef.type error message comparing the assigned/ending type against the promise.
generics-variables-constants.notes: Pure helper for the two by-ref/@param-out rules above, both of which are missing; no equivalent type-vs-promise comparison logic exists for by-ref parameters in src/checker.

generics-variables-constants.name: ThisInGlobalStatementRule
generics-variables-constants.description: Level-0 Rule on Node\Stmt\Global_: reports non-ignorable global.this ('Cannot use $this as global variable.') for each `global $this;` variable in the statement.
generics-variables-constants.notes: StmtKind::Global just binds every listed name to Type::Mixed with no special-casing of the literal name 'this'; grep for 'global.this'/'as global variable' across src/ finds nothing, so `global $this;` produces no diagnostic in the Rust checker.

generics-variables-constants.name: ThisInStaticStatementRule
generics-variables-constants.description: Level-0 Rule on Node\Stmt\Static_: reports non-ignorable static.this ('Cannot use $this as static variable.') for each `static $this = ...;` variable in the statement.
generics-variables-constants.notes: StmtKind::StaticVar just evaluates the default and binds the name with no check against 'this'; grep for 'static.this'/'as static variable' across src/ finds nothing.

generics-variables-constants.name: UnsetRule
generics-variables-constants.description: Level-0 Rule on Node\Stmt\Unset_: for each unset() target, reports unset.readOnlyProperty/unset.readOnlyPropertyByPhpDoc when unsetting a readonly property, unset.hookedProperty when unsetting a hooked property (or unset.possiblyHookedProperty for a non-final/non-private property that might be hooked in a subclass on PHP versions supporting property hooks), unset.variable ('Call to function unset() contains undefined variable $x.') for an already-undefined variable, and unset.offset for an array offset that can't exist on the container's type (recursing through nested ArrayDimFetch).
generics-variables-constants.our_location: src/checker/expr.rs (ExprKind::Call special-case for name=="unset", lines ~76-98) and src/checker/calls.rs is_language_construct
generics-variables-constants.notes: unset() is modeled only as a language construct that removes the variable's entry from Locals (so a subsequent use is later flagged by the ordinary undefined-variable check) - there is no dedicated `unset(...)` statement AST node (unset() parses as an ordinary Call). None of the readonly-property, hooked-property, unset-of-already-undefined-variable, or invalid-array-offset diagnostics that UnsetRule actually emits are implemented; unsetting an undeclared property or offset produces no diagnostic at all.

generics-variables-constants.name: VariableCloningRule
generics-variables-constants.description: Level-3 Rule on Node\Expr\Clone_: uses RuleLevelHelper to find the checked type of the cloned expression and reports clone.nonObject ('Cannot clone non-object variable $x of type T.' or 'Cannot clone T.') when the type is not cloneable (not an object), plus the usual unknown-class error path.
generics-variables-constants.notes: The Clone arm just checks the inner expression and any clone-with overrides and returns the inner's own type unchanged - there is no isCloneable()/isObject() check and no clone.nonObject-equivalent diagnostic anywhere in src/checker; cloning a non-object value (e.g. `clone $intVar`) is never flagged.

methods-keywords-debug-pure.name: DebugScopeRule
methods-keywords-debug-pure.description: A Rule<FuncCall> that recognizes calls to the internal PHPStan\debugScope() intrinsic and reports every variable currently in scope (name: type) as a non-ignorable diagnostic, for debugging PHPStan's own scope-tracking while writing test fixtures.
methods-keywords-debug-pure.notes: phpstan-rs has no equivalent 'dump the current locals map' debug intrinsic. grep for debugscope/DebugScope in src/ returns nothing. This is a developer-facing debugging aid (not a real diagnostic users would see), so building it would be low-value but is not architecturally impossible - classified missing rather than not_applicable since a `phpstan\debugscope()` hook over the existing `locals: HashMap` would be straightforward.

methods-keywords-debug-pure.name: DumpNativeTypeRule
methods-keywords-debug-pure.description: A Rule<FuncCall> recognizing PHPStan\dumpNativeType() calls; reports each argument's native (non-PHPDoc-informed) inferred type as a diagnostic, for fixture-writing.
methods-keywords-debug-pure.notes: No 'dumpnativetype' or 'DumpNativeType' anywhere in src/. phpstan-rs's own type system does not currently separate a distinct 'native type' (ignoring PHPDoc) from the PHPDoc-informed type the way PHPStan's Scope::getNativeType() does, so this would require deeper type-system work beyond just wiring up the intrinsic call.

methods-keywords-debug-pure.name: DumpPhpDocTypeRule
methods-keywords-debug-pure.description: A Rule<FuncCall> recognizing PHPStan\dumpPhpDocType() calls; reports each argument's type rendered as a PHPDoc type-node string (via the PhpDocParser Printer), for fixture-writing.
methods-keywords-debug-pure.notes: No equivalent in src/. phpstan-rs's Type already has a Display/to_string used pervasively (see assertType below), but there is no separate PHPDoc-node-printer rendering path or a dumpPhpDocType() intrinsic wired up.

methods-keywords-debug-pure.name: DumpTypeRule
methods-keywords-debug-pure.description: A Rule<FuncCall> recognizing PHPStan\dumpType() calls; reports each argument's precise inferred type as a diagnostic - PHPStan's own primary tool for writing/verifying NSRT-style fixture expectations.
methods-keywords-debug-pure.our_location: src/checker/expr.rs (comments only, e.g. lines ~2340, ~2416, and throughout src/checker/tests/*)
methods-keywords-debug-pure.notes: Not implemented as an intrinsic in phpstan-rs itself - every 'dumpType()' hit found by grep is a source-code *comment* documenting that a piece of inference logic was verified by running real PHPStan's dumpType() against its own vendored copy, not a Rust reimplementation of the intrinsic. phpstan-rs's own analogous mechanism is assertType() (see FileAssertRule below), which is implemented but is a comparison-assertion, not an unconditional type dump.

methods-keywords-debug-pure.name: FileAssertRule
methods-keywords-debug-pure.description: A Rule<FuncCall> implementing PHPStan's four testing-DSL assertion functions: assertType() (PHPDoc-informed type string match), assertNativeType() (native type string match), assertSuperType() (subtype check against an expected type string), and assertVariableCertainty() (TrinaryLogic-based definedness check for a variable or array offset).
methods-keywords-debug-pure.our_location: src/checker/expr.rs:100-129 (assertType handling in the Call arm of check_expr)
methods-keywords-debug-pure.notes: Only assertType() is implemented: it compares infer_expr(...).to_string() against the literal expected string and reports 'assertType() mismatch: expected type ..., actual type ...' (see src/checker/tests/misc_and_regressions.rs for coverage). assertNativeType(), assertSuperType(), and assertVariableCertainty() have zero hits anywhere in src/ - not implemented. This is used as phpstan-rs's own internal fixture-testing mechanism (mirroring the vendored PHPStan NSRT corpus), not merely a stub.

methods-keywords-debug-pure.name: ContinueBreakInLoopRule
methods-keywords-debug-pure.description: A Rule<Stmt> walking the parent-statement-type chain of every break/continue to verify its (possibly numeric) target level actually lands inside an enclosing loop or switch, not a closure boundary or the top level; reports 'continue.outOfLoop'/'break.outOfLoop' otherwise.
methods-keywords-debug-pure.notes: phpstan-rs tracks a loop_break_states stack for control-flow purposes (used to merge post-break locals into post-loop state) and computes level via checked_sub, but an out-of-range level (or a break/continue with no enclosing loop/switch at all, including across a closure boundary) simply no-ops silently - no diagnostic is ever reported. Confirmed via grep: no 'outOfLoop' or 'used outside of a loop' message anywhere in src/.

methods-keywords-debug-pure.name: DeclareStrictTypesRule
methods-keywords-debug-pure.description: A Rule<Stmt\Declare_> validating declare(strict_types=...): the value must be the integer literal 0 or 1 ('declareStrictTypes.value' otherwise), and if present it must be the very first statement in the file ('declareStrictTypes.notFirst' otherwise).
methods-keywords-debug-pure.notes: The parser recognizes `declare(...)` syntactically but explicitly does NOT model its directives - each declare argument is parsed as a generic expression and discarded ('The directives themselves... aren't modeled - just consumed as generic expressions', per the parser's own comment). No value-validation or first-statement-position check exists anywhere in src/.

methods-keywords-debug-pure.name: GotoUndefinedLabelRule
methods-keywords-debug-pure.description: A Rule<Goto_> reporting 'goto.labelUndefined' when a goto statement's visitor-computed attribute marks its target label as not found anywhere in the enclosing function/file.
methods-keywords-debug-pure.notes: `goto <label>;` is parsed into a StmtKind::Goto(String) AST node, and StmtKind::Label is parsed too, but grep confirms no label-collection/resolution pass exists anywhere in the checker - the goto target name is never cross-checked against any declared label, and control_flow.rs's own comment ('goto/label share the same theoretical gap always_terminates already has everywhere else') documents that gotos are treated purely conservatively for control-flow purposes, not validated for target existence.

methods-keywords-debug-pure.name: RequireFileExistsRule
methods-keywords-debug-pure.description: A Rule<Include_> that resolves the literal-string constant path(s) an include/require/require_once/include_once expression could take (including __DIR__-concatenation and multi-string-union expansion), simulates PHP's own include-path resolution order, and reports 'require.fileNotFound' (etc. per include type) when none of the resolved absolute paths exist as a file - skipped entirely when the include is guarded by file_exists()/is_file()/is_readable()/etc.
methods-keywords-debug-pure.notes: include/include_once/require/require_once are recognized only as language constructs (so they don't trip 'undefined function' diagnostics) - their path argument is type-checked like any other expression but no constant-string extraction, filesystem existence check, include-path simulation, or file_exists()-guard detection exists anywhere in src/.

methods-keywords-debug-pure.name: UnusedLabelRule
methods-keywords-debug-pure.description: A Rule<Stmt\Label> reporting 'label.unused' (ignorable, not nonIgnorable) when a declared goto label's visitor-computed 'is used' attribute is false, i.e. no goto in the file actually targets it.
methods-keywords-debug-pure.notes: StmtKind::Label is parsed and preserved in the AST (src/parser/stmt.rs:302-309, src/ast_walk.rs:150-151) but nothing in src/checker/*.rs tracks whether any goto references a given label - no usage-tracking or 'is unused' diagnostic exists.

methods-keywords-debug-pure.name: AbstractMethodInNonAbstractClassRule
methods-keywords-debug-pure.description: A Rule<Stmt\ClassMethod> reporting 'method.abstract' when a method is declared `abstract` inside a class that is itself not declared abstract (with enum case()/from()/tryFrom() exemptions), and 'method.nonAbstract' when a non-abstract method in a non-abstract, non-interface class has a null body (no `{ ... }`).
methods-keywords-debug-pure.notes: The AST tracks is_abstract on both methods and classes, and phpstan-rs's own Finding 45 (check_class_completeness in checker/oop.rs) checks the *consequence* - that a concrete class provides implementations for every abstract method it inherits - but there is no direct declaration-site check that a method marked `abstract` sits inside a class also marked `abstract`/interface, nor that a non-abstract method actually has a body. Confirmed via grep: no 'method.abstract'/'method.nonAbstract'-style message anywhere in src/checker/.

methods-keywords-debug-pure.name: AbstractPrivateMethodRule
methods-keywords-debug-pure.description: A Rule<InClassMethodNode> reporting 'method.abstractPrivate' when a method is both private and abstract inside a non-trait class (private + abstract is contradictory: an abstract method must be overridable, but private methods aren't visible to subclasses).
methods-keywords-debug-pure.notes: No 'abstractPrivate' or 'cannot be abstract' message anywhere in src/checker/. This specific private+abstract combination is not flagged; visibility and abstractness are tracked independently in the AST/registry but never cross-checked against each other for this contradiction.

methods-keywords-debug-pure.name: AlwaysUsedMethodExtension
methods-keywords-debug-pure.description: A pure marker/extension interface (isAlwaysUsed(ExtendedMethodReflection): bool) that third-party PHPStan extensions implement and register via DI tagging, to tell PHPStan's dead-method-detection machinery that a given method should never be reported as unused even with zero call sites found (e.g. framework lifecycle methods).
methods-keywords-debug-pure.notes: This is PHPStan's own plugin-extension interface for third-party DI-registered extensions (analogous to other *Extension interfaces already classified not_applicable elsewhere in this audit) - it carries no check logic itself, and phpstan-rs has no plugin/extension system or 'unused private method' dead-code rule for this to hook into in the first place.

methods-keywords-debug-pure.name: CallMethodsRule
methods-keywords-debug-pure.description: A Rule<MethodCall> resolving the method name (including a dynamic $methodName string-union expansion via filterByTruthyValue), then delegating to MethodCallCheck (existence/visibility/nullability of the receiver) and FunctionCallParametersCheck (arg count, arg types, named-argument validity, void-result-used, byref-requires-variable, unresolvable-template-type, etc.) for a full method-call diagnostic suite.
methods-keywords-debug-pure.notes: Core, heavily-exercised functionality: method-call existence, arg-count/arg-type checking (shared check_args machinery also used by Call/StaticCall), and dynamic ($obj->$method()) call handling are all present. Not a literal 1:1 port of every one of PHPStan's ~18 distinct message templates, but the underlying diagnostic coverage (missing/unknown/wrong-count/wrong-type parameters) is implemented.

methods-keywords-debug-pure.name: CallPrivateMethodThroughStaticRule
methods-keywords-debug-pure.description: A Rule<StaticCall> (level 2) reporting 'staticClassAccess.privateMethod' when code calls static::method() (late static binding) inside a non-final class and the resolved method turns out to be private - unsafe because a subclass's private method of the same name would silently be called instead at runtime.
methods-keywords-debug-pure.notes: StaticCall resolution (including 'static' via resolve_static_class_name, mirroring self/parent/static-aware lookup) is implemented for arg-checking purposes, but there is no check that specifically flags a private method reached via `static::` as unsafe under non-final classes - grep for 'privateMethod'/'through static'/'Unsafe call to private' finds nothing in src/checker/.

methods-keywords-debug-pure.name: CallStaticMethodsRule
methods-keywords-debug-pure.description: A Rule<StaticCall> - the static-call counterpart to CallMethodsRule - resolving the (possibly dynamic) method name via StaticMethodCallCheck and running the same FunctionCallParametersCheck diagnostic suite (arg count/type/named-args/void-result/etc.), with message text distinguishing 'Static method' vs plain 'Method' by whether the resolved method is actually static.
methods-keywords-debug-pure.our_location: src/checker/expr.rs:923-1000 (ExprKind::StaticCall handling), src/checker/calls.rs:263 (check_args, shared with MethodCall/Call)
methods-keywords-debug-pure.notes: Uses the same resolve_call_args/check_args pipeline as CallMethodsRule and the plain Call arm - method existence, arg count, and arg type checking against the resolved signature are all implemented for static calls, including the Closure::bind special-case for late-bound $this.

methods-keywords-debug-pure.name: CallToConstructorStatementWithoutSideEffectsRule
methods-keywords-debug-pure.description: A Rule<NoopExpressionNode> (level 4) reporting 'new.resultUnused' when a bare `new Foo(...);` statement's result is discarded on its own line and the constructor either doesn't exist, has no phpstan-asserts, and doesn't return via an explicit Never (i.e. genuinely has no observable side effect for the analyzer to care about).
methods-keywords-debug-pure.notes: No 'no effect'/'resultUnused'/'without side effect' diagnostic for a standalone `new X();` statement exists anywhere in src/checker/. phpstan-rs does check that `new` on an abstract class fails (src/checker/expr.rs:881) but does not flag a bare-statement constructor-with-no-side-effect as a discarded-result diagnostic.

methods-keywords-debug-pure.name: CallToMethodStatementWithNoDiscardRule
methods-keywords-debug-pure.description: A Rule<Stmt\Expression> (level 0, PHP 8.5+ only) reporting 'method.resultDiscarded' when a bare method-call statement's return value is thrown away but the method (or, since 8.5, a first-class-callable/pipe chain ending in one) is marked mustUseReturnValue() (via the #[\NoDiscard] attribute or PHPStan's own stub annotations), and conversely 'method.inVoidCast' when such a method's result is wrapped in a (void) cast unnecessarily because it actually allows discarding.
methods-keywords-debug-pure.notes: No mustUseReturnValue/#[NoDiscard]/resultDiscarded/inVoidCast concept exists anywhere in src/. This depends on both PHP 8.5's #[\NoDiscard] attribute (attribute-driven method metadata) and PHPStan's own stub-based must-use annotations, neither of which phpstan-rs's registry/docblock handling currently models - a real gap, not merely a stylistic one, but a substantial standalone feature to add.

methods-keywords-debug-pure.name: CallToMethodStatementWithoutSideEffectsRule
methods-keywords-debug-pure.description: A Rule (level 4) on NoopExpressionNode: flags `$obj->method();` used as a standalone statement when the method has no @-asserts and doesn't return an explicit never, reporting 'Call to method X::Y() on a separate line has no effect.'
methods-keywords-debug-pure.notes: phpstan-rs has no notion of a statement-level 'no side effects' / dead-statement rule at all; grepped src/checker/*.rs for 'has no effect'/'noop'/side-effect analysis and found none. Method calls are only checked for existence/arity/argument-type, never for being pointless when discarded.

methods-keywords-debug-pure.name: CallToStaticMethodStatementWithNoDiscardRule
methods-keywords-debug-pure.description: A Rule (level 0) on Node\Stmt\Expression: on PHP 8.5+, flags a standalone static-method call whose method reflection says mustUseReturnValue() (the #[NoDiscard] attribute) as 'discards return value' (non-ignorable), or the inverse mismatch inside a (void) cast.
methods-keywords-debug-pure.notes: Depends on parsing/modeling the PHP 8.5 #[NoDiscard] attribute and a PhpVersion::supportsNoDiscardAttribute() gate. phpstan-rs's lexer skips all attributes wholesale (src/lexer.rs, 'Attribute like #[Foo(...)] - skip to matching ]') with no attribute-argument modeling, and the project targets no specific bleeding-edge PHP-version feature gating of this kind, so there is no attribute data to check mustUseReturnValue against. Classified not_applicable given the total absence of any attribute-semantics layer to hang this on (distinct from the sibling side-effect rules below, which are just plain unimplemented dead-code detection).

methods-keywords-debug-pure.name: CallToStaticMethodStatementWithoutSideEffectsRule
methods-keywords-debug-pure.description: A Rule (level 4) on NoopExpressionNode: flags `Foo::bar();` used as a standalone statement (excluding constructor-named factory methods) when the static method has no @-asserts and isn't explicitly never-returning, as 'has no effect'.
methods-keywords-debug-pure.notes: Same gap as CallToMethodStatementWithoutSideEffectsRule - no dead/no-effect-statement analysis exists anywhere in src/checker/*.rs.

methods-keywords-debug-pure.name: ConsistentConstructorDeclarationRule
methods-keywords-debug-pure.description: A Rule (level 0) on InClassMethodNode: for a non-final class whose ClassReflection has hasConsistentConstructor() (the @consistent-constructor PHPDoc tag), flags a private __construct as 'cannot be enforced as consistent for child classes.'
methods-keywords-debug-pure.notes: Grepped for 'consistent-constructor'/'ConsistentConstructor' across src/ - zero hits. phpstan-rs's docblock.rs does not parse @consistent-constructor at all, so neither this rule nor the class-reflection flag it depends on exist.

methods-keywords-debug-pure.name: ConsistentConstructorRule
methods-keywords-debug-pure.description: A Rule (level 0) on InClassMethodNode: when a class's __construct overrides a parent that itself carries @consistent-constructor, delegates to MethodParameterComparisonHelper::compare() and MethodVisibilityComparisonHelper::compare() to enforce the child constructor matches the parent's signature/visibility exactly.
methods-keywords-debug-pure.notes: Depends entirely on the @consistent-constructor tag (missing, see ConsistentConstructorDeclarationRule) plus MethodVisibilityComparisonHelper (also missing below); check_method_overrides() in src/checker/oop.rs explicitly skips __construct entirely ('Real PHP deliberately exempts constructors from override-compatibility checking ... so this runs before that exemption'), the opposite of what this rule needs for the consistent-constructor case.

methods-keywords-debug-pure.name: ConstructorReturnTypeRule
methods-keywords-debug-pure.description: A Rule (level 0) on InClassMethodNode: flags a __construct (or a trait's original __construct) that declares any native return type at all, as a non-ignorable 'has a return type' error.
methods-keywords-debug-pure.notes: Grepped src/checker/oop.rs and stmt.rs for any __construct + return-type check - none found. check_method_overrides() skips __construct outright and never separately validates that a constructor declares no return type.

methods-keywords-debug-pure.name: ExistingClassesInTypehintsRule
methods-keywords-debug-pure.description: A Rule (level 0) on InClassMethodNode: delegates to the shared FunctionDefinitionCheck::checkClassMethod() to validate every parameter/return typehint on a method references an existing class, that union types aren't used pre-8.0, that @template types are referenced in a parameter, that native types are resolvable, that @phpstan-self-out is valid, and that #[NoDiscard] isn't misused.
methods-keywords-debug-pure.notes: phpstan-rs validates class existence only at instantiation sites ('new Foo()' -> 'instantiated class X not found', expr.rs ~900) and at method-call/static-call sites via undefined-method checks; it never separately validates that a method's declared parameter/return typehints reference existing classes (resolve_type_hint in src/checker/resolve.rs just resolves names via NameContext, with no existence check). The union-types-pre-8.0, template-not-referenced-in-param, and NoDiscard-target-validity sub-checks have no equivalent at all since the project doesn't model PHP-version gating for those features or attributes.

methods-keywords-debug-pure.name: FinalPrivateMethodRule
methods-keywords-debug-pure.description: A Rule (level 0) on InClassMethodNode: on PHP versions that warn about it, flags a method that is both final and private (excluding __construct) as pointless since it can never be overridden.
methods-keywords-debug-pure.notes: check_method_overrides() and the rest of src/checker/oop.rs only track final-ness for the 'cannot override a final ancestor method' check (find_final_ancestor_method); there is no check that combines a method's own final+private modifiers to flag it as meaningless.

methods-keywords-debug-pure.name: IncompatibleDefaultParameterTypeRule
methods-keywords-debug-pure.description: A Rule (level 2) on InClassMethodNode: for every parameter with a default value, checks the default value's type is accepted by the parameter's (template-bound-resolved) declared type, reporting 'Default value of the parameter ... is incompatible with type ...' otherwise.
methods-keywords-debug-pure.notes: Grepped src/checker/*.rs for any parameter-default-vs-declared-type comparison; none exists. Default values are only used to infer a variable's type when no argument is passed (e.g. stmt.rs 'let ty = default...'), never checked for compatibility against the parameter's own declared type.

methods-keywords-debug-pure.name: MethodAttributesRule
methods-keywords-debug-pure.description: A Rule (level 0) on InClassMethodNode: delegates to the shared AttributesCheck::check() to validate every #[...] attribute on a method (attribute class exists, is itself #[Attribute]-marked, targets TARGET_METHOD, constructor args type-check, etc).
methods-keywords-debug-pure.notes: phpstan-rs's lexer (src/lexer.rs) skips essentially all PHP attributes wholesale as unstructured token spans (only a couple of stub-only attributes get special-cased skip handling for internal purposes) - there is no attrGroups AST representation, no attribute-class reflection, and no AttributesCheck-equivalent anywhere. Since attributes carry no semantic model in this project at all (a deliberate architectural scope cut, not a partial rule), there is nothing for a method-level attribute-validation rule to attach to.

methods-keywords-debug-pure.name: MethodCallCheck
methods-keywords-debug-pure.description: A shared Check (not itself a Rule) invoked by MethodCallRule/MethodCallableRule: given a receiver expression and method name, resolves the receiver's type, reports 'Cannot call method on <type>' for non-object/class-string receivers, falls back through parent-class private-method detection and method_exists()-narrowing before reporting 'Call to an undefined method', and for a found method reports private/protected-visibility violations and (if configured) method-name-case mismatches.
methods-keywords-debug-pure.notes: Undefined-method detection (member_confirmed_missing against registry.lookup_method, with __call as an escape hatch) is implemented and reused for both a plain `->method()` call and a `...->method(...)` first-class-callable reference. Missing: the 'Cannot call method on <non-object type>' report for calling a method on a scalar/class-string receiver, the private/protected access-from-outside-the-declaring-class check (canCallMethod-equivalent - grepped registry.rs/expr.rs for any is_private/Visibility-based call-site gating, none found), the parent-class-private-method special case, the method_exists()-narrowing escape hatch, and the checkFunctionNameCase mismatch report.

methods-keywords-debug-pure.name: MethodCallWithPossiblyRenamedNamedArgumentRule
methods-keywords-debug-pure.description: A Rule (level 0) on CollectedDataNode: cross-references two Collectors (calls using a named argument against a prototype method, and overriding methods that rename a parameter) to flag call sites that pass `paramName: ...` to a prototype method whose actual overriding implementation renamed that parameter.
methods-keywords-debug-pure.notes: Requires PHPStan's Collector infrastructure (cross-file data aggregation processed after all files are analysed); grepped src/ for 'Collector'/'CollectedData' - phpstan-rs has no such architecture at all, it's a single-pass per-file/per-project checker with no collector-then-aggregate phase. Named arguments themselves are parsed and matched by name during ordinary argument checking, but the specific override-renamed-parameter cross-check has no equivalent.

methods-keywords-debug-pure.name: MethodCallableRule
methods-keywords-debug-pure.description: A Rule (level 0) on MethodCallableNode: rejects first-class-callable syntax (`$obj->method(...)`) outright on PHP < 8.1, otherwise delegates existence/visibility checking to MethodCallCheck::check().
methods-keywords-debug-pure.notes: The PHP-8.1-gating half is not_applicable-in-spirit (the project doesn't model a configurable target PHP version cutting off language syntax - `...` first-class-callable syntax is simply always accepted since it's what's being parsed).
