The existence-check delegation is implemented, reusing the same undefined-method/`__call`-fallback logic as MethodCallCheck; it inherits that logic's gaps (no visibility/name-case checks, see MethodCallCheck above).

methods-keywords-debug-pure.name: MethodParameterComparisonHelper
methods-keywords-debug-pure.description: A shared helper used by ConsistentConstructorRule (and OverridingMethodRule, outside this chunk): compares an overriding method's parameter list against its prototype's - missing parameters, named-argument renames (emitted to a Collector), by-reference mismatches, variadic mismatches (including PHP-version-gated 'fewer variadic params' relaxation), optional-vs-required mismatches, and native-type contravariance/equality (version-gated between exact-match and full contravariance).
methods-keywords-debug-pure.notes: check_method_overrides implements the core native-parameter-type contravariance check (is_assignable(ancestor_ty, own_ty), skipping Mixed on either side) with resolve_pseudo handling for self/static. Missing entirely: missing-parameter detection, by-reference mismatch, variadic mismatch, optional/required mismatch, and named-argument-rename Collector emission (no Collector infra exists, see MethodCallWithPossiblyRenamedNamedArgumentRule). No ignorable/nonIgnorable distinction either since diagnostics here have no identifier/ignorability model.

methods-keywords-debug-pure.name: MethodPrototypeFinder
methods-keywords-debug-pure.description: A shared helper (used by OverridingMethodRule, outside this chunk, and implicitly needed by the constructor/signature rules here): given a class and method name, finds the correct ancestor prototype to validate against - checking immediate interfaces first, then abstract trait methods (PHP-version gated), then the parent class (with special-casing for constructors coming from an abstract prototype) - returning both a 'signature prototype' and a separate 'inheritance prototype' plus a visibility-respect flag.
methods-keywords-debug-pure.notes: lookup_ancestor_method_with_owner is a much simpler single-lookup walk (own extends+implements list, first hit wins) with no interface-first-priority ordering, no trait-abstract-method special case, no constructor-declaring-class abstract-prototype special case, and no separate signature-vs-inheritance-prototype distinction or visibility-respect flag - it services check_method_overrides's simpler combined check rather than mirroring this helper's precise algorithm.

methods-keywords-debug-pure.name: MethodSignatureRule
methods-keywords-debug-pure.description: A Rule (level 0, invoked internally by OverridingMethodRule, not auto-tagged) on InClassMethodNode: for every non-constructor, non-private overriding method, walks all parent-method prototypes and reports impure-overrides-pure / impure-overrides-pure-unless-callable-impure, return-type covariance violations (with static-type transformation per declaring class, and special-cased tips when the overridden method is itself Rule::processNode), and parameter-type contravariance violations via checkParameterTypeCompatibility.
methods-keywords-debug-pure.notes: check_method_overrides implements the core native return-type-compatibility check (is_assignable, with a documented static-covariance escape hatch via ancestor_return_uses_static) and the parameter narrowing check described under MethodParameterComparisonHelper above, in a single combined function rather than mirroring this rule's separate return/parameter helper methods. Missing: any purity (@pure/@pure-unless-callable-is-impure) tracking or the impure-overrides-pure diagnostics (docblock.rs was not found to parse @pure at all), the reportMaybes/TrinaryLogic-maybe distinction (checks here are binary yes/no via is_assignable, no 'maybe' tier), and the Rule::processNode-specific tip messages (not relevant to phpstan-rs's own domain anyway).

methods-keywords-debug-pure.name: MethodVisibilityComparisonHelper
methods-keywords-debug-pure.description: A shared helper (used by ConsistentConstructorRule here, and OverridingMethodRule elsewhere): flags an overriding method that narrows visibility relative to its prototype - private/protected overriding public, or private overriding protected - as a non-ignorable 'should also be public'/'should be protected or public' error.
methods-keywords-debug-pure.notes: check_method_overrides() in src/checker/oop.rs never inspects visibility modifiers at all when comparing an overriding method to its ancestor - only parameter types and return types are compared. Grepped oop.rs/registry.rs for any visibility-narrowing-on-override check; none exists.

methods-keywords-debug-pure.name: MethodVisibilityInInterfaceRule
methods-keywords-debug-pure.description: A Rule (level 0) on InClassMethodNode: flags any non-public method declared directly inside an interface as a non-ignorable 'cannot use non-public visibility in interface' error.
methods-keywords-debug-pure.notes: Grepped src/checker/oop.rs for any interface + visibility combination check; none exists. Note this is largely a belt-and-suspenders check in real PHPStan since real PHP itself already rejects non-public interface methods at parse/compile time, so the practical value of adding it is low, but it is still a genuine, currently-missing 1:1 rule.

methods-keywords-debug-pure.name: MissingMagicSerializationMethodsRule
methods-keywords-debug-pure.description: Level-0 InClassNode rule: on PHP versions where Serializable requires magic methods, flags a non-abstract, non-interface, non-enum class implementing Serializable that is missing __serialize() and/or __unserialize(), emitting one class.serializable diagnostic per missing method.
methods-keywords-debug-pure.notes: phpstan-rs has no notion of the built-in Serializable interface at all (grep for 'Serializable' only hits an unrelated parser test string), no PhpVersion-gated behavior, and check_class_completeness (oop.rs) only checks abstract-method completeness, not magic-method presence for a specific built-in interface. No equivalent logic anywhere in src/.

methods-keywords-debug-pure.name: MissingMethodImplementationRule
methods-keywords-debug-pure.description: Level-0 InClassNode rule: a non-abstract, non-interface class containing an inherited abstract method (from a parent class, an interface, or a trait) that it doesn't implement is a fatal-error-shaped bug; reports method.abstract, with a special exemption when a non-abstract built-in ancestor class already provides the interface method at runtime.
methods-keywords-debug-pure.notes: Core behavior (concrete class must implement every abstract method inherited from parent/interface/trait, exempting abstract classes/interfaces/enums-as-abstract) is implemented, matching Finding 45's own doc comment. The built-in-ancestor exemption (isProvidedByBuiltinAncestor, e.g. IntlBreakIterator+IteratorAggregate) has no counterpart since phpstan-rs has no notion of PHP built-in classes with version-gated stub abstractness; low practical impact for a from-scratch project without stub reflection of built-ins.

methods-keywords-debug-pure.name: MissingMethodParameterTypehintRule
methods-keywords-debug-pure.description: Level-6 InClassMethodNode rule delegating to MissingTypehintCheck: flags method parameters (and @param-closure-this / @param-out tags) typed implicit mixed, iterable missing its value type, non-generic use of a generic class, or a callable with no signature.
methods-keywords-debug-pure.notes: No 'missingType.parameter'/'missingType.iterableValue'/'missingType.generics'/'missingType.callable' identifiers or equivalent MissingTypehintCheck-style logic exist anywhere in src/. phpstan-rs has no rule-level concept (level 6 'require typehints' strictness) at all - its checker focuses on correctness bugs (unknown symbols, arg/return mismatches) rather than typehint-completeness style rules. Architecturally sensible to add but currently absent.

methods-keywords-debug-pure.name: MissingMethodReturnTypehintRule
methods-keywords-debug-pure.description: Level-6 InClassMethodNode rule delegating to MissingTypehintCheck: flags a method whose return type is implicit mixed, or whose return type has an iterable-missing-value-type / non-generic-generic-class / no-signature-callable problem.
methods-keywords-debug-pure.notes: Same gap as MissingMethodParameterTypehintRule - no missingType.return / missingType.iterableValue / missingType.generics / missingType.callable checks exist for return types anywhere in src/checker or src/docblock.rs.

methods-keywords-debug-pure.name: MissingMethodSelfOutTypeRule
methods-keywords-debug-pure.description: Level-6 InClassMethodNode rule: same MissingTypehintCheck battery (iterable value type / generic-class-not-parameterized / callable-missing-signature) applied to a method's @phpstan-self-out PHPDoc type, when present.
methods-keywords-debug-pure.notes: phpstan-rs's docblock.rs has no @phpstan-self-out / @param-out parsing or self-out-type modeling at all (grep for self-out/selfOut/self_out is empty), so there is no self-out type for this check to ever run against; the underlying feature (self-out types) is itself unimplemented, making this specific missing-typehint-on-self-out-type rule moot until self-out support exists. Noted as not_applicable for this rule specifically since it has no target to check without that prerequisite feature, though the prerequisite itself would be a 'missing' item elsewhere.

methods-keywords-debug-pure.name: NamedArgumentParameterMethodCallsCollector
methods-keywords-debug-pure.description: A Collector marker class (getNodeType/processNode both throw ShouldNotHappenException) whose collected-data shape (class, method, arg-name, line) is populated elsewhere via the collector-emission mechanism and consumed by MethodCallWithPossiblyRenamedNamedArgumentRule to detect named-argument call sites that might break if an overriding method renamed a parameter.
methods-keywords-debug-pure.notes: The class itself carries no logic (pure DI/collector-registration marker), but the feature it feeds - detecting named-argument method calls whose argument name might not match a renamed parameter in an overriding/overridden method - has no counterpart in phpstan-rs. grep for named_arg/NamedArg/renamed param finds nothing in src/. This is architecturally buildable (registry.rs already models cross-class method info) but not implemented, so classified missing rather than not_applicable.

methods-keywords-debug-pure.name: NullsafeMethodCallRule
methods-keywords-debug-pure.description: Level-4 rule on NullsafeMethodCallExpressionNode: flags `$x?->method()` when the statically-known type of $x can never be null, reporting nullsafe.neverNull ('Use -> instead'), with treatPhpDocTypesAsCertain-aware type selection and an optional tip when native vs PHPDoc types disagree.
methods-keywords-debug-pure.notes: phpstan-rs parses and evaluates nullsafe method calls (ExprKind::MethodCall's nullsafe flag, expr.rs lines ~382-526 and ~1644-1685) and uses the nullsafe flag to shape the resulting type (nulling out on the nullsafe branch), but it never reports a diagnostic for the redundant case of nullsafe-on-a-non-nullable receiver. No 'nullsafe.neverNull' or similar message exists in src/.

methods-keywords-debug-pure.name: OverridingMethodRenamesParameterCollector
methods-keywords-debug-pure.description: A Collector marker class (throws ShouldNotHappenException from both interface methods) whose collected-data shape (class, method, declaring-class, old-name, new-name) is populated by OverridingMethodRule's parameter-comparison path and consumed together with NamedArgumentParameterMethodCallsCollector by MethodCallWithPossiblyRenamedNamedArgumentRule.
methods-keywords-debug-pure.notes: Same situation as its sibling collector: no logic of its own, but check_method_overrides in oop.rs does not track parameter renames at all (it only compares parameter types positionally via MethodParameterComparisonHelper-equivalent logic, never names), so there is no data source in phpstan-rs to feed a rename-detection rule even if one existed.

methods-keywords-debug-pure.name: OverridingMethodRule
methods-keywords-debug-pure.description: Level-0 InClassMethodNode rule: the central override-compatibility check - final-method override, missing #[Override] attribute, static/non-static mismatch, abstract-overriding-non-abstract, visibility narrowing, tentative-return-type covariance (PHP 8.1's #[ReturnTypeWillChange] dance), and full parameter/return-type Liskov covariance/contravariance via MethodParameterComparisonHelper, then chains into MethodSignatureRule for PHPDoc-level signature checks when checkPhpDocMethodSignatures is on.
methods-keywords-debug-pure.our_location: src/checker/oop.rs:check_method_overrides (~line 177), plus find_final_ancestor_method / lookup_ancestor_method_with_owner in registry.rs
methods-keywords-debug-pure.notes: Implements: final-method-override detection (including __construct's parent), per-position parameter-narrowing check via is_assignable with self/static pseudo-type resolution, and native return-type covariance/compatibility check (with a static-covariance escape hatch). Missing: static vs non-static override mismatch, abstract-overriding-non-abstract for regular (non-constructor) methods, visibility-narrowing check (MethodVisibilityComparisonHelper), #[Override] attribute checks entirely (missingOverride / method.override) since phpstan-rs's parser has no attribute AST support at all, tentative-return-type/#[ReturnTypeWillChange] handling, and any PHPDoc-signature-level (checkPhpDocMethodSignatures) pass.

methods-keywords-debug-pure.name: ParentMethodHelper
methods-keywords-debug-pure.description: DI service helper: given a method name and a ClassReflection, collects every non-private parent-class method, every interface method, and every abstract trait method of that name that the class would be overriding, used by rules like MethodOverridingRule/consumers needing 'what am I overriding'.
methods-keywords-debug-pure.notes: phpstan-rs's registry has equivalent single-purpose ancestor-lookup helpers (used by check_method_overrides and check_class_completeness) rather than one general-purpose 'collect all overridden-method candidates across parent+interfaces+traits' helper returning a list; functionally covers the parent-class and interface cases used by check_method_overrides, but there's no direct trait-abstract-method variant analogous to ParentMethodHelper's trait loop (traits are folded into class members before the checker runs, per registry construction, rather than walked separately here).

methods-keywords-debug-pure.name: ReturnTypeRule
methods-keywords-debug-pure.description: Level-3 rule on Stmt\Return_ inside a method: delegates to FunctionReturnTypeCheck to verify a return statement's expression (or lack of one) is compatible with the method's declared return type, plus a PHPStan-dogfooding special case rewriting the specific 'Rule::processNode should return list<IdentifierRuleError>' message.
methods-keywords-debug-pure.our_location: src/checker/stmt.rs:check_stmt, StmtKind::Return(Some(e)) and StmtKind::Return(None) arms (~lines 82-129), report level 3
methods-keywords-debug-pure.notes: Core behavior - flagging `return $expr;` whose type isn't assignable to the declared return type, and flagging a bare `return;` when the declared type is non-void/non-mixed and doesn't accept null - is implemented generically for both functions and methods (shared check_block/check_stmt path), matching FunctionReturnTypeCheck's two main messages and even reusing rule-level 3. Does not special-case generators (though current_function_is_generator suppresses the bare-return check, mirroring FunctionReturnTypeCheck's generator awareness) with the same granularity as PHP-side isGenerator handling for expression returns, has no explicit 'declared never but returned a value' message (relies on is_assignable rejecting everything against Never generically), and the PHPStan-Rule-self-dogfooding special case is not applicable to a Rust rewrite.

methods-keywords-debug-pure.name: StaticMethodCallCheck
methods-keywords-debug-pure.description: DI service used by both StaticCall-expression rules and StaticMethodCallableRule: full static-method-call validation - self/static/parent/class-name resolution and outOfClass/noParent errors, unknown-class check, non-object callee check, undefined-static-method check (with __callStatic exemption), instance-method-called-statically check (with a DOMDocument::loadHTML runtime exemption), visibility (canCallMethod) check, abstract-method-call check, and call-case-mismatch check.
methods-keywords-debug-pure.our_location: src/checker/expr.rs ExprKind::StaticCall handling (~lines 923-1010), resolve_static_class_name in checker/resolve.rs
methods-keywords-debug-pure.notes: Implements: class/method resolution via resolve_static_class_name, existence check for the static method (with a Closure::bind special case) and undefined-static-method reporting with __callStatic exemption, argument checking via check_args. Missing: self/static/parent used outside a class scope (outOfClass.* identifiers), 'class does not extend any class' when parent:: has no parent, non-object callee ('staticMethod.nonObject'), calling a genuinely non-static instance method via Class::method() ('method.staticCall', including the DOMDocument::loadHTML exemption), visibility checks for private/protected static calls ('staticMethod.private'/'protected' - no canCallMethod-equivalent exists for methods at all in phpstan-rs, grep confirms no is_private/is_protected method-visibility checker), abstract-method-call check ('staticMethod.callToAbstract'), and call-name case-mismatch checking.

methods-keywords-debug-pure.name: StaticMethodCallableRule
methods-keywords-debug-pure.description: Level-0 rule on StaticMethodCallableNode (first-class-callable syntax Class::method(...)): errors if the running PHP version doesn't support first-class callables, then delegates existence/visibility/etc. checking to StaticMethodCallCheck::check().
methods-keywords-debug-pure.notes: The existence check for `Class::method(...)` first-class-callable syntax (undefined static method, with __callStatic exemption) is implemented as one arm of the shared FirstClassCallable handling, mirroring StaticMethodCallCheck's core existence logic. Missing the PHP-8.1-version-gate error ('callable.notSupported' - phpstan-rs has no PhpVersion/target-version concept at all) and all the other StaticMethodCallCheck sub-checks noted above (visibility, abstract, non-static-called-statically, case mismatch) that a real Class::method(...) callable expression would also need.

methods-keywords-debug-pure.name: FunctionPurityCheck
methods-keywords-debug-pure.description: DI service shared by PureFunctionRule/PureMethodRule: given a function/method's declared purity (@phpstan-pure / @phpstan-impure / @phpstan-pure-unless-callable-is-impure), its impure/throw points and body statements, reports parameter-by-reference-on-pure, pure-returning-void, impure-points-found-inside-a-declared-pure-function/method, impure-marked-but-has-no-side-effects, and void-return-with-no-side-effects (dead code) diagnostics.
methods-keywords-debug-pure.notes: phpstan-rs has no notion of function/method purity annotations, impure points, or side-effect tracking at all - grep for pure/@phpstan-pure/is_pure across src/ turns up nothing (the few 'pure' string hits are unrelated comments about 'pure noise', 'pure definition site', etc.). This entire PHPDoc-purity-annotation feature area is unimplemented.

methods-keywords-debug-pure.name: PureFunctionRule
methods-keywords-debug-pure.description: Level-2 rule on FunctionReturnStatementsNode: feeds a top-level function's reflection, parameters, return type, collected impure points, throw points, and statements into FunctionPurityCheck::check().
methods-keywords-debug-pure.notes: No equivalent - depends entirely on the unimplemented FunctionPurityCheck/@phpstan-pure infrastructure; no impure-point tracking exists in phpstan-rs's checker (control_flow.rs/calls.rs have no notion of side-effect/impurity classification of calls).

properties-enum-whitespace.name: EnumCaseOutsideEnumRule

properties-enum-whitespace.name: AccessPrivatePropertyThroughStaticRule

properties-enum-whitespace.name: AccessPropertiesCheck

properties-enum-whitespace.name: AccessPropertiesInAssignRule

properties-enum-whitespace.name: AccessPropertiesRule

properties-enum-whitespace.name: AccessStaticPropertiesCheck

properties-enum-whitespace.name: AccessStaticPropertiesInAssignRule

properties-enum-whitespace.name: AccessStaticPropertiesRule

properties-enum-whitespace.notes: Same coverage/gaps as AccessStaticPropertiesCheck above - undefined-static-property detection only.

properties-enum-whitespace.name: DefaultValueTypesAssignedToPropertiesRule

properties-enum-whitespace.name: ExistingClassesInPropertiesRule

properties-enum-whitespace.name: ExistingClassesInPropertyHookTypehintsRule

properties-enum-whitespace.name: FoundPropertyReflection

properties-enum-whitespace.name: GetNonVirtualPropertyHookReadRule

properties-enum-whitespace.notes: Property hook bodies are not semantically analyzed at all in phpstan-rs (see ExistingClassesInPropertyHookTypehintsRule entry); there is no tracking of property reads inside hook bodies, so this dataflow-style check has no counterpart.

properties-enum-whitespace.name: InvalidCallablePropertyTypeRule

Whether the Rust parser even rejects/accepts `callable` as a property type hint at parse time was not separately verified, but no semantic diagnostic exists either way.

properties-enum-whitespace.name: MissingPropertyTypehintRule
properties-enum-whitespace.description: Level-6 rule on the virtual ClassPropertyNode that flags a non-promoted property with an implicit `mixed` (untyped) declaration ('missingType.property'), plus delegating to MissingTypehintCheck for iterable-missing-value-type, generic-class-missing-type-args, and callable-missing-signature diagnostics on the property's type.
properties-enum-whitespace.notes: phpstan-rs has no notion of PHPStan's rule levels and no MissingTypehintCheck equivalent - a repo-wide grep for 'has no type specified'/'no value type specified'/'does not specify its types' finds nothing; untyped properties, bare iterable/array, and non-generic uses of generic classes are not flagged.

properties-enum-whitespace.name: MissingReadOnlyByPhpDocPropertyAssignRule
properties-enum-whitespace.description: Rule on the virtual ClassPropertiesNode mirroring MissingReadOnlyPropertyAssignRule but for properties marked readonly only via the `@readonly` PHPDoc tag (not the native keyword): flags never-initialized, prematurely-accessed, and doubly-assigned such properties.

properties-enum-whitespace.name: MissingReadOnlyPropertyAssignRule
properties-enum-whitespace.description: Rule on the virtual ClassPropertiesNode that uses ClassPropertiesNode::getUninitializedProperties() dataflow to flag readonly properties never assigned by end of constructor ('property.uninitializedReadonly'), premature reads before assignment, and a second/'additional' assignment to an already-initialized readonly property ('assign.readOnlyProperty').
properties-enum-whitespace.notes: phpstan-rs takes a different, blunter approach: any write to a `readonly` property (PropertySig.is_readonly) is flagged unless it occurs textually inside the declaring class's own `__construct` method, per the comment at assignment.rs:250-259. This catches most real readonly-violation cases but does not implement PHPStan's actual dataflow: it never detects a readonly property that falls off the end of the constructor without ever being assigned ('uninitialized'), and does not distinguish a legitimate single constructor-assignment from a true double-assignment within the same constructor.

properties-enum-whitespace.name: NullsafePropertyFetchRule
properties-enum-whitespace.description: Rule on `?->` property fetches: emits 'nullsafe.neverNull' when the type the nullsafe operator is applied to is never null (so `?->` is pointless and `->` should be used), respecting treatPhpDocTypesAsCertain and adding a tip.
properties-enum-whitespace.notes: The Rust checker only USES the nullsafe flag to widen the inferred type with Null (`if *nullsafe && result != Type::Mixed { union_types(result, Type::Null) }`); it never checks whether the base type was already non-nullable and never emits a diagnostic for redundant `?->`. No 'nullsafe.neverNull'-equivalent report exists anywhere in src/checker.

properties-enum-whitespace.name: OverridingPropertyRule
properties-enum-whitespace.description: Large rule (477 lines) checking a property against a same-named property it overrides from a parent class/interface: static/non-static mismatch, readonly/readwrite mismatch, hook readability/writability mismatch, abstract-hook consistency, visibility widening rules, final-property overriding, #[Override] attribute presence/misuse, native-type equality (with hook-based contra/covariance), and PHPDoc readable-type covariance (with reportMaybes-gated maybe-covariant messages).
properties-enum-whitespace.our_location: src/checker/oop.rs (check_method_overrides, lines 177+, is the only override-compatibility check and covers methods only)
properties-enum-whitespace.notes: phpstan-rs's PropertySig (src/registry/class_info.rs) tracks only ty/is_static/is_readonly/set_ty with no visibility, no is_final, no hook readability metadata, so none of these override checks (visibility, static, readonly, final, native-type variance, PHPDoc-type variance, #[Override] attribute) exist for properties. No attribute parsing exists at all (see PropertyAttributesRule notes), so the #[Override]-on-property half is doubly out of reach.

properties-enum-whitespace.name: PropertiesInInterfaceRule
properties-enum-whitespace.description: Rule restricting properties declared directly in an interface: only allowed at all on PHP 8.4+, must be hooked, must be public, non-readonly, non-static, non-abstract, non-final, hooks must not themselves be final, and hooks must have no body (interface hooks are always abstract).
properties-enum-whitespace.our_location: src/checker/oop.rs (no interface-specific property validation); src/registry.rs classes ingestion
properties-enum-whitespace.notes: The parser accepts property declarations inside any class-like container (class/interface/trait/enum) with no kind-specific restriction, and no checker pass inspects ClassKind::Interface plus its properties. PropertyDecl also has no is_final/is_abstract fields, so even a partial version of this check has no data to work from.

properties-enum-whitespace.name: PropertyAssignRefRule
properties-enum-whitespace.description: On PHP 8.4+ (asymmetric visibility support), flags `$x->prop =& $y` when the property found via PropertyReflectionFinder is not writable from the current scope (private(set)/protected(set)/private/protected), via 'property.assignByRef'.
properties-enum-whitespace.notes: phpstan-rs has no `AssignRef` / `=&` expression node at all in src/ast.rs and no parsing of `=&` reference assignment in src/parser/expr.rs (only Foreach's by_ref, Param's by_ref and ClosureUse's by_ref exist) - reference-assignment to a property is not represented, let alone checked. Asymmetric visibility (private(set)/protected(set)) is recognized only as parser syntax (src/parser/classes.rs, tokens.rs) and dropped - PropertyDecl/PropertySig carry no such field, so there's no notion of 'writable from this scope' either.

properties-enum-whitespace.name: PropertyAttributesRule
properties-enum-whitespace.description: Validates a property's PHP attributes: flags #[Override] on a property before PHP 8.5, and (for non-promoted properties) runs the generic AttributesCheck against TARGET_PROPERTY (attribute class exists, is not abstract/interface, respects #[Attribute] target flags, constructor args are valid, etc.).
properties-enum-whitespace.notes: PHP attributes (`#[...]`) are not parsed into the AST anywhere in phpstan-rs (no AttributeGroup/Attribute node type in src/ast.rs, no attribute-target checking machinery like PHPStan's AttributesCheck). Since attributes are a whole unimplemented syntax feature rather than a single rule, and none of the other 17 files in this chunk exercise attributes either, this is treated as not_applicable for this incremental audit rather than 'missing' - closing the gap requires attribute parsing project-wide, not a property-rule-shaped fix.

properties-enum-whitespace.name: PropertyDescriptor
properties-enum-whitespace.description: Small helper service (not a Rule) that formats a human-readable description of a property for error messages, e.g. 'Property Foo::$bar' or 'Static property Foo::$bar', preferring the declaring class's display name when the fetch's static type matches it, else describing the fetched-on type.
properties-enum-whitespace.notes: phpstan-rs inlines an equivalent 'Class::$prop' format string at each property-diagnostic call site rather than having a shared describeProperty() helper; it does not add the 'Static property' prefix distinction, nor does it prefer the fetched-on type's description when the static type diverges from the declaring class. Functionally covers the common case but is duplicated ad hoc rather than centralized, and misses the static-property wording.

properties-enum-whitespace.name: PropertyHookAttributesRule
properties-enum-whitespace.description: Runs AttributesCheck (TARGET_METHOD) against a property hook's own attributes, and additionally rejects #[NoDiscard] specifically on property hooks via 'attribute.target'.
properties-enum-whitespace.notes: Same root cause as PropertyAttributesRule: no attribute parsing exists in phpstan-rs at all, and property hooks (src/ast.rs PropertyHooks) carry no attrGroups field to check even if attribute parsing existed. Treated as not_applicable for this file-level audit for the same reason as PropertyAttributesRule.

properties-enum-whitespace.name: PropertyInClassRule
properties-enum-whitespace.description: Validates a property declared in a regular class: final-property PHP-version gating, abstract properties must be hooked/have an abstract hook/be in an abstract class, private+abstract/private+final/private+final-hook conflicts, abstract+final conflict, hooked properties can't be readonly or static, static properties with asymmetric visibility need PHP 8.5+, virtual hooked properties can't have a default, and property hooks overall require PHP 8.4+.
properties-enum-whitespace.notes: PropertyDecl (src/ast.rs) has no is_final or is_abstract field, and PropertyHooks tracks only get/set bodies with no per-hook body-presence/abstractness distinction beyond `Option`. No checker pass walks PropertyDecl for any of these combinations; property hooks are parsed purely so the file doesn't fail to parse (per the ast.rs comment) and are otherwise inert.

properties-enum-whitespace.name: PropertyReflectionFinder
properties-enum-whitespace.description: Shared helper service (not a Rule) that resolves a PropertyFetch/StaticPropertyFetch AST node plus Scope into one or more FoundPropertyReflection objects, handling dynamic-name property fetches (e.g. `$obj->{$name}`) by enumerating constant-string possibilities and narrowing scope per-candidate.
properties-enum-whitespace.our_location: src/registry.rs lookup_property / lookup_property_with_owner (lines ~722-736); used from src/checker/assignment.rs check_property_assignment
properties-enum-whitespace.notes: phpstan-rs has an analogous lookup helper (`lookup_property_with_owner(class, prop)`) used at property-assignment sites, but it only accepts a statically-known property name straight from `ExprKind::PropertyAccess(base, prop, _)` - there is no DynamicPropertyAccess resolution against constant-string candidates (DynamicPropertyAccess is handled separately in expr.rs and just returns Mixed), no StaticPropertyFetch-name enumeration, and no FoundPropertyReflection-equivalent object carrying readable/writable type distinctly from the declared type outside of set_ty.

properties-enum-whitespace.name: ReadOnlyByPhpDocPropertyAssignRefRule
properties-enum-whitespace.description: Flags `$x->prop =& $y` (or `Class::$prop =& $y`) when the property is only @readonly by PHPDoc (not native `readonly`) and is otherwise writable from scope, via 'property.readOnlyByPhpDocAssignByRef'.
properties-enum-whitespace.notes: Depends on both `=&` reference-assignment parsing (absent, see PropertyAssignRefRule) and @readonly-by-PHPDoc tracking (absent, see ReadOnlyByPhpDocPropertyRule) - neither exists in phpstan-rs.

properties-enum-whitespace.name: ReadOnlyByPhpDocPropertyAssignRule

properties-enum-whitespace.notes: The existing Rust readonly-assignment check only understands the native `readonly` keyword (`prop_sig.is_readonly`) and applies one blanket rule (must be in the declaring class's own __construct); it doesn't know about @readonly-by-PHPDoc at all (no such tag is parsed anywhere in src/docblock.rs), doesn't special-case __unserialize, allowedPrivateMutation, or array-offset writes, and doesn't check 'assigned on $this' specifically.

properties-enum-whitespace.name: ReadOnlyByPhpDocPropertyRule
properties-enum-whitespace.description: Flags a property that is @readonly by PHPDoc (and not allowed-private-mutation) but not also native readonly, if it has a default value, via 'property.readOnlyByPhpDocDefaultValue'.
properties-enum-whitespace.notes: No @readonly PHPDoc tag parsing exists in src/docblock.rs, and PropertySig/PropertyDecl carry no is_readonly_by_phpdoc distinct from the native `readonly` keyword flag they do track.

properties-enum-whitespace.name: ReadOnlyPropertyAssignRefRule
properties-enum-whitespace.description: Flags `$x->prop =& $y` when the property is natively readonly and writable from scope, via 'property.readOnlyAssignByRef'.
properties-enum-whitespace.notes: Same root cause as PropertyAssignRefRule: no `=&` reference-assignment AST node or parsing exists in phpstan-rs, so this check has nothing to hang off of even though native readonly tracking itself exists (PropertySig.is_readonly).

properties-enum-whitespace.name: ReadOnlyPropertyAssignRule
properties-enum-whitespace.description: Enforces native readonly write rules: allowed outside the declaring class only for a non-private(set) property in a subclass on PHP 8.4+ (asymmetric visibility); otherwise must be inside the declaring class's own constructor/__unserialize/(PHP 8.5+) __clone on $this, with a further 'already assigned' check for double-initialization during clone-with reinitialization; else 'assigned outside of the constructor', with an array-offset-write exception.
properties-enum-whitespace.notes: phpstan-rs does implement the core idea (readonly property can only be written inside `self::__construct`) but it is a single blanket condition: `current_class == owner && current_method == "__construct"`. It has none of: the subclass/asymmetric-visibility exception, __unserialize/__clone recognition, 'not assigned on $this' vs 'assigned outside of declaring class' distinction, double-assignment-in-clone detection (assign.readOnlyProperty), or the array-access-offset-write exception. Any write from outside __construct (including from a legitimate subclass or __unserialize) is uniformly flagged, and any write from inside __construct is uniformly allowed regardless of whether it's actually on $this.

properties-enum-whitespace.name: ReadOnlyPropertyRule
properties-enum-whitespace.description: Validates a native readonly property declaration itself: readonly requires PHP 8.1+, must have a native type, cannot have a default value, and cannot be static.
properties-enum-whitespace.notes: No checker pass inspects PropertyDecl.is_readonly against type_hint presence, default presence, or is_static - phpstan-rs tracks is_readonly only to drive the write-site check in assignment.rs, never to validate the declaration site. No PHP-version gating exists anywhere in the project (there is no PhpVersion abstraction at all).

properties-enum-whitespace.name: ReadWritePropertiesExtension
properties-enum-whitespace.description: Pure `@api` extension interface (isAlwaysRead/isAlwaysWritten/isInitialized) that third-party PHPStan extensions implement to describe framework-magic properties (e.g. an ORM property that's 'always written' via reflection) so dead-code/uninitialized-property rules don't false-positive on them.
properties-enum-whitespace.notes: This is a DI-registered plugin/extension-point interface for third-party PHPStan extensions, not analysis logic itself. phpstan-rs has no plugin/extension system at all (no DI container, no extension tags), so there is no sensible Rust-rewrite equivalent to build; any actual behavior it enables would need to be hand-coded per-framework rather than pluggable, which is out of scope.

properties-enum-whitespace.name: ReadingWriteOnlyPropertiesRule
properties-enum-whitespace.description: Flags reading a property (PropertyFetch/StaticPropertyFetch) that is not readable, e.g. a PHP 8.4 hooked property with a `set` hook but no `get` hook (write-only), via 'property.writeOnly'; optionally restricted to $this-only fetches via checkThisOnly, and skips fetches that are themselves the target of an assignment.

No diagnostic for reading a write-only property exists anywhere in src/checker.

properties-enum-whitespace.name: SetNonVirtualPropertyHookAssignRule
properties-enum-whitespace.description: For a non-virtual property's `set` hook, verifies every non-abrupt-terminating execution path of the hook body actually assigns the underlying property storage (tracked via a synthetic PropertyInitializationExpr), else emits 'propertySetHook.noAssign' ('does not assign value to it' / 'does not always assign value to it').
properties-enum-whitespace.notes: Property hook bodies are parsed (PropertyHookBody::Block/Arrow in src/ast.rs) but, per the ast.rs comment, 'the hook bodies aren't type-checked' - no checker pass walks into a set-hook's statements at all, so there's no dataflow tracking of whether the backing store gets written, no execution-end/merge-scope machinery for hooks, and no virtual-property distinction to gate the check.

properties-enum-whitespace.name: SetPropertyHookParameterRule
properties-enum-whitespace.description: Rule on InPropertyHookNode (level 0): for a PHP 8.4 `set` property hook, checks the hook parameter's native type is present iff the property's native type is present and is contravariant with it (nonIgnorable propertySetHook.nativeParameterType), checks the phpdoc parameter type is contravariant with the property's readable type (propertySetHook.parameterType), and (if types differ) runs MissingTypehintCheck against the parameter type for missing iterable value types, missing generic class types, and missing callable signatures.
properties-enum-whitespace.our_location: src/registry/class_info.rs:592 property_hook_set_type(); consumed in src/checker/assignment.rs:270-276 check_property_assignment
properties-enum-whitespace.notes: phpstan-rs parses PHP 8.4 `set(Type $value)` hooks and captures the hook parameter's declared type as `PropertySignature::set_ty`, which is then used as the accepted type when checking `$this->prop = ...` writes elsewhere in the class (assignment.rs). But there is no dedicated check that validates the hook signature itself: no verification that the hook parameter's native type is contravariant with the property's native type, no native-type-presence-mismatch diagnostic, and no MissingTypehintCheck-style pass (missing iterable value type / missing generics / missing callable signature) over the hook parameter. So the underlying data (hook param type) exists and is used for a different purpose, but this rule's own diagnostics are not emitted.

properties-enum-whitespace.name: TypesAssignedToPropertiesRule
properties-enum-whitespace.description: Rule on PropertyAssignNode (level 3): for every property/static-property fetch resolved from an assignment's LHS, checks the assigned expression's type is accepted by the property's writable type (or, inside a matching property-hook body, its readable type), emitting assign.propertyType with a describes-property message (distinguishing static vs instance) and acceptsReasons tip.
properties-enum-whitespace.notes: Instance property writes (`$obj->prop = value` / `$this->prop = value`) are type-checked: the assigned expression's inferred type is checked against the property's declared type (using the property-hook set type when present) and a diagnostic is reported on mismatch, functionally covering the instance-property half of this rule. However, `ExprKind::StaticAccess` (static property writes, `Class::$prop = value`) is never routed through `check_property_assignment` (confirmed by grep: only `ExprKind::PropertyAccess` triggers it), so static property assignment type-checking is missing entirely. There is also no isWritable()/write-vs-read asymmetric-visibility distinction and no per-property-hook readable-type branching.

properties-enum-whitespace.name: UninitializedPropertyRule
properties-enum-whitespace.description: Rule on ClassPropertiesNode: for a class, finds properties with no default value that are never (or not always) initialized by every constructor (via ConstructorsHelper, handling parent constructors too) and reports property.uninitialized both for the declaration itself and for any place the property is read before being guaranteed initialized (premature access), skipping properties that are readonly (native or phpdoc).

This is a real class-level dataflow check (across all constructors plus reads) with no counterpart in phpstan-rs's per-expression checker.

properties-enum-whitespace.name: WritingToReadOnlyPropertiesRule
properties-enum-whitespace.description: Rule on PropertyAssignNode (level 0): for a property fetch resolved from an assignment (optionally restricted to $this-only fetches by config), checks scope->canWriteProperty (asymmetric-visibility aware) and then whether the property reflection reports itself writable; if not, reports assign.propertyReadOnly ('... is not writable.').
properties-enum-whitespace.our_location: src/checker/assignment.rs:250-268 check_property_assignment (readonly check inside the same function as the type check)
properties-enum-whitespace.notes: phpstan-rs flags writes to a `readonly` property outside the declaring class's own constructor ('X::$y is readonly and cannot be modified here'), covering the common real-world case (native readonly properties) including promoted-constructor-parameter exemption. It is a pragmatic, coarser version of PHPStan's rule: no asymmetric-visibility (canWriteProperty / private(set)) modeling, no checkThisOnly config knob, and (as with TypesAssignedToPropertiesRule) static property writes are never routed through this check at all since StaticAccess isn't handled in check_property_assignment.

properties-enum-whitespace.name: FileWhitespaceRule
properties-enum-whitespace.description: Rule on FileNode (level 0): flags a file beginning with a UTF-8 BOM InlineHTML node (whitespace.bom) and flags a file (or the last statement inside a top-level declare/namespace block) ending in a trailing-whitespace-only InlineHTML node after the closing `?>` (whitespace.fileEnd), both purely cosmetic/portability warnings about content leaking before headers are sent.
properties-enum-whitespace.notes: No BOM detection in the lexer (grep for BOM/0xEF/FEFF finds nothing) and no InlineHTML/trailing-whitespace-at-file-end diagnostic anywhere in src/. This is a narrow, purely lexical/textual check unrelated to type inference; phpstan-rs has no equivalent pass over raw file bytes or inline-HTML trailing nodes.

functions-generators.name: ArrayFilterRule
functions-generators.description: Level-5 Rule on FuncCall: for a single-arg array_filter() call, reports arrayFilter.empty (input array is empty), arrayFilter.same (element type contains no falsy values, so the call is a no-op) or arrayFilter.alwaysEmpty (element type is entirely falsy, result is always []), using isIterableAtLeastOnce()/falsey-supertype checks and honoring treatPhpDocTypesAsCertain with a tip.
functions-generators.notes: The Rust checker special-cases array_filter extensively for return-*type* precision (strips falsy/null elements, narrows via instanceof/null-check callback, preserves list-ness) using the same list/accessory-marker machinery PHPStan's own isList()/isIterableAtLeastOnce() rely on (src/types.rs AccessoryKind::ArrayList), but it never emits a diagnostic for an empty input array, an all-non-falsy input (no-op call) or an all-falsy input (always-empty result) - grep for arrayFilter.empty/same/alwaysEmpty found nothing. The type-precision machinery this rule would need already exists; only the diagnostic-emitting half is missing.

functions-generators.name: ArrayValuesRule
functions-generators.description: Level-5 Rule on FuncCall: for array_values() reports arrayValues.empty (empty input array, no effect) or arrayValues.list (input is already a list, call has no effect), honoring treatPhpDocTypesAsCertain with a tip.
functions-generators.notes: array_values() is special-cased for return-type precision (always re-sequences to Intersection[Array, AccessoryKind::ArrayList]), reusing the same list-ness tracking the PHP rule's isList() check needs, but no diagnostic is emitted for an already-list input or an empty input - grep for arrayValues.empty/list found nothing anywhere in src/.

functions-generators.name: ArrowFunctionAttributesRule
functions-generators.description: Level-0 Rule on InArrowFunctionNode delegating to AttributesCheck to validate PHP attributes attached to an arrow function (target = TARGET_FUNCTION, e.g. rejecting attributes that don't apply to functions, or unknown attribute classes).
functions-generators.notes: PHP attribute syntax (#[...]) is not represented in phpstan-rs's AST at all - the lexer (src/lexer.rs, around skip_stub_availability_attribute/skip_language_level_type_aware_attribute, line ~510-530) simply skips over #[...] groups as trivia during tokenization. With no attrGroups node ever surviving into the AST, there is no place an AttributesCheck-equivalent could run against a closure/arrow-fn/function/class node. A real, currently unimplemented feature, not an architectural non-goal.

functions-generators.name: ArrowFunctionReturnNullsafeByRefRule
functions-generators.description: Level-0 Rule on Expr\ArrowFunction: reports a non-ignorable 'Nullsafe cannot be returned by reference' error when a by-ref arrow function's body expression contains a nullsafe (?->) access, since PHP cannot return a nullsafe chain's result by reference.
functions-generators.notes: grep for NullsafeCheck/containsNullSafe/nullsafe.byRef style logic in src/ found nothing. ExprKind::ArrowFn handling in src/checker/expr.rs:1344-1380 checks body type against the declared return type but never inspects a by-ref flag against nullsafe usage in the body; this narrow byRef-arrow-function edge case is not implemented.

functions-generators.name: ArrowFunctionReturnTypeRule
functions-generators.description: Level-3 Rule on InArrowFunctionNode delegating to FunctionReturnTypeCheck::checkReturnType to compare the arrow function's implicit-return expression type against its declared/inferred return type, with generator-aware and never-type-aware special messages.
functions-generators.notes: The arrow function's body expression type is checked via check_expr and, when a native return type is present, compared with is_assignable against the resolved return type, reporting a generic 'return type mismatch: expected X, got Y' diagnostic (src/checker/expr.rs:1370-1377). This is a real equivalent check, though it uses one generic message rather than PHPStan's four distinct wordings (empty-return / void-with-value / mismatch / never-with-return) and has no special-cased Generator-return-type leniency the way the PHP rule's isSuperTypeOf(Generator) branch does.

functions-generators.name: CallCallablesRule
functions-generators.description: Level-2 Rule on Expr\FuncCall where the callee is itself an expression (not a plain function name): reports callable.nonCallable when the invoked value's type is not/maybe-not callable, callable.inaccessibleMethod for an inaccessible first-class-callable target, then runs full FunctionCallParametersCheck argument-count/type checking against the callable's resolved parameter signature(s).
functions-generators.notes: The big FuncCall handling block in check_expr only builds `sig`/runs check_args/emits the undefined-function diagnostic when `resolved_name` was derived from `ExprKind::Name` (a plain, statically-known function name, see the `let resolved_name = match &callee.kind { ExprKind::Name(...) => ..., _ => None }` at ~line 143). When the callee is a variable/expression holding a Closure or other callable value (e.g. `$fn($x)`, `$obj->makeCallback()($x)`), resolved_name and sig stay None and the whole block silently no-ops - no 'not a callable' diagnostic, no inaccessible-method check, and critically no argument-count/type checking against the callable's own signature happens for that call shape at all.

functions-generators.name: CallToFunctionParametersRule
functions-generators.description: Level-0 Rule on Expr\FuncCall for a plain named function call: selects the matching variant via ParametersAcceptorSelector and delegates to FunctionCallParametersCheck to validate argument count (required/optional/variadic), argument types, by-ref-argument-must-be-variable, named-argument validity, and template-type resolvability.
functions-generators.notes: check_args (src/checker/calls.rs) is the direct equivalent: it's called for every resolved function-name call with a known signature, checking argument count against the signature's required/optional/variadic params and per-argument type compatibility (skipped only for spread-argument calls, per a documented false-positive-avoidance comment). Named-argument reordering is handled via resolve_call_args before this. Less granular than PHPStan's identifier taxonomy (missingParameter/unknownParameter/argument.type etc. are folded into fewer message shapes) but the core parameter-checking logic is present and exercised broadly.

functions-generators.name: CallToFunctionStatementWithNoDiscardRule
functions-generators.description: Level-0 Rule on Stmt\Expression: on PHP 8.5+, flags a standalone function/callable call statement whose reflection says mustUseReturnValue() (the #[NoDiscard] attribute) as function.resultDiscarded (non-ignorable), or flags a (void) cast around a call that actually permits discarding as function.inVoidCast.
functions-generators.notes: This depends on PHP 8.5's #[NoDiscard] attribute, which requires attribute-AST support that doesn't exist (see ArrowFunctionAttributesRule notes - attributes are lexically skipped, never reach the AST). grep for NoDiscard/no_discard/mustUseReturnValue in src/ found nothing, and there is no void-cast-on-statement handling either. A real, unimplemented feature rather than an architectural non-goal, since a future attribute-AST addition could support it.

functions-generators.name: CallToFunctionStatementWithoutSideEffectsRule
functions-generators.description: Level-4 Rule on NoopExpressionNode (a function call used as a standalone statement): reports function.resultUnused when the called function has no declared @phpstan-assert(-*) tags, isn't one of PHPStan's own testing/debug functions, and its result type isn't an explicit never - i.e. the call is pure/side-effect-free and its result is thrown away.
functions-generators.notes: grep across src/checker/ for resultUnused/'no effect'/hasSideEffects/isPure/noop-style logic found nothing. phpstan-rs has no notion of a function being side-effect-free (no @phpstan-pure / hasSideEffects concept in the registry or docblock module), so a standalone `strlen($x);` statement is never flagged.

functions-generators.name: CallToNonExistentFunctionRule
functions-generators.description: Level-0 Rule on Expr\FuncCall: reports function.notFound for a call to an unknown function name (unless guarded by function_exists()), with a discoveringSymbolsTip; separately, when checkFunctionNameCase is on, reports function.nameCase when a known function is called with the wrong letter-casing.
functions-generators.notes: The core existence check is implemented: an unresolvable function name (after resolve_function_candidates fails against the registry) is reported as 'call to undefined function {name}()'. Not implemented: the function_exists()-guard suppression PHPStan's isInFunctionExists gives, and the separate case-sensitivity check (function.nameCase) - grep for 'incorrect case'/nameCase/checkFunctionNameCase found nothing in src/.

functions-generators.name: CallUserFuncRule
functions-generators.description: Level-5 Rule on FuncCall: for call_user_func()/call_user_func_array(), reorders/normalizes the call into the underlying callable's own parameter-acceptor via ArgumentsNormalizer and runs the full FunctionCallParametersCheck against it, so passing the wrong argument count/types to the *forwarded* callable is caught at the call_user_func() site.
functions-generators.notes: grep for 'call_user_func' anywhere under src/ (excluding vendor/) found no hits. call_user_func()/call_user_func_array() are treated as ordinary unrecognized function calls (checked only against their own generic phpstorm-stub-style signature, if any is registered) - there is no forwarding of the check to the target callable's own parameter signature.

functions-generators.name: ClosureAttributesRule
functions-generators.description: Level-0 Rule on InClosureNode, structurally identical to ArrowFunctionAttributesRule but for `function(...) {...}` closures: delegates to AttributesCheck with target = TARGET_FUNCTION.
functions-generators.notes: Same underlying gap as ArrowFunctionAttributesRule: attributes are skipped at the lexer level (src/lexer.rs) and never become AST nodes, so there is no attrGroups for any equivalent check to inspect on a Closure literal.

functions-generators.name: ClosureReturnTypeRule
functions-generators.description: Level-3 Rule on ClosureReturnStatementsNode: for every return statement inside a closure, delegates to FunctionReturnTypeCheck::checkReturnType against the closure's declared/inferred return type, substituting an implicit null literal for a bare `return;` when the return type includes null and there's no native return typehint, and passing isGenerator() for generator-aware messaging.
functions-generators.our_location: src/checker/expr.rs:1300-1316 (Closure body dispatch into check_block) + src/checker/stmt.rs:82-129 (StmtKind::Return(Some)/Return(None) checks)
functions-generators.notes: Closure bodies are checked via the same generic check_block/StmtKind::Return machinery used for named functions/methods: each `return expr;` is compared against declared_return via is_assignable (stmt.rs:82-97), and a bare `return;` is checked against a non-void/non-mixed declared return type (stmt.rs:105-128), with current_function_is_generator saved/restored around the closure body (expr.rs:1308-1316) so generator bodies get generator-appropriate treatment. As with ArrowFunctionReturnTypeRule, message wording is generic ('return type mismatch') rather than PHPStan's four distinct phrasings, and the bare-`return;`-implies-null substitution when the return type includes null is handled implicitly by is_assignable(Null, expected) rather than PHPStan's explicit null-literal substitution, but the core check exists and runs.

functions-generators.name: DefineParametersRule
functions-generators.description: Level-0 Rule on FuncCall: on PHP versions before case-insensitive-constant-name removal, reports argument.unused when define() is called with a 3rd ($case_insensitive) argument, since it's silently ignored.
functions-generators.notes: grep for '"define"' in src/checker/ found no special-casing anywhere. define() with 3 arguments is only checked (if at all) against whatever generic phpstorm-stub signature is registered, with no dedicated diagnostic for the ignored 3rd argument.

functions-generators.name: DuplicateFunctionDeclarationRule
functions-generators.description: Rule on InFunctionNode (no #[RegisteredRule] level attribute - registered via #[ValidatesStubFiles] instead) that builds a name->ReflectionFunction[] map across all reflected functions and reports function.duplicate, listing every file:line, when the current function's name maps to 2+ declarations.
functions-generators.notes: The registry stores functions in a plain string-keyed HashMap - a second top-level `function foo() {}` declaration simply overwrites the first entry silently, with no tracking of prior declarations and no diagnostic emitted for the collision.

functions-generators.name: ExistingClassesInArrowFunctionTypehintsRule
functions-generators.description: Level-0 Rule on Expr\ArrowFunction: reports return.neverTypeNotSupported (non-ignorable) if a `never` return type is used on an arrow function pre-PHP-8.2, then delegates to FunctionDefinitionCheck::checkAnonymousFunction to validate every parameter/return type's referenced classes exist, union-type PHP-version support, unresolvable native types, and NoDiscard-on-void-return misuse.
functions-generators.notes: resolve_type_hint just calls registry::resolve_names_in_type, which resolves namespace/use-imports for a class name in a type hint but never validates the resulting class actually exists (no lookup_class/registry.classes.contains-style check found anywhere in oop.rs/resolve.rs/calls.rs). An arrow function parameter or return type referencing a nonexistent class produces no diagnostic. The never-return-type PHP-version gate and NoDiscard interaction are likewise absent (attributes aren't parsed - see ArrowFunctionAttributesRule).

functions-generators.name: ExistingClassesInClosureTypehintsRule
functions-generators.description: Level-0 Rule on Expr\Closure: delegates to the same FunctionDefinitionCheck::checkAnonymousFunction as the arrow-function variant, validating parameter/return typehints' referenced classes exist, PHP-version union-type support, unresolvable native types, and NoDiscard misuse, for plain `function(){}` closures.
functions-generators.notes: Same gap as ExistingClassesInArrowFunctionTypehintsRule: type hints on Closure params/return are resolved (namespace-qualified) via resolve_type_hint but never checked for whether the named class actually exists anywhere in the codebase.

functions-generators.name: ExistingClassesInTypehintsRule
functions-generators.description: Level-0 Rule on InFunctionNode delegating to FunctionDefinitionCheck::checkFunction: validates that every parameter and return typehint on a top-level named function references an existing class, checks PHP-version union-type support, unreferenced template types, unresolvable native types, and NoDiscard attribute misuse.
functions-generators.notes: Same underlying gap as the arrow-function/closure variants, now for top-level `function foo(SomeUnknownClass $x) {}` declarations: no class-existence validation of parameter/return typehints exists anywhere in the checker (confirmed via grep across oop.rs/resolve.rs/calls.rs for any 'class ... not found'-style check outside of `new` instantiation at src/checker/expr.rs:902).

functions-generators.name: FilterVarRule
functions-generators.description: Rule on FuncCall: flags filter_var($v, FILTER_VALIDATE_*, $options) calls whose 3rd-arg flags type provably has both FILTER_NULL_ON_FAILURE and FILTER_THROW_ON_FAILURE set (mutually exclusive), gated on PHP version support for the THROW constant.
functions-generators.notes: No filter_var-specific handling anywhere in src/ (grep for filter_var/FILTER_NULL_ON_FAILURE/FILTER_THROW_ON_FAILURE returns nothing). filter_var is not modeled as a special-cased function at all in checker/calls.rs or expr.rs.

functions-generators.name: FunctionAttributesRule
functions-generators.description: Rule on InFunctionNode: delegates each function declaration's attrGroups to the shared AttributesCheck (validates attribute class exists, target flags, arg types, non-repeatable rules) with TARGET_FUNCTION.
functions-generators.notes: phpstan-rs's lexer discards all `#[...]` PHP attribute syntax during skip_whitespace_and_comments (src/lexer.rs ~line 523) - attributes never reach the AST at all, so no attrGroups exist for any rule to check. No AttributesCheck equivalent exists anywhere in src/.

functions-generators.name: FunctionCallableRule
functions-generators.description: Rule on FunctionCallableNode (PHP 8.1 first-class-callable syntax foo(...)): gates on PHP 8.1 support, checks function-name-case mismatch, reports 'function not found' unless function_exists()-guarded, and for a dynamic (non-Name) callee checks the expression's type is/might-be callable.
functions-generators.notes: Existence checking for foo(...)/$obj->m(...)/Class::m(...) first-class-callables is implemented (reports 'call to undefined function/method/static method'), explicitly modeled to skip argument-count checking for these nodes. Missing: function-name-case mismatch diagnostic (function.nameCase), the PHP<8.1-unsupported diagnostic (not applicable since this project targets modern PHP), and the 'not a callable'/'might not be callable' diagnostics for a dynamic non-Name callee expression (that branch just recurses via check_expr with no callable-ness check).

functions-generators.name: ImplodeParameterCastableToStringRule
functions-generators.description: Rule on FuncCall for implode()/join(): normalizes implode's overloaded (array)/(separator,array) signatures, then checks the array argument's element type is castable to string, reporting a precise 'expects array<string>, X given' message with correct $array/$separator/positional argument naming.
functions-generators.notes: No implode/join special-casing anywhere in src/checker/*.rs (grep for "implode"/"join" in checker files returns nothing). The generic check_args() in calls.rs only does whole-array-type is_assignable checks against a stub signature, not the ParameterCastableToStringCheck's per-element castability with __toString/enum/etc. coercion logic, so this specific diagnostic and its message shape are absent.

functions-generators.name: IncompatibleArrowFunctionDefaultParameterTypeRule
functions-generators.description: Rule on InArrowFunctionNode: for each arrow-fn parameter with a default value, checks the default value's type is accepted by the (template-resolved) declared parameter type, reporting 'Default value ... is incompatible with type ...'.
functions-generators.notes: grep across src/checker/*.rs and src/ast.rs confirms `param.default`/`.default` (the AST field storing default-value expressions) is never read by the checker at all - only parsed and stored. No default-value-vs-parameter-type compatibility check exists for arrow functions, closures, or named functions.

functions-generators.name: IncompatibleClosureDefaultParameterTypeRule
functions-generators.description: Identical logic to the arrow-function variant but for InClosureNode (real `function(...) use(...) {}` closures): checks each parameter's default value type against its declared type.
functions-generators.notes: Same gap as the arrow-function sibling - ExprKind::Closure handling in checker/expr.rs (~line 1267) builds closure_locals from parameter type hints but never inspects or type-checks `param.default` against them.

functions-generators.name: IncompatibleDefaultParameterTypeRule
functions-generators.description: Identical logic again but for InFunctionNode (named top-level functions and, via the shared FunctionReflection, effectively methods too): checks each parameter's default value type against its declared/PHPDoc type.
functions-generators.notes: check_function (src/checker.rs:439) reads f.params/sig.params to build declared parameter types for the body but never validates `param.default` against them - same missing capability as the other two default-parameter-type rules; all three would likely share one implementation point in the Rust rewrite.

functions-generators.name: InnerFunctionRule
functions-generators.description: Rule on Function_: flags any named `function` statement declared inside another function's body (scope->getFunction() !== null) as unsupported by PHPStan, since inner-function declarations execute only when control flow reaches them.
functions-generators.notes: phpstan-rs deliberately does the opposite of PHPStan here: StmtKind::FunctionDecl inside a block (checker/stmt.rs:609) is explicitly recursed into and checked (comment cites the common `if (!function_exists('foo')) { function foo() {} }` polyfill idiom) rather than rejected as unsupported. This is an intentional broader-support design choice already documented in-repo, not a gap to fill - PHPStan's own limitation doesn't apply to phpstan-rs's architecture, so replicating the 'not supported' diagnostic would be a regression, not parity.

functions-generators.name: InvalidLexicalVariablesInClosureUseRule
functions-generators.description: Rule on Closure: validates each `use (...)` lexical-capture variable - errors if it's $this, a superglobal name, or duplicates a closure parameter name.
functions-generators.notes: ExprKind::Closure handling in checker/expr.rs (~line 1267-1290) reads `uses` only to seed closure_locals with the outer variable's type; it never validates the use-variable name against $this, Scope::SUPERGLOBAL_VARIABLES equivalents, or the closure's own parameter names. No diagnostic emitted for any of the three invalid cases.

functions-generators.name: InvalidParameterNameRule
functions-generators.description: Rule on Node\Param: flags a function/method/closure parameter named after a superglobal (e.g. `$_GET`) or named `$this` as invalid (nonIgnorable).
functions-generators.notes: check_function (src/checker.rs:439) and the closure/arrow-fn param-binding code insert every parameter name into locals unconditionally; there is no check against is_superglobal()-style names or against 'this' for parameter declarations specifically (is_superglobal exists in assignment.rs but is only used for read/type-narrowing purposes, never to validate parameter declarations).

functions-generators.name: MissingFunctionParameterTypehintRule
functions-generators.description: Level-6 rule on InFunctionNode: for each parameter (plus @param-closure-this and @param-out pseudo-types), reports implicit-mixed missing typehint, missing iterable value type, missing generic-class type args, or missing callable signature, via the shared MissingTypehintCheck.
functions-generators.notes: No MissingTypehintCheck equivalent, no missingType.parameter/iterableValue/generics/callable identifiers, and no rule-level (0-10) concept at all in phpstan-rs's checker - grep for these strings/concepts across src/checker/*.rs and src/*.rs returns nothing. phpstan-rs's checker is not organized by opt-in PHPStan rule level, so this whole family of 'require explicit types' strictness rules is entirely absent.

functions-generators.name: MissingFunctionReturnTypehintRule
functions-generators.description: Level-6 rule on InFunctionNode: same missing-typehint family as the parameter rule but for the function's own return type (implicit mixed, missing iterable value type, missing generic args, missing callable signature).
functions-generators.notes: Same absence as MissingFunctionParameterTypehintRule - no MissingTypehintCheck, no missingType.return/iterableValue/generics/callable diagnostics anywhere in src/.

functions-generators.name: ParamAttributesRule
functions-generators.description: Rule on Node\Param: delegates each parameter's attrGroups to AttributesCheck with TARGET_PARAMETER (or PARAMETER|PROPERTY for constructor-promoted properties).
functions-generators.notes: Same root cause as FunctionAttributesRule: the lexer strips all `#[...]` attribute syntax before it ever reaches the AST (src/lexer.rs), so parameters carry no attribute data and no AttributesCheck-equivalent exists to validate against.

functions-generators.name: ParameterCastableToNumberRule
functions-generators.description: Rule on FuncCall for array_sum()/array_product(): checks the single array argument's values are all castable to number (PHP-version-gated: objects are rejected pre-8.3 support for objects in array_sum/product), reporting 'expects an array of values castable to number, X given'.
functions-generators.notes: grep for array_sum/array_product across src/checker/*.rs returns nothing - these functions are not special-cased at all; only their stub-declared signature (if any) would flow through the generic is_assignable check_args path, which lacks the toNumber() per-element castability coercion this rule performs.

functions-generators.name: ParameterCastableToStringRule
functions-generators.description: Rule on FuncCall for array_intersect/array_intersect_assoc/array_diff/array_diff_assoc (check all array args) and array_combine/natcasesort/natsort/array_count_values/array_fill_keys (check first arg after normalization): checks array values are castable to string.
functions-generators.notes: grep for these function names in src/checker/*.rs finds only unrelated matches (natsort/natcasesort mentioned in calls.rs purely as functions that preserve array key-order, not for castable-to-string checking). No ParameterCastableToStringCheck equivalent exists in phpstan-rs.

functions-generators.name: PrintfArrayParametersRule
functions-generators.description: Rule on FuncCall for vprintf()/vsprintf(): counts placeholders in the (possibly union of constant-string) format argument via PrintfHelper, computes the args-array's possible size range from its type, and reports a mismatch between placeholder count and array element count.
functions-generators.notes: checker/calls.rs's check_format_string_call (and its caller in expr.rs:250-251) only special-cases 'sprintf'/'printf' literally; 'vprintf'/'vsprintf' are absent from that match and from every other grep in src/checker/*.rs, so the array-form printf functions get no placeholder-vs-array-size validation at all.

functions-generators.name: PrintfHelper
functions-generators.description: Shared helper (not a Rule): parses printf/sprintf format strings into ordered PrintfPlaceholder objects (tracking width/precision '*' sub-placeholders, positional %N$ specifiers, and each specifier's accepted PHP type category), and separately counts scanf-style placeholders via sscanf.
functions-generators.notes: parse_format_specifiers() covers the core case (ordered %d/%s/%f/etc specifiers, skipping %%) and format_specifier_accepts() maps specifiers to accepted argument types - roughly analogous to getPrintfPlaceholders()/getAcceptingTypeBySpecifier(). But it explicitly bails (returns None) on positional specifiers (%1$s) whereas PrintfHelper fully supports and reorders them; it has no width/precision '*' sub-placeholder tracking, no PHP-version-gated hH specifier support, and no scanf-placeholder-counting equivalent (getScanfPlaceholdersCount) at all - sscanf isn't handled anywhere in src/.

functions-generators.name: PrintfParameterTypeRule
functions-generators.description: Rule on FuncCall for printf()/sprintf()/fprintf(): for each format placeholder, checks the corresponding argument's type is compatible with the placeholder's accepted type (int/float/string/mixed, strict or castable depending on a config flag), reporting 'Parameter #N ... is expected to be X by placeholder #N, Y given'.
functions-generators.notes: Covers sprintf/printf specifically (matches PrintfParameterTypeRule's FORMAT_ARGUMENT_POSITIONS for those two) with per-specifier type-acceptance checking and a similar diagnostic message. Missing: fprintf (not in the 'sprintf'|'printf' match), the strict-vs-castable configurable mode (checkStrictPrintfPlaceholderTypes), positional specifiers, and width/precision sub-placeholders (all silently unsupported since parse_format_specifiers returns None for them, which check_format_string_call currently treats as 'nothing to check' rather than emitting the CallToFunctionParametersRule-deferred distinction PHPStan makes).

functions-generators.name: PrintfParametersRule
functions-generators.description: Rule on FuncCall: for printf/sprintf/sscanf/fscanf calls with a literal-constant-string format argument, counts placeholders and errors if the format string is malformed, or if the argument count doesn't exactly equal placeholder count + 1.
functions-generators.our_location: src/checker/calls.rs:376 check_format_string_call, wired only for sprintf/printf at src/checker/expr.rs:250-251; specifier parser at calls.rs:468 parse_format_specifiers
functions-generators.notes: Only sprintf/printf are covered; sscanf/fscanf (format arg at position 1, min 3 args) are not wired at all. Also only flags too-few arguments (specs.len() > provided.len()), never an exact-count mismatch (PHPStan requires argsCount === placeholders+1, so it also flags too many args) - a deliberate narrowing per the code's own comment. No support for multiple candidate format strings from a union type (PHPStan takes the max placeholder count across getConstantStrings()).

functions-generators.name: PrintfPlaceholder
functions-generators.description: Pure value/helper class (not a Rule) representing one parsed printf placeholder; doesArgumentTypeMatchPlaceholder() decides whether an argument's type satisfies that placeholder's accepting-type category (strict-int/int/float/string/mixed), with separate strict vs. non-strict (coercive) matching rules including accessory numeric-string/decimal-int-string allowances.
functions-generators.notes: Rust equivalent is a much coarser match on the raw spec char: for numeric specifiers it only rejects array-like and Object types (i.e. accepts almost everything else including bool/null/mixed); for 's' it only rejects array-like. It has none of PHPStan's strict/non-strict distinction, no decimal-int-string/numeric-string accessory-type awareness, and no rejection of null/bool for string placeholders under strict mode.

functions-generators.name: RandomIntParametersRule
functions-generators.description: Rule on FuncCall: for random_int($min, $max) calls where both args resolve to constant-integer or integer-range types, errors when $min is provably (or, with reportMaybes, possibly) not smaller than $max.
functions-generators.notes: No random_int-specific handling found anywhere in src/ (grep for 'random_int' across src/ returns nothing). No equivalent IntegerRangeType::isSmallerThan-style comparison rule exists for this builtin.

functions-generators.name: RedefinedParametersRule
functions-generators.description: Rule on FunctionLike (functions/methods/closures/arrow-fns): scans the parameter list and reports a non-ignorable error for each parameter name reused later in the same list (e.g. function f($a, $a)).
functions-generators.notes: No duplicate-parameter-name diagnostic exists; grep for 'Redefinition'/'redefin' across src/ finds nothing. Function-signature registry tests (src/registry/tests/function_signatures.rs) exercise how a *stub's* duplicate param collapses for signature lookup purposes, but that's internal signature handling, not a user-facing diagnostic for source-level duplicate params.

functions-generators.name: ReturnNullsafeByRefRule
functions-generators.description: Rule on ReturnStatementsNode: for a function/method declared to return by reference, reports a non-ignorable error on any return statement whose expression contains a nullsafe (?->) access, since a nullsafe result cannot be returned by reference.
functions-generators.notes: Named FunctionDecl (src/ast.rs:129) has no by-ref-return flag at all (only Closure's AST node tracks a by_ref return flag, at src/ast.rs:484, and it is never consulted by any check). No NullsafeCheck-equivalent scan of return expressions exists. Genuinely absent end-to-end, not just unwired.

functions-generators.name: ReturnTypeRule
functions-generators.description: Rule on Stmt\Return_ (functions only, excluding methods and closures): delegates to FunctionReturnTypeCheck to validate a return statement's expression type (or a bare empty return) against the function's declared return type, with distinct messages for empty-return, void-with-value, plain mismatch, and never-with-return-statement cases, skipping the value/key checks for generators.
functions-generators.notes: Core semantics are covered: return-with-expr is checked against declared_return via registry::is_assignable, bare return; is checked against Null-assignability (skipping generators via current_function_is_generator, mirroring PHPStan's own generator carve-out). Differences: uses one generic 'return type mismatch: expected X, got Y' message rather than PHPStan's four distinct message templates, and the Rust check appears to run uniformly for any function-like body (not gated off for closures/anonymous functions the way PHPStan splits this into a separate closures rule) - broader but less precisely scoped than the original.

functions-generators.name: SortParameterCastableToStringRule
functions-generators.description: Rule on FuncCall for array_unique/sort/rsort/asort/arsort: when a SORT_STRING/SORT_LOCALE_STRING/SORT_NATURAL/SORT_NUMERIC flags argument is passed, checks that every element of the input array is castable to the required string and/or float type, via ParameterCastableToStringCheck.
functions-generators.notes: src/checker/calls.rs has by-ref result-type handling for sort/rsort/asort/arsort/etc. (reindexing/list-preservation), but nothing checks array element castability against the sort flags argument. No reference to SORT_STRING/SORT_NUMERIC/etc. constants or a castable-to-string check for these builtins anywhere in src/.

functions-generators.name: UnusedClosureUsesRule
functions-generators.description: Rule on Expr\Closure: for each `use ($x)` clause, delegates to UnusedFunctionParametersCheck to report 'Anonymous function has an unused use $x' when that captured variable is never referenced in the closure body.
functions-generators.notes: No unused-variable/parameter detection exists anywhere in the checker (grep for 'unused' across src/ hits only test files, not checker logic). Closure `use` clauses are parsed and their captured variables are bound into the closure's locals scope, but nothing ever flags an unused one.

functions-generators.name: UselessFunctionReturnValueRule
functions-generators.description: Rule on FuncCall: when var_export()/print_r()/highlight_string()'s result is used as an expression (not a first-level statement) but the 'return output instead of printing' flag argument isn't passed (or is false), reports that the return value is useless (always null/true) and the output was printed instead.
functions-generators.notes: No handling of var_export/print_r/highlight_string's second-argument 'return' flag, and no first-level-statement-vs-used-as-expression distinction for these functions anywhere in src/.

functions-generators.name: VariadicParametersDeclarationRule
functions-generators.description: Rule on FunctionLike: reports a non-ignorable 'Only the last parameter can be variadic.' error for any variadic parameter that isn't the final one in the parameter list.
