functions-generators.notes: The parser (src/parser/functions.rs:55) parses a `variadic` flag per parameter and the checker uses it extensively for call-site arity checks (src/checker/calls.rs), but nothing validates that a variadic parameter, if present, is declared last in a function/method/closure signature.

functions-generators.name: YieldFromTypeRule
functions-generators.description: Rule on Expr\YieldFrom: errors if the delegated expression isn't iterable; otherwise checks the delegated iterable's key/value/TSend types against the enclosing generator function's declared Generator<...> type, plus a 'result of yield from (void) is used' check.
functions-generators.notes: src/checker/expr.rs:656-659 handles YieldFrom by just type-checking the inner expression and returning Type::Mixed unconditionally - no iterable-ness check, no key/value/TSend comparison against a declared Generator<K,V,TSend,TReturn> return type (which isn't modeled as a distinct type shape in src/types.rs either), and no void-result-used check.

functions-generators.name: YieldInGeneratorRule
functions-generators.description: Rule on Expr (filtered to Yield_/YieldFrom): reports 'Yield can be used only inside a function' when outside any function scope, and 'Yield can be used only with these return types: Generator, Iterator, Traversable, iterable' when the enclosing function's declared return type isn't one of those (or mixed).
functions-generators.notes: src/checker/control_flow.rs:151-163 body_contains_yield() detects generator-ness only to skip the ordinary return-type check (stmt.rs), but nothing validates the *converse*: that a function containing yield actually declares a Generator/Iterator/Traversable/iterable return type, nor is there any 'yield outside a function' diagnostic.

functions-generators.name: YieldTypeRule
functions-generators.description: Rule on Expr\Yield_: checks the yielded key type (Integer if omitted) and value type (Null if omitted) against the enclosing generator function's declared Generator<K,V,...> key/value types, plus a 'result of yield (void) is used' check.
functions-generators.notes: src/checker/expr.rs:672-680 type-checks the key/value sub-expressions but always returns Type::Mixed for the yield expression itself and never compares them against a declared Generator<...> return type - matching YieldFromTypeRule's same gap, since neither the generic Generator<K,V,TSend,TReturn> type shape nor this comparison exists in src/types.rs or the checker.

phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.name: IgnoreParseErrorRule
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.description: Level-0 Rule<FileNode> that walks the first-node's 'linesToIgnoreParseErrors' attribute (populated earlier by the ignore-comment parser) and emits a non-ignorable 'ignore.parseError' diagnostic for every malformed @phpstan-ignore expression (bad identifier list/reason syntax) found anywhere in the file.
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.notes: phpstan-rs has no @phpstan-ignore / @phpstan-ignore-next-line / @phpstan-ignore-line support at all anywhere in src/ (no hits for 'phpstan-ignore', 'ignore-next-line', or any IgnoredError-equivalent structure), so there is no ignore-expression parser to have parse errors from in the first place.

phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.name: MissingReturnRule
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.description: Level-0 Rule<ExecutionEndNode> that, when a function/method/closure's statement result doesn't always terminate, compares the declared/PHPDoc return type against void/never/mixed and emits 'return.missing' ('X should return T but return statement is missing') or the non-ignorable 'return.never' for an explicit-never function that falls through, also handling Generator TReturn via yield-aware branches.
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.notes: src/checker/control_flow.rs has an always_terminates() helper used only to merge branch-local variable state for narrowing (if/switch/try merges) - it is never combined with a function's declared return type to flag a fall-through with no return statement. No 'return.missing'/'return.never'-equivalent diagnostic text exists anywhere in src/.

phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.name: AssertRuleHelper
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.description: AutowiredService helper (invoked by FunctionAssertRule and, elsewhere, a MethodAssertRule) that validates every @phpstan-assert/-if-true/-if-false tag on a function/method: unknown referenced parameter, unresolvable asserted expression/type, impossible/already-narrowed assertions, unknown/trait referenced classes, generic-type validity, and missing-typehint checks on the asserted type.
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.notes: docblock.rs's tag parser has no case for 'assert'/'assert-if-true'/'assert-if-false' at all (only param/return/var/property/template variants are handled), so phpstan-rs neither parses nor uses @phpstan-assert tags anywhere - there is nothing for narrowing.rs to consult and nothing for this validation logic to run against.

phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.name: ConditionalReturnTypeRuleHelper
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.description: AutowiredService helper that walks a signature's param/out/closure-this/return types for ConditionalType/ConditionalTypeForParameter nodes and flags one whose subject isn't a real @template (or references an unknown parameter), or whose condition is statically always true/false given the subject's declared type.
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.notes: docblock.rs explicitly documents skipping conditional return type syntax ('($param is Foo ? Bar : Baz)') rather than parsing it into a garbage type - confirmed by src/docblock.rs's own comments and the dedicated test 'a_real_phpstan_conditional_return_type_is_skipped_rather_than_parsed_into_garbage'. With no ConditionalType representation in types.rs, this helper's entire subject has no Rust counterpart.

phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.name: FunctionAssertRule
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.description: Level-2 thin Rule<InFunctionNode> that, for a global function with exactly one signature variant, delegates straight to AssertRuleHelper::check().
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.notes: Pure dispatcher with no logic of its own; missing because its sole dependency, @phpstan-assert tag support (AssertRuleHelper), does not exist in phpstan-rs.

phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.name: FunctionConditionalReturnTypeRule
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.description: Level-2 thin Rule<InFunctionNode> that, for a global function with exactly one signature variant, delegates straight to ConditionalReturnTypeRuleHelper::check().
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.notes: Pure dispatcher; missing because ConditionalReturnTypeRuleHelper (and conditional-return-type parsing generally) is not implemented.

phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.name: GenericCallableRuleHelper
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.description: AutowiredService helper that traverses a type looking for CallableType/ClosureType nodes carrying their own @template tags, runs TemplateTypeCheck on each (existing-class/alias-as-name, invalid/unsupported bound, invalid/non-subtype default, missing-default-after-optional), and separately flags any callable-local template name that shadows an enclosing function's or class's own @template.
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.notes: src/types.rs's Callable/Closure type representation carries no per-callable @template tags (confirmed: no template-bearing Closure/CallableType construct and no 'shadowTemplate'-equivalent diagnostic anywhere in src/), so callable-local generics and the associated shadow check have no Rust counterpart; src/checker/generics.rs's check_generic_bounds is a different, narrower feature (bound-checking on GenericObjectType args only).

phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.name: IncompatibleClassConstantPhpDocTypeRule
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.description: Level-2 Rule<Node\Stmt\ClassConst> that, per declared constant, compares its @var PHPDoc type against any native `const TYPE X = ...` type hint - reporting unresolvable-type, 'classConstant.phpDocType' when incompatible/not-a-subtype - and runs GenericObjectTypeCheck on the PHPDoc type.
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.notes: src/registry/class_info.rs resolves each class constant's type by preferring the @var docblock type (parsed via types::parse_type_string) over infer_const_type()'s native-value inference with no compatibility check between the two whatsoever - the mismatch is silently swallowed by PHPDoc winning outright, never diagnosed.

phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.name: IncompatibleParamImmediatelyInvokedCallableRule
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.description: Level-2 Rule<FunctionLike> that resolves @param-immediately-invoked-callable/@param-later-invoked-callable tags and flags one naming an unknown parameter, or one attached to a parameter whose native type isn't callable ('paramImmediatelyInvokedCallable.nonCallable'/'paramLaterInvokedCallable.nonCallable').
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.notes: Neither tag is recognized by docblock.rs's tag switch (no 'param-immediately-invoked-callable'/'param-later-invoked-callable' case), and no ImmediatelyInvokedCallable-style concept exists elsewhere in src/ (confirmed by an empty grep for 'immediately-invoked'/'ImmediatelyInvoked').

phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.name: IncompatiblePhpDocTypeCheck
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.description: AutowiredService that is the core of PHPDoc/native compatibility checking, shared by IncompatiblePhpDocTypeRule/IncompatiblePropertyHookPhpDocTypeRule: for every @param/@param-out/@param-closure-this tag and the @return tag, checks unknown-parameter, unresolvable type, generic-type validity, generic-callable template shadowing, param-out by-ref requirement, @param-closure-this non-Closure native type, and native-vs-PHPDoc subtype incompatibility ('parameter.phpDocType'/'return.phpDocType', with a @template tip when the mismatch is exactly a bare template).
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.notes: This is the central logic all the sibling Incompatible*PhpDocType rules in this chunk depend on. phpstan-rs has no equivalent: src/registry/function_sig.rs merges a @param/@return docblock type with the native type hint by simply preferring the docblock's type (documented as deliberate 'PHPDoc wins' behavior) rather than validating the two are compatible and erroring when they aren't; @param-out and @param-closure-this tags are not parsed at all.

phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.name: IncompatiblePhpDocTypeRule
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.description: Level-2 Rule<Node\FunctionLike> that gathers native parameter/return types and by-ref flags for a function or method's own doc comment and passes them into IncompatiblePhpDocTypeCheck::check().
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.notes: Thin dispatcher; missing because its sole dependency, IncompatiblePhpDocTypeCheck, is not implemented (see that item).

phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.name: IncompatiblePropertyHookPhpDocTypeRule
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.description: Level-2 Rule<InPropertyHookNode> that gathers a property hook's native parameter/return types and forwards them to the same IncompatiblePhpDocTypeCheck::check() used for regular functions/methods.
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.notes: phpstan-rs does model PHP 8.4 property hooks structurally (PropertySig::set_ty in src/registry/class_info.rs, property_hook_set_type()), but there is no hook-level @param/@return PHPDoc-vs-native compatibility check - the same IncompatiblePhpDocTypeCheck gap applies here.

phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.name: IncompatiblePropertyPhpDocTypeRule
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.description: Level-2 Rule<ClassPropertyNode> that checks a property's (or promoted-parameter's) @var/PHPDoc type against its native type hint for unresolvable-type and phpDocType-incompatibility ('property.phpDocType', with a @template tip), plus GenericCallableRuleHelper and GenericObjectTypeCheck on the PHPDoc type.
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.notes: src/registry/class_info.rs (properties map, ~line 132-154) resolves each property's type via resolve_type(doc @var, native hint) with the docblock type simply taking precedence when present - no comparison, no diagnostic when the two disagree; promoted-constructor-parameter properties follow the identical 'PHPDoc wins silently' pattern a few lines later.

phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.name: IncompatibleSelfOutTypeRule
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.description: Level-2 Rule<InClassMethodNode> that checks a method's @phpstan-self-out type is a subtype of the declaring class ('selfOut.type'), flags it as unsupported on a static method ('selfOut.static'), and runs unresolvable-type and generic-type checks on it.
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.notes: No @phpstan-self-out (or @phpstan-this-out) support exists anywhere in phpstan-rs - confirmed by empty greps for 'self-out'/'self_out'/'SelfOut'/'this-out'/'this_out' across src/ - so there is no self-out type to validate.

phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.name: InvalidPHPStanDocTagRule
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.description: Level-2 Rule<NodeAbstract> that re-tokenizes/re-parses every statement's doc comment with the real phpdoc-parser grammar and flags any '@phpstan-*' tag not in a fixed allow-list of ~38 recognized PHPStan tags as 'Unknown PHPDoc tag' ('phpDoc.phpstanTag').
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.notes: src/docblock.rs's parser is a lenient, best-effort line/regex-style tokenizer (splits '@tag rest', dispatches through a match on a small set of recognized tag names, and silently ignores anything unmatched) with no allow-list validation and no error path for an unrecognized '@phpstan-' tag - unknown tags are simply dropped, never diagnosed.

phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.name: InvalidPhpDocTagValueRule
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.description: Level-2 Rule<NodeAbstract> that re-parses each doc comment and reports any tag whose value node came back as InvalidTagValueNode (or an invalid @phpstan-type alias) as 'PHPDoc tag ... has invalid value ...' ('phpDoc.parseError'), skipping @phan-/@psalm- tags.
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.notes: docblock.rs has no notion of a syntactically-invalid tag value at all - take_type_token()/parse_type_string() either extract something or silently leave the field unset (e.g. the documented conditional-return-type case), never surfacing a parse-error diagnostic; there is no grammar-level PHPDoc parser in phpstan-rs comparable to phpstan/phpdoc-parser that could distinguish valid from invalid tag syntax.

phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.name: InvalidPhpDocVarTagTypeRule
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.description: Level-2 Rule<Node\Stmt> that validates every @var tag on a property/const/class-like/function/method doc comment: unresolvable type, missing iterable-value/generic typehints (when checkMissingVarTagTypehint is on), generic-type validity, referenced-class-is-a-trait, unknown referenced class ('class.notFound', with a discovering-symbols tip), and class-name case-sensitivity via ClassNameCheck.
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.notes: src/checker/stmt.rs's inline_var_annotation() only extracts an inline '/** @var Type $x */' for local-variable narrowing (Type::Mixed fallback on anything odd, no error path); there is no scan of @var-referenced classes for existence/trait-invalidity/case-sensitivity and no missing-typehint check anywhere in src/ (confirmed by empty greps for 'missingType.iterableValue'/'missingType.generics'/'class.notFound').

phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.name: InvalidThrowsPhpDocValueRule
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.description: Level-2 Rule<NodeAbstract> that resolves a function/method/property-hook's @throws PHPDoc type and reports 'throws.notThrowable' when it isn't (recursively, for unions) a subtype of Throwable, honoring interface require-extends tags via intersection.
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.notes: phpstan-rs parses no '@throws' tag anywhere (docblock.rs has no case for it, and empty greps confirm no '@throws'/'throws_type'/'ThrowsTag' usage across the checker or registry), so there is no throws type to validate against Throwable.

phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.name: MethodAssertRule
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.description: A Rule<InClassMethodNode> (level 2) that, for methods with a single signature variant, delegates to AssertRuleHelper to validate @phpstan-assert/@phpstan-assert-if-true/@phpstan-assert-if-false tags (e.g. that asserted parameter names exist, template types used in the assertion are valid).
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.notes: phpstan-rs's docblock.rs only parses @param/@return/@var/@property*/@template*/@extends/@implements (see apply_tag match arms) - there is no @phpstan-assert tag parsing anywhere in src/, and narrowing.rs's assert-related logic (apply_phpunit_assertion_narrowing) is PHPUnit runtime-assertion narrowing, an unrelated feature. No validation of assert-tag correctness exists.

phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.name: MethodConditionalReturnTypeRule
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.description: A Rule<InClassMethodNode> (level 2) that, for single-variant methods, delegates to ConditionalReturnTypeRuleHelper to validate conditional return-type expressions (`($param is Foo ? Bar : Baz)`) used in @return/@phpstan-return tags.
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.notes: docblock.rs's own doc comment and the "return" tag arm explicitly disclaim conditional return types: the code detects a leading `($` and deliberately leaves return_type unset rather than attempting to parse the is/?/: grammar. Since conditional return types are never parsed into a type at all, there is nothing for an equivalent rule to validate.

phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.name: PhpDocLineHelper
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.description: Pure static utility used by several PhpDoc rules to compute the precise source line of a specific PHPDoc tag (via bleeding-edge tag start-line data), falling back to the enclosing node's start line when precise data is unavailable.
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.notes: docblock.rs's line-grouping logic (tag_lines, ~line 89-126) tracks tag text but not per-tag source line offsets, and no caller anywhere reconstructs a tag's own line for diagnostics - phpstan-rs uniformly reports at the enclosing statement/node's line (equivalent to PhpDocLineHelper's fallback branch only, never its precise bleeding-edge branch). Low-impact precision gap, not a missing check.

phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.name: RequireExtendsCheck
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.description: Shared AutowiredService helper (not itself a Rule) that validates @phpstan-require-extends tags: rejects duplicates, non-object types, unknown classes, interfaces (suggesting @phpstan-require-implements instead), non-class reflections, and final classes, and otherwise delegates to ClassNameCheck for case-sensitivity/casing checks.
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.notes: The @phpstan-require-extends tag is not parsed anywhere in src/docblock.rs (apply_tag has no "require-extends" arm), so none of this validation logic - or the underlying data it would validate - exists in phpstan-rs.

phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.name: RequireExtendsDefinitionClassRule
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.description: A Rule<InClassNode> (level 2) that reports an error when @phpstan-require-extends is present on anything other than an interface, otherwise delegates to RequireExtendsCheck::checkExtendsTags.
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.notes: Depends entirely on the unimplemented @phpstan-require-extends tag parsing/RequireExtendsCheck; no equivalent rule or tag support exists in phpstan-rs.

phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.name: RequireExtendsDefinitionTraitRule
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.description: A Rule<Trait_> (level 2) that looks up the trait's reflection and delegates its @phpstan-require-extends tags to RequireExtendsCheck::checkExtendsTags (traits are always a valid target, unlike classes).
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.notes: Same missing @phpstan-require-extends tag/check dependency as the class-rule sibling; no equivalent exists in phpstan-rs's docblock or checker code.

phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.name: RequireImplementsDefinitionClassRule
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.description: A Rule<InClassNode> (level 2) that reports an error whenever @phpstan-require-implements tags are present on any class/interface/enum, since the tag is only legal on traits.
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.notes: The @phpstan-require-implements tag is not parsed anywhere in phpstan-rs (docblock.rs's apply_tag has no such arm), so there is no data to validate and no equivalent rule.

phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.name: RequireImplementsDefinitionTraitRule
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.description: A Rule<Trait_> (level 2) that validates a trait's @phpstan-require-implements tags: non-object types, unknown classes, non-interface targets, and otherwise delegates to ClassNameCheck for casing/case-sensitivity checks.
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.notes: Same dependency on the unimplemented @phpstan-require-implements tag; no equivalent logic exists in phpstan-rs.

phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.name: SealedDefinitionClassRule
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.description: A Rule<InClassNode> (level 2) that rejects @phpstan-sealed tags on enums, and otherwise validates each sealed tag's referenced classes (non-object types, unknown classes) and delegates to ClassNameCheck for casing.
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.notes: The @phpstan-sealed tag is not parsed in phpstan-rs's docblock.rs, and types.rs's unrelated "unsealed shape" comment (line ~349) refers to array-shape `...` markers, not this class-hierarchy-sealing PHPDoc tag. No equivalent exists.

phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.name: SealedDefinitionTraitRule
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.description: A Rule<Trait_> (level 0) that unconditionally reports an error when a trait carries any @phpstan-sealed tags, since the tag is only valid on class/interface.
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.notes: Depends on the unimplemented @phpstan-sealed tag; no equivalent rule exists in phpstan-rs.

phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.name: UnresolvableTypeHelper
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.description: AutowiredService helper that walks a resolved Type tree (via TypeTraverser) looking for ErrorType or implicit (non-explicit) NeverType nodes, signalling that some part of a PHPDoc type failed to resolve, and collecting the human-readable failure reasons.
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.notes: phpstan-rs's Type enum (src/types.rs) has no ErrorType/unresolvable-marker variant at all - failed type resolution presumably falls back silently (e.g. to Mixed) rather than being tracked as an explicit error state, so there is no way for downstream rules to detect and suppress cascading diagnostics the way PHPStan does via this helper.

phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.name: UnresolvableTypeResult
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.description: A tiny readonly value object (list<string> $reasons) returned by UnresolvableTypeHelper::getUnresolvableType() to carry the collected unresolvability reasons; no logic of its own.
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.notes: Pure data holder tied one-to-one to UnresolvableTypeHelper; since that helper's underlying ErrorType concept doesn't exist in phpstan-rs's type system, there is nothing for an equivalent struct to carry.

phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.name: VarTagChangedExpressionTypeRule
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.description: A Rule<VarTagChangedExpressionTypeNode> (level 2) that fires on the virtual node PHPStan emits when an inline @var tag mid-scope changes an expression's already-known type, delegating the actual subtype validation to VarTagTypeRuleHelper::checkExprType.
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.notes: phpstan-rs does recognize an inline `/** @var Type $name */` doc comment on a statement and applies it to the local's tracked type (check_stmt's inline_var handling), which is the same underlying feature PHPStan models as a 'changed expression type' - but it applies the annotation unconditionally with zero validation: no check that the new @var type is a valid subtype of (or otherwise compatible with) the previously-known/native type, and no diagnostic is ever emitted, so the actual rule behavior (catching a wrong/dangerous @var override) is absent.

phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.name: VarTagTypeRuleHelper
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.description: AutowiredService implementing the core @var-tag validation logic shared by WrongVariableNameInVarTagRule and VarTagChangedExpressionTypeRule: checkVarType() resolves which variable(s) an @var tag targets (handling list()/array destructuring recursively) and checkExprType() verifies the tag's type is a valid supertype of the expression's native type (and, optionally, its PHPStan type), plus a dangerous-assumption check when the tag's type equals the current PHPStan type exactly for PHPStan-API Type objects.
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.notes: phpstan-rs parses @var into (name, type) (docblock.rs) and applies it unconditionally to the local variable map (checker/stmt.rs) with no subtype/compatibility checking against the expression's actual/native type, no list()/array-destructuring recursive matching, and no 'assumes always X but it's error-prone' warning. None of VarTagTypeRuleHelper's validation logic has an equivalent.

phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.name: WrongVariableNameInVarTagRule
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.description: A Rule<Node\Stmt> (level 2) that finds all @var tags on a statement's doc comment and validates their target variable name(s) against the statement's actual shape: single assignment (incl. list()/array destructuring), foreach (iteratee/key/value), static var declarations, global declarations, throw/return/bare expressions, and flags tags with no matching variable, ambiguous/multiple tags, or tags misplaced above a class/function/method declaration (where @var has no effect); delegates type-compatibility checking to VarTagTypeRuleHelper.
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.notes: phpstan-rs's inline_var_annotation covers only the simple `$x = expr;` assignment-statement case, and even there it silently no-ops (returns None) rather than emitting a diagnostic when the @var's named variable doesn't match the assignment target or when a bare @var can't be inferred to a single variable. There is no handling at all for foreach/static/global/throw/misplaced-on-declaration cases, no 'variable does not exist' / 'does not match assigned variable' / 'multiple @var tags not supported' / 'has no effect' diagnostics anywhere - only the narrowing side-effect for the one well-formed case exists, none of the rule's actual error-reporting behavior.

phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.name: InvalidTypesInUnionRule
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.description: A Rule<Node> (level 0) that scans native PHP type declarations (function/method params, return types, and class property types) for ComplexType (UnionType/NullableType) nodes containing mixed, never, or void as a union member or as the base of a nullable type - all illegal per PHP's own type-declaration grammar - and reports a non-ignorable error per offending case.
phpdoc-missing-types-ignore.notes: phpstan-rs's native type parser (types.rs) happily builds Type::Union([...Type::Mixed/Never/Void...]) for such declarations with no validation step and no diagnostic - grep across src/ for 'cannot be part of a union'/'unionType.'/'nullableType.' style messages found nothing. This is a real PHP-syntax-level check (would also catch malformed stub/source code) with no phpstan-rs equivalent.

core-types.name: AcceptsResult
core-types.description: Value object wrapping a TrinaryLogic result plus a list of human-readable reasons explaining why a Type::accepts() check failed, with and()/or()/extremeIdentity()/maxMin()/lazyMaxMin() combinators used throughout the double-dispatch accepts() protocol.
core-types.notes: phpstan-rs's type-compatibility check (`is_subtype(sub, sup) -> bool`) is a single boolean with no TrinaryLogic maybe-state and no accumulated human-readable reasons for diagnostics. Real PHPStan uses accepts()/AcceptsResult specifically to explain *why* an argument type mismatches in error messages; phpstan-rs diagnostics construct their explanation text ad hoc at each call site instead. The reasons-accumulation architecture itself is not present.

core-types.name: ArrayType
core-types.description: The general (non-constant) array Type implementation: separate key/item types, isList()/isCallable()/offset get-set-unset, array_* built-in return-type helpers (slice, splice, flip, intersectKey, changeKeyCase, truncateListToSize, etc.), and template-type inference over array key/value.
core-types.our_location: src/types.rs Type::Array(Box<Type>) (line 26), Type::ArrayShape (line 36), src/checker/calls.rs array builtin handling
core-types.notes: Rust's `Type::Array(Box<Type>)` carries only a single value type and no independent key type (real PHPStan's `array<K,V>` two-parameter form is not modeled at all - keys are implicitly int|string). List-ness is tracked structurally via `ArrayShape` field-name-is-sequential-index checks and the `AccessoryKind::ArrayList` intersection member, not via a general `isList(): TrinaryLogic` on every array type. Several array-mutation helpers (setOffsetValueType, unsetOffset, spliceArray, changeKeyCaseArray, fillKeysArray, intersectKeyArray, truncateListToSize) have narrow, ad-hoc counterparts scattered in checker/calls.rs and checker/expr.rs for specific built-in functions rather than a uniform Type-level API.

core-types.name: BenevolentUnionType
core-types.description: A UnionType subclass used for the implicit int|string type PHP gives array keys and other benevolent contexts - describes with parentheses, and every union-producing operation (filterTypes, tryRemove, traverse, getOffsetValueType) re-wraps its result back into a BenevolentUnionType instead of a plain UnionType so identity is preserved through transformations.
core-types.notes: No distinct benevolent-union concept exists; phpstan-rs's plain `Type::Union` is used uniformly. This is a narrow architectural nuance of PHPStan's own type-identity tracking (array key types, mixed-key iteration) with no direct behavioral gap for the diagnostics phpstan-rs currently targets, but the concept - and its describe()-with-parens special-casing referenced by ArrayType::__construct - is absent.

core-types.name: BitwiseFlagHelper
core-types.description: DI-registered helper that determines (as TrinaryLogic) whether a given flag constant is definitely/maybe/never present in a bitwise-OR'd expression of int constants - used by rules that check e.g. `preg_match` or `json_encode` flag arguments.
core-types.notes: phpstan-rs has narrow, function-specific flag parsing (`parse_preg_flags` for PREG_* constants used by preg_match/preg_split) but no general-purpose helper that walks an arbitrary bitwise-OR expression tree and resolves constant references through the symbol table the way BitwiseFlagHelper does generically for any function's flag parameter.

core-types.name: BooleanType
core-types.description: The general (non-constant) bool Type implementation: toInteger/toFloat/toString/toArray coercions, toCoercedArgumentType for weak-typing argument coercion, isTrue()/isFalse() both return maybe, tryRemove(ConstantBooleanType) narrows to the opposite constant, getFiniteTypes() enumerates {true,false}.
core-types.notes: Bool/True/False exist as type variants and participate in subtyping and narrowing (checker/narrowing.rs handles is_bool()-style checks), but there is no toInteger/toFloat/toString/toArray coercion modeling, no toCoercedArgumentType weak-typing union construction, and no getFiniteTypes()-style exhaustive-case enumeration used for match/switch completeness checking on bool.

core-types.name: CallableAssertionsHelper
core-types.description: Converts a callable's conditional-return-type predicate (`callable(mixed $v): ($v is int ? true : false)`) to/from Assertions/AssertTag objects so that invoking such a callable in an `if` condition narrows its argument via TypeSpecifier, and infers template types from a passed callable's own assertions matching by parameter position.
core-types.our_location: n/a - no @phpstan-assert or conditional-return-type support anywhere in src/docblock.rs or src/checker/narrowing.rs
core-types.notes: grep confirms src/docblock.rs has zero handling of `@phpstan-assert`/AssertTag, and the docblock parser explicitly documents (comment near line 179) that it does not parse conditional return types (`is`/`?`/`:`) at all. This entire narrowing-via-callable-predicate mechanism (used by is_int()/is_string()/etc.'s own stub signatures) is absent; narrowing.rs implements is_*() narrowing via hardcoded match arms per function name instead of a general assertion mechanism.

core-types.name: CallableType
core-types.description: Structural `callable(ParamType, ...): ReturnType` Type/CallableParametersAcceptor implementation with parameter list, variadic/purity/static flags, template type map, assertions, and full isSuperTypeOf/accepts logic comparing parameter contravariance and return covariance against any other callable-like type.
core-types.notes: `Type::Callable` is a bare marker with no parameter list, return type, purity, or template map - none of the PHPDoc `callable(int, string): bool` signature syntax is captured structurally, so no parameter/return-type checking against a declared callable signature is possible. Closures/callables passed around are only checked by structural body-walk (checker/expr.rs), not by matching against a CallableType contract.

core-types.name: CallableTypeHelper
core-types.description: Static helper implementing isParametersAcceptorSuperTypeOf() - compares two callable signatures' parameters (with variadic-parameter padding, optional-vs-required mismatches) and return types to decide substitutability, with detailed reason strings for the maybe/no cases.
core-types.notes: Depends entirely on CallableType/ClosureType/CallableParametersAcceptor's structural signature representation (see above), which phpstan-rs does not have; no equivalent parameter-by-parameter callable-signature comparison exists.

core-types.name: CircularTypeAliasDefinitionException
core-types.description: A trivial marker Exception subclass (10 lines, no body) thrown internally while resolving a `@phpstan-type` alias that refers to itself, caught by the type-alias resolver to produce a CircularTypeAliasErrorType instead of infinite recursion.
core-types.notes: phpstan-rs has no `@phpstan-type`/`@phpstan-import-type` alias support at all (confirmed via grep of src/docblock.rs and src/parser/*), so there is no alias-resolution recursion to guard against. Building this exception class alone would be meaningless without the alias feature it protects; it is not a candidate for standalone implementation, though the missing alias feature itself is a real gap that would need its own item outside this file list.

core-types.name: CircularTypeAliasErrorType
core-types.description: A trivial ErrorType subclass (one line body) returned in place of a type alias that was found to be circularly self-referential, so downstream code can distinguish this specific error condition from a generic unresolvable type if needed.
core-types.notes: Same reasoning as CircularTypeAliasDefinitionException: this exists purely to support the `@phpstan-type` alias feature, which phpstan-rs does not implement. phpstan-rs's general unknown/unresolved-type fallback is `Type::Mixed`, with no distinct error-type hierarchy at all.

core-types.name: ClassConstantAccessType
core-types.description: A LateResolvableType representing `Foo::SOME_CONST` written as a PHPDoc type (e.g. in `@template T of self::TYPE_*`) - lazily resolves to the constant's value type once the enclosing type is concrete, used for `static::class_const_name`-style symbolic constant references in generic bounds.
core-types.our_location: n/a (Type::ClassConstAccess grep - src/checker/narrowing.rs:621 handles Foo::class expr resolution, not PHPDoc const-typed generics)
core-types.notes: phpstan-rs resolves `Foo::CONST` as an *expression* (narrowing.rs) to get its runtime value type, but there is no PHPDoc-type-position support for writing `self::CONST_NAME` as a generic template bound/type - the `types.rs` Type enum has no variant for a late-resolvable class-constant-access type, and the docblock parser has no syntax for it.

core-types.name: ClassNameToObjectTypeResult
core-types.description: A tiny value object (Type + uncertainty bool) returned when projecting a class-name-or-object Type to its ObjectType for an instanceof/is_a check - the uncertainty flag marks when the projection lost precision (e.g. a runtime class-string kept symbolic) so callers know the yes/no answer that follows isn't fully reliable.
core-types.notes: phpstan-rs's instanceof/is_a narrowing works directly off resolved class names in the registry (no class-string-to-object projection step with its own uncertainty bookkeeping) since it doesn't model dynamic class-string types with the same generality PHPStan does; there is no equivalent intermediate result object, and none is architecturally needed given the simpler, more direct narrowing path taken.

core-types.name: ClassStringType
core-types.description: A StringType subclass representing the bare (non-generic) `class-string` PHPDoc type - describes as 'class-string', reports isClassString() yes and isNonEmptyString/isNonFalsyString yes, and getClassStringObjectType() returns an unconstrained ObjectWithoutClassType.
core-types.notes: phpstan-rs's `ClassString(Box<Type>)` covers both the generic `class-string<T>` form and, per the comment at line 33, collapses a bare `class-string` (no `<T>`) to `ClassString(Box::new(Type::Mixed))`-equivalent handling in parse_type_keyword_or_class - actually a strict improvement over PHPStan's separate bare-vs-generic class hierarchy (GenericClassStringType extends this) since phpstan-rs unifies both into one variant that always carries an inner type.

core-types.name: ClosureType
core-types.description: The 1011-line structural Closure Type/CallableParametersAcceptor implementation: parameters, return type, variadic/pure/static flags, template maps, throw points, impure points, invalidate-expressions (for method-call cache invalidation), used-variables, assertions, plus full reflection delegation (getMethod/getProperty/getConstant) to the real Closure class and rich isSuperTypeOf/traverse/describe logic mirroring CallableType.
core-types.notes: Every closure-literal expression in phpstan-rs infers the flat marker `Object("Closure", [])`, discarding all parameter/return-type/purity information from the closure's own signature. There is no structural CallableParametersAcceptor equivalent, so nothing downstream can check a Closure-typed value's call signature against an expected callable contract, infer template types through it, or track its throw/impurity/used-variable set the way real PHPStan's ClosureType does.

core-types.name: ClosureTypeFactory
core-types.description: DI service that builds a ClosureType from a live PHP `Closure` object via BetterReflection (used internally by PHPStan's own bootstrap/extension code to reflect closures at runtime, not by ordinary static analysis of user code).
core-types.notes: This factory reflects an already-*running* PHP Closure object (via ReflectionFunction/BetterReflection) - a runtime-introspection capability with no meaning for a static analyzer parsing source text; phpstan-rs never has a live Closure object to reflect. The underlying gap (ClosureType's structural richness) is already captured under ClosureType above.

core-types.name: CompoundType
core-types.description: Marker interface implementing PHPStan's double-dispatch protocol (isAcceptedBy/isSubTypeOf/isGreaterThan/isGreaterThanOrEqual) so composite types (unions, intersections, mixed, never, accessory types, ranges, callables, conditionals) can decompose themselves when a simple type's accepts()/isSuperTypeOf() encounters them as the argument.
core-types.our_location: src/types.rs is_subtype (line 779, notably the Union/Intersection match arms at 840-858)
core-types.notes: Rust has no OOP double-dispatch mechanism, and none is needed: `is_subtype` is a single recursive match function that already handles the same union/intersection member-wise decomposition this interface exists to coordinate (e.g. `(Type::Union(members), _) => members.iter().all(...)`, `(Type::Intersection(_), Type::Intersection(sup_members)) => ...`). The interface itself is pure architecture with no behavior of its own; its behavioral contract is present, just implemented as one function instead of a dispatch protocol across many classes.

core-types.name: ConditionalType
core-types.description: A LateResolvableType/CompoundType representing PHPDoc's `($subject is Target ? If : Else)` conditional return type - resolves once the subject-vs-target relationship is decidable, substituting the subject type (intersected or type-removed) into occurrences within the if/else branches, or unioning both branches when undecidable (still template-dependent).
core-types.our_location: n/a - confirmed absent, src/docblock.rs comment near line 179 states conditional types are deliberately not parsed
core-types.notes: No type variant, parser syntax, or resolver exists for conditional return types anywhere in the codebase. This blocks correctly inferring the return type of any stub/PHPDoc function declared with a conditional return (a common pattern for is_*() predicates and array_key_exists-style functions in real PHPStan stubs, though phpstan-rs's own built-in-function modeling sidesteps this by hardcoding return types per function name in checker/calls.rs instead).

core-types.name: ConditionalTypeForParameter
core-types.description: The parameter-name-keyed variant of ConditionalType used directly in a function/method's own `@return` PHPDoc (`($paramName is Target ? If : Else)`) before the parameter name is bound to an actual argument expression - converts to a full ConditionalType via toConditional() once a call site supplies the subject.
core-types.notes: Same root cause as ConditionalType: no conditional-return-type syntax is parsed at all, so there is no parameter-name-keyed intermediate form either. Functions like is_int()/is_array()/is_callable() that PHPStan's own stubs express via this exact mechanism are instead special-cased by function name directly in checker/narrowing.rs and checker/calls.rs in phpstan-rs, which covers the common built-in cases but gives no general mechanism for user-authored or third-party-stub conditional-return functions.

core-types.name: ConstantScalarType
core-types.description: Marker interface implemented by ConstantIntegerType/ConstantFloatType/ConstantStringType/ConstantBooleanType/NullType, exposing getValue() and letting callers do Type::isConstantValue()/getConstantScalarTypes() instead of instanceof-chasing every literal type.
core-types.notes: The literal values themselves are first-class enum variants, but there is no unifying accessor equivalent to isConstantValue()/getValue()/getConstantScalarTypes() - every call site pattern-matches the individual variants directly instead of going through one shared check.

core-types.name: ConstantTypeHelper
core-types.description: Static getTypeFromValue(mixed): Type - converts an actual runtime PHP value (used for reflection-derived constants, default values, attribute args) into the right Constant*Type/NullType/ObjectType/EnumCaseObjectType, recursively building arrays via ConstantArrayTypeBuilder with a count-limit degrade-to-general-array safety valve.
core-types.notes: phpstan-rs never executes PHP, so the scalar half of this conversion happens at parse time straight from AST literal nodes (int/float/string/bool/null all covered), but there is no array-literal folding into a shaped constant-array type and no object/enum-instance conversion path.

core-types.name: DirectTypeAliasResolverProvider
core-types.description: One-method DI-wiring class implementing TypeAliasResolverProvider by simply returning the injected TypeAliasResolver singleton - zero logic of its own.
core-types.notes: Pure dependency-injection plumbing with no behavior; a rewrite has nothing to port here regardless of whether @phpstan-type alias support itself exists elsewhere (it currently doesn't - registry.rs:871 explicitly notes unresolved-@phpstan-type-alias values are left as-is rather than resolved, but that's a different file's gap, not this one's).

core-types.name: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension
core-types.description: Plugin interface (isFunctionSupported/getTypeFromFunctionCall) letting third-party extensions compute a function call's return type dynamically based on argument types/values, registered via the phpstan.broker.dynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension service tag.
core-types.notes: Consolidated as a single large match-on-function-name dispatch (array_map, array_filter, str_replace, version_compare, array_search, preg_* via preg_shapes.rs, etc.) rather than a registered-extension framework - functionally equivalent for the many builtins actually covered, architecturally a compiled table instead of a plugin registry.

core-types.name: DynamicFunctionThrowTypeExtension
core-types.description: Plugin interface letting extensions say what exception type(s) a specific function call throws, feeding dead-catch/uncaught-exception analysis.
core-types.notes: phpstan-rs has no throw-type inference of any kind - grep for throw_type/ThrowType/@throws across src/ returns nothing, so there is no dead-catch or uncaught-exception checking this extension point would even feed into.

core-types.name: DynamicMethodReturnTypeExtension
core-types.description: Plugin interface (getClass/isMethodSupported/getTypeFromMethodCall) for computing a non-static method call's return type dynamically; real PHPStan ships dozens of core implementations for PDOStatement, ReflectionClass, DateTime, ArrayObject, etc.
core-types.notes: Only a handful of ad hoc method-name special cases exist; the breadth of real PHPStan's built-in dynamic-method extensions (PDOStatement::fetch mode-dependent types, ReflectionClass::isSubclassOf narrowing, DateTime::modify, etc.) has no counterpart, and there is no general per-class extension framework - just scattered matches in expr.rs.

core-types.name: DynamicMethodThrowTypeExtension
core-types.description: Throw-type variant of DynamicMethodReturnTypeExtension for non-static method calls.
core-types.notes: Same as the function-throw-type extension: no throw-type system exists anywhere in phpstan-rs to plug into.

core-types.name: DynamicReturnTypeExtensionRegistry
core-types.description: Runtime service that indexes all registered Dynamic{Method,StaticMethod}ReturnTypeExtensions by lowercased declaring-class name (via ExtensionClassHelper's ancestor+interface walk) and all DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtensions by isFunctionSupported(), memoizing both lookups.
core-types.our_location: src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs (function side); src/checker/expr.rs scattered method-name matches (method side)
core-types.notes: No runtime registry object exists at all - there's no plugin system to index. The function-call side of what this registry enables is well covered by builtin_calls.rs's compiled dispatch; the method-call side is thin, ad hoc, and not indexed by class hierarchy the way real PHPStan's registry does.

core-types.name: DynamicStaticMethodReturnTypeExtension
core-types.description: Static-method variant of the return-type extension interface (getClass/isStaticMethodSupported/getTypeFromStaticMethodCall) - real PHPStan's own core ClosureBindDynamicReturnTypeExtension implements exactly this for Closure::bind().
core-types.notes: The single most important real-world instance of this interface (Closure::bind's $this-rebinding + return-type behavior) is directly hardcoded and works; the general interface/framework for other static methods is absent.

core-types.name: DynamicStaticMethodThrowTypeExtension
core-types.description: Throw-type variant of DynamicStaticMethodReturnTypeExtension for static method calls.
core-types.notes: Same reason as the other two throw-type extension interfaces: no throw-type system exists in phpstan-rs.

core-types.name: ErrorType
core-types.description: A MixedType subclass that marks "type resolution failed here" distinctly from a deliberately-written mixed - describe()s as '*ERROR*' at the top verbosity level, and has self-identity equals()/subtract() so it doesn't get silently absorbed into other mixed handling.
core-types.our_location: src/types.rs (14 raw Type::Mixed fallback sites, no distinct sentinel)
core-types.notes: Every unresolvable/failed type-resolution path in phpstan-rs collapses straight to plain Type::Mixed with no way to later distinguish "genuinely unknown/mixed" from "resolution errored out here" - this loses the cascading-error-suppression signal real PHPStan uses ErrorType for, though day-to-day accepts()/isSuperTypeOf() behavior is unaffected since ErrorType behaves like Mixed anyway.

core-types.name: ExponentiateHelper
core-types.description: Dedicated static exponentiate(base, exponent): Type for PHP's ** operator - unions over a union exponent, gates to ErrorType for a non-numeric-string operand, constant-folds two ConstantScalarTypes (including per-value pow() with int/float result classification) and IntegerRangeType exponents, special-cases exponent 0/1, and falls back to a float/int BenevolentUnionType otherwise.
core-types.notes: Pow is folded into the exact same arm as Sub/Mul: "Float if either operand is Float, else Int". This matches real PHPStan's own coarse fallback shape, but none of the precision machinery exists - no constant-literal pow() computation, no IntegerRangeType-aware exponentiation, no ErrorType gating for a non-numeric-string base/exponent, no exponent-0/1 special casing.

core-types.name: ExpressionTypeResolverExtension
core-types.description: Plugin escape hatch (getType(Expr, Scope): ?Type) letting a third-party extension resolve the type of an arbitrary expression PHPStan's own resolver doesn't otherwise know about, registered via phpstan.broker.expressionTypeResolverExtension.
core-types.notes: Pure third-party extension point with no core PHPStan implementations to port. phpstan-rs's own equivalent - resolving the type of any expression - already lives directly and exhaustively in infer_expr's own match over ExprKind in src/checker/expr.rs; there is no separate seam for an external hook to plug into, nor is one architecturally needed for a closed, from-scratch checker.

core-types.name: ExtensionClassHelper
core-types.description: Static, statically-cached helper returning a class's own name plus every parent class and interface name (two variants: one via ReflectionProvider for analysed code, one via PHP's own class_parents/class_implements for extension classes loaded at runtime) - used to match a receiver's whole ancestor chain against registered dynamic-extension classes.
core-types.our_location: src/registry.rs is_subclass_of / lookup_in_hierarchy (general-purpose equivalent, used for other purposes)
core-types.notes: The specific purpose this helper serves - indexing dynamic-return-type extensions by every ancestor/interface name - has no counterpart because phpstan-rs has no runtime plugin-extension system to index against. The underlying capability it would need (walking a class's full ancestor+interface chain) already exists independently in registry.rs, just serving method/property resolution instead.

core-types.name: FileTypeMapper
core-types.description: Central, heavily-cached service building the per-location NameScope (namespace, use-imports, class/function/trait context, @template inheritance across trait boundaries with use-tag template-argument substitution, @phpstan-type alias maps, phan/psalm/phpstan tag-prefix priority resolution) that every PHPDoc type gets resolved against; caches both a whole file's name-scope map (content-hash-keyed, on disk) and individual resolved PHPDoc blocks (in-memory LRU).
core-types.our_location: src/docblock.rs (stateless per-comment tag parser); src/registry/name_context.rs (NameContext: namespace + use resolution)
core-types.notes: docblock.rs parses one raw doc-comment string at a time with zero notion of namespace/use/class/trait context or caching; NameContext separately does namespace+use resolution for the whole file (not per-docblock-location) with no trait-template-inheritance propagation and no @phpstan-type alias resolution (registry.rs:871 explicitly leaves such aliases unresolved). No file-content-hash caching layer of any kind exists - the whole two-cache-tier design (on-disk name-scope map + in-memory resolved-phpdoc LRU) is absent, though nothing in this from-scratch checker currently needs incremental-analysis-grade caching.

core-types.name: FiniteTypeSet
core-types.description: Identity-keyed hashmap over a UnionType's finite-valued members (null/int/bool/string constants, enum cases) letting membership/superset checks in accepts()/isSuperTypeOf()/equals() run in O(1)/O(n+m) instead of an O(n*m) pairwise scan for large unions (e.g. big string-literal enums).
core-types.our_location: src/types.rs lines 840-841 (is_subtype: members.iter().all/any over a plain Vec<Type>)
core-types.notes: Type::Union is a flat Vec<Type> compared with plain nested iteration - correct but O(n*m). This is purely a performance optimization for pathologically large finite unions (PHPStan's own docstring frames it exactly that way) with no correctness difference from the plain scan; low priority unless a corpus surfaces a large enum-like string-literal union that makes union comparisons a measured hotspot.

core-types.name: FloatType
core-types.description: Concrete Type implementation for PHP's float scalar type: accepts()/isSuperTypeOf() (accepts int too), equals(), describe(), toNumber/toFloat/toInteger/toBitwiseNotType/toArray/toArrayKey/toCoercedArgumentType (widens to int|float|string|bool in non-strict mode), looseCompare(), exponentiate() delegating to ExponentiateHelper, and the full battery of is*() trinary-logic queries (isFloat=yes, everything else no).
core-types.our_location: src/types.rs Type::Float variant, plus scattered match arms (describe at line 106, hint-parsing at 618, union membership at 671-672, is_subtype coercion rules at 792-807, arithmetic at expr.rs 2399-2429)
core-types.notes: Float is a bare unit variant rather than its own polymorphic class - the same flat-enum-with-scattered-match-arms shape used throughout this rewrite. Core semantics (int-accepts-into-float coercion, being scalar/numeric, arithmetic float-promotion, string/int conversion) are all present; more obscure single-purpose methods like toBitwiseNotType/isOffsetAccessLegal weren't individually traced but the load-bearing behavior is there.

core-types.name: FunctionParameterClosureThisExtension
core-types.description: Plugin interface letting a third-party extension say what $this type a Closure argument should be analysed with when passed into a specific function call (e.g. a framework's own array-callback-style API), registered via phpstan.functionParameterClosureThisExtension.
core-types.notes: Grep of vendor/phpstan-src/src for 'implements FunctionParameterClosureThisExtension' finds zero core implementations - this exists solely for third-party framework integrations, out of scope for a from-scratch core rewrite. phpstan-rs's own Closure $this-rebinding (Closure::bind/bindTo, hardcoded in src/checker/expr.rs) addresses an unrelated case - the closure's own bind call, not a generic function-parameter mechanism - and isn't a substitute for this extension point.

core-types.name: FunctionParameterClosureTypeExtension
core-types.description: Pure extension interface (isFunctionSupported/getTypeFromFunctionCall) letting a service infer a closure argument's real parameter types from the specific function call it's passed to; core PHPStan ships 5 built-in implementers (ArrayMap/ArrayFilter/ArrayWalk/ArrayFind/PregReplaceCallback ParameterClosureTypeExtension) that give e.g. array_map's callback the array's element type as its param type.
core-types.notes: The plugin interface itself is DI wiring (not_applicable to port), but the underlying built-in behavior it enables is a real, checked-for gap: grepped src/checker/calls.rs and expr.rs for usort/array_map/array_filter/array_walk closure handling and found none - closures passed to these functions get no parameter-type inference from array element type, so a closure param typed loosely (or untyped) inside array_map/array_filter/usort/array_walk is never checked against the actual element type.

core-types.name: FunctionParameterOutTypeExtension
core-types.description: Pure extension interface (isFunctionSupported/getParameterOutTypeFromFunctionCall) for computing a by-ref parameter's post-call type dynamically per call site; core implementers include PregMatchParameterOutTypeExtension, ParseStrParameterOutTypeExtension, OpenSslEncryptParameterOutTypeExtension.
core-types.notes: No general extension mechanism (expected, no plugin architecture), but the equivalent capability is hardcoded for the highest-value cases: preg_match's $matches shape, and sort/rsort/usort/shuffle/array_push/array_unshift/array_shift/array_pop's list-preserving mutation of their by-ref array. parse_str's and openssl_encrypt's by-ref outputs are not specifically modeled (fall through to the generic declared-type widening).

core-types.name: FunctionTypeSpecifyingExtension
core-types.description: Pure extension interface for type-narrowing effects of function calls used as conditions (e.g. is_int($x), method_exists($x,'y'), in_array($x,$arr)); core PHPStan ships ~24 implementers covering is_array/is_string/is_callable/in_array/array_key_exists/method_exists/property_exists/strlen/ctype_digit/count/assert/class_exists/function_exists/etc.
core-types.notes: No formal extension interface (not needed - single binary), but the functional behavior for the common is_*() family plus in_array/array_key_exists narrowing is hardcoded in narrowing.rs, matching the intent of these core extensions for the highest-traffic cases; coverage of the full ~24-extension roster (e.g. ctype_digit, is_a, is_subclass_of) was not individually verified line-by-line.

core-types.name: GeneralizePrecision
core-types.description: Value-object enum (lessSpecific/moreSpecific/templateArgument) controlling how aggressively Type::generalize() widens a type when merging across loop iterations or branches, e.g. deciding whether a constant string widens to plain string or stays non-empty-string.
core-types.notes: No general Type::generalize()-with-precision-levels API exists in types.rs; type widening across branches/loops is instead handled ad hoc via union_types (simple branch-merge) and a narrower array-shape-specific generalize_by_key_set helper, without the 3-level precision control (lessSpecific/moreSpecific/templateArgument) real PHPStan uses to decide how much detail survives generalization.

core-types.name: InstanceofDeprecated
core-types.description: A PHP #[Attribute] marker (no logic) applied to Type subclasses to flag that user code should not `instanceof` them directly; consumed only by ApiInstanceofTypeRule, a lint rule for PHPStan-extension authors' own code.
core-types.notes: Pure marker attribute plus a meta-lint rule that checks third-party PHPStan-extension source code for instanceof misuse against PHPStan's own Type API - phpstan-rs has no plugin/extension ecosystem for this rule to protect, so there is nothing to build.

core-types.name: IntegerRangeType
core-types.description: Type subclass for int<min,max> ranges (positive-int, non-negative-int, etc.), with full range arithmetic: shift, exponentiate, toAbsoluteNumber, toBitwiseNotType, tryUnion/tryIntersect/tryRemove preserving bounds, isSmallerThan/isGreaterThan comparisons against the range edges, and getFiniteTypes() enumeration for small ranges.
core-types.notes: The range is represented and used for positive-int/negative-int/etc. parsing and basic subtyping (min/max containment), but most of the rich arithmetic in the PHP class is absent: no shift(), no range-preserving exponentiate (src/checker/expr.rs:2689 just collapses IntRange to plain Int for some operations), no toAbsoluteNumber/toBitwiseNotType preserving bounds, no comparison-to-range-edge logic for isSmallerThan/isGreaterThan, no getFiniteTypes() enumeration.

core-types.name: IntegerType
core-types.description: The base int Type class: describe()='int', plus conversion methods (toFloat, toString with AccessoryDecimalIntegerStringType, toArray, toCoercedArgumentType widening under weak typing, toBitwiseNotType, toAbsoluteNumber returning non-negative-int) and looseCompare() honoring PHP 8's non-numeric-string-vs-int loose-comparison change.
core-types.notes: Type::Int exists as a plain enum variant with subtyping/describe support, but none of IntegerType's conversion methods (toFloat/toString/toArray/toCoercedArgumentType/toBitwiseNotType/toAbsoluteNumber) or its PHP-version-aware looseCompare() exist as general Type operations in types.rs - grepped for to_number/to_string_type/coerce/to_absolute and found nothing; any such conversions are handled ad hoc per call site in expr.rs instead of centrally on the type.

core-types.name: IntersectionType
core-types.description: Large (~2000-line) CompoundType implementation representing T1&T2&...: describe() with special-cased rendering for list/non-empty-array/accessory-string intersections, accepts/isSuperTypeOf/isSubTypeOf/isAcceptedBy double-dispatch, and dozens of array/iterable/callable/property/method delegating operations (getOffsetValueType, popArray, shiftArray, sliceArray, getCallableParametersAcceptors combining multiple callable signatures via CombinationsHelper, etc.) that intersect the per-member results.
core-types.notes: Intersection exists and is actively used for the accessory-type idiom (non-empty-string, list<T>, non-empty-array<T>, numeric-string) with correct subtyping and describe formatting for those specific cases - the highest-value real-world use. Not implemented: general object&object intersection types (interface&interface), the callable-intersected-with-array special-casing (isCallable && isArray branches throughout the PHP file), and the many array-operation delegators (popArray/shiftArray/sliceArray/spliceArray/getCallableParametersAcceptors combining multiple callable signatures) - phpstan-rs's array operations are implemented directly on Type::Array/ArrayShape rather than generically intersecting arbitrary member types.

core-types.name: IsSuperTypeOfResult
core-types.description: Value object wrapping a TrinaryLogic (yes/no/maybe) result of a supertype check together with human-readable reasons (eager and lazy) explaining the relationship, with combinators (and/or/negate/extremeIdentity/maxMin/lazyMaxMin) used pervasively across every Type::isSuperTypeOf() implementation.
core-types.notes: phpstan-rs's type-relationship check is a plain bool-returning is_subtype(sub, sup) function - grepped types.rs and checker/*.rs for TrinaryLogic/AcceptsResult/reasons and found none. This is an architectural simplification: no three-valued Yes/No/Maybe distinction (Maybe collapses to either true or false somewhere in is_subtype's match arms) and no structured 'why doesn't this type fit' reasons attached to comparisons, so diagnostic messages can't explain a type mismatch the way real PHPStan's reason strings do.

core-types.name: IterableType
core-types.description: CompoundType for iterable<K,V> = array<K,V>|Traversable<K,V>, with accepts()/isSuperTypeOf() that unify array and Traversable membership, toArrayOrTraversable() union expansion, template-type inference across both branches, and describe() collapsing to bare 'iterable' when both key/value are unrefined mixed.
core-types.notes: No dedicated IterableType variant; iterable<V>/iterable<K,V> is parsed directly into Type::Union([Array(V), <Traversable-like object>]) at parse time (comment explicitly notes this fixes 'iterable' being wrongly treated as bare array). This covers the common accepts-a-value case reasonably via the existing Union subtyping, but loses the dedicated key/value-type accessors, the isSuperTypeOfMixed's explicit-vs-implicit-mixed distinction, and toArrayOrTraversable() being computed once rather than baked into the parse.

core-types.name: JustNullableTypeTrait
core-types.description: Shared PHP trait providing default accepts/isSuperTypeOf/equals/traverse and all the isXxx()->No() boilerplate for simple, non-composite scalar Type classes (IntegerType, StringType, BooleanType, ResourceType, NonexistentParentClassType all `use` it).
core-types.notes: phpstan-rs has no trait-based per-class dispatch (Type is a single Rust enum, not an OOP class hierarchy), so there is no direct file-for-file equivalent, but the behavior the trait centralizes - simple scalar types accepting only themselves, equals-by-variant, no-op traverse - is exactly what the single is_subtype/equals match statements over the Type enum already provide for Int/String/Bool/Resource-like variants; the consolidation is architectural, not a missing capability.

core-types.name: KeyOfType
core-types.description: LateResolvableType implementing PHPDoc's key-of<T> generic, deferring resolution (via LateResolvableTypeTrait) until any TemplateType inside T is resolved, then resolving to T's iterable key type.
core-types.notes: Grepped docblock.rs, registry.rs, and types.rs for "key-of"/"KeyOf" and found no matches anywhere in src/ - the key-of<T> PHPDoc generic syntax is not parsed or resolved at all.

core-types.name: LateResolvableType
core-types.description: Marker interface (resolve()/isResolvable()) for types like KeyOfType/ValueOfType/OffsetAccessType whose final shape depends on a TemplateType that isn't resolved yet at parse time; NodeScopeResolver re-resolves these once generic bindings are known.
core-types.notes: No late-resolution machinery exists in types.rs - phpstan-rs's template/generic substitution (substitute_template, seen in checker/calls.rs) appears to resolve template types eagerly at call sites rather than deferring resolution of derived types like key-of/value-of/offset-access, and since key-of/value-of aren't implemented at all (see KeyOfType), there is nothing yet needing this deferral mechanism.

core-types.name: LazyTypeAliasResolverProvider
core-types.description: Trivial DI-container lazy-wrapper (#[AutowiredService]) that fetches the real TypeAliasResolver from the container on demand, breaking a circular-dependency wiring problem - contains zero resolution logic of its own.
core-types.notes: Pure Nette-DI lazy-service-lookup wrapper with no logic to port; phpstan-rs has no DI container. Separately (not this file's concern but worth flagging), the underlying @phpstan-type alias feature this DI chain ultimately serves is itself only leniently tolerated rather than resolved in phpstan-rs - registry.rs:871 shows @phpstan-type aliases are treated with parse leniency, not actually resolved to their target type.

core-types.name: LooseComparisonHelper
core-types.description: Static helper computing the PHP-version-aware result of `==` between two ConstantScalarType values, handling the numeric-string-vs-number special cases (including the pre-8.0 vs 8.0+ 'numeric string' comparison semantics) before falling back to PHP's native `==` operator.
core-types.notes: infer_binary's BinOp::Eq/NotEq/Identical/NotIdentical/comparisons all just return plain Type::Bool unconditionally (checked directly) - there is no constant-folding of `==`/`!=` between literal operands into a ConstantBooleanType, so phpstan-rs cannot flag or narrow always-true/always-false loose comparisons the way real PHPStan's LooseComparisonHelper-backed IntegerType/StringType::looseCompare() implementations do (e.g. "0 == 'foo'" evaluating to a knowable false).

core-types.name: MethodParameterClosureThisExtension
core-types.description: Pure extension interface for dynamically specifying the $this binding of a closure argument to a method call; grepped phpstan-src core and found zero built-in implementers - it exists purely for third-party extension packages (e.g. framework-specific test/DI libraries) to hook into.
core-types.notes: Core PHPStan itself has no built-in implementer of this interface (Closure::bind/bindTo are instead handled via a separate ClosureBindDynamicReturnTypeExtension, unrelated to this file) - it is purely a plugin hook for third-party packages, which phpstan-rs's monolithic architecture has no analog for. Coincidentally, phpstan-rs does implement the same *conceptual* behavior (closure-argument $this rebinding) hardcoded specifically for Pest's it/test/describe functions - not via any extension mechanism, and not because of this particular interface.

core-types.name: MethodParameterClosureTypeExtension
core-types.description: Pure extension interface, the method-call counterpart to FunctionParameterClosureTypeExtension, for inferring a closure argument's parameter types from the specific method call it's passed to (e.g. Collection::map($fn) inferring $fn's param from the collection's element type in framework-specific extension packages).
core-types.notes: No core phpstan-src implementers found (grepped 'implements MethodParameterClosureTypeExtension' across src/, zero matches) - purely a third-party/framework extension hook (Laravel/Doctrine collection-style fluent APIs), not exercised by PHPStan's own built-in rule set, so there's no core behavior for phpstan-rs to replicate.

core-types.name: MethodParameterOutTypeExtension
core-types.description: Pure extension interface, the method-call counterpart to FunctionParameterOutTypeExtension, for computing a by-ref method parameter's post-call type dynamically (e.g. DateTime-like or DB-driver-specific by-ref outputs in third-party extension packages).
core-types.notes: No core phpstan-src implementers found (grepped 'implements MethodParameterOutTypeExtension' across src/, zero matches) - purely a third-party extension hook with no built-in PHPStan behavior riding on it, so nothing in core analysis depends on phpstan-rs having this mechanism.

core-types.name: MethodTypeSpecifyingExtension
core-types.description: Pure DI extension interface (getClass/isMethodSupported/specifyTypes) that lets third-party packages register custom instance-method-call type narrowing (e.g. PHPUnit's assertInstanceOf, container has()/get() bridges) into TypeSpecifier.
core-types.notes: Plugin-extension interface with no config/DI system in phpstan-rs to register against. The narrowing *behavior* this interface exists to enable is hardcoded directly as match arms in src/checker/narrowing.rs (assertInstanceOf, assertIsString, assertIsArray, etc. around lines 504-556) rather than through an extensible interface, matching the project's stated approach of consolidating extension points into single match arms.

core-types.name: MixedType
core-types.description: The `mixed` Type implementation: top type accepting everything, tracks isExplicitMixed vs implicit and an optional subtractedType (from prior instanceof/is_*() narrowing), and implements ~20 to*()/is*() coercion and array-shape-transform methods used throughout the type system.
core-types.our_location: src/types.rs Type::Mixed (unit variant); registry.rs/narrowing.rs is_subtype and narrowing arms
core-types.notes: Type::Mixed is a bare unit variant with no subtractedType (post-instanceof-negation narrowing on a mixed-typed value is not tracked) and no isExplicitMixed/implicit distinction (level-9 'could not verify explicit mixed' style checks are not modeled). None of MixedType's toNumber/toBoolean/toArray/exponentiate/getIterableValueType-style coercion methods have Rust equivalents - the type system has no per-Type coercion dispatch at all.

core-types.name: NeverType
core-types.description: The bottom type `never`/unreachable-code marker; carries isExplicit (user-written `never` vs. inferred unreachability) and an optional human-readable reason string, and implements the full Type interface (all coercions collapse to itself, all `is*()` checks are No except isObject-adjacent access checks which are Yes for consistency with unreachable-code semantics).
core-types.notes: Type::Never exists and participates in is_subtype/union normalization, but carries no isExplicit flag or reason string - so there is no way to distinguish a user-written `never` return type from inferred dead-code, and no diagnostic-quality 'why is this never' explanation the way PHPStan's DeadCode rules use getReason(). No coercion methods (toNumber/toArray/etc.) exist for it either.

core-types.name: NewObjectType
core-types.description: A CompoundType/LateResolvableType wrapping the type of `new $expr(...)` where `$expr` isn't a literal class name (a class-string<T> variable, a template type, etc.) - resolves lazily to the constructed object type (or class-string's object type) once the inner type is known.
core-types.notes: `new` on a literal class name (including self/parent/static) is handled directly by constructing Type::Object. `new $className()` where $className is a variable (e.g. a class-string<T> parameter, common in factory/container code) falls straight through to `Type::Mixed` (line 1624, the `_ => Type::Mixed` catch-all) instead of resolving to T's object type - a genuine, fairly common inference gap.

core-types.name: NonAcceptingNeverType
core-types.description: A NeverType subclass used specifically for the native `never` return-type hint (as opposed to inferred unreachability): unlike plain NeverType it does NOT accept() other NeverType-only special-cases the same way, used so template-type inference and explicit-vs-inferred-never distinctions behave correctly.
core-types.our_location: src/types.rs Type::Never (single unit variant, no subclassing)
core-types.notes: phpstan-rs collapses both PHPStan-inferred unreachable code and the native `never` return type hint into the same single Type::Never variant with no accepts()/isSuperTypeOf() distinction between the two, so the specific edge cases NonAcceptingNeverType exists to fix (template binding against an explicit `never` return type) aren't reproduced. Low-severity nuance, not a rule-affecting gap in most real code.

core-types.name: NonexistentParentClassType
core-types.description: The Type substituted for `parent` when used inside a class with no declared parent - describes itself as 'parent', denies all property/method/constant access (hasProperty/hasMethod/hasConstant all No, getters throw ShouldNotHappenException), so the illegal `parent::` usage degrades gracefully into ErrorType-producing operations instead of crashing.
core-types.notes: When a class with no `extends` uses `parent`, resolve_pseudo leaves the type as unresolved Type::ParentRef (falls through to `ty.clone()`) rather than erroring or providing a dedicated sentinel type. types.rs line 887 then treats bare ParentRef as assignable to/from any Object, so no crash occurs, but there's no dedicated 'describes as parent, denies all member access' type - member access on a nonexistent parent isn't specifically flagged the way PHPStan's own NonexistentParentClassType-driven rules would.

core-types.name: NullType
core-types.description: The ConstantScalarType for `null`: isSuperTypeOf/accepts is-self-only, comparison operators (isSmallerThan/isSmallerThanOrEqual using PHP's real `null < x` semantics), and ~15 to*()/is*() coercion methods (toArray → [], toString → '', getGreaterType/getSmallerType for loose-comparison range narrowing).
core-types.our_location: src/types.rs Type::Null (unit variant); registry.rs is_subtype; checker/narrowing.rs null-check narrowing
core-types.notes: Type::Null exists and is used pervasively for nullability checks, null-coalescing, and instanceof-adjacent narrowing (assertNull/assertNotNull in narrowing.rs). No loose-comparison range methods (getSmallerType/getGreaterType, used by real PHPStan for `$x < null`-style narrowing) and no coercion methods (toArray/toString/toNumber) exist anywhere in the type system - this is the same systemic gap noted for MixedType/NeverType.

core-types.name: ObjectShapePropertyReflection
core-types.description: An ExtendedPropertyReflection implementation representing one named/typed property of an ObjectShapeType (`object{foo: int}`) - readable-only (never writable), always public, declaring class is stdClass as a placeholder.
core-types.notes: Pure reflection glue for ObjectShapeType, which is itself unimplemented (see ObjectShapeType below) - there is no PHPDoc `object{...}` shape syntax parsed anywhere in src/docblock.rs, so no property-reflection object for it is needed. Listed not_applicable rather than missing because this specific file has no independent purpose apart from the feature it serves.

core-types.name: ObjectShapeType
core-types.description: PHPDoc `object{prop: Type, opt?: Type}` structural-typing support: a Type representing 'any object with these public readable properties of these types', with full accepts()/isSuperTypeOf() logic that checks each candidate object's actual property visibility/readability/type via reflection, plus optional-property and universal-object-crate (stdClass-like) special-casing.
core-types.notes: Confirmed via grep: no `object{` or ObjectShape token anywhere in docblock.rs, types.rs, or the parser. A `@param object{id: int, name: string} $x`-style PHPDoc annotation is not recognized at all and would presumably fall back to plain `object` or be dropped, losing all structural-property checking. Genuine feature gap, not just simplification.

core-types.name: ObjectType
core-types.description: The core class-instance Type (2000+ lines): class-hierarchy-aware accepts()/isSuperTypeOf() (interface vs final vs regular subclassing, allowed-subtypes/sealed hierarchies), property/method/constant reflection lookup with ancestor resolution and per-description static caching, enum-case enumeration, ArrayAccess-aware offset get/set/unset, ArrayObject/UniversalObjectCrate-aware toArray(), __invoke-based callable detection, GMP/SimpleXMLElement/BcMath\Number-specific numeric/string coercion, isCloneable, ::class resolution, ArrayAccess offsetSet-type-checked assignment, and a subtractedType for instanceof-negation narrowing.
core-types.our_location: src/types.rs Type::Object(String, Vec<Type>); src/registry.rs (class metadata, is_subtype, method/property lookup); src/checker/oop.rs, src/checker/generics.rs
core-types.notes: Core identity, generic type-argument carrying, and class-hierarchy subtyping (interfaces, extends chains, final-class shortcuts) are implemented across registry.rs/oop.rs. Missing/unimplemented relative to the PHP original: no subtractedType (instanceof-negation on an object type is not tracked as precisely), no allowedSubTypes/sealed-hierarchy support, no ArrayAccess-aware offset type checking (no ArrayAccess anywhere in src/), no enum-case-object modeling (no EnumCaseObjectType-equivalent - enum instances are just plain Object), no GMP/SimpleXMLElement/BcMath\Number numeric-coercion special-casing, no __toString-based string coercion, and no per-description LRU caching (the Rust registry doesn't need it given its simpler flat lookups, but that also means no ancestor/ambiguity resolution as sophisticated as getAncestorWithClassName's covariant-return handling).

core-types.name: ObjectWithoutClassType
core-types.description: The Type for the native `object` type hint - 'any object, class unknown' - is a supertype of every ObjectType/ObjectShapeType/ClosureType, SubtractableType for instanceof-negation on a bare `object`-typed value.
