core-types.our_location: src/types.rs parse_type_string ("object" keyword, line 757); src/registry.rs is_subtype (line 774, `(Type::Object(_,_), Type::Object(b,_)) if b == "object"`)
core-types.notes: Implemented as a sentinel `Type::Object("object", [])` rather than a distinct variant, with registry::is_subtype special-casing it as a supertype of every real Object - covers the common case (declaring/checking a native `object`-typed value). No subtractedType tracking (narrowing `object` via a series of `!($x instanceof Foo)` checks isn't modeled), and since ObjectShapeType is unimplemented, the `object` vs `object{...}` interaction this class also handles (line 90-92 of the PHP: ObjectShapeType is always accepted) has no counterpart to test against.

core-types.name: OffsetAccessType
core-types.description: A LateResolvableType representing `$array[$offset]`'s type used inside PHPDoc conditional return-type expressions (e.g. `($a is array ? $a[0] : never)`) - lazily resolves via getOffsetValueType() once the array-side type is concrete.
core-types.notes: Conditional return types are only crudely approximated: try_parse_conditional_type parses the `is`/`?`/`:` syntax but doesn't evaluate the condition per call-site at all - it just unions both branches' types textually. Since there's no per-call-site type-expression evaluator, an offset-access expression like `$a[0]` appearing inside a conditional-type branch is parsed as an ordinary (nonsensical) type string, not specially resolved the way OffsetAccessType does.

core-types.name: OperatorTypeSpecifyingExtension
core-types.description: DI extension interface for third-party PHP extensions (e.g. GMP) to describe how arithmetic operators (+, -, *, ^, /) should infer result types for objects that overload them.
core-types.notes: Pure plugin-extension interface with no DI/config system in phpstan-rs to register against, and GMP-style operator-overload inference is not modeled in the binary-operator type inference (src/checker/expr.rs infer_binary) at all.

core-types.name: OperatorTypeSpecifyingExtensionRegistry
core-types.description: Autowired DI service that collects all registered OperatorTypeSpecifyingExtension instances, filters to the ones supporting a given operator/operand-type pair, and unions their inferred result types when TypeCombinator's normal arithmetic-type inference is called.
core-types.notes: Companion DI registry to OperatorTypeSpecifyingExtension above - same justification: no extension/config system to collect implementations for, and no such extensibility point exists in src/checker/expr.rs's binary-operator inference.

core-types.name: ParserNodeTypeToPHPStanType
core-types.description: Static resolve() converting a nikic/php-parser native type-hint AST node (Name, Identifier, NullableType, UnionType, IntersectionType, or null) into a PHPStan Type - handles self/static/parent resolution against a ClassReflection and maps every native PHP type keyword (string/int/bool/float/callable/array/iterable/void/object/true/false/null/mixed/never) to its Type class.
core-types.our_location: src/types.rs parse_type_string (keyword-mapping match, lines ~660-757); src/checker/resolve.rs resolve_type_hint/resolve_pseudo
core-types.notes: Architecturally different (operates on the raw type-hint source substring reconstructed by the parser rather than a retained AST node tree, since the Rust parser doesn't keep separate Name/Identifier/NullableType/UnionType/IntersectionType node types) but semantically equivalent: every native keyword this file maps is mapped identically in parse_type_string, nullable/union/intersection syntax is handled via the surrounding string-splitting logic, and self/parent/static resolution against the current class is handled by resolve_pseudo using the same self/parent-else-fallthrough/static rules.

core-types.name: RecursionGuard
core-types.description: A static run()/runOnObjectIdentity() helper that short-circuits to ErrorType when a Type operation recurses back into itself (by description-string or object-identity key) - protects reflection-driven property/method/iterable-type resolution from infinite loops on self-referential generic/recursive class hierarchies.
core-types.our_location: src/checker/generics.rs class_template_bindings_rec (`seen: HashSet`, line ~289); src/registry.rs (multiple `seen: HashSet` guards, e.g. lines 479, 509, 562, 632, 663, 699)
core-types.notes: No single generic RecursionGuard::run()-style utility exists; instead, each recursive traversal (class-hierarchy walks for method/property/constant/interface resolution in registry.rs, template-binding chain resolution in generics.rs) carries its own local `HashSet<String>` cycle guard. Functionally covers the same cyclic-hierarchy protection PHPStan's RecursionGuard exists for, but is duplicated ad hoc per call site rather than centralized, so a newly-added recursive traversal could forget to add its own guard where PHPStan's version is opt-in-by-wrapping at every Type method that needs it.

core-types.name: ResourceType
core-types.description: The Type for PHP's legacy `resource` value kind (file handles, curl handles pre-8.0, etc.) - is-self-only equality, offset-accessible legal but not truly offset-accessible, toString→StringType, toInteger→IntegerType, toArray wraps itself in a 1-element list.
core-types.our_location: src/types.rs parse_type_string ("resource" keyword, line 679); src/checker/narrowing.rs (is_resource/assertIsResource narrowing, lines 509-512, 852)
core-types.notes: Represented as the same sentinel-Object hack as ObjectWithoutClassType (`Type::Object("resource", [])`), which correctly participates in is_resource()/assertIsResource() narrowing and PHPDoc `resource` type hints. No dedicated coercion behavior (toString/toInteger/toArray/toFloat casts) exists, and because it's modeled as an 'object' rather than a distinct Type variant, nothing prevents nonsensical operations like treating a resource as instanceof-checkable the way a real class would be.

core-types.name: SimultaneousTypeTraverser
core-types.description: A generic utility that walks two Type trees (e.g. a template-typed declaration and a concrete received type) in lockstep, calling a callback at each corresponding pair of nodes and recursing via each Type's own traverseSimultaneously() - the general mechanism inferTemplateTypes() and traverseSimultaneously()-based type intersection use throughout PHPStan's generics support.
core-types.notes: bind_template_param is a hardcoded, special-purpose version of the same 'walk two type trees in parallel, extract bindings at TemplateParam leaves' idea, but only recurses through Array and ClassString wrappers - it has no general dispatch table covering Union/Intersection/generic-Object-type-argument pairs the way real PHPStan's traverseSimultaneously() does per-Type-subclass, so template inference through a union-typed or intersection-typed parameter, or through a user generic class's own type arguments, isn't reconciled the same way.

core-types.name: StaticMethodParameterClosureThisExtension
core-types.description: Pure DI-tagged extension interface (2 methods, no logic) letting third-party extensions dynamically supply the $this-binding type for a closure parameter of a specific static method call.
core-types.notes: Confirmed via grep that phpstan-src itself has zero classes implementing this interface (tag only referenced from NodeScopeResolver's extension-collection plumbing and test fixtures) - it is a pure third-party-plugin extension point, not something real PHPStan's own core behavior depends on. The one concrete behavior it would enable in practice - Closure::bind($closure, $newThis, $scope) rebinding $this inside the closure - is instead implemented directly as hardcoded core logic in phpstan-rs's expr.rs (mirroring how real PHPStan itself handles that specific case outside this extension system). Building a generic third-party extension mechanism makes no sense for phpstan-rs.

core-types.name: StaticMethodParameterClosureTypeExtension
core-types.description: Pure DI-tagged extension interface letting third-party extensions dynamically supply the type of a closure parameter for a specific static method call (e.g. mocking-framework builders).
core-types.notes: Zero implementations within phpstan-src itself (confirmed via grep); purely a third-party-plugin extension surface with no first-party consumer even in real PHPStan. No functional Rust equivalent exists or is warranted - phpstan-rs's approach hardcodes specific well-known behaviors instead of building generic extensibility, and there is no concrete built-in behavior here to hardcode an equivalent of.

core-types.name: StaticMethodParameterOutTypeExtension
core-types.description: Pure DI-tagged extension interface letting third-party extensions dynamically supply a by-ref "parameter-out" type after a specific static method call.
core-types.notes: Zero phpstan-src implementations (confirmed via grep) - a third-party-only plugin extension point. phpstan-rs does model by-ref out-parameter typing for specific well-known ordinary functions (e.g. preg_match's $matches, in checker/calls.rs), but that is unrelated to this static-method-specific extension interface, which has no built-in consumer to mirror.

core-types.name: StaticMethodTypeSpecifyingExtension
core-types.description: Pure DI-tagged extension interface letting third-party extensions narrow types based on a static method call's arguments/condition (analogous to instanceof narrowing but for e.g. Assert::isInstanceOf(...) style static calls).
core-types.notes: Zero implementations in phpstan-src core (confirmed via grep of the STATIC_METHOD_TYPE_SPECIFYING_EXTENSION_TAG and 'implements' usages - only a test fixture exists). The practical capability it exists to provide - narrowing types from a static assertion call like self::assertInstanceOf(...) - is separately covered in phpstan-rs by hardcoded pattern matching in narrowing.rs (assertIsString/assertInstanceOf/etc.), the same way real PHPStan's own core (not this interface) recognizes such calls. The generic extension interface itself has no sensible from-scratch equivalent to build.

core-types.name: StaticType
core-types.description: Represents `static` (late static binding) as a Type: wraps a ClassReflection, supports a SubtractableType-based negative refinement, and delegates almost every Type operation to an underlying ObjectType/GenericObjectType while specially transforming any nested StaticType/ThisType it encounters when resolving members (transformStaticType).
core-types.notes: phpstan-rs models `static` only as a bare marker variant with no attached ClassReflection or generic-argument binding; resolve.rs's resolve_self_static collapses SelfRef/StaticRef to a plain Object(defining_class) at first use, losing the late-static-binding distinction from `self` (a subclass calling an inherited method sees the same Object type StaticType would represent, but PHPStan's own more precise per-call-site resolution - e.g. generic ClassReflection binding, subtracted types propagating through method-return transforms - is entirely absent). No subtraction (getSubtractedType/changeSubtractedType), no distinct GenericObjectType projection for a generic static class, and no `transformStaticType`-style downgrading of nested $this-typed return values when called on `static`.

core-types.name: StaticTypeFactory
core-types.description: Static factory of a handful of cached composite Type constants: falsey()/truthy() (the exact PHP falsy-value union and its complement), argv()/argc() ($argv/$argc superglobal types), and generalOffsetAccessibleType()/intOffsetAccessibleType() (array|ArrayAccess|null, plus string for int offsets).
core-types.our_location: src/checker/narrowing.rs (ad hoc falsy/truthy narrowing sets, e.g. ~line 1161+); src/checker/assignment.rs:361-384 ($argv/$argc typing)
core-types.notes: $argv is typed as plain Array(Mixed) and $argc as plain Int - not the precise non-empty-list<string>/int<1,max> PHPStan produces via IntersectionType/IntegerRangeType. Falsy/truthy narrowing is done via a hand-maintained set of literal comparisons in narrowing.rs rather than a single reusable falsey()/truthy() Type value combined through TypeCombinator::remove. No ArrayAccess-aware offset-accessible union exists at all - ArrayAccess objects are not modeled for index access anywhere in the checker (grep for 'ArrayAccess' in src/ finds nothing), so generalOffsetAccessibleType/intOffsetAccessibleType have no counterpart.

core-types.name: StrictMixedType
core-types.description: A CompoundType variant of mixed used for bleeding-edge/level-9+ "explicit mixed" checking (RuleLevelHelper) and as TemplateMixedType's building block: isSuperTypeOf is always yes, but isAcceptedBy is stricter - only another StrictMixedType or bare MixedType accepts it unconditionally, everything else gets only "maybe".
core-types.notes: phpstan-rs has a single undifferentiated Type::Mixed with no distinction between an implicit/inferred mixed and an explicitly-written `mixed` type-hint, and no level-9/10-style "explicit mixed usage" enforcement at all. Since phpstan-rs does not model PHPStan's rule-level system, there is no natural place to plug this in without first building that level machinery - a genuine feature gap, not an extension point.

core-types.name: StringAlwaysAcceptingObjectWithToStringType
core-types.description: A StringType subclass used in weak (non-strict_types) contexts: overrides accepts()/isSuperTypeOf() so any object class with a native __toString() method is treated as a string, regardless of PHP version, by looking the class up via ReflectionProvider.
core-types.notes: phpstan-rs's is_subtype/is_assignable have no case at all for an object-with-__toString satisfying a string-typed sink (grep for '__toString'/'Stringable' in checker/*.rs finds nothing beyond an unrelated comment). Passing a Stringable object where a string is expected is neither specially accepted nor flagged - it simply isn't checked (falls through to whatever generic object-vs-scalar mismatch/leniency rule applies).

core-types.name: StringNeverAcceptingObjectWithToStringType
core-types.description: The counterpart used for strict_types contexts (or PHP 8+ internal function signatures): always forces accepts($type, true) regardless of the passed strictTypes flag, so no object (even with __toString) is ever coerced into this string.
core-types.notes: Same gap as StringAlwaysAcceptingObjectWithToStringType: phpstan-rs's type system has no strict_types-sensitivity to string acceptance and no Stringable-object handling at all, so there is nothing distinguishing the strict-vs-weak variant.

core-types.name: StringType
core-types.description: The base `string` Type: offset access (string indexing yields non-empty-string), toInteger/toFloat/toArrayKey/toCoercedArgumentType numeric-coercion rules, tryRemove('') upgrading to non-empty-string, isNumericString/isClassString/isLiteralString etc. as TrinaryLogic::maybe() (refined only by accessory intersections or subclasses), and accepts() allowing a __toString object in weak mode.
core-types.our_location: src/types.rs Type::String plus Type::Intersection([String, Accessory(..)]) for the refined forms (non-empty-string/non-falsy-string/literal-string/numeric-string); src/checker/narrowing.rs upgrade-on-exclude logic
core-types.notes: Core string type and its four accessory-refinements are represented structurally (Phase 14, mirroring PHPStan's own IntersectionType([StringType, AccessoryXType]) shape) and narrow_type_excluding upgrades string to non-empty-string on `!== ''`. But there is no isDecimalIntegerString distinction, no toArrayKey coercion-safety modeling (ReportUnsafeArrayStringKeyCastingToggle has no counterpart), no toCoercedArgumentType weak-typing union widening, no string-offset access modeling ($str[0]), and (per the two subclasses above) no __toString-object acceptance.

core-types.name: SubtractableType
core-types.description: A tiny marker interface (getTypeWithoutSubtractedType/changeSubtractedType/getSubtractedType) implemented by ObjectType, StaticType/ThisType, and MixedType, letting TypeCombinator represent "T but definitely not U" (e.g. after `if (!$x instanceof Foo)` on a wider-typed $x) without discarding T entirely.
core-types.notes: phpstan-rs's negative-instanceof narrowing (narrow_type_excluding) only removes a union member when it is exactly equal to the excluded type; a non-union Object type that is merely a supertype of the excluded class (e.g. `Bar` narrowed by `!Bar instanceof Foo` where Foo is a subclass of/unrelated-but-possible for Bar) is left completely unchanged rather than becoming "Bar minus Foo". This is a real, structural gap versus PHPStan's SubtractableType mechanism, not a naming difference.

core-types.name: ThisType
core-types.description: A StaticType subclass representing `$this`/`@return $this`: strictly narrower than StaticType (isSuperTypeOf ANDs in an extra `maybe`), and toClassConstantType collapses `$this::class` to the exact literal class name when the class is `final`.
core-types.notes: phpstan-rs deliberately conflates `$this` and `static` into the single StaticRef variant (explicit comment in parse_type_keyword_or_class: "@return $this is... identical in meaning to @return static"), so PHPStan's own real distinction between the two (ThisType being the narrower, exact-instance type) is entirely collapsed. No `final`-class $this::class literal-narrowing exists either.

core-types.name: Type
core-types.description: The ~150-method central interface every PHPStan type implements: accepts/isSuperTypeOf/equals/describe, property/method/constant reflection accessors, ~25 array-operation methods (setOffsetValueType, sliceArray, mapValueType, ...), numeric/cast coercion methods (toInteger/toBoolean/toArrayKey/toCoercedArgumentType/...), template-type inference, and many is*() trinary predicates.
core-types.notes: phpstan-rs represents the whole Type hierarchy as one closed enum with free functions instead of a polymorphic interface, and implements only a fraction of Type's contract: subtyping (is_subtype/is_assignable), template binding/substitution, and Display (~describe). Missing entirely: the property/method/constant-reflection-returning methods (properties/methods are looked up separately through registry.rs rather than off the Type itself), essentially all ~25 array-mutation methods (setOffsetValueType, sliceArray, spliceArray, chunkArray, flipArray, ...), toCoercedArgumentType/toNumber/toBitwiseNotType/toGetClassResultType/toObjectTypeForInstanceofCheck, generalize(), getFiniteTypes(), and getReferencedTemplateTypes(). union_types (checker/expr.rs) plays a role similar to TypeCombinator::union but is a much smaller, hand-rolled dedup/cap mechanism rather than Type-polymorphic dispatch.

core-types.name: TypeAlias
core-types.description: Lazily resolves and memoizes one @phpstan-type alias's PHPDoc TypeNode into a real Type via TypeNodeResolver, given the NameScope it was declared in; TypeAlias::invalid() represents a circular-alias error.
core-types.notes: @phpstan-type / @phpstan-import-type are not recognized anywhere in docblock.rs (grep finds zero hits). registry.rs even has an explicit comment acknowledging this: an unresolved alias name is treated leniently as an unrecognized object/class name so is_assignable doesn't false-positive against it, rather than being resolved to its real aliased type - i.e. phpstan-rs suppresses the resulting noise instead of implementing the feature.

core-types.name: TypeAliasResolver
core-types.description: Interface for looking up whether a given alias name is defined (optionally scoped to a class) and resolving it to a Type within a NameScope.
core-types.notes: No alias registry or lookup exists in registry.rs; see TypeAlias above for the same underlying gap (@phpstan-type support absent).

core-types.name: TypeAliasResolverProvider
core-types.description: One-method DI accessor interface (getTypeAliasResolver()) used to hand a TypeAliasResolver to consumers like TypeNodeResolver without a hard dependency.
core-types.notes: This specific file is pure DI-indirection boilerplate (a provider-of-a-provider) with no logic of its own - even if TypeAlias/TypeAliasResolver above were implemented, phpstan-rs's architecture (no DI container) would simply call the alias-lookup function directly rather than through an injectable provider interface. The underlying feature gap is already captured by TypeAlias/TypeAliasResolver.

core-types.name: TypeCombinator
core-types.description: The ~2300-line core normalization engine behind union()/intersect()/remove(): flattens nested unions/intersections, merges scalar/enum-case/IntegerRangeType members, distributes A & (B|C), merges ConstantArrayType shapes into tagged unions or generalized ArrayTypes (with an oversized-array fallback once a count limit is hit), threads SubtractableType subtraction through both operations, and provides addNull/removeNull/removeFalsey/removeTruthy helpers.
core-types.our_location: src/checker/expr.rs:2540 union_types (+ MAX_UNION_MEMBERS cap, generalize_by_key_set); src/types.rs (fixed Intersection shapes built directly by the parser, no general intersect() combinator)
core-types.notes: phpstan-rs has no analogue of TypeCombinator::intersect()/remove() at all - Intersection values are only ever constructed directly by the type parser for a small fixed set of known accessory shapes (list/non-empty-string/etc.), never computed generically from two arbitrary types. union_types is a much smaller hand-rolled version of doUnion: exact-equality/Mixed-absorption fast paths, one literal-absorbed-into-its-base-type simplification pass, and a hard member-count cap that falls back to same-key-set ArrayShape merging then to Mixed. Entirely missing versus doUnion/doIntersect: IntegerRangeType tryUnion/tryIntersect merging, ConstantArrayType tagged-union merging (reduceArrays/intersectDefiniteConstantArrays/mergeIntersectionsForUnion), oversized-array generalization, BenevolentUnionType, HasOffsetType/HasOffsetValueType/HasPropertyType resolution, and SubtractableType-aware union/intersect (unionWithSubtractedType/intersectWithSubtractedType) - consistent with SubtractableType itself being unimplemented.

core-types.name: TypeCombinatorCache
core-types.description: A memoization seam that the PHP implementation itself does not use (its methods just delegate straight to TypeCombinator::doUnion/doIntersect/doRemove) - it exists purely so PHPStan's native "Turbo" C++ extension can shadow it with a real memoizing/interning cache for hot-path performance.
core-types.notes: This class's own PHP body is explicitly a no-op passthrough ("This PHP implementation performs no caching at all"); its entire purpose is as an interception point for an optional native-code performance extension that has no bearing on a Rust rewrite, which is already compiled and does not need a scripting-language-oriented memoization shim. Nothing to port beyond what TypeCombinator itself already needs (see above).

core-types.name: TypeResult
core-types.description: Generic immutable value object pairing a resolved Type with a list<string> of human-readable 'reasons' explaining how the result was reached; the base for AcceptsResult/IsSuperTypeOfResult which carry Yes/No/Maybe plus explanatory reasons for error messages.
core-types.notes: phpstan-rs has no TrinaryLogic/AcceptsResult/IsSuperTypeOfResult architecture at all - src/registry.rs and src/checker/*.rs perform plain bool is_subtype()/is_assignable() checks (registry.rs ~L887) with no attached reasoning trail, so there is no equivalent data structure to carry 'why' a type check succeeded or failed. This is a foundational architectural gap, not a one-off missing file.

core-types.name: TypeTraverser
core-types.description: Generic recursive Type-tree mapper: TypeTraverser::map(type, callback) lets a callback replace/inspect any Type node and optionally recurse into its children via the passed $traverse callable; used pervasively (containsTemplateType, resolveLateResolvableTypes, VerbosityLevel's moreVerboseCallback, etc).
core-types.notes: No generic recursive traverse/map combinator exists over src/types.rs's Type enum (grepped for fn traverse/map_type/walk - none found). Each place that needs to walk into Union/Intersection/Array/etc (e.g. is_subtype, substitute_template) hand-rolls its own recursive match instead of sharing one traversal abstraction.

core-types.name: TypeTraverserCallable
core-types.description: Marker interface letting a TypeTraverser callback be implemented as a stateful object (with a traverse(Type,callable):Type method) instead of a plain PHP closure - purely an alternate calling convention for TypeTraverser::map.
core-types.notes: This interface exists only because PHP closures are awkward for stateful/reusable traversal callbacks; Rust closures (and FnMut) serve this purpose natively wherever a traversal combinator would be used, so no separate interface is needed. Companion of the missing TypeTraverser but adds no behavior of its own to port.

core-types.name: TypeUtils
core-types.description: Static utility belt: extracting ConstantIntegerType/IntegerRangeType members out of a union, toBenevolentUnion/toStrictUnion conversions, flattenTypes() (power-set-expanding ConstantArrayType unions with a 16384-variant bailout), findThisType/findCallableType searches, getHasPropertyTypes/getAccessoryTypes collectors, containsTemplateType, and resolveLateResolvableTypes.
core-types.notes: No equivalents found: no BenevolentUnionType concept anywhere in src/types.rs (grepped, zero hits), no power-set array-shape flattening/combinations helper, no findThisType/findCallableType walkers, no containsTemplateType helper (template detection is done ad hoc inline where needed, e.g. in generics.rs binding code, not via a reusable utility). Reflects the broader absence of TypeTraverser-based utilities.

core-types.name: TypeWithClassName
core-types.description: Interface implemented by ObjectType, StaticType, ThisType, EnumCaseObjectType, ClosureType, GenericObjectType to expose getClassName()/getClassReflection()/getAncestorWithClassName() uniformly for any type carrying a concrete class name.
core-types.notes: PHPStan needs this interface because it has many distinct polymorphic Type subclasses that each carry a class name; phpstan-rs instead uses one flat `Type` enum where `Type::Object(name, generic_args)` (and no separate Static/This/EnumCase/Closure-with-class variants) directly exposes the class name as a String field via pattern matching - no interface indirection is needed or sensible in this design.

core-types.name: TypehintHelper
core-types.description: decideTypeFromReflection() converts a native PHP reflection type (union/intersection/named, nullable) into a PHPStan Type; decideType() then reconciles that native type against a parsed PHPDoc type, picking the more specific one while respecting explicit mixed/never, iterable-vs-array-of-mixed-key normalization, and BenevolentUnionType passthrough.
core-types.our_location: src/checker/resolve.rs, src/registry.rs (param/return type resolution merging native hints with @param/@return docblock types)
core-types.notes: phpstan-rs does merge a native type-hint with a PHPDoc type when both are present (docblock type generally wins when compatible), but the merge is a much simpler rule than PHPStan's: no BenevolentUnionType special-casing, no iterable/array-mixed-key normalization, no ArrayType::getItemType() variadic unwrapping, and no per-type-instanceof reconciliation logic mirroring decideType()'s many branches.

core-types.name: UnaryOperatorTypeSpecifyingExtension
core-types.description: Plugin extension interface (DI-tagged) letting third-party extensions override how unary operators (-, +, ~) type-check against non-scalar operands, e.g. GMP objects overloading unary minus.
core-types.notes: Pure third-party plugin extension point wired through PHPStan's Nette DI container; phpstan-rs has no plugin/extension system and hard-codes its own (much simpler) unary-operator inference directly in src/checker/expr.rs (ExprKind::Unary handling), so there is nothing analogous to make pluggable.

core-types.name: UnaryOperatorTypeSpecifyingExtensionRegistry
core-types.description: DI-autowired registry that collects all registered UnaryOperatorTypeSpecifyingExtension instances and dispatches -/+/~ type inference to whichever ones claim to support the given operand type, unioning their results.
core-types.notes: Pure DI-container plumbing for the (not_applicable) extension interface above; phpstan-rs's built-in unary-operator handling in src/checker/expr.rs (lines ~594-633, ~1591-1602) is hard-coded rather than extension-dispatched, so no registry concept applies.

core-types.name: UnionType
core-types.description: The core composite Type for `A|B|C`: implements every Type-interface member by delegating/unioning across its member types (accepts, isSuperTypeOf, property/method/constant resolution, all array-op methods, describe() with dedup/truncation/sorting via UnionTypeHelper, FiniteTypeSet-based fast-path equality/containment checks, template-type inference across union members, traverse/traverseSimultaneously, tryRemove for exhaustive-narrowing).
core-types.our_location: src/types.rs Type::Union(Vec<Type>) and its handling across is_subtype/is_assignable (src/types.rs, src/registry.rs)
core-types.notes: The core union-member-wise dispatch pattern (delegate an operation to each member and combine) is present for the handful of operations phpstan-rs's Type actually supports (subtype checks, Display join with '|'), but almost all of the ~90 specialized methods PHP's UnionType implements (array-shape mutation ops, property/method/constant prototype resolution across members, FiniteTypeSet fast paths, template-type inference on unions, EQUAL_UNION_CLASSES special-casing for DateTime/Throwable, isOffsetAccessible etc.) have no counterpart since those richer Type capabilities don't exist in Rust's flatter enum at all.

core-types.name: UnionTypeHelper
core-types.description: sortTypes(): a deterministic, elaborate multi-criteria comparator (null last, accessory types after value types after non-constant types, numeric value ordering, string value ordering, enum-case ordering, callable/closure ordering, constant-array emptiness-then-string ordering, generic string fallback) used to make UnionType::describe() output stable and readable.
core-types.our_location: src/types.rs Display for Type::Union (plain iteration order, no sorting)
core-types.notes: phpstan-rs's Union Display impl (types.rs ~L137) simply joins members with '|' in insertion order with no deterministic sort - none of UnionTypeHelper's ordering rules (null-last, constants-first, accessory-types-last, etc.) are implemented, so describe()-equivalent output order is whatever order the union was constructed in.

core-types.name: UsefulTypeAliasResolver
core-types.description: Resolves @phpstan-type / @phpstan-local-type alias names (both global config-defined and per-class-local, the latter looked up via ClassReflection::getTypeAliases()) to actual Type objects, with LRU caching, recursion/circularity guards (CircularTypeAliasDefinitionException -> CircularTypeAliasErrorType), and duplicate-with-class-name detection.
core-types.notes: There is no actual alias resolution: registry.rs's comment at line 871 explicitly documents that an unresolved `@phpstan-type` alias name is handled by *leniently treating any assignment to/from it as always OK* rather than by resolving the alias to its real declared type - so type aliases are effectively swallowed as an escape hatch, not modeled. No global-alias config, no per-class local alias parsing/caching, and no circularity detection exist.

core-types.name: ValueOfType
core-types.description: LateResolvableType implementing PHPDoc's `value-of<T>` syntax: resolves (once T is fully known) to the union of an enum's backing-value types, or to T's iterable value type for arrays/collections.
core-types.notes: grepped src/ for 'value-of'/'ValueOfType' - no hits at all; the docblock/type parser (src/docblock.rs, src/types.rs parse_type_keyword_or_class) has no case for `value-of<...>`, so such a PHPDoc annotation would presumably fail to parse or fall back to an unknown/leniently-ignored type rather than resolving to enum backing values or iterable value types.

core-types.name: VerbosityLevel
core-types.description: Four-level enum (typeOnly/value/precise/cache) controlling how much detail Type::describe() includes in error messages, plus getRecommendedLevelByType() which walks a type (via TypeTraverser) to auto-pick the minimum verbosity needed to distinguish two types (constant values, callables, accessory string types, invariant generic template types all bump verbosity).
core-types.notes: phpstan-rs has a single fixed Display formatting for Type (types.rs L94 onward) with no verbosity levels, no cache-key-specific formatting, and no auto-verbosity-detection logic - every diagnostic message uses the same one level of detail there is, so error messages can't selectively show/hide constant values, closure signatures, or accessory-string precision the way PHPStan's does.

core-types.name: VoidType
core-types.description: Type subclass representing PHP's `void` return type: accepts() only null/void, isSuperTypeOf only another VoidType, all scalar/array/string coercion methods (toNumber, toString, toArray, etc.) return ErrorType, toCoercedArgumentType() returns NullType, isVoid() yes, falsey-boolean trait for boolish behavior.
core-types.our_location: src/types.rs Type::Void variant, Display (line 99: write!(f, "void")), parse_type_keyword_or_class (line 681: "void" => Type::Void)
core-types.notes: Void is a first-class Type variant, parsed from PHPDoc/native `: void` return types and displayed correctly. It does not carry VoidType's full battery of per-operation ErrorType-returning methods (no distinct toNumber()/toArray()/etc. dispatch per type), but that mirrors phpstan-rs's overall simpler, non-polymorphic Type model rather than a gap specific to void - basic void semantics (return-type checking, no value-producing operations expected) are present in the checker.

generics-accessory-constant.name: AccessoryArrayListType
generics-accessory-constant.description: CompoundType/AccessoryType implementation for the `list` refinement; only ever appears inside an IntersectionType alongside ArrayType, and overrides ~30 array-operation methods (chunk/slice/splice/flip/reverse/search/shift/pop/intersectKey/makeListMaybe/truncateListToSize etc.) plus isList()=yes, getIterableKeyType()=int<0,max>, describe()='list'.
generics-accessory-constant.notes: Rust models `list`/`non-empty-list` as Type::Intersection([Array(_), Accessory(ArrayList)]) exactly mirroring PHPStan's own representation, with Display/subtype logic for it, but none of the ~30 per-operation overrides (chunkArray, sliceArray, spliceArray, flipArray, searchArray, etc.) exist for Array/ArrayShape types, so list-ness is not propagated through most array transformations the way PHPStan does.

generics-accessory-constant.name: AccessoryDecimalIntegerStringType
generics-accessory-constant.description: Accessory type (with an `inverse` flag) marking strings that are/aren't decimal-integer strings (e.g. "123" vs "+1"/"00"/"1.2"), used to precisely predict whether a string key is coerced to an int array key via toArrayKey().
generics-accessory-constant.notes: No AccessoryKind::DecimalIntegerString (or inverse variant) exists in src/types.rs, and no isDecimalIntegerString()-style distinction is made anywhere; string-to-array-key coercion in the Rust type system doesn't distinguish decimal-integer-string literals from other numeric strings at this level of precision.

generics-accessory-constant.name: AccessoryLiteralStringType
generics-accessory-constant.description: Accessory type for `literal-string` (a string built entirely from literal/constant parts, used e.g. for SQL-injection-safety checks); implements the full CompoundType contract with its own describe/accepts/offset/toArray/hasMethod('__invoke'-style maybe) logic.
generics-accessory-constant.notes: Represented as Intersection([String, Accessory(LiteralString)]) with basic Display and subtype checks (e.g. from StringLiteral), matching PHPStan's own internal representation, but literal-string is never actually *inferred* from concatenation of literal parts the way PHPStan's TypeCombinator/expression evaluator does - only produced by parsing a `literal-string` PHPDoc annotation.

generics-accessory-constant.name: AccessoryLowercaseStringType
generics-accessory-constant.description: Accessory type for `lowercase-string` (produced by strtolower()/mb_strtolower() etc.), with offset access, changeKeyCaseArray-style logic, and interplay with looseCompare against other case-refined strings.
generics-accessory-constant.notes: No AccessoryKind::LowercaseString variant, no `lowercase-string` keyword handling in parse_type_keyword_or_class, and no dynamic-function-return-type modeling of strtolower()'s result as case-refined - grep across src/ for Lowercase/Uppercase finds nothing outside vendor/.

generics-accessory-constant.name: AccessoryNonEmptyStringType
generics-accessory-constant.description: Accessory type for `non-empty-string`; full CompoundType implementation including offset access (first char is itself non-empty-string), toArrayKey, tryRemove('0') widening to non-falsy-string, and looseCompare against null/empty string.
generics-accessory-constant.notes: Represented and displayed correctly as Intersection([String, Accessory(NonEmptyString)]), and StringLiteral values are checked against it (`!s.is_empty()`), but none of the richer behaviors (offset-value typing, tryRemove('0') promoting to non-falsy-string, looseCompare specialization) are implemented.

generics-accessory-constant.name: AccessoryNonFalsyStringType
generics-accessory-constant.description: Accessory type for `non-falsy-string` (non-empty AND not "0"); truthy by construction, subtype of AccessoryNonEmptyStringType, with looseCompare against the full falsy-dominated set (null/false/''/[]).
generics-accessory-constant.notes: Basic representation/display and StringLiteral-based inference (`s != "" && s != "0"`) exist; the offset/array/looseCompare specializations and the AccessoryNonEmptyStringType supertype relationship encoded in isSubTypeOf are not reproduced.

generics-accessory-constant.name: AccessoryNumericStringType
generics-accessory-constant.description: Accessory type for `numeric-string`; converts toNumber()/toArrayKey() using ReportUnsafeArrayStringKeyCastingToggle and AccessoryDecimalIntegerStringType, with looseCompare and tryRemove('0') logic.
generics-accessory-constant.notes: Basic representation and literal-based membership check exist, but toArrayKey()'s decimal-integer-string distinction (which depends on the missing AccessoryDecimalIntegerStringType) and the other operation overrides are absent.

generics-accessory-constant.name: AccessoryType
generics-accessory-constant.description: Marker interface (extends Type) shared by every accessory refinement, declaring only getDefaultBaseType(); documents the convention that accessories only appear inside an IntersectionType alongside a base type, and lists which Type query method each accessory corresponds to.
generics-accessory-constant.notes: The same architectural convention (an accessory-kind value that only ever appears wrapped in Type::Intersection alongside its base type) is explicitly modeled and documented in the AccessoryKind doc-comment ('mirrors real PHPStan's own Accessory*Type family'), but there is no formal per-kind getDefaultBaseType()-equivalent method or a general dispatch table of 'query methods' - callers pattern-match Type::Accessory(kind) directly instead.

generics-accessory-constant.name: AccessoryUppercaseStringType
generics-accessory-constant.description: Accessory type for `uppercase-string` (produced by strtoupper()/mb_strtoupper()), mirror of AccessoryLowercaseStringType.
generics-accessory-constant.notes: No AccessoryKind::UppercaseString and no strtoupper()-result modeling anywhere in src/; symmetric gap with AccessoryLowercaseStringType.

generics-accessory-constant.name: HasMethodType
generics-accessory-constant.description: Accessory type asserting an otherwise-unknown/mixed value has a given method (used e.g. for `@param object{foo(): int}`-less structural checks and callable([$obj,'method']) resolution); implements hasMethod(), getMethod() via DummyMethodReflection, isCallable() for __invoke.
generics-accessory-constant.notes: grep for hasMethod/has_method across src/ (excluding vendor) returns nothing; there is no structural 'has this method' refinement type in the Rust type system at all.

generics-accessory-constant.name: HasOffsetType
generics-accessory-constant.description: Accessory type asserting a (possibly non-constant) array/ArrayAccess has a given offset with an unknown value; attached to a general ArrayType e.g. after array_key_exists() narrowing or an assignment whose value type wasn't tracked; overrides chunkArray/fillKeysArray/sliceArray/etc. to still report NonEmptyArrayType even without knowing the offset's value.
generics-accessory-constant.notes: A narrow, differently-shaped analog exists: `narrow_array_shape_by_key_presence` narrows array_key_exists()'s branches, but only for a Type::ArrayShape with statically-known field names - there is no accessory type attachable to a general Type::Array(_) to record 'has this offset' the way HasOffsetType does, so narrowing after array_key_exists()/isset() on a plain-typed array (not an ArrayShape) is not modeled.

generics-accessory-constant.name: HasOffsetValueType
generics-accessory-constant.description: Accessory type asserting a specific offset with a specific known value type; produced by setOffsetValueType()/generalize() on a ConstantArrayType degrading to a general array, and by TypeSpecifier narrowing; supports flipArray/searchArray/tryRemove and template-type inference through the tracked value.
generics-accessory-constant.notes: `$arr['key'] = $value` is handled by directly mutating a known Type::ArrayShape in assignment.rs rather than via a general-array accessory type; there is no way to record 'this general array has offset K with value type V' the way HasOffsetValueType does for arrays whose overall shape isn't already a tracked ArrayShape (e.g. after generalize()/degradation, or template-type inference through such an offset).

generics-accessory-constant.name: HasPropertyType
generics-accessory-constant.description: Accessory type asserting an otherwise-unknown value has a given instance/static property, with hasProperty()/hasInstanceProperty()/hasStaticProperty(); mirror of HasMethodType for properties.
generics-accessory-constant.notes: grep for hasProperty/has_property across src/ (excluding vendor) returns nothing; no structural 'has this property' refinement exists.

generics-accessory-constant.name: NonEmptyArrayType
generics-accessory-constant.description: Accessory type for `non-empty-array`; asserts isIterableAtLeastOnce()=yes, getArraySize()=int<1,max>, with array-operation overrides (chunkArray/reverseArray/fillKeysArray preserve non-emptiness; popArray/shiftArray/searchArray degrade to mixed).
generics-accessory-constant.notes: Represented via Intersection([Array(_), Accessory(NonEmptyArray)]) and produced by `!empty()`/`count()>0`/`!== []` narrowing (upgrade_array_to_non_empty), matching the common PHPStan idiom, but the array-operation-specific overrides from the PHP class (how chunking/reversing/etc. affect non-emptiness) are not reproduced.

generics-accessory-constant.name: OversizedArrayType
generics-accessory-constant.description: Accessory type marking an array whose literal was too large (>256 keys, ConstantArrayTypeBuilder::ARRAY_COUNT_LIMIT) or had too many closures (>=32) to keep as a precise ConstantArrayType, so it degraded to a general ArrayType while still remembering it 'was' a big literal for isOversizedArray() checks.

It has no lowerBoundTypes concept (no contravariant-position inference tracking), and none of union/intersect/benevolentUnion/resolveToBounds exist as reusable operations - each call site recomputes bindings from scratch rather than merging maps from multiple branches.

generics-accessory-constant.name: TemplateTypeParameterStrategy
generics-accessory-constant.description: A TemplateTypeStrategy implementation used for parameter-acceptance contexts: accepts() simply defers to the bound's own accepts() (or the right-hand CompoundType's isAcceptedBy), no maybe/reasons fallback - the default strategy for ordinary `@template T` parameter positions.
generics-accessory-constant.notes: Same reasoning as TemplateTypeArgumentStrategy: this is one half of the dual accepts()-strategy pattern built around AcceptsResult/CompoundType, machinery phpstan-rs's is_assignable() doesn't have; the underlying default behavior (defer to the bound) is implicitly what is_assignable already does for a TemplateParam's fallback.

generics-accessory-constant.name: TemplateTypeReference
generics-accessory-constant.description: A small value object pairing a TemplateType with its positional TemplateTypeVariance at one usage site, produced by Type::getReferencedTemplateTypes() and consumed by resolveTemplateTypes()/variance validation to know whether a given occurrence of T is in a covariant, contravariant, invariant, or bivariant position, distinguishing multiple occurrences of the same template by object identity.
generics-accessory-constant.notes: phpstan-rs's collect_template_params walks a type tree collecting template *names* into a HashSet (no per-occurrence identity, no variance tag attached per occurrence), and check_variance separately buckets 'input positions' (all params) vs 'output positions' (return type) at the whole-signature level to flag covariant/contravariant misuse - a coarser, signature-level approximation of what TemplateTypeReference's per-occurrence variance tracking supports position-precisely.

generics-accessory-constant.name: TemplateTypeScope
generics-accessory-constant.description: Value object identifying where a template type was declared: anonymous function, named function, class, or class method (four static factories), with equals()/describe() for comparing/rendering scopes - used to distinguish e.g. two classes' own same-named `T`.
generics-accessory-constant.notes: phpstan-rs doesn't have a TemplateTypeScope value object attached to each Type::TemplateParam, but achieves the same practical disambiguation (two unrelated classes' own same-named T not colliding) via class_template_bindings' target-scoped walk and substitute_class_templates' class_scope HashSet restricting substitution to names the specific owning class declares - the doc comments explicitly call out the symfony/type-info NullableType<T>/UnionType<T> collision case this guards against. No scope object exists for function-vs-method-vs-anonymous-closure distinctions specifically, though - only class-level scoping is modeled.

generics-accessory-constant.name: TemplateTypeStrategy
generics-accessory-constant.description: Pure strategy interface (2 methods: accepts(), isArgument()) implemented by TemplateTypeParameterStrategy and TemplateTypeArgumentStrategy, letting a TemplateType behave differently in accepts() depending on whether it represents a declared @template parameter or a call-site-inferred argument's substituted type.
generics-accessory-constant.notes: phpstan-rs's Type::TemplateParam(String) (src/types.rs) is a bare name with no attached strategy object at all - there is no parameter-vs-argument distinction affecting how a template type's accepts()/is_assignable behaves. types::is_assignable_to (src/types.rs ~894) treats any TemplateParam as universally compatible on either side regardless of context, which is a much coarser, strategy-free fallback. Real capability gap, but inseparable from the fact that TemplateParam carries no bound/scope/variance either (see TemplateTypeTrait).

generics-accessory-constant.name: TemplateTypeTrait
generics-accessory-constant.description: Large shared trait mixed into every TemplateType* subclass (TemplateObjectType, TemplateUnionType, etc.) implementing describe(), toArgument(), isValidVariance(), subtract()/getSubtractedType()/changeSubtractedType(), equals(), isAcceptedBy()/accepts(), isSuperTypeOf()/isSubTypeOf(), toClassConstantType(), inferTemplateTypes() (the core call-site unification algorithm, including union-splitting when the bound only partially matches), getReferencedTemplateTypes(), traverse()/traverseSimultaneously(), tryRemove(), and toPhpDocNode().
generics-accessory-constant.notes: Only a thin slice survives: bind_template_param does structural unification for exactly two shapes (bare T, and T[]/array<T> against an array arg) with first-binding-wins and explicitly no union-widening across multiple params - vs. inferTemplateTypes' bound-checked, union-splitting algorithm. There is no equivalent at all for isValidVariance-driven subtyping, subtract/changeSubtractedType (no SubtractableType concept on templates), toClassConstantType (T::class handling), equals()/traverse() polymorphism, or toArgument(). check_variance (generics.rs L190) covers only the input/output-position half of isValidVariance's job, and only for class-level covariant/contravariant name sets, not general type-vs-type variance checks.

generics-accessory-constant.name: TemplateTypeVariance
generics-accessory-constant.description: Value object enumerating invariant/covariant/contravariant/static/bivariant, with compose() (variance algebra for nested generics), isValidVariance() (the actual a<:b / b<:a / equals check per variance kind, with reasons attached), validPosition(), and phpdoc-node round-tripping.
generics-accessory-constant.notes: phpstan-rs models only two of the five variance kinds (covariant/contravariant, as flat per-class HashSet<String> name sets - invariant is implicit-by-absence, and static/bivariant don't exist at all). There is no compose() - the doc comment for check_variance explicitly says it 'doesn't attempt real variance's positional flipping through a nested generic argument', i.e. variance composition through nested generics is unimplemented by design. isValidVariance's actual subtype-direction checking (a->isSuperTypeOf(b) for covariant, etc.) is also absent; only the syntactic input/output-position restriction is checked.

generics-accessory-constant.name: TemplateTypeVarianceMap
generics-accessory-constant.description: Simple immutable map from template-parameter name to its TemplateTypeVariance (plus a cached empty singleton), used when resolving/traversing generic types to know each type argument's variance at that position (e.g. passed into TemplateTypeHelper::resolveTemplateTypes and TemplateTypeTrait::inferTemplateTypes).
generics-accessory-constant.notes: No equivalent data structure exists - phpstan-rs's covariant_templates/contravariant_templates (registry/class_info.rs) are per-class declaration-site sets used only by check_variance's single use-position check, never threaded through generic type substitution/resolution the way TemplateTypeVarianceMap is in PHPStan (substitute_template/substitute_scoped in types.rs and generics.rs carry no variance information at all).

generics-accessory-constant.name: TemplateUnionType
generics-accessory-constant.description: A TemplateType subclass (extends UnionType, uses TemplateTypeTrait) used when a template's bound is itself a union type (e.g. @template T of string|int); overrides filterTypes() so narrowing the union still produces a proper TemplateType wrapper rather than collapsing to a bare UnionType.
generics-accessory-constant.notes: phpstan-rs's Type::TemplateParam(String) never stores a bound at all (see TemplateTypeTrait notes), so there is no representation of 'a template bound to a union type' as a distinct, filterable type - a @template T of string|int declaration's bound is simply not tracked or enforced anywhere in the Rust type system.

generics-accessory-constant.name: TypeProjectionHelper
generics-accessory-constant.description: One static describe() helper that renders a generic type argument together with its use-site variance annotation for error messages, e.g. 'covariant int' or '*' for bivariant, used when PHPStan prints wildcard-style generic type arguments like Collection<covariant int>.
generics-accessory-constant.notes: Purely a describe()-string formatter for a feature that doesn't exist in phpstan-rs at all: per-argument variance/wildcard annotations on generic type references (Collection<covariant T>, Collection<*>) are not parsed anywhere in src/docblock.rs or src/parser/*, and Type::Object's generic type arguments (src/types.rs) are plain Type values with no variance wrapper to describe. With no such syntax supported, there is nothing for this helper to format.

type-misc.name: EnumCaseObjectType
type-misc.description: A Type subclass (extends ObjectType) representing one specific enum case (e.g. `Suit::Hearts`): carries the case name, gives exact equals()/isSuperTypeOf() between same-case fetches, types ->name as a literal string, ->value as the exact backing literal for that case, ::class as class-string&literal-string, and participates in match/switch exhaustiveness via subtraction.
type-misc.notes: phpstan-rs resolves an enum case fetch (`Suit::Hearts`) through the same generic `lookup_const` path as any class constant, typed as plain Type::Object(fqn, []) - there is no per-case singleton Type carrying the case name. ->name is typed as generic Type::String (not a literal), and ->value is unioned from all cases' literals when every case has a bare literal value (registry/class_info.rs ~430+), a coarser fallback than PHPStan's exact per-case value. No equals()/subtraction distinguishing one case from another, so e.g. match-exhaustiveness or type-narrowing on a specific case identity isn't modeled.

type-misc.name: GetTemplateTypeType
type-misc.description: A lazy CompoundType/LateResolvableType wrapping a type expression plus (ancestorClassName, templateTypeName); resolve() (when the wrapped type no longer contains unresolved template types) calls the wrapped type's own getTemplateType() to look up the concrete binding.
type-misc.notes: phpstan-rs's generics model does eager, positional template substitution at each call/access site (checker/generics.rs, types::substitute_template) rather than building a lazy type-tree that defers resolution until every template is bound. There is no deferred-resolution wrapper type at all, so cases PHPStan handles by deferring (a template type used before its own binding is fully known, e.g. through several levels of generic inheritance) have no equivalent mechanism here; eager substitution instead just resolves what it can at each site or falls back to Type::TemplateParam/Mixed.

type-misc.name: ClassNameUsageLocationCreateIdentifierDynamicReturnTypeExtension
type-misc.description: A DynamicMethodReturnTypeExtension registered only for PHPStan's own internal `ClassNameUsageLocation::createIdentifier()` helper method, used when PHPStan's rule-error-identifier machinery is itself statically analysed by PHPStan (self-analysis), to precisely type the identifier strings it produces from constant class-usage-location values.
type-misc.notes: This extension exists solely to make PHPStan's own dogfooding self-analysis (`vendor/bin/phpstan analyse src`) precise about one internal helper class it ships with itself; it is not a general-purpose PHP static-analysis feature. phpstan-rs has no analogous internal self-analysis API or need to model its own error-identifier plumbing this way.

type-misc.name: RegexAlternation
type-misc.description: A mutable value object tracking one `|`-alternation's id, total branch count, and (per branch-combination-index) which capturing groups sit in that branch - used to build alternation-variant $matches shapes.
type-misc.notes: Reimplemented with a different, flatter data shape: rather than a dedicated RegexAlternation object with a groupCombinations map, phpstan-rs stores `alternation: Option<(alt_id, branch_index)>` directly on each RegexCaptureGroup plus a `Vec<(alt_id, branch_count)>` on the scan result. checker/expr/preg_shapes.rs's build_matched_shape (case 2) reconstructs the same per-branch group grouping from this flatter representation and produces the same tagged-union $matches shapes PHPStan's RegexGroupList/RegexAlternation combination drives.

type-misc.name: RegexAstWalkResult
type-misc.description: Immutable accumulator threaded through RegexGroupParser::walkRegexAst: next alternation id, next capture-group id, the map of discovered RegexCapturingGroup objects, any `(*MARK:...)` verb names seen, and the regex subject's own inferred base string type (numeric/non-empty/non-falsy, from the whole-pattern top-level walk).
type-misc.notes: The core bookkeeping (group numbering, alternation ids, discovered groups) is reimplemented via a mutable Scanner struct rather than a persistent immutable value, achieving the same net effect for capture-group enumeration. Two pieces are entirely absent: `(*MARK:...)` verb tracking (markVerbs) has no equivalent anywhere in regex_groups.rs, and there is no subject-base-type refinement (PHPStan infers whether the *whole* matched subject is non-empty/non-falsy/numeric from a top-level walk and applies it to field "0"'s type) - phpstan-rs's field "0" is always plain Type::String (see preg_shapes.rs's preg_leaf_type).

type-misc.name: RegexCapturingGroup
type-misc.description: Per-capturing-group value object: id, optional name, owning RegexAlternation, inOptionalQuantification flag, parent group/non-capturing-group chain, an inferred Type (literal union, or numeric/non-empty/non-falsy string), isOptional()/isTopLevel()/resetsGroupCounter() derived from the parent chain, and forceNonOptional()/forceType() used when building alternation-variant shapes.
type-misc.notes: id/name/optional/top_level/in_optional_quantification/alternation/forced_empty are all ported with equivalent semantics (optional propagation is computed eagerly at quantifier-scan time onto all descendant handles, rather than lazily via a parent-chain walk, but produces the same result). Two things are missing: (1) the group's own inferred Type only ever tracks fully-enumerable literal values (Option<Vec<String>>) - PHPStan's fallback to numeric-string/non-empty-string/non-falsy-string accessory types when literals aren't enumerable (e.g. `(\d+)`, `([a-z]+)`) has no equivalent, so such a group's leaf type in $matches is just plain string in phpstan-rs; (2) resetsGroupCounter()/the `(?|...)` branch-reset construct isn't modeled - the scanner has no match arm for `(?|`, so any pattern using it falls through to the catch-all bail (returns None, no $matches typing at all for that call), a safe but strictly less precise outcome than PHPStan's support for it.

type-misc.name: RegexExpressionHelper
type-misc.description: Shared helper for pattern-string manipulation: strips delimiters/modifiers from a constant pattern (removeDelimitersAndModifiers/getPatternModifiers), and - the more involved half - resolves a Concat expression building a pattern at runtime into a constant string when possible, treating preg_quote() calls as an opaque `(?:.*)` placeholder so partially-dynamic patterns concatenated from static pieces can still be statically analysed (resolvePatternConcat, getPatternDelimiters).
type-misc.notes: Delimiter/modifier stripping for a literal pattern string is ported (split_delimiters_and_modifiers mirrors getEndDelimiterPos/removeDelimitersAndModifiers/getPatternModifiers, including the bracket-style-delimiter cases). The concatenation-resolution half is entirely absent: checker/assignment.rs's literal_string_value(), the only function feeding a pattern string into regex_groups::parse_capture_groups (checker/expr.rs:299,344; checker/narrowing.rs:27), only matches a bare ExprKind::Literal(String) - a Concat expression (e.g. `'/^' . $prefix . '$/'`) is never resolved, so $matches shape inference silently no-ops for any dynamically-built pattern, even ones PHPStan could still statically resolve via preg_quote()-awareness.

type-misc.name: RegexGroupList
type-misc.description: Countable/IteratorAggregate wrapper around the discovered capturing groups, providing the higher-level queries the $matches-shape builder needs: countTrailingOptionals(), forceGroupNonOptional()/forceGroupTypeAndNonOptional() (clone-and-reparent to force one group and its descendants non-optional), removeGroup(), getOnlyOptionalTopLevelGroup() and getOnlyTopLevelAlternation() (the two special-case dispatch conditions).
type-misc.notes: Reimplemented as free functions over a `&[RegexCaptureGroup]` slice instead of a dedicated collection type, but the same queries are present: preg_match_matches_shape computes trailing-optional truncation inline (trailing_optional_count); build_matched_shape detects both special cases (exactly one optional top-level group; exactly one top-level alternation) and rebuilds forced-non-optional/forced-empty/removed variant group lists via functional `.map()`/`.filter_map()` reconstruction rather than OOP clone-and-reparent, producing the same tagged-union $matches shapes confirmed against a live PHP interpreter in the surrounding comments.

type-misc.name: RegexGroupParser
type-misc.description: The main regex-structure parser: parses a pattern via the Hoa\Compiler PCRE grammar, walks the resulting AST twice (once for capturing-group/alternation bookkeeping via walkRegexAst, once per-group for literal/numeric/non-empty/non-falsy type inference via walkGroupAst), handles quantifier ranges, POSIX classes, character escapes, alternation-prefix literal combination, and caps enumeration via LITERALS_LIMIT.
type-misc.notes: A hand-rolled recursive-descent scanner replaces the Hoa grammar + two-pass AST walk, covering: capturing/named-capturing/non-capturing groups, alternation with retroactive optional-marking, bounded/unbounded quantifiers, character classes (including POSIX class lookahead), `\Q...\E` quoted blocks, lookaround (correctly excluded from literal contribution), and literal-value cross-product enumeration with a LITERAL_ENUM_LIMIT (32, vs PHPStan's 100) plus a MAX_QUANTIFIER_REPEAT cap PHPStan doesn't have. Missing relative to PHPStan: the `x` (free-spacing) modifier is not supported at all (PHPStan strips `#`-comments and continues; phpstan-rs bails the whole pattern), `(?|...)` branch-reset groups bail entirely, conditional groups `(?(1)...)` bail (both projects bail these, PHPStan the same), and - the largest gap - the numeric-string/non-empty-string/non-falsy-string trinary fallback (walkGroupAst's TrinaryLogic tracking) for groups whose content isn't a fully enumerable literal set has no equivalent; such a group's inferred leaf type in phpstan-rs is always plain string.

type-misc.name: RegexGroupWalkResult
type-misc.description: Immutable accumulator threaded through walkGroupAst: inOptionalQuantification flag, the running set of onlyLiterals (nulled once a non-enumerable atom is seen), and three TrinaryLogic flags (isNonEmpty/isNonFalsy/isNumeric) used to fall back a group's type to an accessory string refinement when it isn't a finite literal set.
type-misc.notes: phpstan-rs's per-atom/per-branch accumulation (AtomResult, concat_literals, repeat_literals) only tracks the literal-enumeration half of this class - the onlyLiterals equivalent. The three TrinaryLogic fields (isNonEmpty/isNonFalsy/isNumeric) that let RegexGroupParser::createGroupType fall a non-literal group back to numeric-string/non-empty-string/non-falsy-string have no counterpart anywhere in regex_groups.rs; a group that isn't fully literal-enumerable just gets plain Type::String in phpstan-rs, losing this refinement entirely.

type-misc.name: RegexNonCapturingGroup
type-misc.description: A parent-chain node for `(?:...)` and `(?|...)` groups (the latter via resetGroupCounter=true), providing isOptional()/isTopLevel()/getAlternationId() delegation up the chain, and resetsGroupCounter() which disables constant-type inference for groups inside a branch-reset construct.
type-misc.notes: An ordinary `(?:...)` non-capturing group is handled inline (finish_non_capturing_group just scans the body and passes its AtomResult through transparently, with no separate node object - achieving the same net optional/top-level/alternation propagation since nested groups' handles/literal_values flow straight up through the ordinary alternation/branch scanning already in place). The `(?|...)` branch-reset variant (resetsGroupCounter) has no equivalent at all: the scanner recognizes no `(?|` syntax, so any pattern containing it fails to parse (bails to None) rather than being handled with disabled constant-typing the way PHPStan handles it.

type-misc.name: ArrayTypeTrait
type-misc.description: Shared default-method implementation mixed into ArrayType/ConstantArrayType-family classes: isArray()=yes, isOffsetAccessible()=yes, isIterable()=yes, every other is*() scalar/object predicate=no, toNumber()/toString()/toBitwiseNotType()/exponentiate()=ErrorType (i.e. arrays don't support these operations), plus a concrete chunkArray() algorithm building the array_chunk() return shape.
type-misc.our_location: src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs (array_chunk et al.), src/types.rs (Type::Array match arms scattered across is_subtype etc.)
type-misc.notes: phpstan-rs has no polymorphic Type trait/interface at all (its Type is a flat enum with free functions doing exhaustive matches), so there's no single file mirroring this trait's method surface. The user-visible behaviors that matter for diagnostics are covered piecemeal: array_chunk()'s return shape is special-cased directly in checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs (line 395) rather than via a generic chunkArray() Type method, and array-vs-other-type distinctions are handled inline wherever Type::Array/ArrayShape is matched. There's no equivalent of the trait's blanket "arrays reject numeric/string/bitwise coercion" default (toNumber/toBitwiseNotType/exponentiate returning ErrorType) as a queryable API - such coercions on an array-typed value aren't flagged as invalid through any central path in the code checked.

type-misc.name: ConstantNumericComparisonTypeTrait
type-misc.description: Shared getSmallerType()/getSmallerOrEqualType()/getGreaterType()/getGreaterOrEqualType() for ConstantIntegerType/ConstantFloatType: computes, via IntegerRangeType subtraction from mixed (plus PHP's < > loose-comparison quirks with null/false/0.0), the type a variable narrows to after `$x < N`/`$x <= N`/`$x > N`/`$x >= N` against a constant.
type-misc.notes: phpstan-rs's narrowing.rs has no BinOp::Lt/Gt/LtEq/GtEq narrowing at all - the only comparison-operator narrowing found is a narrow special case for `count($x) > 0` / `count($x) >= 1` (narrowing.rs:125-126), and BinOp::Identical/NotIdentical for `===`/`!==`. A condition like `if ($x < 5)` does not narrow $x's type to an int range in phpstan-rs at all, unlike PHPStan which uses exactly this trait's logic to produce e.g. `int<min, 4>`.

type-misc.name: ConstantScalarTypeTrait
type-misc.description: Shared accepts()/isSuperTypeOf()/equals()/isSmallerThan()/isSmallerThanOrEqual()/looseCompare()/isConstantScalarValue() for every constant scalar type (ConstantIntegerType, ConstantFloatType, ConstantStringType, ConstantBooleanType) - includes PHP's full `==` loose-comparison truth table between differing constant scalar kinds via LooseComparisonHelper.
type-misc.notes: Literal equality (via derived PartialEq) and subtype/superset relations between a literal and its base type are present through types::is_subtype and the Type enum's structural equality, covering isSuperTypeOf/equals for the strict-comparison (`===`) cases narrowing.rs already handles. The looseCompare() half - PHP's `==` truth table across differing scalar kinds (e.g. `"abc" == 0`, `"1e2" == "100"`) - has no equivalent anywhere: grep for BinOp::Equal/NotEqual narrowing in narrowing.rs and types.rs found nothing, confirming loose-comparison-based type narrowing isn't modeled at all.

type-misc.name: FalseyBooleanTypeTrait
type-misc.description: A one-method trait: toBoolean() always returns ConstantBooleanType(false) - mixed into every type that is unconditionally falsy (NullType, ConstantBooleanType(false), the 0/0.0/''/'0' constant scalar types, empty-array types), feeding TypeSpecifier's truthy/falsey condition narrowing.
type-misc.notes: phpstan-rs consolidates the equivalent behavior into narrow_type_excluding_falsy, which excludes every type this project recognizes as unconditionally falsy (null, false, 0, '', '0', empty array, and their accessory-refined complements) from a truthy-branch narrowing - the same net effect as querying toBoolean()==false on each candidate type, just implemented as one direct filter function rather than a per-type virtual method plus a separate TypeSpecifier dispatch.

type-misc.name: LateResolvableTypeTrait
type-misc.description: A very large trait (~200 delegating methods) that every LateResolvableType (deferred/lazy type, e.g. GetTemplateTypeType, GetOffsetValueTypeType, GetClassStringType) mixes in: caches resolve() once, then delegates essentially the entire Type interface surface to the resolved type, with isSuperTypeOf() short-circuiting NeverType/other-lazy-types specially before resolving.
type-misc.notes: phpstan-rs has no lazy/deferred Type variant at all - its flat Type enum is always fully resolved at construction time via eager substitution (types::substitute_template), so there is nothing analogous to a LateResolvableType needing this delegation scaffolding. This is the same underlying architectural gap noted for GetTemplateTypeType above: real PHPStan's deferred-resolution design lets template/offset/class-string types resolve correctly even when some inputs aren't fully known yet at construction time, which phpstan-rs's eager approach cannot replicate in the general case.

type-misc.name: MaybeArrayTypeTrait
type-misc.description: Shared default-method implementation for types that might-or-might-not be an array (e.g. MixedType, ObjectType and other non-array/non-definitely-not-array types): isArray()/isConstantArray()/isOversizedArray()/isList()=maybe (TrinaryLogic), getArrays()/getConstantArrays()=[], and every array-transformation method (chunkArray, flipArray, popArray, sliceArray, etc.) returns ErrorType since none of them can be soundly answered without knowing.
type-misc.notes: phpstan-rs has no TrinaryLogic type anywhere in the codebase (confirmed via repo-wide grep), so the specific "maybe" answer this trait provides for uncertain (e.g. Mixed-typed) values passed to array-shape-sensitive builtins has no direct equivalent. In practice phpstan-rs's builtin-function special-casing (checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs) mostly just declines to refine the return type further when the argument isn't confidently array-typed, which is a coarser but broadly similar practical outcome to defaulting every array-transform to ErrorType/ maybe - but there is no queryable "is this maybe an array" API mirroring the trait's method surface.

type-misc.name: MaybeCallableTypeTrait
type-misc.description: A two-method trait: isCallable()=TrinaryLogic::createMaybe(), getCallableParametersAcceptors()=[TrivialParametersAcceptor] - mixed into types that might be callable (e.g. MixedType, ObjectType, string types) so a call through them isn't flatly rejected nor over-trusted.
type-misc.notes: No TrinaryLogic/isCallable() query surface exists in phpstan-rs's flat Type enum. Whether a value used in a call-like position (e.g. passed to array_map, or invoked via $var(...)) is treated leniently is instead handled ad hoc at each call site (e.g. builtin_calls.rs's array_map handling, or the Closure/Callable Type variants), not through a shared 'maybe callable' default answer mirroring this trait.

type-misc.name: MaybeIterableTypeTrait
type-misc.description: Default-implementation trait for Type classes whose iterability is unknown (MixedType, ObjectType, etc.): returns TrinaryLogic::Maybe from isIterable()/isIterableAtLeastOnce(), Mixed for iterable key/value types, and an unbounded IntegerRangeType for getArraySize().
type-misc.notes: phpstan-rs's flat Type enum has no is_iterable()-style trinary query at all. src/checker/stmt.rs's Foreach handling extracts element/key types directly per-variant without ever classifying maybe/definitely/never-iterable, and there is no equivalent of PHPStan's real Rules/Arrays/IterableInForeachRule.php (confirmed absent by grep of stmt.rs/control_flow.rs) which is exactly the rule this default answer feeds — 'Argument of an invalid type X supplied for foreach, only iterables are supported' is never emitted.

type-misc.name: MaybeObjectTypeTrait
type-misc.description: Default 'unsure' answers (TrinaryLogic::Maybe, Mixed template type, dummy property/method/constant reflections) for Type classes that might be an object but aren't sure (MixedType, generic/union members, etc.), letting downstream reflection code proceed without special-casing an unknown receiver.
type-misc.notes: No TrinaryLogic or dummy-reflection scaffolding exists, but the same practical leniency is achieved ad hoc: a non-Object receiver (union member, mixed, etc.) falls through PropertyAccess/MethodCall handling to `_ => Type::Mixed`, and member_confirmed_missing only flags a diagnostic when every union member is known to lack the member (matching the trait's 'assume maybe, don't error' intent for common cases). There is no counterpart to getTemplateType/toObjectTypeForInstanceofCheck/toObjectTypeForIsACheck, which support instanceof/is_a() narrowing against a class name computed at runtime.

type-misc.name: MaybeOffsetAccessibleTypeTrait
type-misc.description: Default 'unsure' offset-access answers (Maybe accessible, Mixed value type on read, identity on write) for Type classes whose ArrayAccess-ability isn't statically known (MixedType, template params, etc.).
type-misc.notes: index_result_type's `_ => Type::Mixed` fallback (expr.rs) reproduces this trait's getOffsetValueType default for any non-array/non-shape container with no diagnostic raised, matching the 'maybe' spirit. But there is no isOffsetAccessible()/isOffsetAccessLegal() concept at all, so nothing distinguishes this 'maybe' case from the 'definitely not offset-accessible' case (see NonOffsetAccessibleTypeTrait) — both currently collapse to the same silent Mixed fallback.

type-misc.name: MaybeStringTypeTrait
type-misc.description: Default Maybe answers for isString/isNumericString/isDecimalIntegerString/isNonEmptyString/isNonFalsyString/isLiteralString/isLowercaseString/isUppercaseString/isClassString/isScalar and empty getConstantStrings(), for Type classes whose string-ness is unresolved.
type-misc.notes: phpstan-rs models the 'definite' string properties as Intersection([String, Accessory(NonEmptyString|NonFalsyString|LiteralString|NumericString)]), applied by narrowing.rs on concrete checks (e.g. strlen()>0). A bare Type::String with no accessory is implicitly the 'maybe' state, so most of the trait's effect falls out of the flat-enum architecture for free. isLowercaseString/isUppercaseString/isDecimalIntegerString have no accessory counterpart at all — never tracked even as 'maybe', so any rule relying on them would have nothing to consult.

type-misc.name: NonArrayTypeTrait
type-misc.description: Default 'definitely not an array' answers (TrinaryLogic::No / ErrorType) for ~20 array-shaped Type interface methods (isArray, isList, getKeysArray, chunkArray, spliceArray, searchArray, etc.), mixed into every non-array Type class so it needn't stub each one individually.
type-misc.notes: Pure PHP-interface-boilerplate avoidance for a one-class-per-type-kind architecture. phpstan-rs's single Type enum answers 'is this an array' and each array operation via one match statement per operation (index_result_type, array_element_type, etc.) rather than ~20 stub methods repeated across dozens of non-array Type classes — there is no file-shaped equivalent to build. The substantive array-function behaviors this trait's real counterpart (ArrayType) implements are audited separately under the array-function-return-type extension files, not here.

type-misc.name: NonCallableTypeTrait
type-misc.description: Default 'not callable' answer (TrinaryLogic::No) plus a ShouldNotHappenException-throwing getCallableParametersAcceptors(), mixed into every Type class that can never be invoked as a callable.
type-misc.notes: Same interface-boilerplate role as NonArrayTypeTrait, for the 'is this callable' side. phpstan-rs's flat enum needs no per-variant stub; callable-ness is decided inline wherever call expressions are checked (src/checker/calls.rs) rather than through a queried Type method, so there is nothing this trait's pattern maps onto.

type-misc.name: NonGeneralizableTypeTrait
type-misc.description: Default generalize(GeneralizePrecision) implementation that just traverses the type's own component types applying generalize() to each — used by composite types (unions, arrays, etc.) whose generalization is 'generalize my parts'.
type-misc.notes: PHPStan's generalize() (widening a literal/precise type for loop-fixpoint stabilization and template-argument inference) has no counterpart anywhere in phpstan-rs. src/checker/calls.rs and assignment.rs do an unrelated, narrower 'widening' for byref-parameter and array-literal-shape merging, but there is no general Type::generalize traversal for control_flow.rs's branch-merging or generics.rs's template binding to call. Nothing to attach a Rust equivalent of this specific default-traversal helper to.

type-misc.name: NonGenericTypeTrait
type-misc.description: Default empty answers for inferTemplateTypes() (returns an empty TemplateTypeMap) and getReferencedTemplateTypes() (returns []), mixed into every Type class that carries no generic/template information of its own.
type-misc.notes: Interface-boilerplate avoidance again. phpstan-rs's template-type inference (src/checker/generics.rs: class_template_bindings/substitute_class_templates, plus call-site binding in calls.rs) operates directly on Type::TemplateParam/Type::Object variants via match, not through a per-instance inferTemplateTypes() virtual call that non-generic classes must stub out to a no-op.

type-misc.name: NonIterableTypeTrait
type-misc.description: Default 'definitely not iterable' answers (TrinaryLogic::No, ErrorType for every array-size/key/value getter) for Type classes that are certain not to be iterable (scalars, etc.) — the definite-No counterpart to MaybeIterableTypeTrait.
type-misc.notes: Same underlying gap as MaybeIterableTypeTrait: no is_iterable()-style query exists on phpstan-rs's Type at all, and there is no equivalent of PHPStan's Rules/Arrays/IterableInForeachRule.php that this trait's 'No' answer is meant to trigger for scalar foreach targets (confirmed absent from stmt.rs's Foreach handling). A `foreach ($intVar as $x)` on a definitely-scalar variable produces no diagnostic in phpstan-rs today.

type-misc.name: NonObjectTypeTrait
type-misc.description: Default 'definitely not an object' answers (TrinaryLogic::No, ShouldNotHappenException-throwing property/method/constant accessors, empty enum-case list) for Type classes certain not to be objects.
