type-misc.notes: phpstan-rs matches `narrow_type_excluding(&base_ty, &Type::Null)` against `Type::Object(...)` for property/method resolution and falls to `_ => Type::Mixed` for every non-object variant (int, string, array, etc.) — i.e. it silently tolerates member access on a definitely-non-object base rather than raising PHPStan's real 'Cannot access property/call method on int/string/...' diagnostic the way this trait's ShouldNotHappenException ultimately supports upstream. The leniency is intentional in places (union members) but means a bare non-object receiver gets no error either.

type-misc.name: NonOffsetAccessibleTypeTrait
type-misc.description: Default 'definitely not offset-accessible' answers (TrinaryLogic::No, ErrorType for every offset getter/setter) for Type classes certain not to support `[]` access (int, bool, etc.).
type-misc.notes: index_result_type (src/checker/expr.rs:2494) has a single `_ => Type::Mixed` fallback for every non-array container type, with no distinction for a definitely-non-offset-accessible base and no diagnostic — real PHPStan uses this default (via InvalidOffsetHandling / the array-dim-fetch rules) to flag 'Cannot access offset X on int'. That check does not exist in phpstan-rs; indexing an int, bool, or plain object silently type-checks to Mixed.

type-misc.name: NonRemoveableTypeTrait
type-misc.description: Default tryRemove(Type $typeToRemove): ?Type implementation returning null (i.e. 'I don't know how to subtract this from myself'), mixed into Type classes with no special subtraction logic.
type-misc.notes: tryRemove() supports PHPStan's TypeCombinator::remove() used when narrowing a union by excluding a member type precisely (e.g. removing null from a nullable custom type via its own subtraction rule). phpstan-rs's narrowing.rs performs the analogous 'exclude a type' operation (narrow_type_excluding) directly via one match over Type variants rather than a per-instance virtual tryRemove() a class can override — there is no separate default-stub file this maps to; the actual behavior lives inline in narrow_type_excluding.

type-misc.name: ObjectTypeTrait
type-misc.description: The substantive shared implementation for real object types: isObject=Yes, canAccessProperties/canCallMethods/canAccessConstants=Yes, isCloneable=Yes, hasProperty/hasMethod/hasConstant=Maybe (resolved via dummy reflections), toClassConstantType (literal class-string for a final class), toArray, looseCompare, toCoercedArgumentType (implicit __toString for non-strict-types), and every isX() scalar-classification answering No.
type-misc.notes: Property/method/constant resolution for Type::Object is implemented directly against the registry (registry.lookup_property_with_owner, lookup_method) rather than through dummy reflections, covering the practical hasProperty/getProperty/hasMethod/getMethod behavior. But several concrete pieces of behavior this trait encodes are absent: no toClassConstantType literal-string-for-final-class special case for `Foo::class`, no looseCompare()/toCoercedArgumentType() implicit-__toString-in-argument-coercion modeling (no strict_types-aware string coercion of objects), and canAccessProperties/canCallMethods/isCloneable aren't queried as distinct trinary facts anywhere.

type-misc.name: SubstractableTypeTrait
type-misc.description: Shared describeSubtractedType() helper that formats a type's own 'subtracted' (negated) component for display, e.g. printing `~null` or `~(A|B)` as part of a type's describe() string.
type-misc.notes: phpstan-rs's Type enum (src/types.rs) has no subtracted/negated-type concept at all — confirmed by grep, no 'subtract' anywhere in the checker. Negative narrowing (e.g. after a failed `instanceof` check) is done instead by filtering Union members in narrow_type_excluding (narrowing.rs:1068), and for a non-Union base type that isn't an exact subtype match, the exclusion is simply lost (the type is returned unchanged) rather than recorded as `T&~U`. This is a real, if narrow, precision gap: repeated/redundant instanceof checks and exhaustiveness reasoning that real PHPStan's subtracted types support have no equivalent here.

type-misc.name: TruthyBooleanTypeTrait
type-misc.description: Default toBoolean(): BooleanType implementation returning ConstantBooleanType(true), mixed into Type classes that are always truthy (ObjectType, non-empty-string types, etc.).
type-misc.notes: phpstan-rs computes truthiness ad hoc per call site inside narrowing (e.g. narrowing.rs's bare-truthiness-check arms distinguish which types are always-truthy for `if ($x)`) rather than via a queryable Type::to_boolean() method every Type variant answers. The specific 'always true' cases this trait encodes (objects, non-falsy strings) are handled where narrowing.rs needs them, but there's no general boolean-classification API a rule elsewhere could reuse the way PHPStan's toBoolean() is reused across many rules (e.g. redundant-condition checks).

type-misc.name: UndecidedBooleanTypeTrait
type-misc.description: Default toBoolean(): BooleanType implementation returning a plain (unresolved) BooleanType, for Type classes whose truthiness can't be determined at all (MixedType, generic scalars, etc.).
type-misc.notes: Same architecture point as TruthyBooleanTypeTrait: the 'give up, truthiness unknown' fallback is implicit whenever narrowing.rs's truthiness match doesn't recognize a variant (falls through without narrowing either branch), rather than being an explicit queryable default. Functionally similar outcome for the common cases, but no reusable API for other rules to consult 'is this type's truthiness known'.

type-misc.name: UndecidedComparisonCompoundTypeTrait
type-misc.description: Default isGreaterThan/isGreaterThanOrEqual answers (TrinaryLogic::Maybe, with a Yes special-case for object-vs-null) for compound Type classes (unions, object types) whose ordering comparison isn't otherwise decided; builds on UndecidedComparisonTypeTrait.
type-misc.notes: phpstan-rs has no isGreaterThan/isSmallerThan-style comparison-outcome API on Type at all. src/checker/expr.rs only maps the spaceship operator (`<=>`) to a plain Type::Int result (expr.rs:2376) and never reasons about `<`,`>`,`<=`,`>=` between two known types (e.g. flagging 'if ($obj > null)' as always-true, or feeding comparison-based narrowing). This whole comparison-classification subsystem — used by real PHPStan for always-true/always-false comparison warnings and numeric-range narrowing on `<`/`>` — is absent.

type-misc.name: UndecidedComparisonTypeTrait
type-misc.description: Default isSmallerThan/isSmallerThanOrEqual/getSmallerType/getSmallerOrEqualType/getGreaterType/getGreaterOrEqualType answers (mostly TrinaryLogic::Maybe / MixedType, with null-specific special cases) for Type classes whose ordering comparison against another type isn't otherwise decided.
type-misc.notes: Same gap as UndecidedComparisonCompoundTypeTrait: no comparison-outcome or comparison-narrowing API exists on phpstan-rs's Type at all (confirmed no `<`/`>`/`<=`/`>=`-based type narrowing anywhere in narrowing.rs, and no IntRange derivation from a comparison narrows a variable's range the way real PHPStan's getSmallerType()/getGreaterType() feed narrowing.php's ComparisonHelper). `if ($x > 5)` narrows nothing about `$x`'s type in phpstan-rs today.

type-misc.name: LateResolvableTraverser
type-misc.description: A TypeTraverserCallable used by TypeTraverser::map() to lazily resolve LateResolvableType nodes (e.g. conditional types, template-type placeholders) while walking a type tree: it repeatedly calls resolve() on a LateResolvableType while the caller has opted into resolving otherwise-unresolvable types (or the type itself reports isResolvable()), and specially suppresses that eager resolution while descending into CallableType/ClosureType parameter/return types (tracked via an ignoreResolveUnresolvableTypesLevel counter) so callable signatures aren't prematurely forced to resolve before their real call-site bindings are known.
type-misc.our_location: src/types.rs:307 try_parse_conditional_type (approximates the one instance PHPStan uses this machinery for)
type-misc.notes: phpstan-rs has no TypeTraverser/TypeTraverserCallable architecture and no LateResolvableType concept at all - Type is a flat, eagerly-constructed enum (src/types.rs:13) with no lazy/deferred resolution step, and no notion of 'resolvable when the caller says so' vs. 'suppressed inside a Callable/Closure signature'. The one place this machinery matters in practice - PHPStan's `($param is X ? T : F)` conditional return type, which is itself a LateResolvableType subtype - is handled in phpstan-rs by eagerly unioning both branches at parse time (src/types.rs:292-326), with an explicit code comment noting 'this project has no per-call-site type-expression evaluation at all.' That is a real, deliberate simplification (imprecise but sound) rather than a lazy-resolution reimplementation, so the traverser's actual mechanism (deferred resolution, call-site-specific binding, Callable/Closure-aware suppression) is genuinely absent, not just differently located.

type-misc.name: UnsafeArrayStringKeyCastingTraverser
type-misc.description: A TypeTraverserCallable, invoked via the static castKeyType() helper, that (only when the `reportUnsafeArrayStringKeyCasting: detect` config toggle is on) rewrites an array key type by replacing any decimal-integer-string component (e.g. the string "123") with `int | non-decimal-integer-string`, modeling PHP's runtime behavior of silently casting such array keys to int on insertion/iteration; used by both ArrayType and ConstantArrayType so a general array and a constant-array shape agree on key type instead of producing a spurious `Maybe` comparison result.
type-misc.notes: phpstan-rs's array representations do not model key types at all: Type::Array only carries a value type (no key type to cast), and Type::ArrayShape's keys are plain Rust Strings with no associated Type/decimal-integer-string tracking. There is no `reportUnsafeArrayStringKeyCasting` config concept, no AccessoryDecimalIntegerStringType equivalent, and no is_numeric_string-driven key-type widening anywhere in src/. This is a genuine, if narrow, precision gap (PHP's numeric-string-array-key-to-int coercion is unmodeled), not merely a relocated feature - the underlying key-type machinery this traverser normalizes doesn't exist to be normalized.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: AbsFunctionDynamicReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for abs(): returns the argument type's toAbsoluteNumber() (e.g. int<0,max> for a ranged int, absolute float, etc.), falling back to null (default stub type) on ErrorType.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: grep for "abs" and toAbsoluteNumber-equivalent logic in src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs and src/types.rs finds nothing; abs() gets whatever the plain function-signature stub (if any) provides, with no argument-based narrowing (e.g. abs(-5) or abs(int<-10,10)) at all.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ArgumentBasedFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: Covers 16 functions (array_unique, array_diff*, array_udiff*, array_intersect*, array_uintersect*) whose return type is simply an ArrayType built from one designated argument's key/value types (index 0 for all of them here), adding NonEmptyArrayType for array_unique when the input is provably non-empty, and handling the unpack/spread-argument case specially.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: Only array_unique is handled (strip_accessory_markers on the input array, dropping list-ness but not modeling NonEmptyArrayType precision). The other 15 functions in FUNCTION_NAMES (array_diff, array_diff_assoc/key/uassoc/ukey, array_udiff*, array_intersect, array_intersect_assoc/uassoc/ukey, array_uintersect*) have no special-cased return-type handling at all in builtin_calls.rs, so they fall through to whatever generic/stub inference exists (likely Mixed-ish).

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ArrayChangeKeyCaseFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: array_change_key_case(): reads the optional CASE_LOWER/CASE_UPPER $case argument's constant scalar value and calls Type::changeKeyCaseArray($case) to produce the recased array type.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No "array_change_key_case" match arm exists in builtin_calls.rs. Also structurally not_applicable-adjacent since our Type::Array has no key-type parameter at all (see Known limitations comments in builtin_calls.rs), so a faithful key-case-changing return type isn't representable yet either way - but classified missing since even the pass-through value-type case isn't handled.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ArrayChunkFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: array_chunk(): validates the array argument (NullType/NeverType per PhpVersion when not an array), detects a negative/zero $length producing a ValueError-or-NeverType/NullType per PhpVersion, and calls Type::chunkArray($lengthType, $preserveKeys) to build the precise chunked array type.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: Rust only returns Array<Array<elem_ty>> from the element type of the first arg - no negative-length ValueError modeling, no PhpVersion-conditional null/never behavior, no preserve_keys handling, and no per-chunk size/key precision (chunkArray's richer logic has no analog since Type::Array carries no key info).

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ArrayColumnFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: array_column(): dispatches to ArrayColumnHelper, using the precise per-key ConstantArrayType handler when the input resolves to exactly one constant array, otherwise falling back to the general handleAnyArray() path.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: Handles ArrayShape rows (literal-key lookup) and generic array rows (uniform element type), adding ArrayList accessory for the 2-arg form - a reasonable simplified analog of handleAnyArray's list marker. Missing: object/property column extraction (row is an object with the named property), the 3-arg $index_key precise per-row key computation (constant-array handleConstantArray keeps per-key precision including optional keys and unsealed-type handling; ours drops to plain Array with no ArrayShape-preserving 3-arg result), and NonEmptyArrayType propagation from isIterableAtLeastOnce().

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ArrayColumnHelper
php-dynamic-extensions.description: Shared helper backing ArrayColumnFunctionReturnTypeExtension: getReturnValueType/getReturnIndexType resolve the column/index via getOffsetOrProperty (array-offset or object-property access, with TrinaryLogic certainty), handleAnyArray builds a generalized ArrayType (with list/non-empty accessory markers), handleConstantArray builds an exact ConstantArrayType per source row (including unsealed-type propagation and castToArrayKeyType's PhpVersion-aware TypeError-vs-int-coercion behavior for non-scalar keys).
php-dynamic-extensions.our_location: src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs:462-505 (folded into the array_column match arm)
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: phpstan-rs folds a much-simplified version of this helper's logic directly into the array_column match arm rather than as a separate helper. Missing entirely: property-based column/index access (object rows), per-row ConstantArrayType precision building with optional-key and unsealed-type handling, castToArrayKeyType's array-key-coercion/TypeError modeling, and the certainty (TrinaryLogic maybe/yes) propagation that decides between a precise vs. degraded result.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ArrayCombineFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: array_combine(): delegates to ArrayCombineHelper for the return type and value-error certainty, then per PhpVersion either returns NeverType/false or unions the array result with false when a ValueError/warning is possible (mismatched key/value counts).
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: Rust just returns the $values argument's array type stripped of accessory markers (treating keys as untracked) when both args look array-like - no ValueError/false-union modeling for mismatched counts, no constant-array precise key/value pairing, and no NonEmptyArrayType propagation.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ArrayCombineFunctionThrowTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionThrowTypeExtension for array_combine(): reuses ArrayCombineHelper's hasValueError certainty to decide whether the call can still throw (falls back to the function stub's declared throw type) or definitely cannot (returns null, suppressing the throw).
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: phpstan-rs has no DynamicFunctionThrowTypeExtension-equivalent mechanism at all (no throws-type modeling / unhandled-exception checking pipeline found via grep for ThrowType/throw_type/ValueError across src/checker), so there is no architectural hook to attach this refinement to; it would only become relevant once a throw-type system exists, at which point it should be revisited (not a case of "no rust equivalent could ever make sense", but out of scope for this checker's current architecture).

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ArrayCombineHelper
php-dynamic-extensions.description: Shared logic for array_combine's return type and possible ValueError: builds an exact ConstantArrayType per pair of same-length constant key/value arrays (including sanitizing key types to int|string, unsealed-type pairing), falls back to a generalized ArrayType (with NonEmptyArrayType) otherwise, and detects the same-variable-passed-twice case (getReturnAndThrowType's certainty is `no` there since $keys and $values always have equal length).
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: Only the crude "pass through $values's array type" behavior exists; none of sanitizeConstantArrayKeyTypes, per-pair ConstantArrayType building, unsealed-type pairing, or the same-variable-passed-twice certainty refinement is implemented.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ArrayCountValuesDynamicReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: array_count_values(): intersects each possible input array's item type with int|string, builds ArrayType(itemType->toArrayKey(), IntegerRangeType::fromInterval(1,null)) per candidate array type, adding NonEmptyArrayType when the input is provably non-empty, unioning the results (or ConstantArrayType([],[]) if none survive).
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No "array_count_values" match arm found in builtin_calls.rs; falls through to whatever default/stub return type exists, losing the int-range->=1 value-type and key-restriction-to-int|string precision entirely.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ArrayCurrentDynamicReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: current($array): returns false when the array is provably empty, the element type when provably non-empty, or a union of the element type with false when uncertain (based on isIterableAtLeastOnce()).
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: grep for "current" as a function-call match arm in builtin_calls.rs found nothing; current() gets no special-cased return-type narrowing at all.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ArrayFillFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: array_fill(): rejects negative $count (ValueError/false per PhpVersion), and for small constant start-index/count builds an exact ConstantArrayType key-by-key (mirroring PHP's actual negative-then-zero-then-increment key-numbering quirk); otherwise builds a generalized ArrayType(int, value) with AccessoryArrayListType when start index is 0 and NonEmptyArrayType when count>=1, unioning with false when the ValueError case isn't certain and the PhpVersion doesn't throw.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: Rust only returns a bare Array(value_ty) - no negative-count ValueError/false handling, no constant-array precise-key building for the common small-literal-count case, and no list/non-empty accessory markers at all.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ArrayFillKeysFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: array_fill_keys(): returns NullType/NeverType per PhpVersion when $keys isn't an array, otherwise calls Type::fillKeysArray($valueType) and intersects with NonEmptyArrayType when the keys array is provably non-empty.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: Rust only returns a bare Array(value_ty) ignoring the keys argument's own key-type contribution entirely (fillKeysArray's real per-key precision has no analog since Type::Array has no key parameter), no non-array-input NullType/NeverType handling, and no NonEmptyArrayType propagation.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ArrayFilterFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: Thin DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension wrapper that extracts the array/callback/flag args from the FuncCall and delegates entirely to ArrayFilterFunctionReturnTypeHelper::getType().
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: The wrapper's own dispatch role is effectively present (the "array_filter" match arm), but its delegated helper (see next item) is only partially reimplemented, so the overall behavior is partial.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ArrayFilterFunctionReturnTypeHelper
php-dynamic-extensions.description: Full array_filter() return-type logic: no-callback case removes falsey values per candidate array type; otherwise determines USE_KEY/USE_BOTH/USE_ITEM mode from the flags argument, then for Closure/ArrowFunction/first-class-callable/string-callback-name callbacks re-evaluates the predicate expression with $item/$key bound via scope->filterByTruthyValue/filterByFalseyValue to narrow per-element (and per-key, for ConstantArrayType inputs, including optional-key and unsealed-type handling) types; falls back to a generalized ArrayType(keyType,itemType) when the callback shape isn't analyzable.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: Implements only two narrow special cases (an explicit `=== null`/`!== null` style filter, and an `instanceof X` filter) plus the no-callback falsy-removal default. Missing: ARRAY_FILTER_USE_KEY/USE_BOTH mode handling entirely, general per-element truthy-narrowing via scope-filtering of an arbitrary closure/arrow-function body (only two syntactic shapes are recognized, not arbitrary boolean expressions), first-class-callable and string-function-name callback support, and per-key ConstantArrayType precision (optional-key/unsealed handling) for filtered results.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ArrayFilterParameterClosureTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: FunctionParameterClosureTypeExtension: when a Closure/ArrowFunction literal is passed as array_filter's $callback argument, supplies that closure's own expected parameter types (item and/or key, per the ARRAY_FILTER_USE_* flag) so the closure body itself can be type-checked (e.g. undefined-variable/argument-type diagnostics against the array's real element/key type) even when the closure has no native type hints.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: grep across src/checker for a mechanism that binds $item/$key parameter types when analyzing the *body* of a closure literal passed directly to array_filter (as opposed to inferring array_filter's own call-site return type, which is the separate, partially-implemented ArrayFilterFunctionReturnTypeHelper concern above) finds nothing; a bare `array_filter($arr, function($x) { ... })` closure body gets no contextual parameter type at all in phpstan-rs.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ArrayFindFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: array_find() (PHP 8.4+): reuses ArrayFilterFunctionReturnTypeHelper's filtering logic to compute what the callback would keep, then returns a union of the resulting array's value type, plus null unless the filtered result is provably non-empty.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No "array_find" match arm in builtin_calls.rs; falls through to whatever generic/stub handling exists for an unrecognized function, with none of the callback-narrowing or definite-non-empty-vs-nullable precision.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ArrayFindKeyFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: array_find_key() (PHP 8.4+): returns a union of the input array's key type with null (a simpler analysis than array_find - it does not attempt to narrow by the callback at all, just guards that the array has at least one known array shape).
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No "array_find_key" match arm in builtin_calls.rs; also structurally limited since our Type::Array has no key-type parameter, so even this function's comparatively simple key-type|null return couldn't be represented precisely without that groundwork first.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ArrayFindParameterClosureTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: FunctionParameterClosureTypeExtension: for array_find/array_find_key/array_any/array_all's 'callback' parameter, builds a ClosureType(value: iterable-value-type, key: iterable-key-type): bool so the callback closure's own params get contextually-typed instead of mixed.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: grep for array_find/array_any/array_all across src/checker and src/registry finds zero hits - these PHP 8.4 functions aren't recognized at all, let alone given contextual closure-parameter types. No FunctionSig entry, no builtin_calls.rs arm.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ArrayFirstLastDynamicReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for array_key_first/array_key_last/array_first/array_last: returns the array's iterable key or value type (null if the array is provably empty, T|null if unproven, bare T if provably non-empty).
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No 'array_key_first'/'array_key_last'/'array_first'/'array_last' match arms anywhere in src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs or elsewhere; falls back to whatever the generic phpstorm-stubs docblock return type resolves to, with no null-when-empty/non-null-when-nonempty refinement.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ArrayFlipFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for array_flip: swaps the array's key and value types via Type::flipArray(), preserving non-emptiness, and returns null/never for a non-array argument depending on PHP version.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No 'array_flip' special case in builtin_calls.rs and no flip-related helper on the Rust Type; Type::Array doesn't even track a separate key type today (only element type), so a faithful key/value swap isn't representable without deeper type-system work first.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ArrayIntersectKeyFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for array_intersect_key: returns the first array's own type when only one array is given, otherwise intersects its keys against the union of the other arrays' key types via intersectKeyArray().
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No 'array_intersect_key' handling anywhere in src/checker; falls through entirely to the generic stub-derived return type (loses shape/element precision that survives the operation).

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ArrayKeyDynamicReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for the internal array-pointer function key(): returns null when the array is provably empty, the iterable key type when provably non-empty, otherwise key-type|null.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No '"key"' match arm exists in builtin_calls.rs/calls.rs/expr.rs; key() isn't special-cased at all and gets whatever the generic stub signature yields (likely bare int|string, no null-based refinement).

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ArrayKeyExistsFunctionTypeSpecifyingExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: FunctionTypeSpecifyingExtension for array_key_exists()/key_exists(): on the true branch narrows the array to HasOffsetType(key) (or NonEmptyArrayType for a non-literal key) and narrows the $array[$key] dim-fetch expression itself to the offset's value type; on the false branch (PHP8+) unsets the offset from the array's type.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: src/checker/narrowing.rs:256-270 has a real equivalent (narrow_array_shape_by_key_presence) driving array_key_exists narrowing, but only for a literal string key against Type::ArrayShape and only narrows the array-argument variable itself (Union-member keep/drop) - it does not narrow the $array[$key] dim-fetch expression's own value type, does not handle a non-literal/int key, and there is no false-branch offset-unset logic for a mixed ArrayShape-vs-other union.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ArrayKeysFunctionDynamicReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for array_keys(): 1-arg form returns getKeysArray() (a real list of the array's key type); 2/3-arg filtered form (with optional strict flag) returns getKeysArrayFiltered().
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs:426 implements the 1-arg form (returns list<key-type> derived from an ArrayShape's own keys, or list<mixed> as a fallback for a non-shape array-like) with a code comment noting round 13's own dumpType() verification. The 2-arg/3-arg $filter_value/$strict form is entirely unhandled (args.len() == 1 guard excludes it, falling to the generic stub).

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ArrayMapFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for array_map(): resolves the callback's per-element return type (constant-array-aware, mapping each tuple slot individually up to a size limit), a null-callback zip form building a tuple of the N arrays' value types, and the multi-array variadic form producing a list<value> intersection; adds NonEmptyArrayType when the source is provably non-empty.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs:116 handles only the common 2-arg single-array-argument shape: infers the input's element type, calls infer_closure_return_with_param_overrides to get the callback's return type, and rewraps accessory (list/non-empty) markers from the input. The null-callback zip form, the 3+-array variadic form, and constant-array per-tuple-slot mapping are all unimplemented, falling back to the generic (imprecise) stub-based array<mixed> return.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ArrayMapParameterClosureTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: FunctionParameterClosureTypeExtension for array_map's 'callback' parameter: builds a ClosureType whose N params are each array argument's iterable value type (expanding spread constant arrays element-by-element), so the callback body itself is checked against those contextual param types.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: The closure-body diagnostic-checking path (ExprKind::Closure/ArrowFn in src/checker/expr.rs:1267/1344) always types untyped params as bare Mixed from the closure's own declared hints - it never receives contextual param types from a call site, so array_map callbacks are never type-checked against the array's real element type for diagnostics (e.g. undefined-method calls on $item go undetected). A parallel, narrower mechanism (infer_closure_return_with_param_overrides, src/checker/expr.rs:2151) does bind override param types, but only to compute array_map/array_reduce's own *return* type in a read-only inference pass - it doesn't feed diagnostics inside the closure, and only handles the single-array 2-arg call shape, not array_map's full multi-array/spread signature.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ArrayMergeFunctionDynamicReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for array_merge(): when every argument is a constant array, precisely merges fields key-by-key (renumbering int keys, overwriting string keys, unioning unsealed slots); otherwise builds a best-effort ArrayType/unsealed-CAT union tracking known string offsets, list-ness, and non-emptiness.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs:289 implements a real approximation: exact field-by-field ArrayShape merging (mirroring spread-array-literal rules) when every argument is an ArrayShape, plus a list-ness/non-emptiness/element-union fallback for array-like arguments (including spread) - a materially different but comparable level of care to the PHP original. It doesn't track individual known string offsets outside the all-ArrayShape case (no HasOffsetValueType-equivalent partial precision), unlike PHPStan's richer offsetTypes bookkeeping for the mixed constant/non-constant case.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ArrayNextDynamicReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for next()/prev(): returns false when the array is provably empty, otherwise iterable-value-type|false (or bare value type when provably non-empty).
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No '"next"'/'"prev"' match arm anywhere in src/checker; these array-pointer functions get whatever the generic phpstorm-stubs signature yields, with no empty-array-aware false-narrowing.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ArrayPadDynamicReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for array_pad(): builds an ArrayType unioning the original key/value types with the pad item's type, adds NonEmptyArrayType when already non-empty or the requested length is provably nonzero, and preserves list-ness when the input was already a list.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No 'array_pad' match arm anywhere in src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs or elsewhere; falls entirely to the generic stub-derived return, losing element-type widening, non-emptiness, and list-ness tracking.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ArrayPointerFunctionsDynamicReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for reset()/end(): returns false when the array is provably empty, otherwise iterable-value-type|false (or bare value type when provably non-empty) - the same shape as ArrayNextDynamicReturnTypeExtension applied to reset/end.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No '"reset"'/'"end"' match arm anywhere in src/checker; these functions fall to the generic stub with no empty-array-aware false-narrowing, mirroring the ArrayNextDynamicReturnTypeExtension gap.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ArrayPopFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for array_pop(): returns null when the array is provably empty, otherwise iterable-value-type|null (or bare value type when provably non-empty) - the value the call itself evaluates to.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: src/checker/calls.rs:170 ('array_shift'|'array_pop' if is_list_like) only updates the by-ref array *argument's own* post-call type (drops the non-empty marker, keeps list-ness) - it does not compute a return type for the array_pop() call expression itself; there's no builtin_calls.rs arm producing element-type|null for `$x = array_pop($arr)`, so that call site falls back to the generic stub return type.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ArrayRandFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for array_rand(): infers whether the returned key(s) are int/string/int|string from the array's key type, then shapes the result as a bare key, an array<int,key> of keys, or a union of both depending on the provable range of the $num argument.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No 'array_rand' handling anywhere in src/checker; falls to the generic stub. Also, Type::Array has no separate key-type slot at all (only an element type), so representing 'array of the array's own key type' the way PHPStan does isn't directly expressible in the current type model without deeper changes.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ArrayReduceFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for array_reduce(): resolves the callback's return type (via ParametersAcceptorSelector on $carry/$item), returning the initial value's type for a provably-empty array, the callback's return type for a provably-non-empty array, or their union otherwise.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs:193 mirrors this closely: binds callback params (carry = initial-arg type or Null, item = array element type) via infer_closure_return_with_param_overrides and returns the closure's resolved return type for the 2/3-arg form. It does not replicate PHPStan's constant-array-aware onlyEmpty/onlyNonEmpty split (always returns the callback's return type rather than unioning with the initial type for an unproven-nonempty array), a minor precision gap rather than a missing feature.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ArrayReplaceFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for array_replace(): the same precise constant-array-aware field-by-field merge logic as ArrayMergeFunctionDynamicReturnTypeExtension, but preserving original key numbering (no int-key renumbering) since array_replace never reindexes.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No 'array_replace' match arm anywhere in src/checker; unlike array_merge (which has a real partial implementation), array_replace gets no special-casing at all and falls to the generic stub, losing shape-merge precision entirely.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ArrayReverseFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for array_reverse(): returns null/never for a non-array argument (PHP-version dependent), otherwise type->reverseArray($preserveKeys) which reverses element order.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs:242 handles the array_reverse(x) and array_reverse(x, false) forms, extracting the element type and rewrapping list/non-empty accessory markers from the input - matches PHPStan's own scoped precision (reversal preserves list-ness only without preserve_keys=true, same rule PHPStan follows). Doesn't special-case the non-array-argument null/never distinction, a minor gap versus a fully separate feature.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ArraySearchFunctionDynamicReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for array_search(): delegates to the haystack ArrayType's searchArray() to compute the precise key-type|false union (honoring $strict), or Null/Never when the haystack isn't array-like, gated by PHP-version-specific behavior.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: Only special-cases a list-like haystack, returning int|false (since Type::Array has no key-type parameter, this is the one case provable without one, per the code's own comment). General array key-type search (string|int|false), the $strict-argument distinction, and the non-array-haystack Null/Never fallback from PhpVersion::arrayFunctionsReturnNullWithNonArray() are all unhandled - falls through to the generic stub's loose return type otherwise.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ArraySearchFunctionTypeSpecifyingExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: FunctionTypeSpecifyingExtension: on the truthy branch of array_search(...) !== false (or similar truthy use), narrows the haystack array argument's own type to non-empty-array.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No occurrence of array_search in src/checker/narrowing.rs or anywhere narrowing logic is applied; this truthy-branch non-emptiness narrowing of the haystack has no counterpart.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ArrayShiftFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for array_shift(): returns the array's iterable value type (unioned with null unless the array is provably non-empty), or plain null when provably empty.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: Rust only handles the by-ref side effect on the array variable itself (list-ness/element-type of what remains after the shift), inside the by-ref-argument-narrowing pass in calls.rs - there is no dedicated computation of array_shift's own return value (the popped element, unioned with null for a possibly-empty array) in builtin_calls.rs; that expression's type falls back to the generic stub.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ArraySliceFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for array_slice(): delegates to ArrayType::sliceArray($offset, $length, $preserveKeys) for precise constant-array slicing, with Null/Never fallback for a non-array first argument.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: Handles only the common, precision-preserving case: 2-3 args, or a literal-false $preserve_keys, re-wrapping the input's element type/accessory markers (list-ness/non-emptiness) unchanged - explicitly not attempting true offset/length-aware constant-array slicing (ArrayType::sliceArray's numeric-key-range logic) or the preserve_keys=true / non-array-argument branches, both deliberately left out per the surrounding comment.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ArraySpliceFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for array_splice(): returns the removed-elements array via ArrayType::sliceArray($offset, $length, TrinaryLogic::createNo()) (the by-ref $array argument's own resulting mutation is handled elsewhere in PHPStan).
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No occurrence of "array_splice" anywhere in src/ - neither its own return-value type nor any narrowing of the mutated by-ref array argument is modeled.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ArraySumFunctionDynamicReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for array_sum(): computes a precise numeric type by symbolically summing a constant array's own value types (with IntegerRangeType for unsealed/variable-length tails), unioned with 0 when the array might be empty.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No occurrence of "array_sum" anywhere in src/ - falls back entirely to the generic native stub's loose int|float return type.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ArrayValuesFunctionDynamicReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for array_values(): re-keys any array into a genuine list (ArrayType::getValuesArray()), or Null/Never for a non-array argument per PHP version.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: Matches the core behavior precisely (element type wrapped as list<V> regardless of input list-ness, verified via dumpType() per the comment). The non-array-argument Null/Never fallback isn't separately handled, but is a minor edge PHPStan itself version-gates.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ArrayWalkParameterClosureTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: FunctionParameterClosureTypeExtension: types array_walk()'s callback parameter as a Closure whose $item/$key/(optional $arg) parameters are inferred from the array argument's iterable value/key types and the optional 3rd argument.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: array_walk only appears in a comment in calls.rs about its array/object union by-ref parameter type (unrelated); no mechanism types the callback closure's own parameters against the array's element/key types the way array_map/array_reduce get via infer_closure_return_with_param_overrides.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: AssertFunctionTypeSpecifyingExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: FunctionTypeSpecifyingExtension: whenever assert(...) is evaluated in a truthy context, specifies types in the condition exactly as if that condition were asserted directly (general condition-context narrowing, not statement-specific).
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: Handles the common idiom - a bare assert($cond); statement narrows $cond via apply_narrowing for code reachable afterward - but only when assert() appears as a top-level ExprKind::Call inside StmtKind::Expression; PHPStan's own extension fires in any truthy condition context (nested in &&, ternaries, if(assert(...))), which this doesn't generalize to.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: AssertThrowTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionThrowTypeExtension: when assert()'s optional 2nd argument is a Throwable-typed value/expression, that becomes assert()'s thrown exception type instead of the default AssertionError.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: phpstan-rs has no @throws / function-throw-type infrastructure at all (confirmed: no "@throws" handling in docblock.rs, no throw-type field anywhere in checker/registry) - there is no consumer (e.g. an unhandled-exception rule) this extension's output would feed into, so there is genuinely nothing to attach it to.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: BackedEnumFromMethodDynamicReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicStaticMethodReturnTypeExtension for BackedEnum::from()/tryFrom(): when called with a constant-scalar value, narrows the result to the exact matching EnumCaseObjectType(s) (or null for tryFrom on no match), by comparing against each case's own backing value.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No enum-case backing-value tracking exists anywhere (registry.rs has no getEnumCases/backing-value lookup; oop.rs's only enum-case logic is the unrelated duplicate-backing-value declaration check at line 101). A ::from()/::tryFrom() static call on an enum finds no matching stub/method and falls back to Type::Mixed.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: Base64DecodeDynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for base64_decode(): returns plain string unless the 2nd $strict argument could be true, in which case it's string|false.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No occurrence of "base64_decode" anywhere in src/ - falls back to the generic native stub.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: BcMathNumberOperatorTypeSpecifyingExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: OperatorTypeSpecifyingExtension: models BcMath\Number's PHP 8.4 operator-overloading for -,+,*,/,**,%,comparisons,<=> when either operand is a BcMath\Number, producing BcMath\Number, bool, or int-range results (ErrorType for invalid combos like float operands).
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: src/checker/expr.rs's infer_binary has no object-type-aware operand dispatch at all (comparisons unconditionally return Type::Bool, Add/etc. never inspect object operands) - there is no operator-overloading mechanism of any kind for user or built-in classes, so this specific BcMath\Number case has no counterpart.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: BcMathNumberUnaryOperatorTypeSpecifyingExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: UnaryOperatorTypeSpecifyingExtension: unary +/- on a BcMath\Number operand (PHP 8.4) stays a BcMath\Number.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: Same root cause as the binary BcMath extension above - no unary-operator/object-overload dispatch exists in the Rust checker at all.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: BcMathStringOrNullReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension covering bcdiv/bcmod/bcpowmod/bcsqrt: works out, per-argument (divisor-by-zero, negative sqrt operand, non-numeric args, negative exponent for powmod), whether the call returns a numeric-string, null, false, or throws (never), version-gated by PhpVersion::throwsTypeErrorForInternalFunctions().
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No occurrence of bcdiv/bcmod/bcpowmod/bcsqrt/BcMath anywhere in src/ - none of the bc* math functions get any special-cased return-type handling.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ClassExistsFunctionTypeSpecifyingExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: FunctionTypeSpecifyingExtension for class_exists()/interface_exists()/trait_exists()/enum_exists(): on the truthy branch narrows a literal class-name-string argument to class-string (or NeverType when the reflection provider already knows the name can't match the requested kind), and for a single known constant string chains an AlwaysRememberedExpr equivalence with class_exists() itself.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: registry.rs's own mention of class_exists (around line 239) is unrelated - it's about which of two conditionally-declared same-named classes wins indexing, not runtime type narrowing. src/checker/narrowing.rs has no is_a/class_exists-family narrowing at all (only is_string/is_int/etc.); no class-string narrowing after a truthy class_exists() check exists.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ClassImplementsFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for class_implements()/class_uses()/class_parents(): strips the false-on-failure member from the stub's return type when the argument is provably an object or class-string/autoloadable, else falls back toward a benevolent union or false.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No occurrence of class_implements/class_uses/class_parents anywhere in src/ - falls back entirely to the generic native stub union type.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ClosureBindDynamicReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicStaticMethodReturnTypeExtension for Closure::bind(): returns the rebound ClosureType (BenevolentUnionType with null for the general case; for a static closure, exactly the closure or exactly null depending on whether $newThis is provably null).
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: Implements the arguably more valuable half - re-checking the closure literal's body with the rebound $this type via check_closure_literal_with_this - but only when the first argument is a literal closure/arrow-fn expression (not an arbitrary Closure-typed value), and does not compute ClosureBindDynamicReturnTypeExtension's own precise return type at all: since no stub declares Closure::bind's signature (no "Closure"/"bind" entry found in registry.rs), the expression's inferred type falls through to plain Mixed rather than ClosureType|null.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ClosureBindToDynamicReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicMethodReturnTypeExtension for Closure::bindTo(): if the receiver is a static closure and the new-$this argument is provably null, returns the closure type unchanged; if provably non-null, returns NullType (rebinding a static closure always fails at runtime); otherwise returns a benevolent union of Closure|null.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: phpstan-rs has real bindTo-aware logic, but it solves a different problem: it re-checks the closure BODY under a rebound $this type (to catch invalid property/method access), reusing the same machinery as Closure::bind and Pest's it()/test(). It does not compute bindTo's own return type (Closure|null vs bare Closure vs NullType based on isStaticClosure()+null-ness of the new-$this arg) - that call's return type falls back to whatever the phpstorm-stubs signature for Closure::bindTo declares generically. So the 'rebind-and-check-body' behavior exists; the 'narrow the bindTo() return type itself' behavior does not.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ClosureFromCallableDynamicReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicStaticMethodReturnTypeExtension for Closure::fromCallable(): inspects the callable-typed argument's callable-parameter-acceptor variants and returns a matching ClosureType (or ErrorType if the argument isn't callable at all).
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No 'fromCallable' handling anywhere in src/checker or src/types.rs; grep for fromCallable/getCurrent in the checker turns up nothing. Closure::fromCallable($x) falls back to the generic phpstorm-stubs signature (a bare Closure return), losing the parameter/return-type transfer from the callable argument.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ClosureGetCurrentDynamicReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicStaticMethodReturnTypeExtension for Closure::getCurrent(): returns NeverType outside an anonymous function, otherwise the reflected type of the currently-executing closure.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No equivalent in src/; requires tracking 'the closure literal currently being analyzed' as a first-class scope concept, which phpstan-rs's Locals/Checker state doesn't model. Falls back to the generic stub return type (static Closure) unconditionally.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: CompactFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for compact(): when every argument resolves to constant string(s) (directly or via a sealed constant array of strings), builds a precise ConstantArrayType keyed by those variable names, using each name's current variable type (and hasVariableType's maybe-ness for optional-key handling); bails to null (generic array) if any argument isn't a knowable constant string set.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: grep for 'compact' across src/checker/*.rs and src/registry.rs finds nothing. compact() resolves only via the generic phpstorm-stubs signature (array<string,mixed> or similar), never building a shaped ConstantArrayType from the actual local variable names/types in scope.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ConstantFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for constant(): for each constant-string argument, builds an Expr for that constant name via ConstantHelper and asks Scope for that expression's type, unioning the results (ErrorType if a name can't be turned into a constant-fetch expression).
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: grep for '"constant"' in checker/expr* finds nothing. constant('FOO') / constant('Class::FOO') resolves only through the generic stub signature (mixed), with no attempt to look up the named constant's actual declared/inferred type.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ConstantHelper
php-dynamic-extensions.description: Pure helper (no check logic of its own): parses a constant-name string ('Foo::BAR' or 'BAR') into a synthetic ClassConstFetch or ConstFetch AST Expr node, used only by ConstantFunctionReturnTypeExtension.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: This is plumbing solely in service of ConstantFunctionReturnTypeExtension's missing feature above; it has no independent behavior to port. Marked not_applicable rather than missing since porting it in isolation (without the extension that calls it) would add nothing - it would need to be reintroduced together with that extension if that feature is ever built.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: CountCharsFunctionDynamicReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for count_chars(): when mode (0-2, default 0) can only be an int in [0,2], returns array<int,int> (or that unioned with false pre-PHP8 ValueError days); otherwise returns string, both PHP-version-gated on whether internal functions throw ValueError.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No 'count_chars' hits anywhere in src/. Falls back to whatever generic stub signature phpstorm-stubs declares for count_chars (a fixed union, not mode-dependent), losing the mode-based array-vs-string distinction and the PHP-version-gated false branch.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: CountFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for count()/sizeof(): for a 'normal' count (1-arg, or explicit COUNT_NORMAL, or the array isn't itself an array-of-arrays) returns the argument's precise getArraySize() (e.g. an exact int for a literal/shaped array); for COUNT_RECURSIVE (or ambiguous mode) falls back to int<1,max> when the argument is provably non-empty-iterable, else null (generic int).
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: grep confirms no 'count'/'sizeof' return-type-extension logic exists (only narrowing.rs's unrelated count($x)>0 narrowing, see CountFunctionTypeSpecifyingExtension below). count($arr) for a literal array like [1,2,3] is not inferred as the constant int 3 anywhere in src/checker or src/types.rs - it resolves to the generic stub 'int' return type only.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: CountFunctionTypeSpecifyingExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: FunctionTypeSpecifyingExtension for count()/sizeof(): in any non-null TypeSpecifierContext, if the first argument's static type is already known to be an array, narrows it to NonEmptyArrayType via the TypeSpecifier machinery (used for e.g. 'if (count($x))' truthy branches).
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: phpstan-rs implements a narrow slice of this: only the literal comparison shapes 'count($x) > 0' and 'count($x) >= 1' on the left-hand side (matched via a Binary op arm), upgrading the array to non-empty via upgrade_array_to_non_empty. It does not implement the general TypeSpecifierContext-based mechanism PHPStan uses (which also covers plain truthy 'if (count($x))', '!count($x)' falsey narrowing, reversed operand order '0 < count($x)', and any other truthy/falsey context), so most real-world count() narrowing idioms outside the two hardcoded comparison shapes are not narrowed.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: CtypeDigitFunctionTypeSpecifyingExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: FunctionTypeSpecifyingExtension for ctype_digit(): narrows the argument to a union of ASCII-digit-range ints (48-57), ints>=256 (interpreted as strings by ctype_*), and (in the true branch) a numeric-string intersection type; additionally, if the argument is a (string) cast, propagates a parallel narrowing onto the pre-cast inner expression.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: grep for 'ctype_digit' across src/checker and src/ top-level finds zero hits. No type-narrowing or return-type handling for any ctype_* function exists in phpstan-rs.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: CurlGetinfoFunctionDynamicReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for curl_getinfo(): with 1 arg (or null/ambiguous 2nd arg) returns a benevolent union of false and a full shaped ConstantArrayType covering ~48 named CURLINFO_* keys; with a 2nd arg resolving to one specific CURLINFO_* constant, returns that option's own precise per-constant type (string/int/float/list/false-union/etc.) from a ~75-entry table matched against actual reflected constant values.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: phpstan-rs implements the 2-argument per-option-constant-type path, but only for a curated ~20-entry subset of the real ~75 CURLINFO_* constants (explicitly documented in the code comment as covering only 'commonly-used constants... rather than transcribing the full table', omitting RTSP/proxy/microsecond/bignum variants). The 1-argument 'return the full shaped array of all curl_getinfo() keys' branch (createAllComponentsReturnType, the ~48-key named-string-keyed array) is not implemented at all - only the 2-arg per-constant path exists.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: DateFormatFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for date_format(): delegates the 2nd (format-string) argument to DateFunctionReturnTypeHelper::getTypeFromFormatType, falling back to plain string with <2 args.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No 'date_format' handling in src/; grep across src/ for DateTime/date_format/DateInterval/createFromDateString all return zero hits outside this audit. Resolves via the generic phpstorm-stubs signature only (a bare string return), with no per-format-character literal-string inference.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: DateFormatMethodReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicMethodReturnTypeExtension for DateTimeInterface::format(): same delegation to DateFunctionReturnTypeHelper as the function-form above, applied to the method-call receiver's format-string argument.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: Same gap as DateFormatFunctionReturnTypeExtension - no DateTimeInterface/DateTime-specific method return-type logic anywhere in src/checker; ->format() resolves only via whatever generic method signature the stubs provide.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: DateFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for date(): same DateFunctionReturnTypeHelper delegation as date_format()/format(), but with useMicrosec=false (date() has no microseconds, unlike DateTime::format()).
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: Same as the two format extensions above - date() has no dedicated handling in src/checker; falls back to the generic stub string return.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: DateFunctionReturnTypeHelper
php-dynamic-extensions.description: Shared helper (not a rule/extension itself) used by the three extensions above: for each constant-string format literal, builds a precise per-format-character return type by switching on known date() format characters (d/j/N/w/m/n/t/L/g/G/h/H/I/u/v get bespoke numeric-range or numeric-string types), and for any other single character calls PHP's real date() function at analysis time to sniff a sample value's shape (numeric-string vs non-falsy-string vs literal constant string).
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No equivalent in src/docblock.rs, src/types.rs, or src/checker/*. This is the core logic all three Date*ReturnTypeExtension classes depend on; its absence is the direct cause of all three being 'missing' above. Building it would require: (1) a per-format-char table mirroring PHP's date() format syntax, and (2) for the general fallback case, literally invoking a PHP-compatible date() formatter at analysis time (or a hardcoded lookup table) since Rust has no native `date()` builtin to shell out to the way real PHPStan does.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: DateIntervalConstructorThrowTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicStaticMethodThrowTypeExtension for `new DateInterval(...)`: for each constant-string ISO-8601 duration argument, actually constructs a real PHP DateInterval to see if it throws; if any literal throws (or the argument type isn't fully covered by literals), reports DateMalformedIntervalStringException (PHP 8.3+) or Exception as a possible throw type.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: phpstan-rs has no dynamic-throw-type-extension mechanism at all (no equivalent of DynamicStaticMethodThrowTypeExtension / per-callee throw-type override), and more fundamentally this specific technique - literally constructing a `new DateInterval($literal)` at analysis time in the host language to observe whether it throws - has no Rust equivalent since Rust cannot instantiate PHP's DateInterval class. A faithful port would need a hand-written ISO-8601 duration-string validator instead of PHP's own real constructor; nothing like that exists in phpstan-rs's checker, and there is no general 'possible throw types from a constructor' feature in src/checker to hang it on regardless.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: DateIntervalCreateFromDateStringThrowTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicStaticMethodThrowTypeExtension for DateInterval::createFromDateString(): same real-PHP-invocation technique as the constructor extension above, but for the relative-date-string parser, PHP-version-gated (only on versions with hasDateTimeExceptions()).
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: Same reasoning as DateIntervalConstructorThrowTypeExtension: no dynamic-throw-type-extension mechanism exists in phpstan-rs, and this specific technique depends on shelling out to real PHP's own relative-date-string parser at analysis time, which has no Rust equivalent to port faithfully.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: DateIntervalDynamicReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicStaticMethodReturnTypeExtension for DateInterval::createFromDateString(): for each constant-string argument, actually calls PHP's real DateInterval::createFromDateString() to see whether it returns false or a DateInterval; if all literals fail, returns NeverType (post-exceptions PHP) or `false`; if all succeed, returns DateInterval; if mixed, returns null (generic fallback: DateInterval|false).
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: grep for 'DateInterval'/'createFromDateString' across src/ returns nothing. Beyond the general 'no dynamic-return-type-extension mechanism for this callee' gap, this again depends on invoking real PHP's date-string parser at analysis time (the same technique noted for the two throw-type extensions above), which has no straightforward Rust port; unlike those two, this one affects an ordinary return type rather than a throw type, so classified missing rather than not_applicable since a hardcoded/approximate relative-date-string validator could plausibly be built to cover it, unlike the throw-type siblings which have no rule surface at all to attach to.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: DateIntervalFormatDynamicReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicMethodReturnTypeExtension for DateInterval::format($format) - delegates to DateIntervalFormatReturnTypeHelper with the format-string arg type and the receiver's type to compute a refined string type.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No DateInterval-specific handling anywhere in src/checker (grep for DateInterval/date_interval_format in src/ finds nothing outside unrelated lexer test comments). Only a generic phpstorm-stubs-derived signature for ->format() would apply (plain string return), with none of the per-literal accessory-type narrowing.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: DateIntervalFormatFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for the global date_interval_format($interval, $format) function, delegating to the same DateIntervalFormatReturnTypeHelper as the method extension.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: Same gap as the method variant - no special-case for date_interval_format in src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs's dynamic-return-type dispatch (infer_builtin_call_return_type).

php-dynamic-extensions.name: DateIntervalFormatReturnTypeHelper
php-dynamic-extensions.description: Shared Helper (not a Rule/extension itself) that, for each constant format-string literal, actually formats a real DateInterval to derive accessory string types (numeric/non-empty/non-falsy/lowercase/uppercase) for the two extensions above.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: This simulate-then-classify technique (running the real PHP stdlib function on literal inputs to derive accessory string types) has no counterpart in phpstan-rs; nothing in types.rs or checker/expr builds AccessoryKind combinations from a DateInterval::format simulation.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: DatePeriodConstructorReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicStaticMethodReturnTypeExtension for `new DatePeriod(...)` that builds the generic GenericObjectType<DatePeriod<TStart,TEnd,TRecurrences>> from the constructor's first/third args (string->DateTime coercion, DateTimeInterface vs int third arg).
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: grep for DatePeriod anywhere under src/ returns nothing. phpstan-rs's generics.rs has general class-template-binding machinery (class_template_bindings/substitute_class_templates) but nothing populates DatePeriod's three template slots from constructor-arg-shape logic the way this extension does; a bare `new DatePeriod(...)` would get whatever generic stub signature phpstorm-stubs supplies, unrefined.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: DateTimeConstructorThrowTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicStaticMethodThrowTypeExtension for `new DateTime(...)`/`new DateTimeImmutable(...)` - simulates parsing each constant-string arg through a real DateTime constructor and reports DateMalformedStringException/Exception as a possible throw type on parse failure or a non-constant arg.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: phpstan-rs has no checked-exception / throw-type tracking system at all (grep for throw_type/ThrowType across src/checker/*.rs finds no dedicated mechanism, only unrelated comments), so no @throws-based extension of any kind - including this one - has an equivalent.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: DateTimeCreateDynamicReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for date_create()/date_create_immutable() - runs date_create() on each constant-string literal arg to decide, per literal, whether the result is DateTime/DateTimeImmutable or `false`.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No date_create handling in src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs's special-cased function list; only a plain phpstorm-stubs-derived signature (unrefined union incl. false) would apply.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: DateTimeDynamicReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for date_create_from_format()/date_create_immutable_from_format() - cross-validates every (format-literal, datetime-literal) pair via DateTime::createFromFormat() to decide DateTime(Immutable) vs `false` per combination.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No equivalent special-casing found anywhere in src/checker; same gap pattern as DateTimeCreateDynamicReturnTypeExtension.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: DateTimeModifyMethodThrowTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicMethodThrowTypeExtension for DateTime::modify()/DateTimeImmutable::modify() (PHP >= 8.3 only) - simulates ->modify() on each constant-string literal to detect a possible DateMalformedStringException throw.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: Same absent-throw-type-system gap as DateTimeConstructorThrowTypeExtension; no PhpVersion-gated exception modeling exists for DateTime methods.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: DateTimeModifyReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicMethodReturnTypeExtension (not #[AutowiredService] - registered per-class via a constructor `$dateTimeClass` param, once for DateTime and once for DateTimeImmutable) for ->modify() - simulates modify() on literal args to decide between `false`/never/null/narrowed-caller-type return, including narrowing a union caller type down to its DateTimeInterface members via TypeTraverser.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No DateTime::modify special-casing anywhere in src/checker; also no TypeTraverser-equivalent generic type-tree-mapping utility was found used this way in expr.rs.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: DateTimeSubMethodThrowTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicMethodThrowTypeExtension for DateTime::sub()/DateTimeImmutable::sub() - unconditionally reports DateInvalidOperationException as a possible throw when PHP >= 8.3's DateTime exceptions are active and at least one arg is passed.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: Same absent-throw-type-system gap; trivial in PHPStan (no argument analysis, just a version+method-name gate) but still requires the throw-type infrastructure phpstan-rs doesn't have.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: DateTimeZoneConstructorThrowTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicStaticMethodThrowTypeExtension for `new DateTimeZone(...)` - simulates the constructor on constant-string literals to detect DateInvalidTimeZoneException/Exception.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: Same absent-throw-type-system gap as the other DateTime*ThrowTypeExtension entries; no DateTimeZone handling found in src/ at all.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: DefineConstantTypeSpecifyingExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: FunctionTypeSpecifyingExtension (TypeSpecifierAwareExtension) that, after a `define('NAME', $value)` call in null/statement context, registers NAME's ConstFetch as having $value's type for the rest of the scope (an always-overwrite narrowing).
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: phpstan-rs has no dedicated AST node or type-inference path for a bare constant reference at all (no ConstFetch equivalent in src/ast.rs, confirmed by grep across ast.rs/checker), and GlobalConst (`const X = ...`) statements are only inspected for yield-containment in control_flow.rs, never given a tracked type. There is no scope-level type-narrowing hook (TypeSpecifier-equivalent) for constants to build this on.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: DefinedConstantTypeSpecifyingExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: FunctionTypeSpecifyingExtension that, in the truthy branch of `defined('NAME')`, tells TypeSpecifier that NAME's ConstFetch expression is now known/typed (via ConstantHelper), letting later code use the constant without an 'undefined constant' complaint.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: Same root cause as DefineConstantTypeSpecifyingExtension - no constant-fetch expression modeling or narrowing-by-condition system for constants exists to hang this off of; grep for "defined"/ConstFetch-style handling in checker/narrowing.rs and checker/expr.rs finds nothing.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: DioStatDynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for the dio extension's dio_stat() - hardcodes the exact 13-key int-valued constant array shape (or null) it returns, since the PHP manual/stubs can't express that structural detail as a static signature.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No dio_stat handling in src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs; a plain phpstorm-stubs-derived signature (likely array|false or similar) would apply with none of the specific 13-key shape. Low-impact (dio is a rarely-installed PECL extension) but not architecturally inapplicable - phpstan-rs already builds equivalent hardcoded ConstantArrayTypeBuilder-style shapes for other functions (e.g. curl_getinfo in the same builtin_calls.rs file), so this is a real, buildable gap, not a not_applicable case.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: DomDocumentCreateElementDynamicReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicMethodReturnTypeExtension for DOMDocument::createElement() - runs the real DOMDocument::createElement() on each constant-string tag-name literal to detect a guaranteed-valid name, then strips the `false` member from the normal return-type variant when every literal is valid.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No DOMDocument/createElement handling anywhere in src/ (grep confirms). extension_loaded() gating is also unmodeled - phpstan-rs has no concept of which PHP extensions are considered loaded/available.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: DomDocumentCreateElementDynamicThrowTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicMethodThrowTypeExtension mirroring the return-type extension above - reports DOMException as a possible throw unless every constant-string tag-name literal arg is proven valid via the same real-createElement simulation.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: Same absent-throw-type-system gap as the DateTime*ThrowTypeExtension entries, plus the same total absence of DOMDocument-specific handling.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: DsMapDynamicMethodThrowTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicMethodThrowTypeExtension for the php-ds extension's Ds\Map::get()/remove() - reports the method's declared throw type (OutOfBoundsException, from the stub's @throws) only when called with the 1-arg (no default) form, and VoidType (no throw) when a default/second arg is supplied.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No throw-type system in phpstan-rs at all (see DateTime*ThrowTypeExtension notes), and Ds\Map is a rarely-installed PECL extension; not marked not_applicable since a throws-tracking feature is architecturally plausible to add, just entirely unbuilt.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: DsMapDynamicReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicMethodReturnTypeExtension for Ds\Map::get($key)/remove($key) (1-arg form only) that walks the receiver's ancestor-with-class-name to Ds\Map and returns its active TValue template-type binding directly.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: phpstan-rs has no Ds\Map-specific code, but it does have a general class-template + method-template substitution pipeline (generics.rs's substitute_class_templates combined with expr.rs's infer_call_return_type, wired together for method calls around expr.rs:1665-1696). Empirically verified: for `/** @param \Ds\Map<string,int> $m */ function f($m){ $v = $m->get('a'); }`, phpstan-rs's checker infers `$v` as `int|mixed` (vendored ds.php stub's TValue resolves correctly to int via class-template propagation, but the method's own @template TDefault - unbound since no 2nd arg was passed - falls back to Mixed instead of PHPStan's more precise `int|null`, since default-parameter-value-implied template binding isn't modeled). So the general mechanism covers the common case with a real but less-precise result than the dedicated extension; the specific ancestor-walk/arg-count logic itself is not separately implemented.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ExplodeFunctionDynamicReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for explode(): computes empty-delimiter error/false cases, lowercase/uppercase-preserving accessory types on elements, a precise single-element result for limit 0/1, a guaranteed-2+-element split when str_contains/str_starts_with/str_ends_with prove the delimiter occurs, non-empty-array intersection for non-negative/-1 limits, and a benevolent union when the delimiter type is Mixed.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: Implemented as a fixed simplified answer: always Array<String> & ArrayList & NonEmptyArray for the 2-3 arg form, regardless of limit value, delimiter content, or provable-substring reasoning. None of PHP's limit-based branching (single-element for limit<=1, exact 2..N-element constant-array shapes, unsealed-with-cap for larger limits), the empty-delimiter false/never case, the lower/upper-case accessory propagation, or the Mixed-delimiter benevolent-union case are modeled. Comment in source explicitly notes this is a corpus-driven simplification of the real extension.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: FilterFunctionReturnTypeHelper
php-dynamic-extensions.description: Shared helper (not itself a Rule/extension, but injected into 4 filter_* extensions below) implementing the full filter_var/filter_input semantics: maps FILTER_VALIDATE_*/FILTER_SANITIZE_* constants to result types, applies FILTER_NULL_ON_FAILURE/FILTER_REQUIRE_ARRAY/FILTER_FORCE_ARRAY/FILTER_THROW_ON_FAILURE flag logic, exact-value narrowing for literal inputs (bool/int/float/string coercion rules including octal/hex parsing), min_range/max_range option handling via IntegerRangeType, and non-empty-string preservation.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No filter_var/filter_input handling of any kind exists in src/ (grepped for filter_var, filter_input, FILTER_VALIDATE, FILTER_DEFAULT - zero hits outside this audit). Calls to filter_var()/filter_input() fall back to whatever static stub signature vendor/phpstorm-stubs provides via src/php_stubs.rs, with none of this per-call narrowing.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: FilterInputDynamicReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: Thin DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension wrapper for filter_input(): resolves the INPUT_GET/POST/COOKIE/SERVER/ENV type argument and delegates the rest to FilterFunctionReturnTypeHelper::getInputType.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No dispatch on 'filter_input' anywhere in src/; depends entirely on the missing FilterFunctionReturnTypeHelper.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: FilterVarArrayDynamicReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for filter_var_array()/filter_input_array(): builds a per-key constant-array result type by matching each input array key against either a single filter id or a per-key filter-definition array, honoring the $add_empty option and unsealed/optional-key propagation.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No dispatch on 'filter_var_array'/'filter_input_array' in src/; depends on the missing FilterFunctionReturnTypeHelper.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: FilterVarDynamicReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: Thin DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension wrapper for filter_var(): resolves input/filter/flags argument types and delegates to FilterFunctionReturnTypeHelper::getType.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No dispatch on 'filter_var' in src/; filter_var() calls get only the generic phpstorm-stubs static signature (mixed/bool|... depending on stub), none of the constant-driven narrowing.
