php-dynamic-extensions.name: FilterVarThrowTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionThrowTypeExtension for filter_var(): when the flags argument may include FILTER_THROW_ON_FAILURE (PHP 8.5+), declares the call can throw Filter\FilterFailedException.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No DynamicFunctionThrowTypeExtension-equivalent mechanism exists in phpstan-rs at all (grepped for ThrowType/throw_type/DynamicFunctionThrowType - zero hits), so per-call throw-type inference for any function, not just filter_var, is entirely absent. Combined with the missing FilterFunctionReturnTypeHelper (FILTER_THROW_ON_FAILURE constant/flag detection), this is unreachable as-is.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: FunctionExistsFunctionTypeSpecifyingExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: FunctionTypeSpecifyingExtension: in the true branch of `function_exists($x)`, narrows a literal string argument by re-running the check against the leading-backslash-stripped name, and narrows a non-literal argument's type to CallableType.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: narrowing.rs has no case for 'function_exists' (grepped narrowing.rs/*.rs - zero direct hits; the one hit in stmt.rs is unrelated dead-code-declaration handling for `if (!function_exists('foo')) { function foo(){} }`, not type narrowing of the argument expression). No CallableType narrowing on function_exists()'s truthy branch exists.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: GetCalledClassDynamicReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for get_called_class(): returns the late-static-bound `static::class` type when inside a class, else ConstantBooleanType(false).
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No 'get_called_class' dispatch anywhere in src/; calls fall back to the generic phpstorm-stubs signature (plain class-string|false), losing the late-static-binding precision get_class-with-no-args-style extensions provide.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: GetClassDynamicReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for get_class(): 0-arg form returns ClassStringType in a trait or the enclosing class's literal class-string outside one (or false outside any class); 1-arg form special-cases $this-typed values in traits and otherwise delegates to Type::toGetClassResultType().
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: Only the 1-arg case is handled, and only when the argument's inferred type is exactly Type::Object(class, _): returns ClassString(Object(class)). Missing: the 0-arg form entirely (no ClassConstFetch('static')-equivalent lookup, no trait-vs-class-vs-global distinction); trait-scope $this-type special case; and the general toGetClassResultType() dispatch for non-Object argument types (unions of objects, StaticType/ThisType, etc.) - those fall through to whatever the generic call-return inference produces instead of a proper class-string union.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: GetDebugTypeFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for get_debug_type(): maps the argument's type to the exact string get_debug_type() would report at runtime ('null','bool','int','float','string','array', or the concrete/anonymous class name for objects, with union-type argument handled member-wise).
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No 'get_debug_type' dispatch in src/; falls back to the generic stub (plain string), losing all literal-string narrowing.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: GetDefinedVarsFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for get_defined_vars(): when the scope tracks all variables precisely, builds a constant array type keyed by each currently-defined variable name (required) and each maybe-defined variable name (optional) mapped to its scope-tracked type; otherwise falls back to array<string, mixed>.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No 'get_defined_vars' dispatch in src/, despite phpstan-rs's Locals map being a plausible source for exactly this kind of per-variable-type introspection; calls get only the generic array<string, mixed>-shaped stub.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: GetParentClassDynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for get_parent_class(): resolves the parent-class literal string (or false when there is none, or class-string|false when the class is unknown/an interface) for the 0-arg in-class form and for 1-arg forms driven by literal class-name strings, $this/static values (including late-static-binding's class-string<Parent> widening for non-final classes), with trait-scope handled as unresolvable (null).
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No 'get_parent_class' dispatch in src/; falls back to the generic phpstorm-stubs signature (class-string|false, unnarrowed).

php-dynamic-extensions.name: GettimeofdayDynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for gettimeofday(): returns a fixed-shape constant array type when $as_float is absent or provably false, float when provably true, and a (benevolent, for Mixed) union of both when unknown.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No 'gettimeofday' dispatch in src/; falls back to the generic stub union type without the argument-driven narrowing.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: GettypeFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for gettype(): maps the argument's type to the exact runtime string gettype() would return ('string','array','boolean','resource'|'resource (closed)','integer','double','NULL','object', or the full 10-way union when nothing is known), traversing through union/intersection members via TypeTraverser.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No 'gettype' dispatch in src/; falls back to the generic stub (plain string), losing all literal-string narrowing.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: GmpOperatorTypeSpecifyingExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: OperatorTypeSpecifyingExtension: for binary arithmetic/bitwise/comparison operators where either operand is a GMP object, returns bool for comparisons, int<-1,1> for spaceship, and GMP for arithmetic/bitwise ops when the other operand is int/numeric-string/GMP (else ErrorType).
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: infer_binary (src/checker/expr.rs:2338) has no operator-type-specifying-extension mechanism at all - every arithmetic/bitwise operator arm assumes plain numeric operands (int/float promotion only); there is no hook for object-operand overloading of any kind (GMP or otherwise), so GMP objects used with arithmetic operators get the generic Int/Float/Union(Int,Float) answer instead of GMP/ErrorType. No GMP class stub-specific handling found either.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: GmpUnaryOperatorTypeSpecifyingExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: UnaryOperatorTypeSpecifyingExtension: unary -, +, ~ on a GMP object operand returns GMP.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No unary-operator-type-specifying-extension mechanism exists in phpstan-rs (same gap as the binary GMP extension above); unary operators on any object operand aren't given special-cased handling.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: HashFunctionsReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension covering hash()/hash_file()/hash_hkdf()/hash_hmac()/hash_hmac_file()/hash_pbkdf2(): for a literal algorithm-name argument, checks it against the runtime hash_algos() list and (for the *_hmac*/hkdf/pbkdf2 variants) against a non-cryptographic-algorithm blocklist, returning a non-falsy lowercase-or-not string intersection type or a never/false 'invalid algorithm' type per PHP-version throw semantics, unioned with false where the function can fail on I/O.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No dispatch on any of these 6 function names in src/; all fall back to generic phpstorm-stubs signatures (typically string|false), losing the algorithm-validity and non-falsy/lowercase narrowing.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: HighlightStringDynamicReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for highlight_string(): with $return provably true returns string, otherwise bool (or true, on PHP versions where the function no longer returns false).
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No 'highlight_string' dispatch in src/; falls back to the generic stub, without narrowing on the $return argument.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: HrtimeFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: Dynamic return-type extension for hrtime(): with no args or a falsy $as_number arg returns a fixed 2-tuple list array<int<1,max>, int<0,999999999>>; with a truthy arg returns int<1,max>|float; uncertain arg returns the union of both.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: grep for "hrtime" across src/ finds nothing. phpstan-rs's build.rs generates hrtime's signature straight from phpstorm-stubs (a static declared return type), but no Rust code special-cases the boolean-argument overload the way this extension does, so callers just get the stub's generic union, not the arg-dependent narrowed array/number split.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: IdateFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: Dynamic return-type extension for idate(): delegates to IdateFunctionReturnTypeHelper using the literal format-character argument's type; returns false for a zero-arg call.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No "idate" occurrence anywhere in src/. Falls back entirely to whatever generic signature the generated phpstorm-stubs give idate() (bool|int), with none of the per-format-character narrowing.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: IdateFunctionReturnTypeHelper
php-dynamic-extensions.description: Pure helper mapping each idate()/date() format character (d, h, H, i, m, N, s, w, y, z, ...) to a specific IntegerRangeType (or plain int, or false for unrecognized characters).
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: Companion helper to IdateFunctionReturnTypeExtension above; same absence. No format-character-to-IntegerRange table exists in src/ for idate/date.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ImplodeFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: Dynamic return-type extension for implode()/join(): for constant array + constant separator, incrementally constant-folds every possible resulting string (respecting optional/sealed keys, capped by CALCULATE_SCALARS_LIMIT); otherwise infers accessory string types (non-empty/non-falsy/literal-string/lowercase/uppercase) from the array's iterable value type and separator.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No "implode" or "join" special-casing found in src/checker or src/types.rs; implode/join get only the generic `string` return type from the generated phpstorm-stubs signature. No constant-folding of literal arrays into constant strings, and none of the accessory-type (non-empty-string, literal-string, etc.) propagation.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: InArrayFunctionTypeSpecifyingExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: TypeSpecifyingExtension for in_array(): for a literal array-expression haystack, combines per-item ===/== comparisons; otherwise (loose or strict) narrows the needle to the array's value type (true branch) or the intersection/exclusion of guaranteed finite values (false branch, only when every possible array variant has literal-valued required keys), and asserts the haystack is a NonEmptyArrayType on truthy match.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: Phase 33 Finding 2 (documented in-code) deliberately narrows only the strict-comparison, all-bare-literal-array-elements case: needle narrowed to/excluding the union of the haystack's literal values via narrow_type_to/narrow_type_excluding. Missing vs. real PHPStan: non-strict-comparison narrowing to the array's iterable value type, per-item Identical/Equal decomposition for a literal Array_ haystack whose elements aren't all bare literals, enum-aware auto-strict detection, and the NonEmptyArrayType assertion on the haystack argument itself.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: IniGetReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: Dynamic return-type extension for ini_get(): maps specific known ini key literals (date.timezone, memory_limit, max_execution_time, precision, etc., plus max_memory_limit when the target PHP version supports it) to string or numeric-string types; falls through to the default (string|false) for unrecognized keys.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No "ini_get" occurrence in src/. ini_get() gets only the generic phpstorm-stubs-derived signature (string|false); none of the per-key type refinement exists.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: IntdivThrowTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionThrowTypeExtension for intdiv(): reports ArithmeticError when dividend could be PHP_INT_MIN and divisor could be -1, and DivisionByZeroError when the divisor could be 0.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No "intdiv" special-casing in src/, and more fundamentally phpstan-rs has no DynamicFunctionThrowTypeExtension-equivalent mechanism at all (no per-call-site throw-type inference feeding an uncaught-exception or uncaught-checked-exception rule) - grep for throw_type/ThrowType/DivisionByZeroError/ArithmeticError across src/ returns nothing. This is a whole missing subsystem, not just this one function.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: IsAFunctionTypeSpecifyingExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: TypeSpecifyingExtension for is_a($obj, $class, $allow_string = false): narrows the first argument's type to the target class (via IsAFunctionTypeSpecifyingHelper), requiring the class-name argument to be a single known constant string unless in a truthy context.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: grep for "is_a"/IsAFunction across src/ finds nothing (registry.rs's is_subclass_of is an unrelated internal class-hierarchy helper, not a runtime is_a()-call type specifier). No narrowing occurs on `if (is_a($x, Foo::class))` in phpstan-rs today.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: IsAFunctionTypeSpecifyingHelper
php-dynamic-extensions.description: Shared helper used by both the is_a() and is_subclass_of() type-specifying extensions: delegates to Type::toObjectTypeForIsACheck() and suppresses the narrowing when the result would be a false-positive (uncertain result whose type is already a supertype of the input).
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No equivalent helper or Type::toObjectTypeForIsACheck-style method exists in src/types.rs; companion to the two missing extensions above and below.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: IsArrayFunctionTypeSpecifyingExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: TypeSpecifyingExtension for is_array(): narrows the argument to ArrayType(mixed, mixed) in both the true and false context.
php-dynamic-extensions.our_location: src/checker/narrowing.rs:832 (narrowing_type_for_predicate table, "is_array" => Type::Array(Box::new(Type::Mixed))), applied at src/checker/narrowing.rs:227-235
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: Functionally equivalent for single-argument is_array($x) calls in both if-true and if-false (else) branches, including inside Or-chains via or_chain_narrowing_target. Minor gap: Rust's Type::Mixed doesn't distinguish PHPStan's "implicit mixed" marker used in the real extension's MixedType(true), which has no observable effect here.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: IsCallableFunctionTypeSpecifyingExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: TypeSpecifyingExtension for is_callable(): ordinary case narrows the argument to CallableType; special-cased when the argument is a 2-element array literal [$obj, 'method'] and the array is already a plausibly-callable constant array, which it rewrites into a method_exists() check via MethodExistsTypeSpecifyingExtension combined with a CallableType assertion on the whole array expression.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: The base narrowing (single-arg is_callable($x) narrows to/excludes Type::Callable in true/false context) works via the same generic predicate table as is_array/is_string. Missing: the [$obj, 'method']-array special case entirely - there is no method_exists narrowing in src/ at all (grep for method_exists in narrowing.rs is empty), so is_callable([$x, 'foo']) never narrows $x's array-callable-ness the way real PHPStan does.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: IsIterableFunctionTypeSpecifyingExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: TypeSpecifyingExtension for is_iterable(): narrows the argument to IterableType(mixed, mixed) in both true and false context.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: narrowing_type_for_predicate's table (src/checker/narrowing.rs:826-866) covers is_string/is_int/is_float/is_bool/is_array/is_countable/is_null/is_object/is_callable/is_resource/is_scalar but has no "is_iterable" entry, so `if (is_iterable($x))` performs no narrowing today.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: IsSubclassOfFunctionTypeSpecifyingExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: TypeSpecifyingExtension for is_subclass_of($obj, $class, $allow_string = true): only narrows in the true context, delegating to IsAFunctionTypeSpecifyingHelper::determineType with allowSameClass=false (unlike is_a, a class is not considered its own subclass here).
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No runtime is_subclass_of()-call type-specifying logic exists in src/ (registry.rs's is_subclass_of is an unrelated internal class-hierarchy query used by the checker itself, e.g. in checker/stmt.rs and checker/expr.rs, not a condition-narrowing extension for user code calling the PHP function is_subclass_of()).

php-dynamic-extensions.name: IteratorToArrayFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: Dynamic return-type extension for iterator_to_array(): when $preserve_keys is definitely false, returns a re-indexed list (int keys from 0, AccessoryArrayListType); otherwise returns ArrayType keyed by the traversable's own key type coerced to a valid array key (or NeverType if that key type can't be a valid array key at all).
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: grep for "iterator_to_array" across src/ returns nothing; it falls back to the generic phpstorm-stubs-derived array return type with no preserve-keys-aware narrowing or list-ness inference.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: JsonThrowOnErrorDynamicReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: Dynamic return-type extension covering both json_encode() and json_decode(): for json_decode, narrows the return type from a literal JSON string argument (actually running json_decode on it, respecting the assoc/force-array flag derived from either the 2nd bool arg or the 4th-arg JSON_OBJECT_AS_ARRAY flag) or removes ObjectWithoutClassType when force-array is certain; for both functions, strips the `false` member from the return type when the flags argument's bitwise-OR chain provably contains JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: Only the json_encode half (stripping `false` when JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR is present in the flags bitwise-OR chain) is implemented, explicitly noted in-code as "Phase 32 Finding J". The json_decode half is entirely absent: no THROW_ON_ERROR-based false-stripping for json_decode, and no literal-string constant-folding / force-array-aware narrowing of json_decode's return type (grep for json_decode in checker/php_stubs shows no special-case logic, only generic stub coverage in a test).

php-dynamic-extensions.name: JsonThrowTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionThrowTypeExtension for json_encode()/json_decode(): reports a possible JsonException throw whenever the relevant flags argument's bitwise-OR chain could contain JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: Same root cause as IntdivThrowTypeExtension: phpstan-rs has no throw-type extension mechanism at all, so even though the JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR bit-flag detection helper itself exists and is reused for json_encode's return-type stripping (contains_json_throw_on_error in builtin_calls.rs), there is no corresponding throw-type / uncaught-exception consumer of that fact.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: LocaltimeFunctionDynamicReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: Dynamic return-type extension for localtime(): builds a precise constant-array shape (either a numeric list or an associative tm_sec/tm_min/.../tm_isdst array, each field with a specific IntegerRangeType) depending on whether the associative-mode second argument is certainly true, certainly false, or unknown (union of both shapes).
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No "localtime" occurrence in src/; falls back to the generic phpstorm-stubs signature, with no field-level range typing or associative/list-shape distinction.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: LtrimFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: Dynamic return-type extension for ltrim(): propagates lowercase/uppercase accessory string types from the input when no charlist trimming would break them; for a constant input string and constant charlist, constant-folds the exact ltrim() result (also special-casing '\\' preserving class-string-ness and a non-digit charlist preserving numeric-string-ness).
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No "ltrim" special-casing anywhere in src/ (grep across checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs, types.rs turns up nothing); ltrim() gets only the generic phpstorm-stubs `string` return type, with none of the accessory-type propagation or constant-folding.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: MbConvertEncodingFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for mb_convert_encoding(): intersects the stub's return type with a generalized (array-structure-preserving but literal-value-stripping) version of the subject's type, and reasons about the $from_encoding argument (array with 2+ candidates, or a comma-list/'auto' string) to decide whether `false` (auto-detect failure) stays in the return type, PHP-version-gated via PhpVersion::throwsValueErrorForInternalFunctions().
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: Rust only implements the array-stripping half, scoped to a string (not array) subject via `strip_array_member`; it does not generalize array-shaped subjects, does not inspect $from_encoding at all, and does not do the false-removal/PHP-version-gated ValueError reasoning. Comment in source explicitly says 'only the array-stripping half is evidenced here'.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: MbFunctionsReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for mb_http_output, mb_regex_encoding, mb_internal_encoding, mb_encoding_aliases, mb_chr, mb_ord: reads the encoding argument at a per-function fixed position, validates it against the real supported-encodings list (via the trait), and narrows the stub's bool/string union or removes/keeps `false` accordingly (throwing NeverType on invalid encoding when PhpVersion::throwsOnInvalidMbStringEncoding()).
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No handling for any of mb_http_output/mb_regex_encoding/mb_internal_encoding/mb_encoding_aliases/mb_chr/mb_ord in src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs or elsewhere; grep across src/ for these names finds nothing beyond stub-level signatures (if any).

php-dynamic-extensions.name: MbFunctionsReturnTypeExtensionTrait
php-dynamic-extensions.description: Shared trait (helper, no rule of its own) providing isSupportedEncoding()/getSupportedEncodings(), which queries the real PHP runtime's mb_list_encodings()/mb_encoding_aliases() to build the true set of valid mbstring encoding names (with a PHP 7.3/7.4 'pass'/'none' carve-out), used by MbFunctionsReturnTypeExtension and MbStrlenFunctionReturnTypeExtension.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: Pure helper class, not a rule by itself, so graded on whether its capability exists anywhere in Rust: it doesn't - there is no encoding-name validation list/lookup in src/, since none of its two consumers are implemented either.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: MbStrlenFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for mb_strlen(): for constant-string subjects with valid/known encodings it computes exact possible lengths (union of ConstantIntegerType or an IntegerRangeType when the lengths form a contiguous run) by actually invoking PHP's mb_strlen() at analysis time; otherwise falls back to non-empty-string/boolean-aware int<1,max>/int<0,1> ranges, unioned with `false` when an unsupported encoding could be passed and the PHP version doesn't throw for it.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No mb_strlen special-casing found anywhere in src/; falls through to whatever the plain function-signature stub declares, with no length computation, no encoding validation, no false-removal logic.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: MbSubstituteCharacterDynamicReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for mb_substitute_character(): with no args returns the union of valid string keywords ('none'/'long'/'entity') and valid code-point integer ranges (PHP-version-gated for surrogate exclusion and 0-based vs 1-based minimum); with an arg, evaluates whether a given int/string/null constant is a valid substitute-character value and returns a ConstantBooleanType(true/false) or NeverType depending on PHP-version throw behavior.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No mb_substitute_character handling anywhere in src/checker; would fall through to the generic stub return type with none of this constant-value validation.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: MethodExistsTypeSpecifyingExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: FunctionTypeSpecifyingExtension for method_exists($obj, 'methodName') in a truthy context: when the method name is a single constant string and the given object/class type doesn't already statically declare that method, narrows the first argument's type to an intersection/union carrying a HasMethodType(methodName) accessory (or, for a non-class-string, a plain ConstantBooleanType(true) fact) so later code proving method_exists() true can call that dynamic method without a rule-level 'method not found' error.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: phpstan-rs's narrowing_type_for_predicate table explicitly excludes method_exists (and property_exists/class_exists/function_exists/in_array/array_key_exists) - src/checker/tests/narrowing.rs:192-203 documents this was a deliberate scoping decision, not an oversight, since the mechanism only fits single-arg predicates narrowing a bare variable to one concrete Type, and there is no HasMethodType-style accessory kind in AccessoryKind (src/types.rs:85) to represent 'has this dynamic method' at all.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: MicrotimeFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for microtime($as_float): with no arg or a literal false, returns a non-falsy-string intersection type; with a literal true, returns float; with a MixedType arg, returns a BenevolentUnionType of both; otherwise a plain UnionType of both.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: Core true/false-literal narrowing (float vs string) is implemented via types::is_subtype against Type::True/Type::False. Gaps: the no-arg/false case returns plain Type::String rather than the real non-falsy-string intersection (AccessoryNonFalsyStringType not applied here), and there is no BenevolentUnionType concept for the Mixed-argument case (falls through to whatever default union the generic stub produces).

php-dynamic-extensions.name: MinMaxFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for min()/max(): for the 2-arg scalar form, rewrites the call as a Smaller-comparison ternary and reuses the scope's own ternary-type inference; for constant arrays/iterables/variadic argument lists, it constant-folds by directly comparing ConstantScalarType/ConstantArrayType values (recursively for nested arrays) to pick the exact min/max member type where determinable, falling back to a plain union otherwise; also reasons about array emptiness to add/remove ConstantBooleanType(false) per PhpVersion::throwsValueErrorForInternalFunctions().
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No special-casing of "min"/"max" function names found anywhere in src/checker or src/types.rs (the only "min"/"max" hits in src/types.rs are unrelated - IntegerRangeType's own open-ended-bound keyword parsing at types.rs:580-587). Calls to min()/max() fall through to the plain function-signature stub with no constant-folding narrowing.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: NonEmptyStringFunctionsReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for addslashes, addcslashes, escapeshellarg, escapeshellcmd, htmlspecialchars, htmlentities, urlencode, urldecode, preg_quote, rawurlencode, rawurldecode: propagates the subject argument's non-falsy-string or non-empty-string accessory type onto the (otherwise plain string) return type; for htmlspecialchars/htmlentities specifically, only does so when the ENT_SUBSTITUTE flag bit is set on a constant-int flags argument (or absent, defaulting to substitute-enabled), since otherwise invalid UTF-8 input can make the function return an empty string.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: grep for any of addslashes/htmlspecialchars/urlencode/preg_quote/escapeshellarg/rawurlencode in src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs finds no matches - these all fall through to whatever plain `string` return the stub table declares, with no non-empty/non-falsy propagation.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: NumberFormatFunctionDynamicReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for number_format(): when the 4th ($thousands_sep) argument is the constant empty string and the 3rd ($decimal_separator) argument is a constant '.', '', or null, returns a numeric-string-accessory-intersected string type instead of a plain string.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No number_format handling found in src/; falls through to plain `string` stub return with no AccessoryNumericStringType-equivalent refinement (the AccessoryKind enum does have NumericString at src/types.rs:165, so the type-system building block exists, but nothing wires number_format's specific argument-shape reasoning to it).

php-dynamic-extensions.name: OpenSslCipherMethodsProvider
php-dynamic-extensions.description: Plain helper/provider service (no Type/Rule interface of its own) that queries the real PHP runtime's openssl_get_cipher_methods()/openssl_cipher_iv_length() to build and cache a lowercase list of actually-usable OpenSSL cipher method names, shared by OpenSslEncryptParameterOutTypeExtension and OpensslCipherFunctionsReturnTypeExtension.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No OpenSSL-related handling of any kind exists in src/ (grep for 'openssl' across src/ finds zero matches outside this audit). Since this helper only exists to serve the two other openssl extensions below, and neither of those is implemented, there's nothing in Rust for it to back.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: OpenSslEncryptParameterOutTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: FunctionParameterOutTypeExtension for openssl_encrypt()'s by-ref $tag parameter: for each constant-string cipher name given as $cipher, determines the by-ref output type of $tag as a non-empty-string (for GCM/CCM AEAD modes) or null (non-AEAD modes, or an unsupported cipher name), unioning across all possible cipher values.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: openssl_encrypt is not referenced anywhere in src/; more generally, while phpstan-rs does have an ad hoc mechanism for by-ref-parameter output types (e.g. preg_match's $matches shape in src/checker/expr/preg_shapes.rs and src/checker/calls.rs:38), it is not a generic FunctionParameterOutTypeExtension-style dispatch table, and openssl_encrypt's $tag parameter has no hook into it at all.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: OpensslCipherFunctionsReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for openssl_cipher_iv_length() and openssl_cipher_key_length(): on PHP versions that throw a ValueError for invalid internal-function arguments, checks the constant-string algorithm argument against OpenSslCipherMethodsProvider's supported-methods list and removes `false` from (or collapses entirely to) the return type accordingly.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No openssl_cipher_iv_length/openssl_cipher_key_length handling anywhere in src/checker; these fall through to the plain stub-declared return type unconditionally.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: OutputBufferingDynamicReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for ob_get_contents/ob_get_clean/ob_get_flush/ob_get_length: recursively asks the scope for the current type of ob_get_level() and, if that's provably >=1 (i.e. output buffering is known active from an unbalanced prior ob_start() in the same scope), converts the default return type to a BenevolentUnionType so the false-error branch doesn't need to be checked.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No ob_get_contents/ob_get_clean/ob_get_flush/ob_get_length/ob_get_level handling anywhere in src/; also, phpstan-rs's Type enum has no BenevolentUnionType-equivalent concept at all in src/types.rs, so even a partial reimplementation would need a new type variant, not just a new match arm.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: PDOConnectReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicStaticMethodReturnTypeExtension for PDO::connect(): when PhpVersion::hasPDOSubclasses() (PHP 8.4+) and the DSN argument is one or more constant strings with a recognized driver prefix (mysql:/firebird:/dblib:/odbc:/pgsql:/sqlite:), returns a union of the corresponding PDO\<Driver> subclass ObjectTypes instead of the generic declared PDO return type.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: grep for 'connect' / static-method-call dynamic return type dispatch in src/checker/calls.rs finds nothing - phpstan-rs has no DynamicStaticMethodReturnTypeExtension-equivalent mechanism at all, and PDO subclass modeling (PDO\Mysql etc.) is absent from the class registry (registry.rs's only PDO mentions are unrelated doc-comment text about vendor stub file layout).

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ParseStrParameterOutTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: FunctionParameterOutTypeExtension for parse_str()/mb_parse_str()'s by-ref $result parameter: builds an array<string, string> type for it (with the value type carrying lowercase/uppercase-string accessories propagated from the subject $string argument's own case-ness), or array<int|string, array|string> to account for PHP's nested-bracket-syntax query-string parsing.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: parse_str/mb_parse_str are not referenced anywhere in src/. Additionally, AccessoryKind (src/types.rs:85-91) has no LowercaseString/UppercaseString variant, so even the case-propagation half has no type-system building block to hang off of.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ParseUrlFunctionDynamicReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for parse_url(): for constant-string URL arguments, actually invokes PHP's own parse_url() at analysis time to compute an exact literal return value/type per possible $component; otherwise builds a cached lookup table mapping each PHP_URL_* component constant (and the no-component 'all components' case) to precise per-key types (string|false|null, an int<0,65535> port range, or a components ConstantArrayType), lowercase-string-aware when the URL argument is known lowercase.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: parse_url is not referenced anywhere in src/checker; falls through to whatever the plain stub declares (likely a much looser array|string|int|false|null union with no per-component precision and no literal-URL evaluation).

php-dynamic-extensions.name: PathinfoFunctionDynamicReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for pathinfo(): with 1 arg, builds a precise shaped array (dirname/basename/extension/filename keys, dirname optional only when the path isn't known non-empty, extension always optional) instead of the generic array; with a 2nd $flags arg, resolves the PATHINFO_ALL constant's actual integer value via reflection and, for constant flag values, returns either the full shaped array (if flags === PATHINFO_ALL) or plain string per possible flag value, unioned.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: pathinfo is not referenced anywhere in src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs or elsewhere in src/; falls through to whatever generic array|string the stub table declares, with no shaped-array modeling and no PATHINFO_* flag-constant reasoning.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: PowFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for pow($base,$exp): delegates entirely to scope->getType() on a synthesized ** (Pow) binary-op AST node, reusing whatever precision the Pow operator's own type inference has (including literal constant-folding).
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: pow() itself is never special-cased in builtin_calls.rs (grep for "pow" finds nothing besides the ** parser/AST token), so a pow() call just gets the generic stub return type. Even the underlying `**` BinOp::Pow arithmetic that PHPStan's extension would delegate to is only Int/Float widening in Rust (no literal folding to a ConstantIntegerType/ConstantFloatType), so wiring pow() to it today wouldn't fully match PHPStan's precision either. Real Rust-rewrite equivalent is sensible (route pow() through the same BinOp::Pow inference path) but not built.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: PregFilterFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for preg_filter(): narrows the 3rd (subject) arg's type to array<int,string> when it's array, string|null when it's string, else falls back to the default stub-derived return type.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: Rust groups preg_filter with preg_replace/preg_replace_callback under one arm that only handles the string-subject case (subject arg is a String subtype -> strip_array_member(generic)). The array-subject case (narrowing specifically to ArrayType(int,string), which is what PHPStan's dedicated PregFilterFunctionReturnTypeExtension does) isn't modeled - an array subject just falls through to the generic stub type unnarrowed.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: PregMatchParameterOutTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: FunctionParameterOutTypeExtension: computes the by-ref type written into preg_match's/preg_match_all's $matches parameter after the call, via RegexArrayShapeMatcher::matchExpr/matchAllExpr (unioned with empty-array for the no-match case on preg_match).
php-dynamic-extensions.our_location: src/checker/expr.rs:270-370 (preg_match/preg_match_all by-ref $matches handling, using preg_match_matches_shape/preg_match_all_pattern_order_shape/build_matched_shape from src/checker/expr/preg_shapes.rs)
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: Phase 12 work assigns the regex-derived shape type to the $matches variable as a definitional side effect of the call, mirroring this extension's parameter-out mechanism, including the preg_match empty-array union for the no-match case.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: PregMatchTypeSpecifyingExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: FunctionTypeSpecifyingExtension: in an `if (preg_match(...))`-shaped condition, narrows both the $matches out-arg (via RegexArrayShapeMatcher, keyed off truthy/falsy context) and, separately, the $subject arg's own type (via matchSubjectExpr, e.g. to a more specific string for an anchored pattern).
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: Implements the core $matches-narrowing half for the bare/compared `if (preg_match(...))` idiom (matching TrinaryLogic-based wasMatched dispatch into the shape matcher), explicitly scoped to plain preg_match only (own comment: "not preg_match_all"). Missing: preg_match_all narrowing, the $subject-type narrowing half (RegexArrayShapeMatcher::matchSubjectExpr - narrowing the subject string itself based on the pattern), the isSubExprOfMatchesArg guard, and general TypeSpecifierContext handling beyond a bare truthy/falsy if-condition.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: PregReplaceCallbackClosureTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: FunctionParameterClosureTypeExtension: gives preg_replace_callback's $callback parameter a precise ClosureType whose single parameter is typed via RegexArrayShapeMatcher::matchExpr against the pattern argument, so code inside the callback sees an accurate $matches shape.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: Rust's preg_replace_callback handling (src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs:581) only computes the call's own return type; it never pushes a regex-derived parameter type into the callback closure for checking the closure body. Rust has no general mechanism for injecting an inferred param type into a closure passed to a builtin based on other arguments (infer_closure_return_with_param_overrides only produces a return type for the outer call, e.g. array_map, not enriched typing for the closure's own body-check).

php-dynamic-extensions.name: PregSplitDynamicReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for preg_split(): for literal pattern+subject actually runs preg_split() and builds an exact constant array type; otherwise builds a general list<string|array{string,int}>|false type accounting for PREG_SPLIT_NO_EMPTY/OFFSET_CAPTURE flags, invalid regex -> ErrorType, and non-empty-string propagation.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: Implements the general-case fallback only: list<string>|false, narrowed to list<non-empty-string>|false when PREG_SPLIT_NO_EMPTY is present (checked via a lenient bitwise-OR name scan, per its own comment deliberately matching PHPStan's fallback precision). Does not constant-fold literal pattern/subject calls, does not model PREG_SPLIT_OFFSET_CAPTURE's [string,int] tuple element, does not detect invalid patterns to return an error type, and ignores the $limit argument entirely.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: PropertyExistsTypeSpecifyingExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: FunctionTypeSpecifyingExtension: on a truthy property_exists($obj, $prop) check with a known property-name string, narrows $obj to an intersection with HasPropertyType($prop) (or a plain true-typed property_exists() call node when the property is already a known native declared property).
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: Explicitly and deliberately not implemented - src/checker/tests/narrowing.rs:192-203 documents that property_exists (along with method_exists/class_exists/etc.) was considered against the is_callable-style single-arg predicate table and rejected because it's a 2-arg call that doesn't fit that mechanism; no HasPropertyType-equivalent accessory/narrowing exists in Rust's type system for this.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: RandomIntFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for random_int()/rand()/mt_rand(): computes an IntegerRangeType result from the min/max argument types (or [0, +inf) for the zero-arg rand()/mt_rand() form), unioning bounds across union-typed args.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No special-casing for random_int/rand/mt_rand anywhere in builtin_calls.rs despite Type::IntRange (Rust's IntegerRangeType equivalent) existing and being used elsewhere (e.g. positive-int, range()). These calls fall back to the generic stub return type (plain int), losing the range precision.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: RangeFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for range(): for fully-constant start/end/step actually evaluates PHP's range() to build an exact constant-array list (falling back to an IntegerRangeType-typed non-empty list past a 50-element threshold), otherwise derives a non-empty-list<T> from the argument types' general kind (int/float/numeric-string/string/benevolent-union).
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: Implements only the exactly-2-argument case with int or single-character-string bounds, returning a generic non-empty-list<int|string> (no literal enumeration/constant-array building for small ranges, no IntegerRangeType-bounded element type, no float handling, no 3-argument $step support). Own code comment explicitly scopes this to "the two real corpus shapes" it was built to cover, not the full extension.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ReflectionClassConstructorThrowTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicStaticMethodThrowTypeExtension: suppresses ReflectionClass::__construct()'s declared throw type when the argument is statically known to be a class-string or object (only a bad string/other type can actually throw at runtime).
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: phpstan-rs has no throw-type / @throws checking subsystem at all (grep for throw_type/ThrowType/@throws across src/checker and src/*.rs returns nothing), so there is no place this extension's suppression logic could plug into. Architecturally sensible future feature, currently entirely absent rather than not_applicable.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ReflectionClassIsSubclassOfTypeSpecifyingExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: MethodTypeSpecifyingExtension: narrows a ReflectionClass<T> variable's own template type after a $reflection->isSubclassOf($someClass) check, intersecting T with the class named by the argument.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No modeling of ReflectionClass or its generic template parameter anywhere in the registry/type system (grep for ReflectionClass/ReflectionMethod/etc. across src/*.rs and src/checker/*.rs turns up nothing beyond an unrelated comment in registry.rs), so this generics-aware narrowing has no substrate to be built on yet.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ReflectionFunctionConstructorThrowTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicStaticMethodThrowTypeExtension: suppresses ReflectionFunction::__construct()'s throw type when every possible constant-string argument names a function ReflectionProvider actually knows about (or is the empty string, which always throws so returns null i.e. "no suppression" is skipped oddly - actually empty string returns null meaning never throws, matching PHP behavior where ReflectionFunction('') throws a TypeError caught... per code it returns null suppressing the throw entirely for empty string case, an edge-case detail).
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: Same absent throw-type subsystem as the other Reflection*ConstructorThrowTypeExtension files; also depends on ReflectionProvider::hasFunction()-equivalent lookups against the function-name argument, which nothing in registry.rs currently wires into a throw-type check.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ReflectionGetAttributesMethodReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicMethodReturnTypeExtension (registered once per reflection class) for ->getAttributes($className): returns list<ReflectionAttribute<T>> where T is the class-string argument's resolved object type, matching it against the declared return type's own ReflectionAttribute subclasses when the method has multiple @template-based variants.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No Reflection* class/method modeling exists in phpstan-rs at all (see notes on the sibling Reflection* files), so getAttributes()'s generic ReflectionAttribute<T> return-type narrowing has nothing to attach to; a getAttributes() call today would just get whatever generic method-call handling exists, with no class-string-argument-aware narrowing.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ReflectionMethodConstructorThrowTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicStaticMethodThrowTypeExtension: suppresses ReflectionMethod::__construct($class, $method)'s throw type when every possible class (from a constant string or a GenericClassStringType) is known to ReflectionProvider and actually has every possible $method name as a real method.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: Same absent throw-type subsystem; also needs ClassReflection::hasMethod()-style lookups PHPStan uses here, which have no throw-type consumer in Rust.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ReflectionPropertyConstructorThrowTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicStaticMethodThrowTypeExtension: suppresses ReflectionProperty::__construct($class, $property)'s throw type when every possible class name is known and has every possible property name as a real instance property.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: Same absent throw-type subsystem as the other Reflection*ConstructorThrowTypeExtension files; structurally identical logic to ReflectionMethodConstructorThrowTypeExtension but checking hasInstanceProperty() instead of hasMethod().

php-dynamic-extensions.name: RegexArrayShapeMatcher
php-dynamic-extensions.description: Shared helper (not a Rule/extension itself) used by the preg_match(_all) parameter-out/type-specifying extensions: parses a regex pattern's capturing groups (via RegexGroupParser/Hoa) and builds the precise $matches array-shape type for a given wasMatched certainty, matchesAll mode, and PREG_* flag combination, including special-cased tagged unions for a single optional top-level group or a single top-level alternation, and MARK-verb key support.
php-dynamic-extensions.our_location: src/regex_groups.rs (from-scratch PCRE group/alternation parser), src/checker/expr/preg_shapes.rs (preg_match_matches_shape, build_matched_shape, preg_match_all_pattern_order_shape, parse_preg_flags)
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: A substantial independent reimplementation of the core algorithm exists: the single-optional-top-level-group tagged union, the single-top-level-alternation tagged union (including the alternation-wrapped-in-optional-quantifier and branch-count-mismatch cases), the general fallback shape, PREG_OFFSET_CAPTURE's [text,offset] tuple, and PREG_UNMATCHED_AS_NULL/PREG_PATTERN_ORDER/PREG_SET_ORDER flag handling are all present and comment-documented as verified against live PHP/dumpType(). Missing: MARK-verb ('MARK' key) support entirely, matchSubjectExpr's subject-type derivation (used by PregMatchTypeSpecifyingExtension, itself unimplemented), and PhpVersion-gated PREG_UNMATCHED_AS_NULL support-on-72/73 nuance (Rust has no PhpVersion-conditional gate here at all).

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ReplaceFunctionsDynamicReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension covering preg_replace/preg_replace_callback/preg_replace_callback_array/str_replace/str_ireplace/substr_replace/strtr: computes the subject-shaped return type (string vs mapped array, with per-key-optional array results for the preg_* family), adds null when a preg_* function's subject isn't provably an array, and propagates non-falsy/non-empty/lowercase/uppercase accessory string types when both subject and replacement share them.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: Handles a narrow slice: for str_replace/str_ireplace, only recognizes the 3rd arg being a String subtype and returns plain Type::String (no array-subject mapping, no accessory-type propagation). For the preg_* family, only handles the string-subject case (subject arg subtype of String) via strip_array_member(generic) - array-subject mapping (with per-key optionality) isn't modeled. strtr() is not special-cased at all - falls to the generic stub. No non-falsy/non-empty/lowercase/uppercase accessory-string preservation logic exists anywhere in this arm.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: RoundFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for round()/ceil()/floor(): models PHP-version-dependent behavior - PHP 8's stricter TypeError (NeverType) when the first arg can't be an int/float/numeric-string/null/bool (broader in non-strict_types files) or is missing, versus PHP 7's null-on-missing-arg / false-on-array-arg, otherwise FloatType.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No special-casing for round/ceil/floor anywhere in builtin_calls.rs; these fall back to whatever the generic php_stubs signature declares (presumably a plain float), losing the PHP-version-gated NeverType-on-invalid-argument and PHP7 false-on-array modeling entirely.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: SetTypeFunctionTypeSpecifyingExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: FunctionTypeSpecifyingExtension for settype($var, $type) calls (context 'null', i.e. as a statement): reads the constant-string type-name argument(s), maps each ('bool'/'int'/'float'/'string'/'array'/'object'/'null') to the corresponding toBoolean()/toInteger()/.../toArray() conversion of the current value type (falling back to all 7 possibilities when the type-name arg isn't a constant string), unions them, and narrows $var to that union via TypeSpecifier with setAlwaysOverwriteTypes().
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: grep for "settype" across src/ returns nothing at all - no handling of settype() as either a call or a narrowing point. The narrowing infrastructure this would plug into exists (src/checker/narrowing.rs, TypeSpecifier-equivalent), but no settype-specific logic uses it.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: SimpleXMLElementAsXMLMethodReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicMethodReturnTypeExtension for SimpleXMLElement::asXML(): returns bool when called with a filename argument (1 arg), or string|false when called with no filename (0 args).
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No SimpleXMLElement-specific method handling anywhere in src/ (grep for SimpleXML across src/*.rs turns up only an incidental test fixture in misc_and_regressions.rs that happens to pass by coincidence of the generic (bool) cast handling, not because SimpleXMLElement methods are modeled).

php-dynamic-extensions.name: SimpleXMLElementClassPropertyReflectionExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: PropertiesClassReflectionExtension that makes every dynamic/magic property access on a SimpleXMLElement (or subclass) resolve to a BenevolentUnionType of SimpleXMLElement|null, modeling SimpleXML's magic __get for child-element access.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: phpstan-rs has no class-reflection-extension equivalent registered for SimpleXMLElement; its registry/OOP property lookup (src/registry.rs, src/checker/oop.rs) has no special-case for magic/dynamic properties on this class, so an unknown property on a SimpleXMLElement variable would fall through to the normal (likely 'undefined property') path instead of being treated as another SimpleXMLElement|null.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: SimpleXMLElementConstructorThrowTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicStaticMethodThrowTypeExtension for `new SimpleXMLElement($data)`: when the first constructor argument is one or more constant strings, actually parses each with libxml (errors suppressed via libxml_use_internal_errors) to decide whether the throw type should be suppressed (valid XML literal -> no throw) or kept (invalid XML / non-constant argument -> keeps the declared throw type).
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: phpstan-rs has no dynamic-throw-type-extension mechanism at all (per-argument-value-dependent narrowing of a constructor's throw type), and more fundamentally has no XML-parsing capability to actually validate literal XML strings the way this extension does - reimplementing this would require embedding an XML parser purely to refine an already-declared-throws annotation, which is out of scope for the coarser exception-tracking phpstan-rs otherwise does. Distinguish from the other SimpleXML files: this one specifically depends on runtime XML validation, which is not sensibly portable.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: SimpleXMLElementXpathMethodReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicMethodReturnTypeExtension for SimpleXMLElement::xpath($expr): when the xpath expression argument is a constant string, actually evaluates it against a dummy SimpleXMLElement to check it's not a namespaced/invalid expression, and if so strips `false` off the declared return type's union (since a plain non-namespaced xpath never returns false for those inputs).
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No SimpleXMLElement-specific method return-type narrowing exists in src/; same underlying gap as the other SimpleXMLElement files (no class-specific method extension mechanism for this built-in class at all).

php-dynamic-extensions.name: SprintfFunctionDynamicReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for sprintf()/vsprintf(): computes constant-string results when all arguments are constant scalars (combinatorially, up to a limit), otherwise infers accessory string flags (non-empty/non-falsy/lowercase/numeric) from the format string's constant parts and single-placeholder special-casing (e.g. `sprintf('%s', $x)` returns $x's own string type).
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: phpstan-rs has `check_format_string_call` (src/checker/calls.rs, invoked from src/checker/expr.rs:250-252) for sprintf/printf, but that is the diagnostic-emitting placeholder/argument-count validation (PHPStan's separate PrintfParametersRule concern), not this file's return-type inference. There is no code anywhere that narrows sprintf/vsprintf's *return type* beyond whatever the generic builtin signature stub declares (plain string) - no constant-folding, no accessory-type propagation from the format string or argument types.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: SscanfFunctionDynamicReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for sscanf()/fscanf() with 2 args (no output-variable refs): parses the format string's %-specifiers via regex and builds a constant-shaped nullable array type (string/int/float per specifier, each nullable) representing the by-value 2-arg return form.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: grep for "sscanf"/"fscanf" across src/ (excluding tests) returns nothing; no format-specifier-driven array-shape inference for these functions exists.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: StatDynamicReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: Both a DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension (for stat/lstat/fstat/ssh2_sftp_stat) and DynamicMethodReturnTypeExtension (for SplFileObject::fstat), returning a fixed constant-array shape (both numeric 0-12 keys and named keys dev/ino/mode/.../blocks, all int-valued) unioned with `false` for the function form.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: grep for "stat"/"lstat"/"fstat"/"ssh2_sftp_stat" across src/ (excluding tests) returns nothing; these functions get whatever plain generic return type the builtin stub declares, not the detailed dual-keyed constant-array shape.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: StrCaseFunctionsReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension covering strtoupper/strtolower/mb_strtoupper/mb_strtolower/lcfirst/ucfirst/mb_lcfirst/mb_ucfirst/ucwords/mb_convert_case/mb_convert_kana: computes exact constant-string results for constant string inputs (respecting the case-mode argument for mb_convert_case/ucwords/mb_convert_kana), else attaches lowercase/uppercase/numeric/non-falsy/non-empty accessory types to the general string return based on what's provable about the input.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: grep for these function names (strtoupper, strtolower, mb_strtoupper, ucfirst, lcfirst, ucwords, mb_convert_case) across src/ (excluding tests) returns nothing; also, phpstan-rs's Type enum has no Lowercase/Uppercase accessory-string kinds at all (only NonEmptyString/NonFalsyString/LiteralString/NumericString exist in src/types.rs), so even a partial port of the accessory-flag logic would need new Type variants first.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: StrContainingTypeSpecifyingExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: FunctionTypeSpecifyingExtension for the truthy branch of fnmatch/str_contains/str_starts_with/str_ends_with/strpos/strrpos/stripos/strripos/strstr/mb_strpos/mb_strrpos/mb_stripos/mb_strripos/mb_strstr: when the needle is a known non-empty constant string, narrows the haystack to a non-empty/non-falsy-string intersection type in that branch (plus, for the boolean-returning trio, additionally proves the call expression's own value truthy).
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: grep for str_contains/str_starts_with/strpos/strstr across src/checker/narrowing.rs and other checker files (excluding tests) returns nothing - no condition-narrowing logic keys off these functions to refine the haystack variable's type in the truthy branch of an if/while.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: StrIncrementDecrementFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for PHP 8.3's str_increment()/str_decrement(): for constant scalar inputs, actually runs the real str_increment/str_decrement (swallowing ValueError for empty-string or out-of-range inputs) to compute exact constant-string results, unioning them (or NeverType if every candidate throws).
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: grep for str_increment/str_decrement across src/ returns nothing at all - not even a plain builtin signature entry, so these PHP 8.3 functions likely aren't recognized as callable builtins at all in phpstan-rs, let alone given return-type narrowing.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: StrPadFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for str_pad(): attaches non-empty/non-falsy accessory string types (from the input string's own accessories or a length argument known to be >=1), plus literal/lowercase/uppercase accessories when both the input and pad-string arguments carry them.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: grep for "str_pad" across src/ (excluding tests) returns nothing; str_pad gets whatever the plain builtin stub declares (bare string), with none of the accessory-type propagation.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: StrRepeatFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for str_repeat(): returns '' for a multiplier of exactly 0, NeverType for a provably-negative multiplier, exact constant-string unions when both input and (constant-int) multiplier are known and the result stays small (<100 chars), and otherwise propagates non-empty/non-falsy/literal/numeric/lowercase/uppercase accessory types from the input string.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: grep for "str_repeat" across src/ (excluding tests) returns nothing; no special-case handling exists, so it falls back to the generic builtin stub's plain string return with no constant-folding or accessory propagation.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: StrSplitFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for str_split()/mb_str_split(): computes exact constant list-array results for constant-string inputs with a resolvable split length/encoding (PHP-version-aware for empty-string edge cases), otherwise builds a non-empty-string-valued list array type, unioned with false when the length argument can't be proven positive on PHP versions that return false rather than throw.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: grep for "str_split"/"mb_str_split" across src/ (excluding tests) returns nothing; no per-function return-type logic, list-ness/non-emptiness of the array is not modeled for this function specifically (phpstan-rs does model array list-ness generally elsewhere, e.g. array_column/array_values, but that machinery isn't wired to str_split).

php-dynamic-extensions.name: StrTokFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for the 2-argument form of strtok($str, $delimiters): returns constant `false` when the delimiter argument is provably the empty string, or a non-empty-string intersection type when it's provably non-empty, else null (no narrowing) when it's unknown.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: grep for "strtok" across src/ (excluding tests) returns nothing; falls back to the plain builtin stub return type with no delimiter-dependent narrowing.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: StrWordCountFunctionDynamicReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for str_word_count(): returns int for the 1-arg call, and for the 2/3-arg call branches on the constant-int format argument (0 -> int, 1/2 -> array<int,string>, other -> false), or a broad int|array<int,string>|false union when the format argument isn't a known constant.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: grep for "str_word_count" across src/ (excluding tests) returns nothing; the format-argument-dependent return-type branching (int vs array vs false) is entirely absent, so callers get only whatever the generic builtin stub declares regardless of the format argument passed.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: StrlenFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for strlen(): computes an exact IntegerRangeType/union-of-constants from constant scalar inputs' actual lengths, or int<0,1> for a boolean input, int<1,max> for a provably non-empty/numeric string, or the exact constant 0 for a provably-empty string.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: src/main.rs only looks up strlen's plain builtin FunctionSig for a debug-print CLI path; no dynamic narrowing of strlen's return type by argument content exists anywhere in the checker. phpstan-rs's Type system has no IntegerRangeType-equivalent variant at all (only Type::Accessory kinds for strings), so representing the int<0,1>/int<1,max> shapes this extension produces isn't even structurally possible without first adding an integer-range type.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: StrlenFunctionTypeSpecifyingExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: FunctionTypeSpecifyingExtension for strlen()/mb_strlen() used in a boolean condition on a known-string argument: narrows the argument to non-empty-string in the branch where the call result is truthy (and the inverse falsey/empty branch), independent of any specific comparison against 0.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: grep for strlen/mb_strlen in src/checker/narrowing.rs (and elsewhere, excluding tests) returns nothing; no condition-based narrowing ties a `strlen($x)`/`mb_strlen($x)` truthiness check back to $x's own non-emptiness.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: StrrevFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for strrev(): reverses constant-string arguments into literal ConstantStringType unions, and otherwise preserves lowercase/uppercase/non-empty/non-falsy accessory intersection types from the input onto the result.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: grep for 'strrev' in src/ finds nothing outside vendor. strrev() resolves only through the generic phpstorm-stubs-generated signature (plain string return), with no per-call narrowing of literal strings or accessory-type (lowercase/uppercase/non-empty) preservation. No LowercaseString/UppercaseString accessory kinds even exist in src/types.rs's AccessoryKind (only NonEmptyString, NonFalsyString, NumericString), so full parity would also need extending the type system.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: StrtotimeFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for strtotime(): evaluates constant-string time expressions at analysis time, returning ConstantBooleanType(false) on parse failure, IntegerRangeType::createAllGreaterThan(0) when all literal results are positive timestamps, or plain int/benevolent-union otherwise (mixed input widens to benevolent union of the default variant type).
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No 'strtotime' special-casing anywhere in src/. Falls back to the generic phpstorm-stubs signature (int|false), with none of the literal-evaluation, positive-timestamp IntegerRangeType narrowing, or mixed-argument benevolent-union widening PHPStan performs.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: StrvalFamilyFunctionReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension covering strval/intval/boolval/floatval/doubleval: delegates to the argument type's own toString()/toInteger()/toBoolean()/toFloat() polymorphic cast methods (falling back to a bare IntegerType/FloatType if the cast produces an ErrorType), and returns NullType for the zero-argument call.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: No 'strval'/'intval'/'boolval'/'floatval'/'doubleval' special-casing in src/checker/, and no toInteger()/toFloat()/toBoolean()/toString() cast-dispatch methods exist on the Type enum in src/types.rs at all - these calls resolve only through the generic phpstorm-stubs signatures (e.g. strval(mixed): string), so a call like intval('5') does not narrow to int(5) the way real PHPStan does.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: SubstrDynamicReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for substr()/mb_substr(): evaluates constant-string+constant-offset+constant-length combinations exactly (including PHP-version-aware false-vs-empty-string legacy substr() behavior), and otherwise derives lowercase/uppercase/non-empty/non-falsy accessory types on the result from the input string and offset/length sign analysis.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: grep for '"substr"'/'"mb_substr"' in src/ finds nothing outside vendor; these resolve only through the generic phpstorm-stubs stub signature. None of the literal-string evaluation, offset/length-sign accessory narrowing, or PhpVersion-gated false-vs-empty-string simulation is implemented; LowercaseString/UppercaseString accessory kinds also don't exist in src/types.rs.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: ThrowableReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicMethodReturnTypeExtension for Throwable::getCode(): returns BenevolentUnionType(int|string) for PDOException, Throwable/Exception/RuntimeException base classes (and any @method getCode() PHPDoc tag override), else falls back to plain int for other Throwable subclasses.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: Throwable is referenced in src/checker/stmt.rs only for catch/throw validity checks (is_subclass_of 'Throwable'); grep for 'getCode'/'getcode' in src/checker turns up nothing - method-call return-type inference has no per-method extension mechanism for Throwable::getCode(), so it would fall back to whatever generic ClassInfo method-return type (or Mixed) exists for the resolved class, without the PDOException/int|string special-casing.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: TriggerErrorDynamicReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for trigger_error(): 1-arg call always returns true; 2-arg call narrows on the literal error-level constant, returning NeverType for E_USER_ERROR (or any non-recognized level on PHP versions that throw ValueError for it), false for a non-recognized level on older PHP, and true for E_USER_WARNING/NOTICE/DEPRECATED.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: grep for 'trigger_error' in src/ finds nothing outside vendor. No special-casing exists; falls back to the generic phpstorm-stubs stub (bool return), missing the NeverType-for-E_USER_ERROR unreachability signal entirely, which affects dead-code/control-flow reasoning downstream.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: TrimFunctionDynamicReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for trim/rtrim/chop: evaluates constant-string+constant-charlist combinations exactly into literal ConstantStringType results, preserves lowercase/uppercase accessory types when not evaluable, and detects a numeric-string-preserving case when the charlist has no digits.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: grep for '"trim"'/'"rtrim"'/'"chop"' in src/checker finds nothing; these resolve only through the generic phpstorm-stubs signature (string return), with none of the literal evaluation, accessory-type propagation, or numeric-string-preservation logic implemented.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: VersionCompareFunctionDynamicReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension for version_compare(): with no operator arg, evaluates constant version strings (including a PHP_VERSION const-fetch special case resolved via the configured PHP version range) into a union of ConstantIntegerType(-1|0|1); with an operator arg, evaluates into ConstantBooleanType results (or a benevolent bool|null / plain bool default when the operator is non-constant or invalid, version-gated on whether the runtime throws ValueError for bad operators).
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: Only the 2-argument, no-operator form is special-cased, and only to a generic Type::Int - not the real union of ConstantIntegerType(-1)|(0)|(1), and with no constant-string evaluation of the actual version_compare() result at all (git log shows this was added specifically in round 19 of the Piwigo cleanup, commit 65c8483). The 3-argument operator form, literal-value evaluation via constant strings, PHP_VERSION const-fetch handling, and the invalid-operator-to-null/bool degradation are all unimplemented; 3-arg calls fall through to the generic phpstorm-stubs int|bool stub.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: VersionCompareFunctionDynamicThrowTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: DynamicFunctionThrowTypeExtension for version_compare(): on PHP versions that throw ValueError for internal-function argument errors, reports the function's declared throw type when a 3rd operator argument is present and is (or might be, if not a constant string) not one of the valid operator strings.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: grep across src/ for 'ValueError'/'throw_type'/'ThrowType'/'DynamicFunctionThrowType' finds no such infrastructure anywhere in phpstan-rs - there is no throw-type/exception-type modeling concept in the checker at all (calls.rs's one ValueError comment is just a doc note about real PHP behavior, not modeled logic). Marked not_applicable rather than missing because this isn't a gap in a single extension but a whole absent subsystem (DynamicFunctionThrowTypeExtension and its call sites in exception-flow analysis) that would need its own architectural decision before this specific extension could be ported; still worth flagging in the roadmap as a candidate feature area, not a one-off fix.

php-dynamic-extensions.name: XMLReaderOpenReturnTypeExtension
php-dynamic-extensions.description: Dynamic method/static-method return-type extension for XMLReader::open(): the instance-method form always returns bool, while the static-method form (XMLReader::open(...) as a factory) returns XMLReader|false.
php-dynamic-extensions.notes: grep for 'XMLReader'/'XmlReader' in src/ finds nothing outside vendor. No special-casing exists for this static-vs-instance return-type divergence; a call would fall back to whatever generic phpstorm-stubs signature is generated for XMLReader::open(), without PHPStan's split between the deprecated static factory (nullable-object-or-false) and instance method (plain bool).

clusters.root_cause: phpstan-rs's DocBlock parser (src/docblock.rs) has no @throws tag at all (confirmed by reading its full tag list: params/return/var/template/extends/implements/properties - nothing exception-related), no reflection field anywhere stores a declared or inferred throw-type for a function/method, and the checker never collects 'ThrowPoints' (the set of exception types a statement/expression can actually throw) while walking a function/method body. Every rule in PHPStan's Rules/Exceptions/*ThrowsRule family, plus CatchWithUnthrownExceptionRule and MethodThrowTypeCovarianceRule, is built on exactly these two missing primitives (declared @throws type + collected ThrowPoints), so they all share one underlying gap even though they live in different files.
clusters.rust_location: src/docblock.rs (add an @throws field to DocBlock::parse), src/registry/function_sig.rs + class_info.rs (add a throw_type field to function/method reflection), and a new ThrowPoint-collection pass in src/checker/stmt.rs/expr.rs (walk statements/expressions the way return-statement collection already does, recording every throw site's resolved type)
clusters.notes: This is a coherent 11-item subsystem in PHPStan itself (a shared @throws/ThrowPoint engine feeding ~9 dispatcher rules plus a config-driven checked/unchecked classifier). Real-world value is genuinely mixed: the 'dead catch' half of CatchWithUnthrownExceptionRule (catching an exception type nothing in the try block can throw, or that an earlier catch already exhausts) is a common, high-signal real bug and is probably worth carving out first even though it shares the ThrowPoint-collection primitive with the rest. The checked-exceptions convention (@throws-must-match-body, @throws-must-not-be-too-wide) is an opt-in PHPStan feature many real codebases never enable, so the remaining 10 items are lower marginal value per item despite the large item count. Recommend splitting into a 'ThrowPoint collection' sub-milestone (unlocks the dead-catch half of CatchWithUnthrownExceptionRule immediately) before building out full @throws PHPDoc parsing for the rest.

clusters.root_cause: src/checker/stmt.rs's StmtKind::Try handling (line 472) merges try/catch/finally control flow for local-variable narrowing purposes, but never collects or compares the set of 'exit points' (return/throw/continue/break) reachable from the try/catch body against the set reachable from the finally body - so it has no way to detect that a finally-block exit point silently overwrites/discards a try-or-catch exit point (a well-known PHP footgun: `finally { return $x; }` after `try { return $y; }` silently drops $y).
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/stmt.rs StmtKind::Try (~line 472) - needs a new exit-point-collection helper (walk try/catch body vs. finally body for terminal return/throw/continue/break nodes) alongside the existing narrowing merge
clusters.notes: Self-contained: builds on the Try/finally CFG structure phpstan-rs already has (see bright spots) rather than requiring new type-system machinery. Genuinely useful bug class (silent value loss) but relatively rare in practice compared to e.g. null-safety or undefined-variable bugs.

clusters.root_cause: src/checker/resolve.rs:39 (`resolve_name_expr`) unconditionally returns `Type::Object(name, ..)` for any class name regardless of whether the registry actually has that class - confirmed directly by reading the function, which has no registry-lookup/failure branch at all. There is no class.notFound/function.notFound/constant.notFound diagnostic anywhere in the checker, and no equivalent of PHPStan's shared ClassNameCheck (case-sensitivity + deprecated-class-usage checking). This single missing 'does this name actually resolve' layer is the root cause behind both the catch-clause gap and the use-import gap - they are literally the same missing primitive applied at two different syntactic sites.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/resolve.rs (resolve_name_expr and friends need a registry-lookup existence check), plus call sites in src/checker/stmt.rs (catch-type loop, ~496-520) and a new pass over `use`/`use function`/`use const`/group-use statements (src/parser/stmt.rs parses them, src/project.rs/registry.rs currently only consume them to build the alias map)
clusters.notes: Both ExistingNamesInGroupUseRule and ExistingNamesInUseRule are registered at PHPStan level 0 (core baseline, not opt-in), and 'class/function not found' is arguably one of the single most valuable diagnostic classes in all of static PHP analysis - far more common in real code (typo'd use-imports, renamed classes, wrong namespace) than most of what's in this audit category.
