Scored L rather than XL because the Throwable-subtype check in CaughtExceptionExistenceRule already proves the surrounding scaffolding (catch-type loop) exists; the missing piece is purely the existence-check primitive itself, but it needs to be threaded through resolve_name_expr carefully since many other checker paths call it and currently rely on its 'always succeeds' behavior.

clusters.cluster_name: Duplicate name/alias collision within a namespace block
clusters.root_cause: No pass anywhere in the checker looks for case-insensitive collisions between a file's own class/interface/trait/enum declarations and its `use`-alias imports within the same namespace block; `use` handling (src/parser/stmt.rs + registry.rs add_uses) only ever builds a forward alias->FQN map, never checks the map (or the file's own declarations) for duplicates.
clusters.rust_location: A new per-namespace-block validation pass, likely in src/project.rs or a new src/checker/names.rs, run once per file after parsing (independent of the alias-map-building code path, which stays as-is)
clusters.notes: Standalone and fairly cheap - no type-system dependency, just a same-file name-collision scan. Low real-world value: PHP itself fatal-errors on true duplicate class declarations in one file, so the surviving surface (alias collisions specifically) is a narrower, less common mistake.

clusters.root_cause: No stage of phpstan-rs parses or stores an @internal PHPDoc tag on any reflection kind (class, function, method, property, class constant) - confirmed by the same DocBlock field audit as the @throws cluster - and there is no 'restricted usage' dispatch mechanism (a check, run at every method-call/static-call/property-fetch/constant-fetch/function-call/first-class-callable/`(string)`-cast-invoking-__toString site, that compares the accessed symbol's declaring namespace against the call site's namespace). PHPStan implements this as one small extension-point family (RestrictedUsage/*) driven by one tag-detection helper (InternalTag/RestrictedInternalUsageHelper); all 16 items here are that same single mechanism applied to six different node kinds (class name, function, method, static method, property, static property, class constant, plus the first-class-callable and __toString-cast variants of several of those).
clusters.rust_location: src/docblock.rs (add an @internal flag to DocBlock), src/registry/class_info.rs + function_sig.rs (store is_internal + owning root-namespace on ClassInfo/FunctionInfo/MethodInfo/PropertyInfo/ConstInfo), and a new src/checker/internal_usage.rs dispatched from every access site in src/checker/calls.rs and src/checker/oop.rs (method/static calls, property/static-property fetches, class-constant fetches, function calls, and the `(string)`-cast-triggers-__toString special case)
clusters.notes: Large item count (16 of the category's 75) but genuinely one root cause - a tag plus a namespace-comparison dispatched at ~8 call-site shapes, no new type-system concepts needed. Value is medium rather than high: @internal-enforcement matters most for library/framework authors protecting their own internal API surface from downstream consumers; for an application codebase being analyzed (the kind of corpus phpstan-rs has been validating against, e.g. Piwigo) @internal usage across namespace boundaries is comparatively rare. Two of these rules (RestrictedClassConstantUsageRule at level 0, RestrictedMethodUsageRule/RestrictedPropertyUsageRule at level 2) are default-registered, so this isn't purely opt-in, but the underlying bug class is much less common than e.g. the symbol-existence or type-mismatch categories.

clusters.root_cause: The Throwable-subtype check that PHPStan's ThrowExprTypeRule performs is implemented in phpstan-rs, but only on the statement form of throw (StmtKind::Throw, src/checker/stmt.rs:560-578); the expression form (ExprKind::Throw, used in constructs like `$x ?? throw new Foo()`) is handled separately in src/checker/expr.rs:652-655 and simply evaluates the inner expression, returning Type::Never without ever calling the same check - a plain code-path omission (the check exists, it just isn't reached from the second of the two AST node kinds that both represent 'throw').
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/expr.rs:652-655 (ExprKind::Throw) - call the same Throwable-subtype-check helper already used by src/checker/stmt.rs:560-578 (StmtKind::Throw) instead of duplicating logic
clusters.notes: This is the single cheapest, highest-confidence fix in the whole category - existing logic just needs to be shared across two AST node kinds. Throw-as-expression (`??`, arrow functions, match arms) is common enough in modern PHP that the current gap is a real, reachable false-negative, not a corner case.

bright_spots: The Throwable-subtype check for `throw` statements (src/checker/stmt.rs:560-578, Finding 57) and for catch-clause types (src/checker/stmt.rs:496-520) both correctly call registry.is_subclass_of(class, "Throwable") - a real, working piece of exception-safety analysis that most of this audit category assumed didn't exist at all.

Try/catch/finally control-flow merging (StmtKind::Try, src/checker/stmt.rs:472) already does real CFG work - merging narrowed-variable state across try/catch/finally branches - which is exactly the scaffolding OverwrittenExitPointByFinallyRule's exit-point collection would build on top of, making that cluster cheaper than it would be from a cold start.

The investigation itself is unusually rigorous: nearly every 'missing'/'not_applicable' verdict cites a specific grep run (e.g. 'grepped for throws/ThrowPoint/TooWide - nothing beyond unrelated comments', 'grep across src/checker and src/*.rs') rather than asserting absence from memory, and distinguishes level-0/level-2-registered rules from issue-bot-only Playground rules by reading conf/*.neon directly - this is load-bearing, well-sourced audit data, not guesswork. Verified independently in this session: src/checker/resolve.rs:39 does indeed unconditionally return Type::Object with no existence check, and src/docblock.rs's DocBlock struct genuinely has no @throws/@internal fields, exactly as the raw notes claimed.
clusters_by_category.not_applicable_summary: 45 of the 75 items are not_applicable, falling into five clean families with no invented/placeholder-looking entries: (1) the 11-item Api/* BC-promise rule family (ApiClassConstFetchRule, ApiMethodCallRule, etc.) plus its ApiRuleHelper, GetTemplateTypeRule, and three PHP-parser-v4/reflection-migration rules - all gate on referencing PHPStan's own `PHPStan\` PHP namespace, which has no meaning for a Rust rewrite with no such namespace; (2) the 11-item Playground/* family (ArrayDimCastRule, FunctionNeverRule, NoPhpCodeRule, PromoteParameterRule, etc.) - verified via conf/*.neon greps to be registered only in phpstan.org's separate issue-bot/playground service, never the CLI analyzer; (3) two PHP-8.0-version-gate rules (NoncapturingCatchRule, ThrowExpressionRule) - not applicable because phpstan-rs has no configurable target-PHP-version concept at all; (4) three PHP-8.4-property-hook counterparts (MissingCheckedExceptionInPropertyHookThrowsRule, ThrowsVoidPropertyHookWithExplicitThrowPointRule, TooWidePropertyHookThrowTypeRule) - property hooks aren't modeled anywhere in phpstan-rs's AST/parser; (5) 8 pure marker/DTO/decorator classes (RestrictedUsage, five RestrictedUsage*Extension interfaces, three RewrittenDeclaringClass* reflection decorators) that carry zero logic of their own - their concrete behavior is tracked as 'missing' on the dispatcher rules that consume them, not double-counted here. No placeholder or suspiciously generic entries were found; every item carried a specific, checkable claim.

All 31 items are genuinely applicable audit findings (29 "missing", 2 "partial") — no placeholder or invented entries. Notes are specific throughout (concrete file/line/function references), and the two "partial" items point at one real, working-but-narrow implementation (check_shape_key_access) rather than a vague hedge, so nothing here needs to be discounted or excluded as N/A.
bright_spots: infer_array_literal_type (src/checker/expr.rs ~1845) already correctly implements PHP's 'a later duplicate key overwrites an earlier one' runtime semantics during type inference — the key-collision-detection loop DuplicateKeysInLiteralArraysRule needs already exists structurally, it just never emits a diagnostic when it fires. Likely the cheapest 'missing' item in this entire category (probably S effort, no new subsystem).

check_shape_key_access (src/checker/assignment.rs, invoked from expr.rs's Index arm) is a real, working existence check for ArrayShape-typed containers accessed with literal keys — genuine narrow parity with NonexistentOffsetInArrayDimFetchCheck/Rule, not a stub. It just needs generalizing to plain Type::Array and given reportMaybes-style configurability.

The PHP 8.5 |> pipe operator already has full operator-level parity: it is lexed as a distinct token (Token::PipeGt, kept apart from bitwise-or's Token::Pipe), parsed into its own BinOp::Pipe, and evaluated separately — real, correct work on a feature that only just shipped upstream. Only the by-ref-first-parameter diagnostic layered on top is missing.

check_assignment_target/bind_assignment_target (src/checker/assignment.rs) already recurses correctly through nested list()/[...] destructuring targets, including binding element types via ArrayShape field lookup for nested targets — substantial, real structural infrastructure that both InvalidAssignVarRule and ArrayDestructuringRule's missing validation logic can be layered directly onto rather than built from scratch.

infer_spread_array_literal_type (src/checker/expr.rs ~1881) already merges spread sources' key and value types for inference purposes, which happens to compute most of the raw material ArrayUnpackingRule's string-key check and UnpackIterableInArrayRule's iterability check would need — the gating logic is what's missing, not the underlying type extraction.

clusters.root_cause: There is no 'legal array key type' concept anywhere in phpstan-rs (no int|string|bool|float|null coercion/validation primitive equivalent to AllowedArrayKeysTypes::getType()); array-literal and array-dim-fetch key expressions are accepted regardless of their inferred type.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/expr.rs infer_array_literal_type (array-item keys) and the Index arm (~802, array-dim-fetch keys); would need a new helper analogous to AllowedArrayKeysTypes, likely in src/types.rs
clusters.notes: AllowedArrayKeysTypes itself isn't a Rule (no diagnostic of its own) but is the shared primitive both real rules key off; building it once unlocks both. Real-world value is moderate — object/resource-as-array-key mistakes happen but are less common than offset-existence or cast bugs.

clusters.root_cause: The only offset-existence check in phpstan-rs (check_shape_key_access) is narrowly scoped to Type::ArrayShape with a literal key; there is no general Type::Array offset-existence check, no reportMaybes/possibly-nonexistent configurability, no array_key_first/array_key_last/array_rand/count()-1 safe-idiom exemptions, and no 'is base even offset-accessible' precheck.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/assignment.rs check_shape_key_access; src/checker/expr.rs Index arm (~802)
clusters.notes: ArrayDestructuringRule's recursive nested-list() existence check is the same underlying gap as the Check helper; it additionally needs a small separate 'is RHS array-like at all' guard (a non-array RHS to list()/[...] destructuring is currently never flagged). This is one of the highest-value gaps in the category — nonexistent-offset access is an extremely common real PHP bug.

clusters.root_cause: write_index_into() in src/checker/assignment.rs always either succeeds or silently no-ops (returns None meaning 'don't guess'); there is no notion of a container type structurally rejecting a given offset key type (e.g. writing a string key into what's known to be a list), so no setOffsetValueType()-style validity check exists for either assignment form.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/assignment.rs write_index_into (used by bind_assignment_target)
clusters.notes: Both rules are literally the same setOffsetValueType()-based check applied to '=' vs 'op='; building the underlying container/dim-type compatibility function once covers both call sites.

clusters.root_cause: phpstan-rs has no modeling of ArrayAccess-implementing objects for `$obj[$k] = $v` — only plain array/ArrayShape containers are tracked for offset writes, and even those never validate the assigned value's type against a declared value type (i.e. no offsetSet() interface-method-signature lookup).
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/assignment.rs (offset-write path has no object/interface-method branch at all)
clusters.notes: Distinct from the plain-array offset-write cluster because it requires resolving a class's ArrayAccess::offsetSet() declared parameter type through the class/interface model, not just container-type reasoning. Real-world ArrayAccess usage (and PHPStan diagnostics on it) is comparatively rare.

clusters.cluster_name: Dimless array read outside assignment target
clusters.root_cause: The Index arm's dim is Option<Expr>, but a None dim in a *read* position (bare `$x[]` used somewhere other than an assignment/foreach-value target) is never special-cased — no diagnostic path exists for it at all.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/expr.rs Index arm
clusters.notes: Small, self-contained: just needs to check 'is this Index-with-no-dim currently in a write/foreach-target position?' and emit if not. Genuinely standalone, no shared infrastructure needed.

clusters.cluster_name: Iterable/array-type gating on foreach and spread
clusters.root_cause: Both the foreach subject (IterableInForeachRule) and array-spread sources (UnpackIterableInArrayRule) already have their *element types* extracted for inference purposes, but neither call site ever checks whether the base type actually qualifies as iterable/array-like before doing so — non-iterable subjects just silently degrade to Mixed/unwrap_or(Mixed) instead of producing a diagnostic.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/stmt.rs Foreach arm and src/checker/control_flow.rs CFG counterpart; src/checker/expr.rs infer_spread_array_literal_type (~1881)
clusters.notes: IterableInForeachRule in particular is high-value — foreach over a possibly-null/possibly-scalar value is an extremely common real-code mistake PHPStan catches today. The type-level 'is this iterable' predicate needed is a straightforward match over Type variants, reusable at both call sites.

clusters.root_cause: No 'this expression is provably always empty' fact exists anywhere in the type/control-flow model; DeadForeachRule needs an isIterableAtLeastOnce()-style determination (e.g. an empty array literal, or a call known to return an always-empty array) that phpstan-rs has no equivalent of.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/stmt.rs Foreach arm (would need a new definite-emptiness query, likely on Type or via literal-array-shape inspection)
clusters.notes: Standalone — distinct from the iterability-gating cluster above (that's about 'is this iterable at all', this is about 'is this iterable but guaranteed to yield zero elements'). Foreach over a literal empty array is an uncommon real-code pattern, so value is modest despite being conceptually simple for the empty-array-literal case.

clusters.root_cause: infer_array_literal_type already detects and applies duplicate-key overwrite semantics for inference correctness, but discards the fact that a duplication occurred instead of surfacing it as a diagnostic.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/expr.rs infer_array_literal_type (~1845)
clusters.notes: Cheapest item in the category — the detection loop already exists, this is purely 'also emit a diagnostic listing the duplicate positions' rather than new analysis. Duplicate literal array keys are a real, if not hugely common, copy-paste bug.

clusters.root_cause: phpstan-rs has no concept anywhere of a configured/target PHP version, so no version-gated deprecation or removed-feature diagnostic can ever fire — this is a named recurring gap across the Cast and Operators rule families, not specific to one rule.
clusters.rust_location: No existing location — greenfield: would need a new config/version module plus threading a PhpVersion value through Checker construction and every call site below
clusters.notes: This is foundational infra: on its own it fully unlocks UnsetCastRule (pure version-gate, (unset) cast removed in 8.0) and ArrayUnpackingRule (string-key spread pre-8.1 — the key-type extraction this needs is already computed by infer_spread_array_literal_type as a bright spot). It also PARTIALLY unlocks DeprecatedCastRule, VoidCastRule, and BacktickRule below, each of which needs this subsystem PLUS its own separate AST/context fix — those are listed as their own clusters with this one as a prerequisite. Individually each version-gated rule is low-frequency (most target PHP 8.0-8.4 code, not the 8.5 deprecations), but the subsystem unlocks a whole recurring category so is rated medium overall.

clusters.cluster_name: Cast alias spelling erased at parse time
clusters.root_cause: try_parse_cast immediately normalizes every non-canonical cast spelling — (integer)->int, (double)/(real)->float, (binary)->string, (boolean)->bool — into one canonical string during parsing, discarding which spelling was actually written; the AST cannot represent the distinction DeprecatedCastRule depends on.
clusters.rust_location: src/parser/expr.rs try_parse_cast (~395-429); the Cast AST node itself would need a 'raw spelling' field
clusters.notes: Needs the PhpVersion subsystem as a prerequisite (the rule only fires on PHP 8.5+) plus its own AST change to preserve spelling. Low value: aliased cast spellings like (integer)/(boolean) are already rare in modern PHP, and this only matters once a codebase targets 8.5+.

clusters.root_cause: Type has no toInteger()/toBoolean()/toFloat()/toString() coercion-validity concept at all; the Cast arm unconditionally maps a cast keyword to its target Type variant regardless of source type, and echo/print/string-interpolation never check whether their operand's type can legally coerce to string (including no tracking of which objects implement __toString).
clusters.rust_location: src/types.rs (Type would need coercion-validity methods); src/checker/expr.rs Cast arm (check_expr ~636, infer_expr ~1581) and Interpolated arm (~1173); src/checker/stmt.rs Echo arm (~130); src/checker/calls.rs print handling (~453)
clusters.notes: Single shared root cause across four rules touching four call sites — building one castability primitive on Type (plus __toString tracking on class metadata) unlocks all four at once. High real-world value: 'array to string conversion' / uncastable-object errors are among the most commonly hit PHPStan diagnostics in real codebases (echo/print/string interpolation of arrays and bare objects is a very frequent mistake).

clusters.root_cause: Beyond needing PhpVersion for its 8.5-gated half, VoidCastRule also needs a 'is this (void) cast used as a first-level statement vs. nested inside a larger expression' determination that nothing in Scope/Checker currently tracks.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/expr.rs Cast arm (~636-648, 'void' currently falls into the default Type::Mixed arm); would need new statement-vs-expression-position context on Scope
clusters.notes: Two independent gaps bundled in one rule: the version-agnostic 'cast.void used mid-expression' half needs new context-tracking infrastructure (this cluster), the version-gated half needs the PhpVersion subsystem. (void) cast is extremely rare in real code.

clusters.cluster_name: Backtick operator desugared at parse time
clusters.root_cause: The parser immediately desugars ShellExec (backtick) expressions into an equivalent shell_exec() call during parsing itself, erasing the backtick-vs-function-call distinction before the checker ever sees the AST — so even a version-agnostic 'backtick used' diagnostic isn't representable, on top of needing PhpVersion for the actual 8.5-deprecation gate.
clusters.rust_location: src/parser/postfix.rs Token::ShellExec handling (~584-596)
clusters.notes: phpstan-rs also has no autofix/Fixable mechanism at all (BacktickRule's upstream diagnostic includes an auto-rewrite to shell_exec()) — that's a separate, broader gap not worth its own cluster for a single item, but means even a full fix here would only get the diagnostic, not the suggested fix. Backticks are rare/discouraged in modern PHP, so value is low regardless.

clusters.root_cause: check_assignment_target recurses through valid destructuring/property/index targets and binds their types, but never rejects a genuinely non-assignable LHS (e.g. assigning to a function-call result or literal), and never checks for nullsafe (?->) operators appearing in an assignment target or an AssignRef's RHS.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/assignment.rs check_assignment_target (~22-86)
clusters.notes: The recursive destructuring/binding infrastructure this would build on already exists (bright spot) — this is mostly 'add a fallback else-branch that flags anything not Variable/PropertyFetch/ArrayDimFetch/StaticPropertyFetch' plus a nullsafe-in-target scan. Conceptually related to InvalidIncDecOperationRule's lvalue-check gap below (both ask 'is this expression kind a legal write target'), though the two aren't identical checks.

clusters.cluster_name: No invalid-operand-combination error type for binary/comparison/unary operators
clusters.root_cause: infer_binary and the unary-operator arms always compute a best-effort, permissive result type for every operand-type combination (falling back to Mixed, Union([Int,Float]), or plain Bool) and never treat any pairing as an outright type error — there is no ErrorType-equivalent concept in Type, and no synthesize-and-reevaluate mechanism analogous to PHPStan's TypeExpr substitution that could surface one.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/expr.rs infer_binary (BinOp::Add ~2377, Sub/Mul/Pow ~2399, Concat ~2349, comparison ops Eq/Identical/NotEq/Lt/Gt/LtEq/GtEq ~2362-2372) and the Unary arm (Not/Neg/Plus/BitwiseNot ~619-634, with BitwiseNot falling into an untyped generic passthrough)
clusters.notes: Single shared root cause across three operator-family rules (binary, comparison, unary) — the fix is one new Type-level ErrorType/invalidity concept plus an operand-validity matrix consulted from three match sites. High value: array+object, string-array comparisons, and ~ on an array/object are common real fatal-adjacent PHP bugs PHPStan is specifically good at catching today.

clusters.cluster_name: Inc/dec operand legality and type-support checking
clusters.root_cause: The PreInc/PostInc/PreDec/PostDec arm only updates the tracked variable type and infers a result; it never validates that the operand is a legal lvalue-like target (the same class of check as InvalidAssignVarRule, applied to a different expression-kind allowlist) nor that the operand's type actually supports ++/-- (float/int/numeric-string/SimpleXMLElement/GMP/BcMath\Number/null/bool per PHP semantics).
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/expr.rs ExprKind::Unary PreInc/PostInc/PreDec/PostDec (~594-618)
clusters.notes: Two sub-checks bundled together (lvalue legality, conceptually reusable from the InvalidAssignVarRule cluster's work; and a type-legality allowlist, novel). The PHP-version-gated deprecation tips additionally need the PhpVersion subsystem, though the core diagnostic doesn't strictly require it. ++/-- on an unsupported type is a fairly rare real-code mistake.

clusters.root_cause: BinOp::Pipe is typed as Type::Mixed unconditionally; the checker never inspects the right-hand callable's parameter list to see whether its first parameter is declared by-reference (which a pipe's implicit temporary value can't satisfy).
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/expr.rs BinOp::Pipe handling (~2436-2440)
clusters.notes: Operator-level parsing/lexing is already full parity (bright spot) — this is purely 'look up the RHS callable's first-parameter by-ref flag', likely reusable from existing call-argument-binding logic elsewhere in the checker. Value is low simply because the |> operator is brand new (PHP 8.5) and essentially unused in real code yet.

clusters.root_cause: regex_groups.rs implements a hand-rolled PCRE-subset parser, but purely to infer named/numbered capture groups for preg_match()'s $matches shape; on any pattern it can't confidently parse it silently returns None rather than validating the pattern is well-formed PCRE and reporting a syntax error — there is no PCRE-validity engine or diagnostic path at all.
clusters.rust_location: src/regex_groups.rs (parse_capture_groups and its supporting atom scanner)
clusters.notes: Genuinely a new capability, not a small extension of the existing parser — real PCRE validation needs to catch a much broader class of malformed patterns than the capture-group scanner currently handles (unbalanced groups, bad quantifiers, invalid character classes, etc.), likely requiring either a fuller hand-written validator or shelling out to a regex engine. High value: malformed preg_* patterns (typo'd delimiters, unescaped special characters) are a very common real PHP bug that PHPStan reliably catches.

clusters.root_cause: No equivalent logic exists anywhere in src/ — no delimiter-extraction-from-pattern helper, no cross-referencing of a preg_quote() sub-call's optional delimiter argument against the enclosing pattern's actual delimiter character.
clusters.rust_location: none — would be new logic in src/checker/calls.rs alongside preg_* call handling
clusters.notes: Narrow, standalone check. Could reuse a pattern-argument-extraction helper if RegularExpressionPatternRule's cluster is built first (soft/non-blocking prerequisite — both need to locate the pattern argument on preg_* FuncCall nodes), but doesn't strictly require it. The specific mistake this catches (forgetting or mismatching preg_quote()'s delimiter arg) is real but fairly narrow in real-code frequency.

clusters.root_cause: phpstan-rs has no centralized 'every class-name usage gets a side-channel validation pass' hook. Class names referenced anywhere in the AST go straight into type resolution; nothing compares as-written case against declared case, and nothing pattern-matches for PHP-Scoper/Rector/Box/PHPUnit leaked-prefix artifacts. ClassNameCheck in real PHPStan is purely a dispatcher over the other two, so with both sub-checks absent the dispatcher has literally nothing to dispatch to.
clusters.rust_location: No existing file owns this; would be a new module (e.g. src/checker/class_name.rs) hooked wherever class-name identifiers are currently resolved to types (the name-resolution path used by types.rs/checker.rs), plus a small declared-name-registry to compare canonical vs. as-written case.
clusters.notes: Self-contained and easy to build in isolation (string/registry comparisons, no type-system depth needed), but real-world payoff is thin: case mismatches rarely survive case-sensitive Linux CI/autoloading in practice, and the forbidden-prefix check only fires on PHAR-scoped/rector-prefixed code, a narrow slice of real codebases.

clusters.cluster_name: Attribute AST support and semantic validation
clusters.root_cause: The parser itself has no AST node representing a #[Attribute(...)] group outside of stub-file lexer skipping (lexer.rs's skip_stub_availability_attribute etc. discards the syntax rather than producing a node). With no attribute node in the tree, there is nothing downstream for a checker pass to walk, so no semantic validation (class exists / is an Attribute / target flags / repeatability / deprecation / constructor-arg validity) can exist yet.
clusters.rust_location: Needs an AST node addition in the parser/AST definition (wherever the expression/declaration node enum lives) plus a new checker module analogous to AttributesCheck, once attribute nodes exist to visit.
clusters.notes: This is architectural, not incremental: it requires parser/AST work before any checker logic is possible. Real-world value is climbing as attribute-heavy frameworks (Symfony, Doctrine, PHPUnit) spread, but the specific diagnostics here (wrong target, non-repeatable duplicate, bad constructor args) are a moderate-frequency correctness net, not a top-tier one.

clusters.root_cause: PHPStan's approach here is unusual — it actually constructs a native DateTime/DateInterval from a literal argument string and inspects the runtime result/errors. phpstan-rs has no equivalent 'probe a literal by simulating the target function's real parsing semantics' pattern anywhere, and no ISO-8601-duration or DateTime-format parser exists in the codebase at all to reimplement it natively.
clusters.rust_location: New special-case logic, likely alongside other builtin-function call handling in src/checker/calls.rs (a `new DateTime`/`new DateTimeImmutable`/`new DateInterval` branch keyed on a string-literal argument).
clusters.notes: Two items, one shared root cause and shared implementation shape (probe-a-literal-string). Genuinely useful in practice — malformed date/interval format strings are a common real bug PHPStan catches — but scoped narrowly to two constructors.

clusters.root_cause: calls.rs's check_args implements only the MVP core of PHPStan's argument-binding model: positional arity counting and a per-positional-argument type check. It never grew a model for named arguments (unknown/duplicate/positional-after-named), unpacked/spread arguments, or by-reference target legality — the latter needs exactly the 'does this access chain contain a nullsafe operator anywhere' walk that NullsafeCheck provides in real PHPStan, which phpstan-rs has never built despite already tracking nullsafe for nullability widening elsewhere in expr.rs.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/calls.rs — check_args (~line 262) for the argument-binding gaps, and the by-ref handling block (~lines 60-140) for the by-ref-target legality gap.
clusters.notes: The existing partial implementation (arity + positional type-check) is real and load-bearing, so this is extension rather than a rewrite. Named-argument and by-ref misuse are common in modern PHP; this is one of the highest real-world-value gaps in the whole standalone-checks category. Template-resolution and allowed-constant/exclusive-group/bitmask sub-features are lower-frequency additions within the same file, bundled here rather than split out since they attach to the same check_args entry point.

clusters.root_cause: phpstan-rs performs no 'class referenced in a parameter or return type does not exist' diagnostic anywhere in the checker — confirmed by zero class-existence report sites across src/checker/*. There is also no pass for the declaration-era deprecation diagnostics (implicit-nullable param, pre-8.0 union types, required-after-optional, @self-out, #[NoDiscard] misuse) or for checking that a declared @template is actually used in a parameter (distinct from generics.rs's existing template-variance misuse check).
clusters.rust_location: No existing pass owns this; needs a new declaration-time walk over function/method/closure signatures (native + PHPDoc types), likely invoked from wherever declarations are first visited in the checker's top-level walk, with a class-existence lookup against the same registry types.rs already uses for resolution.
clusters.notes: The 'referenced class doesn't exist' sub-check alone is high-value — nonexistent/typo'd class names in type hints are one of the most commonly-triggered real PHPStan diagnostics. The deprecation-era sub-checks are lower value (legacy-PHP-version specific) but ride along in the same declaration walk.

clusters.root_cause: stmt.rs's Return handling funnels every case through one generic is_assignable mismatch path with no special-casing for a `never`-typed function actually reaching a return, and no dedicated 'value returned from a void function' diagnostic — consistent with Type::Void apparently having no dedicated is_assignable branch in the type system.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/stmt.rs Return handling (~lines 80-100); likely also needs a Type::Void-specific branch in the is_assignable logic (types.rs/checker.rs).
clusters.notes: The general return-type-mismatch and generator-aware bare-return handling are already implemented and working — this is a narrow, mechanical extension of an existing, functioning code path rather than new infrastructure.

clusters.root_cause: This is a deliberate design choice, not an unimplemented feature: expr.rs computes is_existence_probe specifically to route isset()/empty()/?? arguments through check_expr_quiet_root, explicitly opting out of ever flagging 'offset doesn't exist'-style diagnostics for these constructs, per the code's own comment. Reversing it means building an equivalent to PHPStan's IssetabilityResolution chain (variable/offset/property existence links) from scratch.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/expr.rs ~lines 195-224 (is_existence_probe / check_expr_quiet_root); a full fix needs a new resolution-chain subsystem, not just deleting the suppression.
clusters.notes: Real PHPStan users do hit 'always exists / never defined / redundant nullsafe' diagnostics often enough that this is a meaningful gap, but phpstan-rs's opt-out looks intentional (isset() is widely used defensively, so a naive implementation risks high false-positive rates) — this is more a product-scope decision than a bug.

clusters.root_cause: No generic recursive Type-tree walker exists for detecting a bare iterable/array with no value type, a non-generic use of a class that is itself generic (missing template args), or a Closure/callable type with no declared signature — this is a type-system helper, not tied to any specific rule's call site.
clusters.rust_location: Would live as a new helper alongside type definitions in types.rs, since it needs to walk a resolved Type value generically.
clusters.notes: Mostly a strictness/pedantic-level concern (PHPStan gates most of this behind higher analysis levels) rather than a correctness-bug catcher; useful for teams chasing full generic coverage but not a common source of real production bugs.

clusters.root_cause: String-consuming array functions (implode/join, sort comparators, castable-to-number contexts) aren't specially modeled in the call checker to validate that every element type of an array argument survives a cast (toString/toNumber) without producing an error type — no such per-element-cast helper exists.
clusters.rust_location: Function-specific special-casing area of src/checker/calls.rs, alongside other builtin-function argument checks.
clusters.notes: implode()/join() called on an array containing objects without __toString() is a genuinely common real-world bug; this is a small, self-contained helper once the array-of-elements type is already resolved.

clusters.root_cause: phpstan-rs has no dead-code-analysis category of any kind — grepping for 'unused' anywhere in non-test src/ returns zero hits. Building this requires a full variable-usage walker over a function/closure body (recursive, with func_get_args()/get_defined_vars()/compact()/dynamic-name-variable escape hatches that force treating all variables as used), which has no partial equivalent anywhere to extend.
clusters.rust_location: Would be an entirely new module (e.g. src/checker/dead_code.rs) hooked at constructor-promoted-parameter and closure-declaration check points.
clusters.notes: Code-cleanliness signal rather than a correctness-bug catcher — commonly enabled in real projects' CI but rarely the check that prevents an actual production defect. The dynamic-name-variable/compact()/func_get_args() escape hatches add real complexity for a check whose payoff is mostly stylistic.

bright_spots: FunctionCallParametersCheck (partial): calls.rs already implements a real, working core — positional arity checking (too-few/too-many) plus a per-argument type-compatibility check against resolved parameter types with a Mixed short-circuit. This is genuine parity with PHPStan's most load-bearing call-site diagnostics, not a stub.

FunctionReturnTypeCheck (partial): stmt.rs's Return handling already correctly special-cases generators (skipping the getReturn()-only case) when validating bare `return;` against the declared type at severity level 3 — a subtlety easy to get wrong that phpstan-rs got right.

generics.rs already implements template-variance misuse checking (covariant-in-input-position etc., ~line 218), showing real generics infrastructure exists even though it isn't yet wired into FunctionDefinitionCheck's 'template declared but unused' diagnostic or FunctionCallParametersCheck's unresolvable-template reporting.

The IssetCheck gap is best read as an intentional scope decision (explicitly commented in expr.rs) rather than an oversight — phpstan-rs's authors evidently weighed false-positive risk on a very commonly-used defensive construct and chose to opt out, which is a defensible engineering call, not neglect.
clusters_by_category.not_applicable_summary: All 14 raw items are legitimate and directly clusterable — none look like placeholder or invented data. Every entry carries specific file paths, line-number anchors, and concrete grep/design evidence (e.g. 'lexer.rs skip_stub_availability_attribute', 'calls.rs ~line 60-140', 'expr.rs ~195-224 is_existence_probe'), and the two 'partial' items include precise descriptions of exactly which sub-behaviors are and aren't covered rather than vague hedging. No item needed to be excluded as not-applicable to a phpstan-rs parity roadmap.

clusters.cluster_name: Duplicate-declaration scan within a class/trait body
clusters.root_cause: No scan exists anywhere in the checker for redeclared enum cases, constants, properties (incl. promoted params), or methods within one class/trait body — grep for 'Cannot redeclare'/'redeclare property'/'redeclare method' across src/ returns nothing.
clusters.rust_location: new function in src/checker/oop.rs, alongside the existing check_enum_case_values / check_trait_conflicts
clusters.notes: PHP itself already fatals on a literal duplicate method/property/const written twice in the SAME class body, so this rule's real value is narrower than the name suggests: it mainly catches duplicate enum cases and duplicates arising from composing multiple traits (which PHP does NOT reject at parse time).

clusters.root_cause: The registry is a single global name->ClassInfo map with last-write-wins semantics; checker.rs's own doc comment (~line 98) documents cross-file name collisions as an accepted simplification in the OPPOSITE direction (silently pick one) rather than flagging them.
clusters.rust_location: src/registry.rs (registry build), checker.rs:~98
clusters.notes: Requires tracking multiple declarations per name project-wide, which cuts directly against the core single-map registry design. Real bug in practice (stray duplicate class in a legacy tree) but relatively rare.

clusters.root_cause: ClassInfo.consts is `HashMap<String, Type>` (src/registry/class_info.rs:38, populated ~line 393; read via src/registry.rs:741 lookup_const) with no visibility, finality, native-type, value, or trait-origin metadata attached to each constant.
clusters.rust_location: src/registry/class_info.rs (consts field + its population), src/checker/expr.rs StaticAccess handling (~lines 1013-1083, 1701-1729)
clusters.notes: CORRECTION to raw data: ConflictingTraitConstantsRule's note claims 'class constants aren't tracked in the registry at all' — this is false; consts ARE tracked as a name->Type map (class_info.rs:38). The real gap is narrower: no visibility/finality/value/trait-origin fields, not the absence of constant tracking itself. Only the private/protected-visibility and onTrait sub-parts of ClassConstantRule belong here; its other sub-parts belong to the class-name-validation cluster below.

clusters.root_cause: ClassKind is tracked per class (src/ast.rs:213-218) and the registry can resolve a name to a ClassInfo, but no checker function walks the various syntactic positions where a class-like name is referenced (extends clause, implements clause, trait use, instanceof RHS) to validate that it (a) resolves to a known declaration and (b) is the expected kind (class vs interface vs trait vs enum). This is one reusable 'resolve-name-and-check-kind' utility that stock PHPStan itself shares across these Rules, missing from phpstan-rs entirely.
clusters.rust_location: new shared function (e.g. in src/checker/oop.rs or a new src/checker/class_refs.rs), called from wherever ClassDecl.extends/implements/uses and InstanceOf expressions are walked
clusters.notes: One of the highest-value clusters in this category: misspelled class names and kind mismatches (implementing a trait instead of an interface, etc.) are extremely common real-world PHP bugs, and the prerequisite data (ClassKind) already exists — this is checker wiring, not a new data model. check_final_class_extension (oop.rs:16-34) already implements the final-class-extension sub-check of ExistingClassInClassExtendsRule using this same registry data, so that rule is closer to done than its 'missing' status alone suggests.

clusters.root_cause: No 'impossible condition' analysis engine exists for instanceof at all — it is used only for flow-sensitive narrowing (src/checker/narrowing.rs narrow_instanceof_true and friends), never fed back into a static-truth-value diagnostic.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/narrowing.rs (would need a paired always-true/false detector comparing the narrowed type against Never/against the pre-narrowing type)
clusters.notes: Redundant/impossible instanceof checks are a very common and high-signal PHPStan finding on real codebases (dead defensive code, refactor debt); this is a real capability gap, not plumbing.

clusters.cluster_name: new Foo(...) first-class-callable syntax not distinctly represented
clusters.root_cause: The parser already recognizes `new Foo(...)` (comment at src/parser/postfix.rs:389 notes this syntax doesn't exist in PHP) but silently drops the ellipsis flag and parses it as an ordinary `new`, instead of producing a distinct AST shape the checker could flag.
clusters.rust_location: src/parser/postfix.rs:389-397
clusters.notes: Bright spot: the parser already detects and comments on this exact syntax — only needs the flag threaded through plus one unconditional diagnostic. Low value because `new Foo(...)` is invalid PHP that essentially never appears in real code; PHPStan's rule exists mainly for a friendly error message.

clusters.root_cause: Beyond the kind-check gap (shared with the class-name-validation cluster), InstantiationRule is missing: private/protected constructor-visibility errors, 'no constructor + args given', and self/parent/static-outside-class errors — the last because self/parent/static resolution silently falls back through resolve_pseudo instead of erroring when used out of class context.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/expr.rs:836-909 (ExprKind::New arm), src/checker/resolve.rs (resolve_pseudo)
clusters.notes: Bright spot: interface/abstract-class instantiation errors, class-not-found, and full constructor argument-count/type checking (mirroring FunctionCallParametersCheck) are already implemented — this rule is substantially further along than its 'partial' status implies; the trait/enum-instantiation sub-parts should be picked up for free once the class-name-validation cluster lands.

clusters.cluster_name: PHP attribute AST support entirely absent
clusters.root_cause: The lexer treats `#[...]` as raw skipped bytes (src/lexer.rs skip_whitespace_and_comments, ~lines 520-540), special-cased only for two specific stub-only attributes needed for signature gating. No Attribute/AttrGroup AST node exists anywhere in the codebase (verified: grep for 'Attribute'/'attr_groups' across src/ast.rs and src/parser/*.rs returns nothing).
clusters.rust_location: src/lexer.rs (attribute skip logic), src/ast.rs (no attribute node type), every parser site that would attach one (classes, traits, methods, properties, consts, params)
clusters.notes: CORRECTION to raw data: the NonClassAttributeClassRule item claims 'Attribute groups (#[...]) are parsed into the AST (grep confirms attr_groups/AttrGroup exist in parser/classes.rs and ast.rs)' — this is factually wrong. I re-ran the same greps during clustering and both parser/classes.rs and ast.rs have zero matches for Attribute/attr_groups; the lexer only skips attribute bytes, it never builds structured nodes. That item's root cause is identical to ClassAttributesRule's (no attribute AST at all), not a separate 'parsed but unchecked' situation. This needs real lexing (not skip) plus parser support at every attachable site before any attribute-content rule can exist.

clusters.root_cause: src/docblock.rs has no parsing of `@phpstan-type` or `@phpstan-import-type` tags at all (only @param/@return/@var/@template/@extends/@implements-family tags are handled).
clusters.rust_location: src/docblock.rs
clusters.notes: @phpstan-type is a commonly used readability feature in well-typed PHP codebases (complex union/shape types given a name). The TraitUse variant additionally needs per-use-site re-resolution against the using class's template args, a smaller wrinkle on top of the base tag-parsing work.

clusters.root_cause: src/docblock.rs never parses `@method` tags, so magic/virtual methods declared via phpdoc are neither registered as callable methods in the registry nor validated.
clusters.rust_location: src/docblock.rs, src/registry/class_info.rs (would need to synthesize a method entry the way @property already synthesizes a field)
clusters.notes: @method tags are extremely common for __call-based magic APIs in real frameworks and libraries; the gap here is broader than this Rules category alone — it likely also causes spurious 'undefined method' false positives elsewhere in phpstan-rs today.

clusters.root_cause: src/docblock.rs never parses `@mixin` tags, so a class doesn't get another type's methods/properties folded in, and the tag itself is never validated.
clusters.rust_location: src/docblock.rs
clusters.notes: Common in some framework-heavy codebases (Laravel-style facades/traits) but less universal than @method.

clusters.root_cause: src/registry/class_info.rs already parses @property/@property-read/@property-write tags and uses them to synthesize magic properties for type inference (~lines 184-207), but no validation pass exists for the tags themselves.
clusters.rust_location: new checker pass consuming the same parsed tag data in src/registry/class_info.rs; no equivalent to PropertyTagCheck exists in src/checker/*
clusters.notes: Bright spot: this is the one docblock-tag family where phpstan-rs already built the harder half (parsing + real type-inference integration) — only the diagnostic-emitting half (unknown class ref, trait-as-invalid-type, missing generics/iterable-value/callable-signature, generic-object-type conformance) is missing, making this cheaper than the sibling @method/@mixin clusters despite being architecturally similar.

clusters.root_cause: src/docblock.rs has no parsing for @require-extends/@require-implements tags at all, and no template/require-tag machinery references them.
clusters.rust_location: src/docblock.rs
clusters.notes: A comparatively newer, narrower PHPStan feature mostly used in generic trait/interface library code; real but lower-frequency than the other tag families.

clusters.root_cause: src/docblock.rs never parses the `@consistent-constructor` tag (grep confirms), and separately no checker code ever emits an 'unsafe new static()' or 'new static in abstract static method' diagnostic even though the type-inference side (Type::StaticRef / resolve_pseudo) already resolves `new static()`'s type correctly.
clusters.rust_location: src/docblock.rs (tag parsing), src/checker/expr.rs:1609-1625 and src/checker/resolve.rs (resolve_pseudo) for the diagnostic-emitting side
clusters.notes: `new static()` misuse causing runtime fatals is a known real gotcha in abstract-factory-style OOP code, so this has decent real-world value despite being a narrow feature.

clusters.root_cause: The parser already records promoted_visibility/promoted_readonly/hooks per constructor parameter (src/parser/functions.rs), but nothing in src/checker validates that promotion is constructor-only, non-variadic, or (for the newest sub-case) PHP-version-gated.
clusters.rust_location: new check consuming src/parser/functions.rs's existing promoted_visibility/promoted_readonly fields, likely in src/checker/oop.rs or wherever FunctionLike nodes are walked
clusters.notes: The non-version-gated sub-checks (promotion outside a constructor, variadic promoted parameter) are buildable today from data the parser already captures; only the PHP 8.5 final-promoted-property version gate is blocked on the missing PhpVersion concept below.

clusters.root_cause: phpstan-rs has no PhpVersion/target-version abstraction anywhere in the codebase (grep for PhpVersion/php_version across src/ is empty), so any diagnostic that depends on 'is this construct supported by the configured target PHP version' is structurally impossible today.
clusters.rust_location: would need a new config-loaded PhpVersion value threaded through src/checker/* to every version-gated call site
clusters.notes: Cross-cutting architectural prerequisite rather than a single call site — it gates a version-gated sub-check inside several other clusters as well as these two standalone rules. Matters most for teams targeting older PHP versions; PHPStan's own defaults often assume a fairly current runtime, so overall value is real but not top-tier.

clusters.root_cause: grep for 'unused' across src/checker/*.rs returns nothing — phpstan-rs has no unused-parameter detection at all, for constructors or ordinary functions/methods (no UnusedFunctionParametersCheck equivalent exists anywhere).
clusters.rust_location: new checker pass (a variable-usage scan over the parameter list vs. the function body), likely in src/checker/functions.rs or similar
clusters.notes: Unused parameters are one of the most common lint findings in real PHP code review; the underlying machinery (usage scanning) would likely be reusable well beyond this one Rule (ordinary unused-parameter checks elsewhere in PHPStan's Rules/Functions are presumably in the same boat, though that's outside this category's scope).

clusters.root_cause: phpstan-rs has no Collector abstraction or project-wide two-pass (per-file collect, then aggregate) analysis phase at all — this is pure architectural plumbing that exists in PHPStan solely to feed cross-file rules like 'this trait is declared but never used anywhere'.
clusters.rust_location: would require a new aggregation phase in the overall checker driver, not any single existing file
clusters.notes: 'Unused trait declaration' is a rare, nice-to-have finding; low priority relative to its architectural cost. Note phpstan-rs does read per-class `use Trait` lists elsewhere (registry.rs's own `uses` field, consumed by flatten_traits) but only for member-flattening, not for this cross-file unused-trait purpose.

clusters.root_cause: No pluggable extension-point or sealed-hierarchy concept exists anywhere in src/registry.rs or src/checker/*; this PHPStan Rule is inert in stock PHPStan too unless a third-party extension registers allowed subtypes.
clusters.rust_location: would need a new extension-point mechanism (even a hardcoded/config-driven allow-list would do) — no natural home in the current codebase
clusters.notes: Standalone, genuinely unbuilt generic mechanism (not DI-only plumbing) but low real-world value since it requires opt-in configuration even in real PHPStan.

clusters.root_cause: Only the duplicate-backing-value check is implemented (src/checker/oop.rs check_enum_case_values, lines 94-121), and only for literal int/string case values. The other five checks (constructor/destructor/magic-method bans, native cases()/from()/tryFrom() redeclaration ban, backing-type-must-be-int-or-string, Serializable ban, value-presence-consistency and case-value-type-match) are each small independent structural checks against data (ClassKind::Enum, method lists, backing type) that mostly already exists in the registry.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/oop.rs check_enum_case_values (extend alongside)
clusters.notes: Bright spot: the hardest sub-check (matching duplicate values across cases) is already done; the remaining checks are comparatively mechanical since enum member/method data is already tracked in the registry.

bright_spots: InstantiationRule: interface/abstract-class instantiation errors, class-not-found, and full constructor argument-count/type checking (mirroring FunctionCallParametersCheck) are already implemented — much further along than its 'partial' status suggests.

PropertyTagCheck family: @property/@property-read/@property-write tags are already parsed AND wired into real type inference (magic property synthesis in registry/class_info.rs) — only the validation/diagnostic half is missing, unlike @method/@mixin where nothing is built yet.

InstantiationCallableRule: the parser already detects and comments on the invalid `new Foo(...)` syntax at src/parser/postfix.rs:389 — just needs the dropped flag threaded through to a diagnostic (S effort).

ExistingClassInClassExtendsRule: the final-class-extension sub-check is already implemented via check_final_class_extension (oop.rs:16-34) using registry data that would also power the rest of the class-name-validation cluster.
EnumSanityRule: the trickiest sub-check (duplicate backing values across enum cases) is already implemented in check_enum_case_values (oop.rs:94-121).
clusters_by_category.not_applicable_summary: None of the 51 raw items in this category were marked not_applicable — every one is a genuine coverage gap (missing or partial) rather than DI-only plumbing or something structurally inapplicable to phpstan-rs's design. The closest candidates to low-value/inert (AllowedSubTypesRule, which is itself inert in stock PHPStan without a third-party extension, and the Collector-based NotAnalysedTraitRule/TraitDeclarationCollector/TraitUseCollector trio) are still real, buildable mechanisms, so they were clustered and rated low-value rather than excluded.

DirectRegistry, LazyRegistry, Registry, and Rule (4 of 10 items) are all correctly marked not_applicable — they are the interface/impl/DI-plumbing for PHPStan's runtime, third-party-pluggable Rule-registration architecture (services tagged phpstan.rules.rule, resolved per-AST-node-type through a DI container or reflection-based class-hierarchy cache). phpstan-rs has no plugin/extension model and no DI container: every check is a hardcoded Rust function called directly from match arms in src/checker/stmt.rs and src/checker/expr.rs, so there is no seam a runtime Registry/Rule interface would fill. No placeholder or invented data detected — all 10 notes carry specific file:line references and concrete architectural reasoning distinct from one another; item_count_received matches the 10 supplied.

clusters.cluster_name: Diagnostic metadata builder (identifiers, tips, nonIgnorable, fixNode)
clusters.root_cause: Diagnostic (src/checker.rs:71) is a flat 4-field struct {location, message, span, level} populated via ad hoc struct literals / format!() calls scattered across src/checker/*.rs, with no identifier field, no tip/canned-tip helpers, no metadata bag, no nonIgnorable flag, and no fixNode/auto-fix support — and no fluent builder to assemble any of it consistently.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker.rs:71 (struct Diagnostic) plus every diagnostic-construction call site under src/checker/*.rs
clusters.notes: Core struct change is small, but real parity requires threading an identifier convention (PHPStan's error-identifiers scheme) and tip text through dozens of existing call sites, plus deciding on a Rust-idiomatic builder API. Mostly a tooling/UX and ignoreErrors-by-identifier parity gap rather than a missed-bug-detection gap on its own — but it is a prerequisite for the identifier half of ClassNameUsageLocation in the next cluster.

clusters.cluster_name: Configurable type-acceptance checking with combinable reasons
clusters.root_cause: is_assignable(sub, sup) -> bool (src/registry.rs:752) is a single unconditional class-hierarchy-aware compatibility check: it has no checkNullables/checkUnionTypes/checkExplicitMixed/checkImplicitMixed/checkBenevolentUnionTypes toggles (phpstan-rs has no rule-level-gating concept for these dimensions at all), no CallableType/ClosureType inner-return-type transform, no isThis() helper, and returns a bare bool instead of a structured, combinable result carrying rejection reasons.
clusters.rust_location: src/registry.rs:752 fn is_assignable
clusters.notes: Affects precision/explainability of type-mismatch diagnostics (why was this rejected) and correctness on mixed/benevolent-union/nullable edge cases used across many 'access to X on Y' rules. Reworking a single bool-returning function into a configurable, reason-carrying one touches every current caller of is_assignable, but is contained to one function's contract rather than a new subsystem.

clusters.cluster_name: Unified unknown-class usage collection & reporting pipeline
clusters.root_cause: phpstan-rs has no centralized 'resolve a type, split union/intersection members, collect per-class existence errors while respecting class_exists()/interface_exists() guards, and tag each with a usage-location-specific message + identifier' pipeline (PHPStan's RuleLevelHelper::findTypeToCheck + ClassNameUsageLocation taxonomy + ClassNameNodePair DTO). Instead, unknown-class checks are hand-rolled one-off per call site (src/checker/expr.rs:902, src/checker/stmt.rs:515/574) with no shared collection abstraction, no union-splitting, no class_exists()-guard exemption, and no case-sensitivity checking; most of PHPStan's ~27 usage-location kinds (assert-tag, template bound/default, sealed, mixin, requireExtends/requireImplements, type-alias, self-out) have no counterpart check anywhere in src/.
clusters.rust_location: new module (e.g. src/checker/class_usage.rs) replacing/wrapping the ad hoc checks at src/checker/expr.rs:902 and src/checker/stmt.rs:515/574, extended to every existing and currently-missing unknown-class check site
prerequisite_clusters: Diagnostic metadata builder (identifiers, tips, nonIgnorable, fixNode)
clusters.notes: Unknown/misspelled class references (typos, missing use-imports, deleted classes) are one of the most common and highest-value classes of real PHP bugs PHPStan catches, so this is the highest-value gap in the category — but it's genuinely structural: it needs a new location taxonomy, a new collection/DTO pairing, union/intersection-splitting logic, class_exists()-guard awareness, and net-new coverage for several site kinds that have no existing hook at all. Also structurally depends on phpdoc-tag AST support for assert/template/sealed/mixin/requireExtends/requireImplements tags (an out-of-category prerequisite) to reach several of the ~27 usage-location kinds.

bright_spots: RuleLevelHelper (partial): src/registry.rs:752's is_assignable already does a genuine class-hierarchy-aware compatibility check, not a stub — it's a real, working subset of accepts()'s core job even though it lacks the configurability toggles and reasons output.

RuleErrorBuilder (partial): the Diagnostic struct at src/checker.rs:71 already carries the essential message+location pairing every diagnostic needs, giving PHPStan-equivalent output for the common case even without the identifier/tip/metadata machinery layered on top.

clusters.root_cause: phpstan-rs infers the correct Type (including literal Type::True/Type::False) for every boolean-producing expression (&&, ||, !, ==, !=, ===, !==, <, <=, >, >=, xor, ternary condition, if/elseif/while/do-while conditions) purely to drive downstream narrowing or the expression's own result type — but there is no step anywhere that takes that already-computed type, checks whether it is a compile-time-constant boolean, and emits an 'always true/false' Diagnostic. The type-system primitive (Type::True/Type::False) already exists; the missing piece is a shared 'is this expr's type a constant bool -> report' helper plus wiring it at ~13 call sites, together with the Diagnostic emission itself.
clusters.rust_location: New shared helper (e.g. src/checker/constant_condition.rs) consumed from: src/checker/expr.rs (binary-op/boolean-op Type::Bool inference, ~line 2363-2372) and src/checker/stmt.rs (StmtKind::If/While/DoWhile condition handling, DoWhile arm at line ~199)
clusters.notes: Highest-value cluster in the category: always-true/false conditions (leftover debug flags, defensive-but-impossible checks, `if (true)`) are extremely common in real PHP. WhileLoopAlwaysTrueConditionRule is nearly free: control_flow.rs's is_truthy_literal()+stmt_contains_break() (line 90) already detects the exact while(true)-no-break shape for termination analysis, it just isn't surfaced as its own diagnostic. elseif is represented as nested If inside else in stmt.rs, so ElseIfConstantConditionRule reuses the same wiring as If. PossiblyImpureTipHelper and the ConstantConditionInTrait/FunctionCallConstantCondition dedup machinery are deliberately excluded from this cluster (see separate clusters) since they are polish/dedup layers on top, not part of core detection.

clusters.cluster_name: Match/switch arm dead-code and match exhaustiveness
clusters.root_cause: src/checker/expr.rs's Match handling and src/checker/stmt.rs's Switch handling already do real arm-by-arm narrowed-scope tracking for downstream type inference and control-flow merging, but never (a) compare an arm/case's implicit equality against the subject for constant truthiness (dead-arm / always-true-arm detection), (b) check for duplicate case labels, or (c) enumerate a match's remaining unhandled enum/value space for exhaustiveness. (a)/(b) share the Cluster-A-style constant-comparison primitive; (c) additionally needs enum-case-exhaustiveness reasoning that doesn't exist yet.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/expr.rs (Match handling, ~lines 1179-1266 and 1510-1550), src/checker/stmt.rs (StmtKind::Switch, ~lines 366-470)
clusters.notes: match is idiomatic in modern PHP (8.1+) and 'unhandled match value' / dead match arm are both routinely-hit real bugs, so this ranks close to Cluster A despite needing extra exhaustiveness logic beyond the basic constant-comparison primitive.

clusters.root_cause: Match's result-type computation in expr.rs always produces an ordinary Type (never a distinct 'keep-void' marker) and nothing checks whether a match expression is being consumed as a value versus used as a bare statement.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/expr.rs (Match handling)
clusters.notes: Narrow, rarely-hit pattern (all-void match arms whose result is then used); standalone and cheap but low real-world frequency.

clusters.root_cause: narrowing.rs already computes real per-condition-shape narrowing targets (instanceof, is_*, preg_match, in_array) to update branch-local variable types, but there is no companion step that compares that narrowing target against the argument's PRE-EXISTING type via a superset/subset check to decide the check is impossible (disjoint) or redundant (already guaranteed), nor any of PHPStan's special-cased call analyses (assert(), function_exists(), count()/sizeof(), defined(), method_exists() via reflection).
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/narrowing.rs (apply_narrowing target computation) plus new comparison step; src/checker/calls.rs and src/checker/oop.rs for method/static-call resolution needed by the method-call variant
clusters.notes: ImpossibleCheckTypeHelper is 555 lines in PHPStan with many special cases (assert, method_exists+reflection, in_array strict/loose over ConstantArrayType, enum needles) — this is the single biggest logic gap in the whole category. Real-world value is high: redundant/impossible is_string()/instanceof checks in already-narrowed code are very common defensive-programming leftovers.

clusters.root_cause: narrowing.rs's in_array handling (~line 349) only builds a narrowing-target type for use as a branch condition; it never compares the needle's type against each individual value in a constant-array haystack to flag haystack entries that can never match (a per-element type-equality comparison, distinct from the narrowing-target-vs-argument comparison in the Impossible-Check-Type cluster).
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/narrowing.rs (in_array_target_type, ~line 349), extended for a new per-element haystack-vs-needle comparison pass
clusters.notes: Adjacent to the Impossible-Check-Type cluster thematically (also in_array) but a materially different comparison (per-haystack-element vs. narrowing-target). Fairly narrow real-world pattern.

clusters.root_cause: phpstan-rs's checker is a single-process, file-by-file pass that emits diagnostics eagerly; there is no PHPStan-style two-phase Collector -> CollectedDataNode whole-program aggregation pass. This blocks the dedup layer that decides 'a trait's constant condition should be reported once in the trait, not once per using class' and 'a call site already owned by ImpossibleCheckType* shouldn't also be reported by the generic constant-condition rule'.
clusters.rust_location: src/registry.rs / src/project.rs (no CollectedDataNode-equivalent final aggregation pass over all analyzed files)
clusters.notes: Genuine architectural feature (new cross-file pass), but it adds no new detection capability by itself — it only prevents duplicate/inconsistent reports in edge cases (same trait method used by several classes; a call site double-owned by two rule families). Low priority relative to its cost unless false-positive-duplication complaints from the underlying rules (once built) become a real problem.

clusters.cluster_name: Function/method/constructor purity tracking and unused-pure-call-result dead code
clusters.root_cause: There is no purity/impurity concept anywhere in phpstan-rs's reflection model — FunctionReflection/MethodReflection carry no isPure/hasSideEffects/impure-points fields (confirmed via grep and explicitly called out in ROADMAP.md as future Phase 41). This blocks both the whole-program purity-graph resolver and every 'call on its own line has no effect' rule for functions, methods, static methods, and constructors.
clusters.rust_location: src/registry.rs (FunctionReflection/MethodReflection struct definitions, need new purity fields) plus a new whole-program purity-graph pass (depends on the collector architecture above)
clusters.notes: Largest single cluster by item count (12). Catches real mistakes (discarding the result of an immutable-style method or a pure computation), but purity inference is inherently conservative even in PHPStan itself, so real-world hit rate is moderate rather than high, and false positives are a real risk without careful modeling.

clusters.cluster_name: Possibly-impure tip decoration on constant-condition diagnostics
clusters.root_cause: src/checker.rs's Diagnostic struct (line 71) has only {location, message, span, level} — no identifier or tip/annotation field — so there is no mechanism to append a supplementary note to an existing diagnostic, which is what this helper does (and it also needs purity data that doesn't exist).
clusters.rust_location: src/checker.rs (Diagnostic struct, line 71)
clusters.notes: Pure UX polish (an informational tip appended to an already-emitted diagnostic); only meaningful once both the constant-condition rule family and purity tracking exist.
prerequisite_clusters: Function/method/constructor purity tracking and unused-pure-call-result dead code

clusters.root_cause: No statement-level check exists for a side-effect-free bare expression statement (stray comparison, logical op, or ternary used as a whole statement, or any other non-call/non-assign/non-closure expression with a discarded result) — src/checker/stmt.rs has no such analysis at all, and it isn't even named in ROADMAP's Phase 15 DeadCode bullet list.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/stmt.rs (expression-statement handling)
clusters.notes: Catches real typos (e.g. `$x == 5;` where `$x = 5;` was meant, or a forgotten `return`/`echo`). Currently untracked even in the project's own roadmap, so it's a genuine gap, not just deferred work.

clusters.root_cause: control_flow.rs already computes always_terminates()-style reachability for if/switch/try/match branches, but that result is only consumed to merge/narrow local-variable state across branches — it is never used to flag a subsequent statement as unreachable and emit a diagnostic for it.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/control_flow.rs (always_terminates, already computed) + src/checker/stmt.rs (statement-sequence walking, needs to consume the result and emit a diagnostic)
clusters.notes: Best effort-to-value ratio in the entire category: the hard analytical primitive already exists and is exercised elsewhere, so this is essentially wiring plus a diagnostic call. Dead code after return/throw/continue/break is one of the most common and highest-signal real-world PHPStan findings. Explicitly named as open work in ROADMAP's Phase 15.

clusters.root_cause: No per-class aggregation of member-usage sites exists anywhere: nothing walks a class's ::CONST fetches, method-call sites (including array-callable literals like [$this,'foo']), or property-fetch sites to determine which private constants/methods/properties are ever referenced from outside their own declaration/recursive self-use.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/oop.rs (class/member resolution, needs a new per-class usage-site collection pass)
clusters.notes: Very common, high-signal real-world finding, especially after refactors leave dead private methods/props behind. UnusedPrivatePropertyRule is materially more elaborate than the other two (five distinct read/write/never-read/never-written/only-read messages, @phpstan-always-read/-written tag support), but shares the identical root-cause gap (no usage-site aggregation), so it's grouped here rather than split out.

clusters.root_cause: No 'narrow a declared type against the union of actually-produced values' comparison utility exists (types.rs has nothing analogous to TooWideTypeCheck) — nothing unions a function/method/closure/arrow-function's actual return statements, or a property's actual assignments, and compares that union against the declared type to flag unused union members or an over-wide bool.
clusters.rust_location: src/types.rs (needs a new narrow-declared-vs-observed-union helper); consumed from function/method/closure/property-assignment analysis in src/checker/*.rs
clusters.notes: Directly the subject of ROADMAP's open Phase 45. More of a type-hygiene/precision nit than a correctness-bug catcher, so moderate rather than high real-world value, but still a well-defined, self-contained feature once the core comparison helper exists.

clusters.root_cause: phpstan-rs has no @param-out phpdoc tag concept at all (grepped docblock.rs/registry.rs — no param-out/ParamOut/by-ref-out fields), which is a harder prerequisite gap than the return-type variant: there's no declared out-type to even compare against, in addition to lacking the same TooWideTypeCheck-style comparison engine.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker (docblock/phpdoc parsing — new @param-out tag support) + src/types.rs comparison helper + src/checker/control_flow.rs (execution-end/return scopes needed to compute actual by-ref-assigned type)
clusters.notes: @param-out is a rarely-used phpdoc convention in real-world PHP, so this is low priority even though the mechanical shape mirrors the return-type cluster.

bright_spots: The Type enum already has literal Type::True/Type::False constant-boolean variants — the core type-system primitive underlying the entire 14-item constant-condition-rule family already exists; what's missing is purely the comparison-and-report wiring, not new type-system work.

src/checker/control_flow.rs already computes always_terminates()-style reachability across if/switch/try/match branches for narrowing/merge purposes — this is directly reusable, nearly as-is, for UnreachableStatementRule (rated S effort as a result).

control_flow.rs's is_truthy_literal() + stmt_contains_break() combination already specifically detects the 'while(true) with no break' shape for definite-termination analysis — most of WhileLoopAlwaysTrueConditionRule's detection logic already exists, it just isn't surfaced as its own diagnostic.

src/checker/narrowing.rs has genuinely sophisticated per-condition-shape narrowing (instanceof, is_*, preg_match, in_array target inference, and/or chain handling) that goes well beyond a naive implementation — it's the right foundation to build the Impossible-Check-Type family on top of, once a narrowing-target-vs-current-type comparison step is added.

src/checker/stmt.rs's Switch handling already does real narrowed_locals/native-narrowed/exit_states tracking arm-by-arm (documented at length in-line) that closely mirrors what SwitchConditionRule's own arm-by-arm dead-code logic needs structurally.
clusters_by_category.not_applicable_summary: Sanity check: item_count_received (57) matches the 57 raw items exactly, and every item's notes are specific and well-evidenced (concrete file/line references into phpstan-rs's src/, grep results, ROADMAP.md cross-references) rather than generic or placeholder text — no fabricated/invented data detected. Two items are correctly marked not_applicable and excluded from clusters: CollectedConstantConditionError and ImpossibleCheckTypeReportedCollector are both pure plumbing for PHPStan's parallel-worker/result-cache architecture (JSON-crossing-a-process-boundary path rewriting, and a marker-only collector with both methods throwing ShouldNotHappenException) — phpstan-rs is single-process with no result-cache serialization boundary and no collector marker mechanism, so there is no sensible porting target for these two classes specifically; the real detection logic they support is fully captured by the 'missing' Rule/Helper classes assessed in the clusters above.

2 of 49 items are genuinely not_applicable: AlwaysUsedClassConstantsExtension (a zero-logic DI extension-point interface for a dead-code check phpstan-rs doesn't implement at all) and DynamicClassConstantFetchRule (blocked by an AST representation choice - StaticAccess(String,String) can't hold a dynamic-expression class-constant name - needs a parser/AST redesign, not a checker addition). Separately, 6 of the 49 raw records (EnumTemplateTypeRule, FunctionSignatureVarianceRule, FunctionTemplateTypeRule, InterfaceTemplateTypeRule, MethodTemplateTypeRule, TraitTemplateTypeRule) are missing the status/kind/our_location fields every other record has; their status was inferred from their description/notes prose (all read as "missing", consistent with grep-confirmed absence of equivalent Rust logic) rather than fabricated, but this looks like truncated/incomplete input worth flagging rather than silently treating as complete data.
bright_spots: DefinedVariableRule (undefined-variable diagnostic) is a solid, well-exercised implementation covering both definite and possibly-undefined branch-merge cases via Locals/merge_scopes, with real test coverage - not a stub.

The IssetCheck 'quiet root' suppression (check_expr_quiet_root/is_existence_probe in expr.rs) - the architecturally harder half of isset()/empty()/??'s special handling, since it must propagate through nested property/array-access chains - is already built and correctly shared across all three call sites. Only the second, better-scoped half (the 'is always null'/'is not nullable' diagnostic) is missing.

check_generic_bounds/check_class_generic_bounds (generics.rs) implement genuine recursive subtype checking through Object/Array/ClassString/Union/Intersection/ArrayShape for generic bound violations, and are reused as the shared engine behind four different PHPStan rule-equivalents (ClassAncestorsRule, GenericAncestorsCheck, GenericObjectTypeCheck, InterfaceAncestorsRule) - a nontrivial, well-factored core even though the surrounding count/unresolvable/variance checks are absent.

Checker::check_variance is a self-aware, deliberately-scoped simplification (its own doc comment says so) of VarianceCheck's algorithm, and is correctly wired into every class method's contravariant-param/covariant-return checking - real, working variance enforcement for the common case.

unset() at least removes the target's Locals entry today, so a subsequent use of an unset variable still surfaces via the ordinary undefined-variable diagnostic even though UnsetRule's own readonly/hooked/offset diagnostics are absent.
NullCoalesceRule's ?? operator already participates in real type inference (narrowing/widening via narrowing.rs) independent of the two missing IssetCheck-specific diagnostics.

clusters.root_cause: No validation rejects a class constant literally named 'class'; ClassConst's existing `name` field is never checked against the reserved word.
clusters.rust_location: src/parser/classes.rs / src/checker/oop.rs (new check on ClassConst.name)
clusters.notes: Standalone, cheapest possible fix - no new AST fields needed, just a name-equality check.

clusters.root_cause: ClassConst in src/ast.rs stores only {name, value, doc_comment, span} - the parser never captures `final`, visibility, or a native type on `const` declarations, and registry ClassInfo.consts is a flat HashMap<String,Type> with no per-constant reflection.
clusters.rust_location: src/ast.rs ClassConst struct; src/parser/classes.rs constant parsing; registry/class_info.rs ClassInfo.consts
clusters.notes: FinalPrivateConstantRule's own final+private check needs no PhpVersion gating and could ship as soon as the fields exist; FinalConstantRule and NativeTypedClassConstantRule additionally need the PhpVersion cluster for their 'not supported before PHP X.Y' half.

clusters.root_cause: phpstan-rs has no concept of a configured target PHP version anywhere in the codebase, so no rule can gate a diagnostic on 'only invalid before PHP X.Y' / 'only valid since PHP X.Y'.
clusters.rust_location: none currently - would need a new Config.php_version-equivalent threaded into Checker
clusters.notes: Recurs across multiple categories in the audit (this is only the constants slice of it); building it once pays off broadly, which argues for prioritizing it as shared infrastructure rather than per-rule.

clusters.cluster_name: Class-constant type reflection is a flattened single Type
clusters.root_cause: registry ClassInfo.consts stores one resolved Type per constant name with no native-vs-phpdoc distinction and no per-class-in-hierarchy prototype tracking, so neither a value-vs-declared-type check nor a hierarchy override-compatibility check (the analogue of the method-override checks that already exist in oop.rs) has any data to work against.
clusters.rust_location: registry/class_info.rs ClassInfo.consts; src/checker/oop.rs (would add a const-override check beside the existing method-override logic)
