clusters.notes: OverridingConstantRule is a real, comparably-sized gap next to the method-override checks phpstan-rs already has - not a whole missing feature family, just this one symmetric piece.

clusters.root_cause: Bare identifier constant fetches parse as ExprKind::Name and are typed unconditionally as Type::Mixed (expr.rs:1480); there is no known-constants table (builtins or user-defined) to check existence against.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/expr.rs:1480
clusters.notes: Undefined-constant typos are a common, easy-to-hit real bug (PHP treats it as fatal since 8.0); moderate implementation cost for high real-world payoff.

clusters.root_cause: No user-config feature exists (a phpstan.neon-equivalent mapping constant names to expected types), so there is no ConstantResolver::getConfiguredGlobalConstantType() analogue for either define() calls or `const` statements to consult.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/calls.rs (no define() case); src/checker/control_flow.rs:200 (GlobalConst only used for yield detection)
clusters.notes: Opt-in PHPStan feature most real projects never configure; needs a config-schema surface before any checker logic is useful.

clusters.root_cause: No distinct MagicConst AST node exists - __CLASS__/__FUNCTION__/__METHOD__/__NAMESPACE__ parse as ordinary ExprKind::Name identifiers with no context tracking (only __DIR__ gets narrow special-casing, unrelated to this rule, in composer.rs).
clusters.rust_location: src/lexer.rs; src/ast.rs (no MagicConst variant)
clusters.notes: Mostly catches copy-pasted trait/global-scope code; niche but cheap-ish once a MagicConst node exists.

clusters.root_cause: Attributes are lexed but never modeled into the AST as attrGroups and never validated for target/args anywhere in phpstan-rs - a whole missing subsystem, not specific to constants.
clusters.rust_location: src/lexer.rs (attribute tokens only); no attrGroups field anywhere in src/ast.rs
clusters.notes: This item is the constants-specific tip of a much larger cross-cutting gap; building full attribute support purely to unlock this one rule would be poor ROI - only worth doing if other categories' audits also need it.

clusters.root_cause: No equivalent of PHPStan's MissingTypehintCheck (iterable-without-value-type / non-generic-class-used-generically / callable-without-signature) exists anywhere in phpstan-rs, for any declaration kind.
clusters.rust_location: none - would be a new shared checker module
clusters.notes: This is a whole feature family shared with params/returns/properties elsewhere in the audit (out of category); building it just for class constants would be wasteful - track as one cross-category initiative.
prerequisite_clusters: missing-type-specificity checks for params/returns/properties (out-of-category, same MissingTypehintCheck subsystem)

clusters.root_cause: template_bounds/templates parsed in docblock.rs are only ever consumed later for usage-site substitution/bound-violation checking (check_generic_bounds); there is no declaration-time validation pass at all - no name-collision-with-existing-class check, no bound-kind support check, no default-vs-bound subtyping, no required-after-optional ordering, no method-vs-class template shadow check.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/generics.rs (would add a new check_template_declarations); src/docblock.rs (source data already parsed)
clusters.notes: Six PHPStan classes collapse to one root cause since they're all just 'run TemplateTypeCheck on this declaration kind's own @template tags' - the underlying data (template_bounds) already exists, only the declaration-time validation logic is missing. FunctionTemplateTypeRule, InterfaceTemplateTypeRule, MethodTemplateTypeRule and TraitTemplateTypeRule are among the 6 records missing status fields in the raw input; inferred missing from their notes.

clusters.cluster_name: Enum cannot be generic - check missing
clusters.root_cause: docblock.rs parses @template tags uniformly for any class-like including enums; no check anywhere rejects an enum carrying @template tags.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/generics.rs or checker.rs EnumDecl arm
clusters.notes: Trivial once isolated - existing data (templates on an enum's ClassInfo) is already there, just needs an 'is_enum && !templates.is_empty()' guard.

clusters.root_cause: checker.rs's StmtKind::EnumDecl arm (line 337) never calls check_class_generic_bounds - that call is gated to ClassDecl only (line 324) - so enums get zero generic-ancestor checking, not even the partial bound-checking classes already receive; enums also need a distinct '@extends is always invalid on an enum' special case since enums can't extend.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker.rs line 324 vs 337
clusters.notes: Cheap quick win - reuses the already-implemented check_class_generic_bounds machinery, just needs to be wired into the enum branch plus one new always-invalid case for @extends.

clusters.root_cause: Checker::check_class_generic_bounds/check_generic_bounds (generics.rs:32,125) implement only the bound-subtype-violation core; they never check argument-count mismatches, unresolvable types, 'target isn't actually generic', trait-used-as-generic-arg, or call-site variance, because call-site variance syntax (e.g. `Collection<covariant T>`) isn't even parsed by the docblock/type parser.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/generics.rs:32 (check_generic_bounds), :125 (check_class_generic_bounds)
clusters.notes: Four PHPStan rule-equivalents share literally the same partial implementation and the same missing pieces. Generic-collection arg-count mismatches are a very common real-world finding in typed-collection-heavy codebases, making this the highest-value cluster in the generics half.

clusters.root_cause: No code walks a class's full interface/parent graph to detect the same generic interface reached via two different paths with incompatible template bindings; check_class_generic_bounds only ever looks at a class's own direct extends/implements arguments.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/generics.rs (new helper needed)
clusters.notes: Composes on top of the ancestor-checking cluster; diamond generic-interface conflicts are a real but infrequent pattern.

clusters.root_cause: docblock.rs has zero @method tag parsing - magic-method-via-PHPDoc declarations aren't modeled at all, so any @template sub-tags nested inside such tags have no data to validate.
clusters.rust_location: src/docblock.rs
clusters.notes: Base @method tag support would have value beyond just this rule (magic methods are common in ORMs/DI containers), but the specific 'template nested inside @method' sub-validation this cluster targets is a deep corner case on top of that base work.

clusters.root_cause: docblock.rs has no @use tag parsing, and registry ClassInfo.uses is a plain list of trait names with no per-use type-argument tracking.
clusters.rust_location: src/docblock.rs; registry.rs ClassInfo.uses
clusters.notes: Generic traits (e.g. `@use Collection<int>`) are a fairly rare/advanced pattern in real codebases.

clusters.cluster_name: Variance checking gaps (conservative algorithm, not wired to functions/properties)
clusters.root_cause: Checker::check_variance (generics.rs:190) is a deliberately simplified direct-occurrence check rather than true positional variance composition through nested generic arguments (a T nested inside another class's own Collection<T> isn't re-derived through that class's variance); it is wired only for methods with a known class (checker.rs:592-594), never for top-level functions or properties, and has no param-out tracking or function-scoped-variance-annotation-validity check.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/generics.rs:190 check_variance; src/checker.rs:592-594 call site
clusters.notes: Wiring to top-level functions is a small addition on top of existing logic; true positional composition through nested generics is a genuine algorithmic rewrite, and PropertyVarianceRule additionally needs property mutability/hook metadata that doesn't exist yet.

clusters.root_cause: phpstan-rs's property model carries no readonly/private(set)/property-hook distinction at all, so nothing that needs to know 'is this property's write access restricted' has data to consult.
clusters.rust_location: registry/class_info.rs property representation; src/ast.rs property declaration node
clusters.notes: Shared prerequisite feeding into two different rule clusters rather than a rule-unlock in its own right.

clusters.root_cause: phpstan-rs implements only the 'suppress undefined-variable/property checks inside the probed expression of isset()/empty()/??' half (check_expr_quiet_root in expr.rs); the actual IssetCheck diagnostic logic that reports 'is always null'/'is not nullable'/'is always falsy' from the probed expression's statically known type was never ported.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/expr.rs (check_expr_quiet_root, is_existence_probe)
clusters.notes: The harder architectural half (quiet-root suppression through nested chains) is already built and shared correctly; only a well-scoped type-to-message mapping remains. NullCoalesceRule additionally needs the separate unnecessaryNullCoalesce feature-toggle check. isset($x)-on-never-null is a very common real PHPStan finding, making this a strong effort-to-value ratio.

clusters.root_cause: check_assignment_target's bare-Variable arm, StmtKind::Global handling, and StmtKind::StaticVar handling all treat the literal name 'this' like any other identifier, despite PHP itself forbidding $this reassignment/global/static declarations.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/assignment.rs check_assignment_target; src/checker/stmt.rs lines 584 (Global) and 589 (StaticVar)
clusters.notes: Three mechanically identical name=="this" checks at three call sites - cheapest real bug-catching cluster in the whole variables set.

clusters.root_cause: @param-out is never parsed anywhere in docblock.rs, and there is no ExecutionEndNode-equivalent (end-of-function-control-flow point) concept in the checker for the execution-end variant of the check.
clusters.rust_location: src/docblock.rs (no @param-out parsing); no execution-end-flow concept anywhere in src/checker
clusters.notes: By-ref params with explicit @param-out annotations are a fairly advanced/rare pattern outside stub-heavy stdlib-adjacent code.

clusters.root_cause: compact() is handled as an ordinary unresolved call; nothing extracts constant-string (or constant-array-of-strings) variable-name arguments to cross-check against defined-variable scope.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/calls.rs (no compact() case)
clusters.notes: Can reuse the existing undefined-variable check once the argument-name extraction exists; compact() typos are a real, moderately common bug in template-rendering PHP.

clusters.cluster_name: Foreach by-ref value overwrite-on-reassign tracking absent
clusters.root_cause: Foreach handling (stmt.rs ~282) binds the loop value's element type via bind_assignment_target but keeps no synthetic marker for 'this variable currently holds an unset foreach-by-ref value', so a later plain reassignment to it is never flagged as the classic accidental-array-corruption footgun.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/stmt.rs ~282 (Foreach handling)
clusters.notes: Well-known PHP idiom-specific footgun but not a frequent real-world hit.

clusters.cluster_name: unset() modeled only as a language construct, no dedicated diagnostics
clusters.root_cause: `unset(...)` isn't a distinct statement/expression AST node - it parses as an ordinary Call special-cased only to remove the target's Locals entry; none of readonly-property, hooked-property, already-undefined-variable, or invalid-array-offset diagnostics that the real UnsetRule emits are implemented.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/expr.rs ExprKind::Call special-case (~lines 76-98); src/checker/calls.rs is_language_construct
clusters.notes: Readonly-property and invalid-offset sub-checks can reuse existing property/array-type machinery once unset() targets are walked properly; the hooked-property sub-diagnostic depends on the separate property-hook-metadata cluster.

clusters.root_cause: The Clone AST arm (expr.rs line 665) type-checks the inner expression and any clone-with overrides but never verifies the resulting type is actually an object before permitting the clone.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/expr.rs line 665 (ExprKind::Clone handling)
clusters.notes: Cheap, self-contained addition; cloning a non-object is a real, if not everyday, type-confusion bug.

clusters_by_category.not_applicable_summary: Sanity check: 52/52 items received, matches expected count. Every item carries specific file:line evidence (real grep-verified locations, real quoted messages/identifiers) and individually-reasoned notes rather than generic boilerplate — no placeholder or fabricated-looking entries detected. Genuine not_applicable items: AlwaysUsedMethodExtension (a third-party DI-extension marker interface for PHPStan's own plugin system — phpstan-rs has no plugin/extension architecture and no dead-method-detection rule for it to hook into) and MissingMethodSelfOutTypeRule (moot until @phpstan-self-out/@param-out PHPDoc parsing exists at all — a real prerequisite gap, but the missing-typehint check on top of it has no target to run against). Two items the original auditor marked not_applicable — MethodAttributesRule and CallToStaticMethodStatementWithNoDiscardRule — are re-grouped here into the 'Attribute semantics for methods' cluster below rather than treated as pure dead ends, since they share one concrete, nameable root cause (no attribute AST/semantics layer) with the 'missing' item CallToMethodStatementWithNoDiscardRule; building that layer would unlock all three together.
bright_spots: CallMethodsRule and CallStaticMethodsRule: full existence + arg-count/arg-type checking is implemented and shared (check_args in calls.rs) across plain calls, method calls, and static calls, including the Closure::bind late-bound-$this special case for static calls — this is real, heavily-exercised core functionality, not a stub.

MethodCallableRule and the StaticCall first-class-callable arm: `$obj->method(...)` and `Class::method(...)` existence checking (with __call/__callStatic exemptions) is implemented by reusing the same undefined-method logic as the plain-call paths — good architectural reuse.

ReturnTypeRule: implemented generically for both functions and methods at the correct PHPStan rule-level (3), including generator-awareness (current_function_is_generator suppresses the bare-return check) — a faithful, non-trivial port, not a simplification.

MissingMethodImplementationRule: check_class_completeness correctly implements the core Liskov-completeness contract (concrete class must implement every abstract method inherited from parent/interface/trait, with abstract-class/interface/enum exemptions) — matches real PHPStan's central behavior, missing only the built-in-ancestor (e.g. IntlBreakIterator) exemption which has no analogue without stub reflection of PHP built-ins.

FileAssertRule's assertType() half: implemented and is phpstan-rs's own internal fixture-testing DSL, mirroring PHPStan's vendored NSRT corpus mechanism — used pervasively across src/checker/tests/*, i.e. real load-bearing test infrastructure even though 3 of its 4 sibling assertions are unimplemented.

OverridingMethodRule / check_method_overrides: despite being a single combined function rather than PHPStan's decomposed Rule+3-helpers architecture, it already gets the two highest-value checks right — final-method-override detection and native parameter/return-type Liskov contravariance/covariance (with a documented static-covariance escape hatch) — which is most of the real-world bug-catching value of this rule family.

clusters.root_cause: The Call arm of check_expr special-cases PHPStan's pseudo-function testing/debug DSL (assertType/assertNativeType/assertSuperType/assertVariableCertainty/dumpType/dumpNativeType/dumpPhpDocType/debugScope), but only assertType() was ever wired up; the rest of the family has no dispatch arm at all.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/expr.rs:100-129 (assertType handling in the Call arm of check_expr) — the same arm needs additional match cases
clusters.notes: Not real end-user bug detection — these are fixture-authoring/debugging aids only reachable via literal PHPStan\ pseudo-function calls in test files. assertNativeType/assertSuperType/assertVariableCertainty/dumpType/debugScope are mechanically straightforward (compare-and-report or dump-locals, same shape as the existing assertType arm). dumpNativeType() and dumpPhpDocType() are the two exceptions: they need a separate native (non-PHPDoc-informed) type computation and a PHPDoc-node-string printer respectively, neither of which phpstan-rs's Type/Display currently distinguishes — real, if modest, type-system work beyond just adding a match arm.

clusters.root_cause: control_flow.rs tracks a loop_break_states stack and computes the break/continue level via checked_sub, but an invalid level (deeper than the actual loop nesting, or none at all — including across a closure boundary) is silently absorbed with no diagnostic; PHPStan's continue.outOfLoop/break.outOfLoop reporting has no counterpart.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/stmt.rs:629-634 (StmtKind::Break handling), src/checker/control_flow.rs (loop_break_states stack)
clusters.notes: The nesting-depth bookkeeping this needs already exists for control-flow-merge purposes; turning a currently-silent checked_sub underflow / stack-empty case into a diagnostic is a small, self-contained change. Genuine real-world value: `break 2;` miscounting nesting levels is a common, hard-to-spot bug in real PHP code.

clusters.root_cause: The parser recognizes declare(...) syntactically but explicitly discards each directive as a generic expression rather than modeling it, so there is no value to validate (must be literal 0/1) and no way to check first-statement-in-file position.
clusters.rust_location: src/parser/stmt.rs:266-282
clusters.notes: Requires capturing the declare directive's name/value in the AST instead of discarding it, then a small checker pass. Low frequency in practice (most projects get this right once and never touch it again, and many editors/templates already enforce it), but cheap to add given the AST already visits declare statements.

clusters.root_cause: goto and label statements are both parsed into distinct AST nodes, but no pass anywhere collects declared labels per function/file or cross-references goto targets against them — control_flow.rs treats every goto purely conservatively for reachability purposes and never validates target existence or tracks usage.
clusters.rust_location: src/parser/stmt.rs:296-309 (Goto/Label parsing), src/ast.rs:85,89 (StmtKind::Goto/Label), src/checker/control_flow.rs (goto handling)
clusters.notes: Needs a new label-collection-then-cross-reference pass (per enclosing function/file scope) — not just a match-arm addition, but also not a deep architectural change since both node kinds already exist in the AST. goto is rare enough in modern PHP that real-world impact is low.

clusters.root_cause: include/require/require_once/include_once are recognized only as language constructs so they don't trip undefined-function diagnostics; there is no constant-string-expression evaluator, no __DIR__-concatenation/union-expansion resolution, no filesystem-existence check, and no file_exists()-guard detection.

clusters.notes: Requires several new pieces working together: constant-expression folding (including __DIR__ concatenation and string-union expansion), PHP's own include-path resolution order simulation, an actual filesystem existence check, and static guard-pattern detection (file_exists()/is_file()/is_readable()) to suppress false positives. Broken require/include paths are a real, if not extremely common, class of bug in real deployments (path typos surviving until runtime).

clusters.root_cause: Method and class modifier flags (is_abstract, visibility, is_final) are all tracked independently in the AST/registry, but nothing cross-validates combinations of them at the declaration site itself — only the consequence of abstractness (does a concrete class implement every abstract method) is checked, not the modifier combination's own internal consistency.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/oop.rs (new function alongside check_method_overrides/check_class_completeness, e.g. check_method_modifier_consistency), reading existing src/ast.rs is_abstract/visibility/is_final fields
clusters.notes: All four are simple boolean-flag-combination checks over data the AST/registry already carries — no new modeling needed, just a new pass reading existing fields, so they cluster as one small, uniform batch of match-arm-style additions. Several of these combinations (abstract-in-non-abstract-class, private-abstract, non-body non-abstract method) are actually PHP compile-time fatal errors in real PHP, but phpstan-rs's own parser is more lenient than the PHP engine and currently accepts them silently — so this closes a real gap for any input that reaches phpstan-rs without first passing through a real PHP compile step. MethodVisibilityInInterfaceRule specifically is lower-value belt-and-suspenders since PHP itself already rejects non-public interface methods at parse time.

clusters.root_cause: docblock.rs has zero parsing for the @consistent-constructor PHPDoc tag, so there is no class-level 'has consistent constructor' flag for either rule to key off, and check_method_overrides() unconditionally exempts __construct from all comparison (the opposite of what enforcing this tag requires).
clusters.rust_location: src/docblock.rs (new tag), src/checker/oop.rs check_method_overrides (currently hard-exempts __construct; would need a conditional path for the consistent-constructor case)
clusters.notes: Two-part: (1) parse and store the new PHPDoc tag on class reflection, (2) special-case __construct back into comparison scope only when the tag is present, reusing whatever visibility/parameter-comparison logic the override-rewrite cluster produces. @consistent-constructor is a niche tag (mostly used by a handful of frameworks doing static-return-type factory patterns), hence low value.

clusters.root_cause: No check anywhere validates that a __construct (or trait-provided constructor) declares no native return type at all; check_method_overrides skips __construct outright and there is no separate standalone check for this.

clusters.notes: Simple: iterate class methods, if name is __construct and it declares a return-type annotation, report. Real PHP also rejects this at compile time (Fatal error: Constructor cannot declare a return type), so — like the modifier-consistency cluster — this closes a gap only relevant to lenient/pre-compile analysis of code phpstan-rs accepts more permissively than the real PHP engine.

clusters.root_cause: check_method_overrides() is one simplified, combined function that only checks native parameter-type contravariance and native return-type covariance, positionally; it never compares visibility, never detects missing/extra/variadic/by-ref parameter mismatches, and its ancestor lookup (lookup_ancestor_method_with_owner) is a single first-hit walk with no interface-first priority, no trait-abstract-method special case, and no separate signature-vs-inheritance-prototype distinction the way PHPStan's MethodPrototypeFinder has.

clusters.notes: This is the single highest real-world-value cluster in the batch: visibility-narrowing overrides, missing/extra parameters, and static/non-static mismatches on override are extremely common real PHP mistakes that PHPStan users hit constantly, and phpstan-rs already has the hard part (type contravariance/covariance) working — this is 'decompose and extend an existing simplified function' rather than build from nothing. The #[Override] attribute sub-check and tentative-return-type/#[ReturnTypeWillChange] handling inside OverridingMethodRule specifically need attribute AST support first (see the attribute-semantics cluster) — everything else in this cluster does not.

clusters.root_cause: checker/expr.rs's MethodCall/StaticCall arms do existence and arg-checking but never enforce caller-context-vs-declared-visibility at all — no is_private/is_protected gating exists anywhere for a call site (as opposed to declaration-site checks), and related call-context checks (non-object receiver, method_exists()-narrowing, name-case mismatch, abstract-method-call, instance-method-called-statically, self/static/parent-outside-class-scope) are likewise entirely absent.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/expr.rs (MethodCall arm ~382-526, StaticCall arm ~923-1010), src/checker/resolve.rs (resolve_static_class_name), src/registry.rs (would need a visibility-lookup-against-caller-context helper)
clusters.notes: Requires threading 'what class is the calling code currently inside' through to every call site and comparing it against the target method's declared visibility plus declaring-class relationship (self/parent/unrelated) — a genuinely new capability, not an extension of existing logic, since visibility is currently tracked but never consulted at call sites. High value: calling a private/protected method from the wrong scope is one of the most common PHPStan catches in real codebases. CallPrivateMethodThroughStaticRule's static::-reaches-a-private-method-unsafely case is a natural extra check once the visibility-lookup plumbing exists.

clusters.cluster_name: Statement-level 'no side effect' / dead call-statement detection
clusters.root_cause: phpstan-rs has no NoopExpressionNode-equivalent concept at all — no pass ever asks whether a bare expression-statement (a standalone `new Foo();`, `$obj->method();`, or `Foo::bar();`) actually has an observable effect worth keeping.

Building it once (a shared 'is this call statement possibly-side-effect-free' helper) covers all three call kinds. Real-world value: this is a genuine common PHPStan level-4 catch (e.g. forgetting `$x = ` before a getter call, or a leftover debug call).

clusters.cluster_name: Attribute semantics for methods (#[NoDiscard]/#[Override]/general attribute validation)
clusters.root_cause: The lexer skips essentially every #[...] attribute wholesale as an unstructured token span (src/lexer.rs) — there is no attrGroups AST representation, no attribute-class reflection, and no way to read an attribute's target or constructor arguments, so nothing that depends on attribute semantics (as opposed to just tolerating the syntax) can be built.

clusters.notes: This is a structural/architectural change — new AST node kinds for attribute groups, attribute-class existence/target/constructor-arg checking, and (for the NoDiscard pair specifically) a stub-based must-use-return-value annotation system layered on top. It is a hard prerequisite for any attribute-driven check, present or future, so its value is broader than just these 3 items suggest, but PHP 8.1+ attribute usage (especially #[Override], #[NoDiscard]) is still growing rather than universal in real codebases today — hence medium rather than high.

clusters.root_cause: phpstan-rs's checker is oriented entirely around correctness bugs (unknown symbols, arg/return mismatches); it has no MissingTypehintCheck-equivalent battery at all — no detection of implicit-mixed parameters/returns, iterable-missing-value-type, non-generic use of a generic class, or callable-with-no-signature.
clusters.rust_location: would need a new module, e.g. src/checker/missing_typehint.rs, invoked from both parameter and return-type checking paths in oop.rs/stmt.rs

High real-world value despite the size: PHPStan level 6 ('require types everywhere') is a common target for serious PHPStan users, and implicit-mixed / missing-generics are two of its most-hit diagnostics. MissingMethodSelfOutTypeRule is the same battery applied to @phpstan-self-out types, but self-out itself isn't modeled at all yet, so it stays out of this cluster as a further-blocked not_applicable item rather than a third 'unlocks' entry.

clusters.root_cause: phpstan-rs is architecturally a single-pass per-file/per-project checker with no equivalent of PHPStan's Collector mechanism (emit-then-aggregate-after-all-files-analyzed data flow) — the two Collector marker classes and the Rule that consumes them all depend on that missing multi-pass architecture, not on any narrower missing feature.

Not worth building the general Collector infrastructure for this alone — only worth doing if some higher-value future rule also needs cross-file aggregation.

clusters.root_cause: The MethodCall arm already computes and uses the nullsafe flag to shape the resulting type (nulling it on the nullsafe branch), but never checks the inverse direction — whether the receiver's statically-known type could be null at all — so a redundant `$x?->method()` on a never-null $x is never flagged.

Genuinely common in real code (defensive `?->` used out of habit after a variable's nullability was already narrowed away).

The PHP-version-gated union-types-pre-8.0 and @template-not-referenced-in-param sub-checks stay out of scope since phpstan-rs doesn't model target-PHP-version gating at all.

clusters.root_cause: No comparison exists anywhere between a parameter's default value and its declared type — default values are only ever used to infer a call-site variable's type when the argument is omitted, never validated against the parameter's own declared type.

clusters.root_cause: phpstan-rs has no model of PHP's built-in Serializable interface (or built-in interfaces generally) at all — there is no registry entry, version-gating, or magic-method-presence check tied to implementing it.

Serializable itself is legacy and discouraged in modern PHP (superseded by __serialize/__unserialize being checked independently of the interface), so real-world impact is low.

clusters.root_cause: phpstan-rs has zero notion of @phpstan-pure/@phpstan-impure/@phpstan-pure-unless-callable-is-impure PHPDoc annotations, and no impure-point or side-effect classification of calls exists anywhere in calls.rs/control_flow.rs for such a check to consume.

clusters.root_cause: phpstan-rs has zero attribute syntax support: no AttributeGroup/Attribute node type in src/ast.rs, no parser handling in src/parser/*.rs, and no AttributesCheck-equivalent target-validation logic anywhere.
