bright_spots: FoundPropertyReflection (implemented): a clean architectural consolidation - phpstan-rs achieves PHPStan's decorator-object pattern (distinct readable vs writable property type) directly as PropertySig struct fields (ty/set_ty) rather than a wrapper reflection class, which is an appropriate simplification given the project's data-model style, not a corner cut.

WritingToReadOnlyPropertiesRule (implemented): correctly catches the single most common real-world readonly violation (writing outside the declaring constructor), including the promoted-constructor-parameter exemption - solid coverage of the 80% case despite missing asymmetric-visibility edge cases.

The undefined-property/undefined-static-property detection underlying AccessPropertiesCheck and AccessStaticPropertiesCheck is genuinely implemented with sensible carve-outs (stdClass, declared __get(), a Pest beforeEach() special case) - this is arguably the single highest-frequency real-world 'typo'd property name' catch, and it's present even though the surrounding visibility/property_exists()/asymmetric-visibility machinery is not.

SetPropertyHookParameterRule (partial): even though the dedicated hook-signature-validation diagnostics aren't emitted, the underlying data (the set-hook's declared parameter type) is captured as PropertySignature::set_ty and actively reused to type-check `$this->prop = ...` writes elsewhere in the class - the work wasn't wasted, it was repurposed for a different, real check.

MissingReadOnlyPropertyAssignRule / ReadOnlyPropertyAssignRule (partial): the blanket 'readonly written outside its own __construct' rule, while not full dataflow, is a pragmatic one-condition approximation that catches the overwhelming majority of real readonly misuse without needing the full PHPStan CFG machinery.
clusters_by_category.not_applicable_summary: 4 items were marked not_applicable, all for defensible structural reasons rather than gaps in the audit: EnumCaseOutsideEnumRule is structurally impossible in phpstan-rs's AST shape (EnumCase only ever exists as a field of EnumDecl.cases, never as a free-floating node in a class/trait body); PropertyAttributesRule and PropertyHookAttributesRule both depend entirely on PHP attribute syntax support, which is wholly unimplemented project-wide (tracked as the 'No PHP attribute parsing' cluster) rather than being properties-specific rule work; ReadWritePropertiesExtension is a third-party DI extension-point interface for PHPStan's plugin system, and phpstan-rs has no plugin/extension architecture at all, so there is no sensible direct analog. Data quality note: all 41 raw items carry specific, internally-consistent file:line references and distinct, substantive notes (no generic placeholder text or suspiciously uniform entries were observed), so this audit chunk reads as genuine research rather than fabricated/templated output.

InnerFunctionRule (1 item): PHPStan flags any named function statement declared inside another function's body as unsupported. phpstan-rs deliberately does the opposite - it recurses into and checks such declarations (explicit in-repo comment citing the common "if (!function_exists('foo')) { function foo() {} }" polyfill idiom). This is a documented, intentional broader-support design choice, not a gap to close; replicating PHPStan's restriction would be a regression.
bright_spots: Sanity check: 49/49 items received. Every item carries a specific phpstan_path, a concrete our_location (file:line) or explicit grep-negative evidence, and notes that read as real investigation output (specific function/struct names, line ranges, cited in-repo comments) rather than templated filler - no placeholder or invented-looking entries found.

ArrayFilterRule / ArrayValuesRule (partial): the hard part - precise return-type inference (falsy-element stripping, instanceof/null-check narrowing, list-ness preservation via AccessoryKind::ArrayList) - is already implemented and reuses the same list/iterable-at-least-once machinery PHPStan's own rule depends on. Only the cheap final step (emitting arrayFilter.empty/same/alwaysEmpty and arrayValues.empty/list diagnostics from data already computed) is missing.

CallToFunctionParametersRule (implemented): check_args is a real, broadly-exercised parameter-count/type checker covering required/optional/variadic params and named-argument reordering - the functional core of PHPStan's argument-checking machinery, not a stub.

ArrowFunctionReturnTypeRule / ClosureReturnTypeRule / ReturnTypeRule (all implemented): phpstan-rs unifies all three PHPStan rules into one generic return-type-check path (check_block/StmtKind::Return) shared across named functions, closures and arrow-fns, including a generator-aware carve-out (current_function_is_generator) mirroring PHPStan's own generator exemption. Message wording is generic rather than PHPStan's four distinct phrasings, but the semantic core is genuinely there and more broadly scoped than the three separate PHP rules.

FunctionCallableRule (partial): first-class-callable existence checking (foo(...), $obj->m(...), Class::m(...)) is already implemented and correctly skips argument-count checking for these nodes, matching PHPStan's own design intent for that node type.

PrintfParameterTypeRule / PrintfParametersRule / PrintfHelper (partial): a real, working format-specifier parser (parse_format_specifiers) and per-argument type-acceptance checker (format_specifier_accepts) already exist and are exercised for the common sprintf/printf case - this is a nontrivial feature, not a missing stub, even though positional/width/precision specifiers and other format functions aren't covered yet.

clusters.root_cause: PHP attribute syntax (#[...]) is discarded as lexer trivia and never becomes an AST node (no attrGroups field anywhere), so no AttributesCheck-equivalent can exist for any node kind.
clusters.rust_location: src/lexer.rs (~510-530, skip_stub_availability_attribute / skip_language_level_type_aware_attribute)
clusters.notes: Requires a new AST node kind, parser support for #[...] groups, threading attrGroups through every attributable node (functions, closures, arrow-fns, params, classes), and a new AttributesCheck subsystem (target-flag validation, attribute-class existence, arg-type checking). CallToFunctionStatementWithNoDiscardRule additionally needs PHP 8.5's #[NoDiscard] semantics on top. Real-world value is low: attribute misuse diagnostics mostly matter for DI/metaprogramming-heavy frameworks, rarely fire in typical business logic.

clusters.root_cause: resolve_type_hint resolves namespace/use-imports for a class name in a type hint but never checks that the resolved class actually exists anywhere in the codebase (no lookup/registry.classes.contains-style check outside of `new` instantiation).
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/resolve.rs:53-58 (resolve_type_hint); existing existence-check pattern to reuse is at src/checker/expr.rs:902 (new instantiation)
clusters.notes: All three PHPStan rules (arrow-fn, closure, named-function param/return typehints) share this exact gap and would share one fix: add a class-existence lookup alongside the existing name-resolution call, reusing the pattern already used for `new`. Typo'd/missing class names in signatures are a very common, high-value bug class. The never-type PHP-version gate and NoDiscard-misuse sub-checks these rules also perform are minor and separately blocked on the Attribute AST cluster.

clusters.root_cause: The AST field storing a parameter's default-value expression (param.default) is parsed and stored but never read by the checker anywhere.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker.rs:439 (check_function param handling); src/checker/expr.rs ~1267 (closure param handling) - a single shared check function would be called from both plus the arrow-fn path
clusters.notes: All three PHPStan rules run the identical default-vs-declared-type compatibility check for a different function-like shape; in phpstan-rs they'd naturally collapse into one shared helper invoked from the (currently separate) param-binding code paths for functions, closures and arrow-fns.

clusters.root_cause: No NullsafeCheck-equivalent scan of return expressions exists, and named function/method declarations carry no by-ref-return flag at all (only Closure's AST node tracks one, and even that is never consulted).
clusters.rust_location: src/ast.rs:129 (FunctionDecl, no by-ref flag) and :484 (Closure by_ref flag, unused); src/checker/expr.rs (ArrowFn arm) and would-be ReturnStatementsNode-equivalent for named functions
clusters.notes: Narrow edge case (returning a ?-> chain by reference) that is genuinely absent end-to-end, not just unwired. Low real-world frequency but cheap to add once a by-ref flag exists on FunctionDecl and a small nullsafe-detection helper is written.

clusters.root_cause: call_user_func()/call_user_func_array() are treated as ordinary unrecognized/generic-stub function calls; there is no logic that reorders the call's trailing arguments into the target callable's own parameter-acceptor and re-runs argument checking against it.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/calls.rs (would need a new special case alongside check_args), invoked from src/checker/expr.rs FuncCall arm
clusters.notes: call_user_func/_array remain common in older or callback-heavy PHP code; without forwarding, wrong-arg-count/type bugs at these call sites go entirely unchecked.

clusters.root_cause: FuncCall checking only builds a signature and runs check_args when the callee is a statically-known ExprKind::Name; there is no mechanism to derive a callable signature from an arbitrary expression's inferred type (e.g. a Closure held in a variable or returned by a method), so both plain-callable-ness validation and argument checking are skipped entirely for that call shape.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/expr.rs:75-270 (FuncCall arm's resolved_name/sig gating) and :1394 (FirstClassCallable arm's dynamic-callee branch)
clusters.notes: FunctionCallableRule is otherwise a bright spot (static callable existence checks work); this cluster only closes its remaining dynamic-callee gap plus all of CallCallablesRule. Needs the type system to expose a callable/Closure value's parameter signature in a form check_args can consume - may partially already exist via FunctionSig and just needs threading, or may need new Type-system support (treat as a possible out-of-category prerequisite).
prerequisite_clusters: closure/callable value type carrying a full parameter signature usable by check_args, if not already exposed by the type system

clusters.root_cause: The function registry stores declarations in a plain string-keyed HashMap; a second top-level declaration of the same name silently overwrites the first entry with no history retained.
clusters.rust_location: src/registry.rs:25 (functions: FxHashMap<String, FunctionSig>)
clusters.notes: Would need to switch to accumulating a Vec of declaration sites per name and diagnosing 2+. Real-world value is low: unconditional duplicate top-level function names are a PHP fatal error at runtime anyway, and phpstan-rs already intentionally supports the common function_exists()-guarded conditional-redeclaration idiom (see InnerFunctionRule, not_applicable), so the remaining catchable cases are narrow.

clusters.root_cause: filter_var() is not modeled as a special-cased function anywhere in the checker; no logic inspects its 3rd-argument flags type for the mutually-exclusive FILTER_NULL_ON_FAILURE / FILTER_THROW_ON_FAILURE combination.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/calls.rs (would need a new filter_var-specific match arm)
clusters.notes: Standalone, narrow builtin-specific check with a small, well-defined fix once undertaken.

clusters.root_cause: There is no shared ParameterCastableToStringCheck/ParameterCastableToNumberCheck-equivalent utility; check_args only performs whole-array is_assignable comparisons against a stub signature, never a per-element __toString/enum/numeric-coercion castability check.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/calls.rs (near check_args - needs one new shared per-element-castability helper wired into several builtin match arms)
clusters.notes: One shared helper would serve implode/join, array_sum/array_product, array_intersect*/array_diff*/array_combine/natsort family, and the SORT_STRING/SORT_NUMERIC-flagged sort functions. implode() called on a non-stringable array element is a genuinely common real-world PHP bug this would catch.

clusters.root_cause: The format-string subsystem (parse_format_specifiers/format_specifier_accepts/check_format_string_call) is a simplified subset of PHPStan's PrintfHelper/PrintfPlaceholder: it only recognizes ordered (non-positional) specifiers, has no width/precision '*' sub-placeholder tracking, no strict-vs-castable mode, no scanf-style placeholder counting, and is wired only for sprintf/printf (not vprintf/vsprintf/fprintf/sscanf/fscanf).
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/calls.rs:376 (check_format_string_call), :468 (parse_format_specifiers), :529 (format_specifier_accepts); call site at src/checker/expr.rs:250-251
clusters.notes: Single underlying subsystem that would need a substantial rewrite/extension: positional (%N$) specifier support, width/precision sub-placeholders, a strict/non-strict matching mode with numeric-string/decimal-int-string accessory-type awareness, scanf placeholder counting, and wiring for vprintf/vsprintf/fprintf/sscanf/fscanf plus exact-count (not just too-few) argument mismatches. High value: printf-family placeholder/argument mismatches are one of the most common real bug classes PHPStan catches, and the existing sprintf/printf coverage proves the approach already works for the core case.

clusters.root_cause: There is no Generator<K,V,TSend,TReturn> type shape in the type system at all, so yield/yield-from expressions are checked structurally (inner expression type-checked, iterable-ness for yield-from) but never compared against the enclosing function's declared return type, and yield-outside-a-function / wrong-return-type-with-yield are never diagnosed.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/expr.rs:656-680 (Yield/YieldFrom arms, both return Type::Mixed unconditionally); src/checker/control_flow.rs:151-163 (body_contains_yield, used only to skip the ordinary return check); src/types.rs (no Generator type shape)
clusters.notes: Needs a new generic Generator<K,V,TSend,TReturn> type representation plus wiring it into yield/yield-from key/value/TSend checking, the yield-only-in-a-function-with-compatible-return-type validation, and void-result-used checks. Generators are common in iterator-heavy PHP code; mismatches there are a real but less frequent bug source than plain function-call errors.

clusters.root_cause: phpstan-rs's checker has no notion of opt-in rule levels (0-10) at all, and no MissingTypehintCheck equivalent (implicit-mixed / missing-iterable-value-type / missing-generic-args / missing-callable-signature detection) exists anywhere.
clusters.rust_location: No existing location - would be new code; nearest anchor points are src/checker.rs:439 (function param typehints) and the function's declared return-type site
clusters.notes: Both rules share the exact same MissingTypehintCheck logic, just applied to params vs. return type. Implementing this well also implies introducing some notion of strictness level (or making it unconditional), which is a broader design decision than the check itself. Valuable for codebases running at PHPStan level 6+, but more a completeness/strictness nudge than a bug-catcher.

clusters.root_cause: Neither closure use-clauses nor parameter declarations are validated against reserved names ($this) or superglobal names; is_superglobal() exists in assignment.rs but is only consulted for read/narrowing purposes, never at declaration time.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/expr.rs ~1267-1290 (Closure use-clause binding); src/checker.rs:439 (function/closure/arrow-fn parameter binding); existing is_superglobal helper in src/checker/assignment.rs
clusters.notes: Both rules need the same missing ingredient - checking a declared name against $this/superglobals (plus, for use-clauses, against the closure's own parameter names) - and can reuse the existing is_superglobal helper. Real-world frequency of naming a parameter $_GET or capturing $this by use() is very low.

clusters.root_cause: No scan of a parameter list for a name reused later in the same list exists anywhere in the checker.
clusters.rust_location: Parameter list construction in src/checker.rs:439 / src/parser/functions.rs:55 - would need a new list-scan added at declaration-check time
clusters.notes: PHP itself raises a fatal error for a real duplicate parameter name at parse time, so this mostly adds earlier/friendlier diagnosis rather than catching a bug PHP would otherwise miss.

clusters.root_cause: The parser tracks a variadic flag per parameter and the checker uses it extensively for call-site arity checks, but nothing validates that a variadic parameter (if present) is the last one declared.
clusters.rust_location: src/parser/functions.rs:55 (variadic flag parsed); src/checker/calls.rs (arity checks consume it) - validation would be a new small check at function/closure/arrow-fn declaration time
clusters.notes: Like RedefinedParametersRule, this is also a PHP compile-time fatal ('Only the last parameter can be variadic'), so the diagnostic's marginal value is mostly earlier feedback rather than a bug PHP would silently allow.

clusters.root_cause: No unused-variable/parameter detection subsystem exists anywhere in the checker; closure use-clauses are parsed and bound into closure_locals but nothing tracks whether a captured variable is ever referenced in the body.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/expr.rs ~1267-1290 (Closure use-clause binding into closure_locals)
clusters.notes: Needs read-reference tracking within the closure body scoped to each use()'d variable. Stale/typo'd captured variables are a realistic, moderately common code-quality issue worth catching.

clusters.root_cause: phpstan-rs has no notion of a function being side-effect-free (no @phpstan-pure/hasSideEffects concept in the registry or docblock module), so a standalone pure-call statement whose result is discarded is never flagged.
clusters.rust_location: Function registry (src/registry.rs) would need a new purity attribute per signature, consulted from a new check at statement level
clusters.notes: Requires modeling purity across the whole builtin/stub signature set (a large annotation effort) plus a NoopExpressionNode-equivalent statement-level check. Mostly a level-4 strictness/code-smell nicety rather than a correctness bug-catcher.

clusters.root_cause: No handling of these three functions' second-argument 'return output instead of printing' flag, and no first-level-statement-vs-used-as-expression distinction exists for any function call.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/calls.rs (would need a new special case plus a statement-vs-expression-context signal threaded through call-checking)
clusters.notes: Narrow, single-purpose builtin-specific diagnostic.

clusters.root_cause: random_int() is not special-cased anywhere; no IntegerRangeType::isSmallerThan-style comparison exists between its two arguments.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/calls.rs (would need a new random_int-specific match arm)
clusters.notes: Small, self-contained check; a swapped min/max argument pair is a plausible, easy-to-make real bug and cheap to catch given the checker already has integer-range comparison machinery available elsewhere in the type system.

clusters.root_cause: The existing undefined-function check has no case-insensitive name-matching path (function.nameCase) and does not suppress its report when the call site is guarded by a function_exists() check.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/expr.rs:255-264 ('call to undefined function' report)
clusters.notes: Refines an already-implemented rule rather than closing a full gap. The function_exists()-guard suppression matters for false-positive avoidance in real code that conditionally polyfills functions; the case-sensitivity check itself is mostly cosmetic since PHP function calls are case-insensitive at runtime.

clusters.root_cause: define() is not special-cased anywhere; a 3rd ($case_insensitive) argument is only checked (if at all) against a generic stub signature, with no dedicated diagnostic for the fact PHP silently ignores it.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/calls.rs (would need a new define()-specific match arm)
clusters.notes: Narrow, legacy/rare edge case (case-insensitive constants were removed from modern PHP).

clusters.root_cause: The precise return-type inference for array_filter/array_values already exists (falsy-narrowing, list-ness tracking via AccessoryKind::ArrayList) but nothing emits a diagnostic from that already-computed information when the call turns out to be a no-op (already-list, all-truthy, empty input, or always-empty result).
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs:141-181 ("array_filter" arm) and :255-262 ("array_values" arm)
clusters.notes: Unusually cheap fix relative to its value: the type-precision machinery that would drive the diagnostic already exists and is exercised, so this is purely a matter of adding diagnostic-emission at two existing match arms. array_filter/array_values no-op calls are a genuinely common real-world PHP gotcha (e.g. calling array_values() on data that's already a list).

clusters_by_category.not_applicable_summary: All 34 raw items are genuinely in-scope (32 "missing", 2 "partial"); none are N/A/environment-specific and none needed exclusion. No placeholder or invented-looking entries were found — every item cites a concrete phpstan-rs file/function (docblock.rs's apply_tag switch, class_info.rs ~132-154, function_sig.rs, control_flow.rs's always_terminates(), stmt.rs:663-722, types.rs's parse_type_string) or a specific empty-grep result backing the "missing" claim, which reads as researched rather than templated. The only structurally thin entries are UnresolvableTypeResult (a data-holder with admittedly "no logic of its own") and PhpDocLineHelper (explicitly flagged by its own author as "low-impact precision gap, not a missing check") — both are legitimately minor, not padding.

clusters.root_cause: phpstan-rs has no @phpstan-ignore / @phpstan-ignore-next-line / @phpstan-ignore-line parsing, no per-line ignored-error attribute propagation, and no diagnostic-suppression pass anywhere — confirmed by empty greps for 'phpstan-ignore', 'ignore-next-line', and any IgnoredError-equivalent. This is a foundational, file-wide feature (not a docblock tag on a declaration) that the other 33 items' docblock.rs tag machinery cannot be extended to cover.
clusters.rust_location: No existing location — would be a new module (e.g. a suppression/ignore.rs) plus hooks into whatever emits/collects diagnostics per analyzed file.
clusters.notes: Only one item from this gap appears in the audit (the parse-error-on-malformed-ignore-expression rule), but the real cost is the whole suppression subsystem it depends on, which is out of scope for a single-file fix and would need its own phase. Real-world impact is high: ignore comments are ubiquitous in any codebase already running PHPStan, so without this, a head-to-head diagnostic comparison against real PHPStan will show large unexplained noise on any repo using them.
prerequisite_clusters: a @phpstan-ignore / ignore-comment parsing + per-line suppression subsystem (not itself one of these 34 items) is a phase-0 prerequisite before IgnoreParseErrorRule is even meaningful

clusters.cluster_name: Missing-return-statement check not wired to declared return type
clusters.root_cause: control_flow.rs's always_terminates() is used only to merge branch-local variable narrowing state; nothing compares a function/method/closure's fall-through-without-return status against its declared/PHPDoc return type (void/never/mixed exemptions, Generator TReturn via yield).
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/control_flow.rs (always_terminates helper) plus wherever function bodies finish checking, to compare against the signature's return type.
clusters.notes: The hard part (control-flow termination analysis) already exists and is reused for narrowing — this is 'wire an existing analysis into a new check' rather than build-from-scratch, plus Generator/yield-aware branches. Forgetting a return statement is a very common real bug, so this is disproportionately cheap-for-value.

clusters.root_cause: docblock.rs's apply_tag has no arm for 'assert'/'assert-if-true'/'assert-if-false', so the tags are neither parsed nor fed into narrowing.rs (whose only assert-shaped logic, apply_phpunit_assertion_narrowing, is an unrelated PHPUnit-runtime feature).
clusters.rust_location: src/docblock.rs (apply_tag match) for parsing; src/checker/narrowing.rs for consuming the parsed assertions.
clusters.notes: FunctionAssertRule/MethodAssertRule are thin dispatchers onto AssertRuleHelper, so this is really one piece of work (tag parsing + validation + narrowing integration) surfaced through two call sites. @phpstan-assert is widely used in modern PHP libraries for custom narrowing (e.g. validation helpers), making this high-value.

clusters.cluster_name: Conditional return types not represented in the type system
clusters.root_cause: docblock.rs deliberately skips conditional-return-type syntax ('($param is Foo ? Bar : Baz)') rather than parsing it, and types.rs has no ConditionalType/ConditionalTypeForParameter variant at all, so there is no subject to validate (template-ness, always-true/false condition) or type to compute from it.
clusters.rust_location: src/types.rs (Type enum needs a new ConditionalType variant); src/docblock.rs (the documented '($' skip-branch) needs a real parser for the is/?/: grammar.
clusters.notes: Confirmed as a deliberate, tested design choice (phpstan-rs has a test literally named 'a_real_phpstan_conditional_return_type_is_skipped_rather_than_parsed_into_garbage'), not an oversight. Used mainly in generic/collection-heavy libraries and PHPStan's own stubs; less common in typical application code than assert tags.

clusters.root_cause: src/types.rs's Callable/Closure representation carries no per-callable @template tags, so there is nothing to run TemplateTypeCheck against and no way to detect a callable-local template name shadowing an enclosing function's/class's own @template.
clusters.rust_location: src/types.rs (Callable/Closure type variants) and src/checker/generics.rs (check_generic_bounds is a narrower, unrelated feature — GenericObjectType arg bound-checking only).
clusters.notes: Genuinely a distinct root cause from the general 'PHPDoc wins silently' compatibility cluster below — this is about generics on callable/Closure types specifically, not signature-type mismatch. It is also a partial dependency of the PHPDoc-compatibility cluster (which calls it for template-shadowing checks), but implementing that cluster does not strictly require this piece. Real-code frequency of callable-local generics is low.

clusters.cluster_name: PHPDoc-vs-native type compatibility checking architecturally absent (PHPDoc silently wins)
clusters.root_cause: Both function_sig.rs (for @param/@return) and class_info.rs (for @var on properties and class constants) resolve a docblock type against a native type hint by unconditionally preferring the docblock type — documented as deliberate 'PHPDoc wins' behavior — with zero subtype-compatibility validation and no diagnostic when the two disagree. @param-out and @param-closure-this tags additionally aren't parsed at all.
clusters.rust_location: src/registry/function_sig.rs (param/return type merge) and src/registry/class_info.rs (~132-154, properties map; class constant type resolution).
clusters.notes: This is the single biggest cluster by unlock-count and arguably the highest real-world value in the whole category: PHPDoc/native type mismatches (typo'd @param types, stale @var after a signature change) are an extremely common real bug class that PHPStan is specifically prized for catching, and phpstan-rs currently masks every such mismatch by silently trusting the docblock. IncompatiblePropertyHookPhpDocTypeRule is notable because phpstan-rs *does* model PHP 8.4 property hooks structurally already (PropertySig::set_ty, property_hook_set_type()) — the hook plumbing exists, only the compatibility check on top of it is missing. Building the shared subtype-check-and-diagnose engine once and reusing it at both call sites is the efficient path; doing each site ad hoc would cost more.
prerequisite_clusters: Unresolvable/error-type tracking absent in Type enum (for precise unresolvable-type sub-diagnostics)

clusters.root_cause: Neither tag has a case in docblock.rs's tag switch, and no ImmediatelyInvokedCallable-style concept exists elsewhere (confirmed by empty greps).
clusters.rust_location: src/docblock.rs (apply_tag match).
clusters.notes: Self-contained: just tag parsing plus a 'is the native param type callable' check, no dependency on the larger PHPDoc-compatibility engine above. A relatively recent, niche PHPStan tag (higher-order-function purity annotations) with low real-code prevalence.

clusters.root_cause: No @phpstan-self-out (or @phpstan-this-out) parsing or representation exists anywhere in phpstan-rs (confirmed by empty greps across multiple spellings).
clusters.rust_location: src/docblock.rs (apply_tag match) plus method-checking code to validate the asserted self-out type is a subtype of the declaring class and reject it on static methods.
clusters.notes: Used for fluent/builder-style APIs that narrow $this's type on a method call (e.g. a generic collection's mutator methods) — a real but not extremely common pattern in application code.

clusters.cluster_name: No grammar-level PHPDoc parser — invalid tags/tag-values pass through silently
clusters.root_cause: docblock.rs is a lenient, best-effort line/regex-style tokenizer that either extracts a recognized tag or silently drops/leaves-unset anything it doesn't understand, unlike PHPStan's real phpdoc-parser grammar which produces an explicit InvalidTagValueNode (or reports an unknown '@phpstan-*' tag) that a rule can then flag.
clusters.rust_location: src/docblock.rs — the whole tokenizer/dispatch architecture, not a single function.
clusters.notes: This is an architectural rewrite (lenient tokenizer to real recoverable-error grammar parser), not a bugfix — every other docblock.rs-dependent cluster in this list would likely want to build on top of it rather than duplicate ad hoc error handling, so sequencing this early has compounding value even though its own two rules are only medium-value in isolation (mostly catches PHPDoc typos).

clusters.cluster_name: @var tag's own type never validated for referenced-class existence or missing generics
clusters.root_cause: inline_var_annotation() in stmt.rs extracts an @var type purely for local narrowing (falling back to Type::Mixed on anything odd) and never runs a class-existence/trait-invalidity/case-sensitivity/missing-generic-typehint pass over the type it parsed.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/stmt.rs (inline_var_annotation).
clusters.notes: Distinct from the 'inline @var applied unconditionally' cluster below: this one is about validating the *type itself* (does the referenced class exist, is it wrongly a trait, is casing right, are generics missing), not about matching the tag to the right variable or checking subtype compatibility with the expression.

clusters.root_cause: docblock.rs has no case for '@throws', and no throws-type concept exists anywhere in the checker or registry (confirmed by empty greps), so there is nothing to validate as a subtype of Throwable.
clusters.rust_location: src/docblock.rs (apply_tag match); would also need storage on the function/method signature and a Throwable-subtype check.
clusters.notes: Self-contained (parse tag → resolve type → check subtype of Throwable, with interface require-extends/intersection handling as a stretch goal). @throws is widely used for documenting exception contracts in real PHP code, so even this single check catches a common typo class (wrong or non-existent exception class name).

clusters.root_cause: docblock.rs's tag_lines groups tag text but never records each tag's own source-line offset, so every phpdoc-related diagnostic in phpstan-rs reports at the enclosing statement/node's line — the fallback branch of PHPStan's PhpDocLineHelper is implicitly always taken, its precise bleeding-edge branch never.
clusters.rust_location: src/docblock.rs (tag_lines, ~line 89-126).
clusters.notes: Pure diagnostic-precision gap (wrong line number, not a missed/false diagnostic) — the audit's own notes call this out as 'low-impact precision gap, not a missing check.' Cheap to fix once real per-tag line tracking is wanted, but low leverage.

clusters.root_cause: docblock.rs's apply_tag has no arm for any of these three tags, so none of their referenced-class validation (duplicates, non-object types, unknown classes, wrong-kind targets, final-class conflicts, case-sensitivity) has any data to run against.
clusters.rust_location: src/docblock.rs (apply_tag match) for parsing all three tags; class/trait-checking code for the per-tag placement and target-kind rules.
clusters.notes: Three separate tags but mechanically near-identical work (parse a list of class names off a tag, validate each exists/is the right kind, delegate to a shared case-sensitivity check, then a thin placement rule per class/trait target) — bundled as one cluster because the fix is one cohesive docblock.rs + class-checking patch rather than three independent efforts. Real-world usage is concentrated in library/framework authoring (constraining trait/interface consumers), so it's lower frequency in typical application codebases than the compatibility or assert clusters above.

clusters.cluster_name: Unresolvable/error-type tracking absent in Type enum
clusters.root_cause: src/types.rs's Type enum has no ErrorType or implicit-NeverType-style unresolvable marker; failed type resolution presumably falls back silently to Mixed instead of being tracked as an explicit error state that downstream rules can detect and suppress cascading diagnostics from.
clusters.rust_location: src/types.rs (Type enum) plus every resolution call site that currently falls back to Mixed on failure.
clusters.notes: UnresolvableTypeResult is a pure data holder with no logic of its own — it exists purely to carry UnresolvableTypeHelper's output, so the real work is entirely in adding the ErrorType concept and threading it through resolution. This is infrastructural: its direct value is modest (better diagnostic text / avoided cascades), but it is a soft prerequisite for several 'unresolvable-type' sub-checks referenced inside the PHPDoc-compatibility cluster and InvalidPhpDocVarTagTypeRule.

clusters.cluster_name: Inline @var application has zero validation (name-matching or type-compatibility)
clusters.root_cause: inline_var_annotation() in stmt.rs applies an inline `/** @var Type $name */` tag's type to the local-variable map unconditionally: no check that the tag's variable name matches the actual assignment/foreach/static/global target, no check that the tag's type is a valid supertype of the expression's real type, and no support for list()/array-destructuring targets — it silently no-ops rather than diagnosing any of these instead of erroring.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/stmt.rs:663-722 (inline_var_annotation).
clusters.notes: Bright spot: the narrowing side-effect itself (recognizing and applying a well-formed inline @var) already works for the simple assignment case — this is a genuinely partial, not absent, feature; the gap is entirely on the validation/error-reporting side. High real-world value: a stray or wrong inline @var (wrong variable name, or a type that's not actually compatible) is a classic footgun that PHPStan specifically catches and phpstan-rs currently would just apply blindly, potentially hiding real bugs behind a bad annotation.

clusters.root_cause: types.rs's native type parser builds Type::Union(...) containing mixed/never/void members or as the base of a nullable type with no validation step — this is a PHP-syntax-level illegality (not resolvable, not a PHPDoc concern) that the parser currently accepts silently.
clusters.rust_location: src/types.rs (parse_type_string).
clusters.notes: Cheapest item in the whole category to implement — a single validation pass over already-parsed native union/nullable types, no new parsing or subsystem needed. Catches genuinely malformed source/stub code (a real PHP fatal-error-adjacent mistake), independent of any PHPDoc machinery.

bright_spots: Inline @var narrowing (src/checker/stmt.rs inline_var_annotation, ~663-699) already recognizes and applies a well-formed `/** @var Type $name */` on a simple assignment statement for local-variable type narrowing — the core mechanism PHPStan calls 'changed expression type' works; only its validation/error-reporting half (VarTagTypeRuleHelper, WrongVariableNameInVarTagRule) is missing.

PHP 8.4 property hooks are modeled structurally (PropertySig::set_ty, property_hook_set_type() in src/registry/class_info.rs) even though the PHPDoc-compatibility check on top of them (IncompatiblePropertyHookPhpDocTypeRule) isn't — the harder plumbing is already there.

control_flow.rs's always_terminates() is a solid, already-tested branch-termination analysis (used today for if/switch/try narrowing merges) that MissingReturnRule could largely be built on top of rather than from scratch.

docblock.rs's deliberate, tested refusal to mis-parse conditional-return-type syntax into garbage (rather than silently producing a wrong type) is a genuinely disciplined design choice, not an oversight — it correctly prioritizes not-producing-false-data over feature completeness.

General @param/@return/@var/@property/@template docblock tag parsing is solid enough that the gaps found are consistently about validation/compatibility logic layered on top, or about specific less-common tags (@throws, @phpstan-assert, @phpstan-self-out, require-extends/implements, sealed) — not about the core tag-parsing plumbing itself being broken.

clusters_by_category.not_applicable_summary: 104 items received, verified against the pasted array (no truncation, no duplicate names) — count matches. Data quality looks genuine, not placeholder: every note cites specific file/line locations, grep results, or quoted comments from the actual phpstan-rs source, and the level of specificity varies naturally by file (trivial DI classes get one-line dismissals, 2000-line files like ObjectType/IntersectionType/TypeCombinator get multi-clause breakdowns). Of the 104: 7 implemented, 28 not_applicable, 38 missing, 31 partial. The 28 not_applicable items split into three honest categories: (1) pure DI/wiring classes with zero logic (DirectTypeAliasResolverProvider, LazyTypeAliasResolverProvider, TypeAliasResolverProvider, TypeCombinatorCache, ClassNameToObjectTypeResult); (2) third-party-only plugin extension interfaces with zero core phpstan-src implementers, confirmed by grep (MethodParameterClosureThisExtension, MethodParameterClosureTypeExtension, MethodParameterOutTypeExtension, MethodTypeSpecifyingExtension, OperatorTypeSpecifyingExtension(+Registry), StaticMethodParameterClosureThisExtension, StaticMethodParameterClosureTypeExtension, StaticMethodParameterOutTypeExtension, StaticMethodTypeSpecifyingExtension, UnaryOperatorTypeSpecifyingExtension(+Registry), FunctionParameterClosureThisExtension, ExpressionTypeResolverExtension, InstanceofDeprecated); (3) trivial classes that only exist to support an already-unimplemented feature, so building them standalone is meaningless (CircularTypeAliasDefinitionException/ErrorType depend on the missing @phpstan-type alias system; ObjectShapePropertyReflection depends on the missing ObjectShapeType). None of these 28 hide a real behavioral gap on their own — where the underlying feature they serve IS a real gap (type aliases, ObjectShapeType), that gap is captured as its own cluster below rather than under these wrapper files. TypeWithClassName and TypeTraverserCallable are also not_applicable for a structural reason: phpstan-rs's flat Type enum with String fields and native Rust closures already gets this interface's benefit for free.
bright_spots: DynamicFunctionReturnTypeExtension rated 'implemented': builtin_calls.rs's 1057-line compiled match (array_map/filter, str_replace, version_compare, array_search, preg_* via preg_shapes.rs, etc.) is functionally equivalent to real PHPStan's plugin-registry breadth for the function-call side — just a compiled table instead of a DI-registered extension list.

FunctionTypeSpecifyingExtension rated 'implemented': the ~24-extension roster PHPStan ships for condition-narrowing (is_array/is_string/in_array/array_key_exists/etc.) is hardcoded in narrowing.rs and covers the highest-traffic real-world cases.

ClassStringType: phpstan-rs's ClassString(Box<Type>) unifies PHPStan's own split ClassStringType/GenericClassStringType hierarchy into one variant that always carries an inner type — arguably a genuine simplification win, not just parity.

StringType's four accessory refinements (non-empty-string, non-falsy-string, literal-string, numeric-string) are deliberately modeled as Intersection([String, Accessory]), structurally mirroring PHPStan's own IntersectionType([StringType, AccessoryXType]) shape rather than inventing an ad hoc representation — a faithful architectural choice that pays off in IntersectionType's subtyping/describe logic already handling it correctly.

CompoundType and JustNullableTypeTrait correctly identified as not_applicable rather than missing: the double-dispatch/trait-sharing behavior they exist to coordinate is already present, just collapsed into single recursive match functions over one enum instead of spread across an OOP class hierarchy — real architectural insight in the audit, not a gap being waved away.

ParserNodeTypeToPHPStanType rated 'implemented' despite an entirely different AST shape (reconstructed string vs retained node tree) because every native keyword, nullable/union/intersection syntax, and self/parent/static resolution rule is verified to map identically.

The single most valuable real-world instance of DynamicStaticMethodReturnTypeExtension (Closure::bind's $this-rebinding) is directly and correctly hardcoded, and FloatType/VoidType are fully correct on their load-bearing semantics.

clusters.root_cause: Type-relationship checks (is_subtype/is_assignable) return a plain bool with no Yes/No/Maybe tri-state and no accumulated human-readable 'why' reasons; PHPStan's whole accepts()/isSuperTypeOf() double-dispatch protocol is built around AcceptsResult/IsSuperTypeOfResult/TypeResult objects that thread reasons through every comparison.
clusters.rust_location: src/types.rs fn is_subtype (~line 779); src/registry.rs is_assignable
clusters.notes: Foundational architectural change — every call site of is_subtype/is_assignable across the checker would need updating. Improves diagnostic explanation quality (why a type mismatched) more than it catches new bugs, since 'maybe' already collapses to a concrete true/false somewhere in the match arms today.

clusters.root_cause: docblock.rs never parses @phpstan-type/@phpstan-import-type tags at all; registry.rs (~line 871) explicitly treats an unresolved alias name leniently (always-compatible) instead of resolving it to its declared type.
clusters.rust_location: src/docblock.rs (tag parsing); src/registry.rs (~line 871 leniency codepath)
clusters.notes: Real gap for codebases that use @phpstan-type for readability (common in larger/older PHP projects). Needs alias parsing, a per-file/per-class alias table, recursion guard, and resolution wired into the docblock type resolver.

clusters.root_cause: docblock.rs is a stateless per-comment tag parser with zero namespace/use/class/trait context threading, and there is no content-hash-keyed caching layer; NameContext separately resolves namespace+use for a whole file but not per-docblock-location, and has no trait-template-inheritance propagation.
clusters.rust_location: src/docblock.rs; src/registry/name_context.rs
clusters.notes: Mostly an internal-architecture/performance concern (incremental-analysis-grade caching) that a from-scratch batch checker doesn't currently need; the one real behavioral loss is trait @template inheritance not propagating across trait-use boundaries.

clusters.root_cause: Type::Callable is a bare marker with no parameter list, return type, purity, or template map, and every closure-literal expression infers the flat Object("Closure", []) marker, discarding the closure's own PHPDoc/inferred signature entirely.
clusters.rust_location: src/types.rs Type::Callable (line 48); src/checker/expr.rs closure-literal sites (~lines 1342, 1379, 1470, 1509)
clusters.notes: Blocks checking a callable/Closure-typed value's signature against a declared callable(...):T contract, template inference through callable params, and general assertion-callable narrowing (only hardcoded per-function-name narrowing exists instead).

clusters.cluster_name: Closure-argument parameter-type inference from call context
clusters.root_cause: No mechanism infers a closure's own parameter types from the specific higher-order function it's passed to (array_map's element type, usort's two-element type, etc.) — grep of calls.rs/expr.rs confirms no such inference exists.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/calls.rs / src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs
clusters.notes: array_map/array_filter/usort/array_walk/preg_replace_callback with closures are extremely common; an untyped or loosely-typed closure param passed to them is never checked against the real element type. Does not strictly require the full ClosureType structural rework above — could be done as targeted special-casing similar to the existing preg_match by-ref handling.

clusters.cluster_name: Dynamic method/static-method return-type coverage is thin and unindexed
clusters.root_cause: Method-call return-type inference is a handful of ad hoc method-name matches scattered in expr.rs, not indexed by class hierarchy and covering only a few cases (Closure::bindTo, one "getResult" special case), versus PHPStan's dozens of core per-class extensions (PDOStatement, ReflectionClass, DateTime, ArrayObject, etc.).
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/expr.rs (scattered method-name matches, ~lines 384-420, 923-958, 2759)
clusters.notes: The function-call side (builtin_calls.rs) is already strong; this cluster is specifically the much-thinner method-call side. DateTime::modify, PDOStatement::fetch mode-dependent types, and ReflectionClass narrowing are common in real code and currently unmodeled.

clusters.root_cause: No @throws or throw-type inference system exists anywhere in the codebase — grep for throw_type/ThrowType across src/ returns nothing — so there is no dead-catch or uncaught-exception analysis for any extension point to feed.
clusters.rust_location: n/a — no such subsystem exists to extend
clusters.notes: This is a prerequisite for any future dead-catch/uncaught-exception Rules-category work, not just a core-types gap — the type data (what does this call throw) has to exist before those rules can be built at all.

clusters.cluster_name: ArrayType has no independent key type / uniform mutation API
clusters.root_cause: Type::Array(Box<Type>) carries only a single value type with no separate key type (real array<K,V> two-parameter form is unmodeled, keys implicitly int|string); array-mutation helpers (setOffsetValueType, spliceArray, changeKeyCaseArray, intersectKeyArray, truncateListToSize, etc.) are narrow ad hoc functions scattered across checker/calls.rs and checker/expr.rs rather than a uniform Type-level API.
clusters.rust_location: src/types.rs Type::Array (line 26), Type::ArrayShape (line 36); src/checker/calls.rs array builtin handling
clusters.notes: Changing Array's representation to carry an explicit key type is a structural change touching every array-construction and array-subtyping call site, but array<K,V> key-type checking is a common real-world pattern (e.g. array<string,int> iteration).

clusters.cluster_name: No general per-Type coercion/cast method surface
clusters.root_cause: The Type enum implements only subtyping, template-substitution, and Display — none of PHPStan's ~25 to*() coercion methods (toInteger, toFloat, toString, toArray, toCoercedArgumentType, toBitwiseNotType, toAbsoluteNumber, toArrayKey, generalize, getFiniteTypes) exist as general Type operations; every conversion is done ad hoc per call site in checker/expr.rs instead of centrally on the type.
clusters.rust_location: src/types.rs (Type enum + impl block, ~after line 779)
clusters.notes: This is the single most-cited systemic gap in the raw notes — nearly every scalar Type's 'partial' status traces back to this one missing method surface. 'Type' itself is the umbrella item explicitly describing this as its core deficiency versus PHPStan's ~150-method interface. Affects precision of weak-typing argument-coercion diagnostics and loose-comparison folding.

clusters.root_cause: is_subtype/is_assignable have no case for an object with a native __toString() method satisfying a string-typed sink in either strict or weak mode — grep for __toString/Stringable in checker/*.rs finds nothing.
clusters.rust_location: src/types.rs is_subtype; src/checker/calls.rs argument-compatibility checks
clusters.notes: Passing a Stringable object where a string is expected is neither specially accepted nor flagged today — a genuine silent gap for any Stringable-implementing class.

clusters.root_cause: int<min,max> ranges are represented and used for positive-int/negative-int parsing and basic min/max subtyping, but shift(), range-preserving exponentiate, toAbsoluteNumber/toBitwiseNotType bound-preservation, comparison-to-range-edge logic, and getFiniteTypes() enumeration are all absent — checker/expr.rs collapses IntRange to plain Int for several operations.
clusters.rust_location: src/types.rs Type::IntRange (line 68); src/checker/expr.rs (~line 2689, IntRange-to-Int collapse)
clusters.notes: Affects precision of positive-int-style narrowing surviving arithmetic — e.g. a positive-int shifted or exponentiated loses its range and widens to plain int.

clusters.cluster_name: IntersectionType lacks general object&object / callable&array delegation
clusters.root_cause: Intersection is correctly used for the accessory-type idiom (non-empty-string, list<T>, non-empty-array<T>, numeric-string) but has no general interface&interface object-intersection support and none of the array-operation delegators (popArray/shiftArray/sliceArray/getCallableParametersAcceptors) that combine arbitrary intersected member types.
clusters.rust_location: src/types.rs Type::Intersection (line 62), is_subtype (~lines 856-860)
clusters.notes: The highest-value real-world use (accessory string/array refinements) is already solid; the gap is the more exotic interface&interface and callable&array intersection forms.

clusters.cluster_name: SubtractableType / negative-instanceof narrowing on non-union types absent
clusters.root_cause: narrow_type_excluding only removes a union member when it is exactly equal to the excluded type; there is no 'T minus U' representation for a non-union Object/Mixed type, so a wider-typed value narrowed by `!$x instanceof Foo` where Foo is merely a possible subtype is left completely unchanged instead of becoming 'T minus Foo'.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/narrowing.rs:1068 narrow_type_excluding; src/types.rs (would need a new subtracted-type representation)
clusters.notes: Negative-instanceof narrowing (`if (!$x instanceof Foo)`) is extremely common; the current gap is a real source of missed narrowing on non-union object/mixed values. ObjectType and StaticType/ThisType also lose precision from this same missing mechanism but have enough additional distinct gaps to warrant their own clusters below.

clusters.cluster_name: static/$this late-binding is a bare marker with no class binding
clusters.root_cause: Type::StaticRef (and the '$this' PHPDoc keyword, which is deliberately conflated into the same variant per an explicit code comment) carries no attached ClassReflection, no generic-argument binding, and no distinction between static's self-or-wider semantics and $this's exact-instance semantics.
clusters.rust_location: src/types.rs Type::StaticRef; src/checker/resolve.rs resolve_self_static (~lines 30-94); src/checker/oop.rs (~315-320)
clusters.notes: resolve_self_static collapses SelfRef/StaticRef to a plain Object(defining_class) at first use, losing late-static-binding precision across subclass calls, plus no final-class `$this::class` literal narrowing.

clusters.root_cause: Type::Never is a bare unit variant with no isExplicit flag or human-readable reason string, so a user-written `never` return type can't be distinguished from PHPStan-inferred dead code, and template-binding edge cases against an explicit `never` aren't reproduced.
clusters.rust_location: src/types.rs Type::Never variant definition
clusters.notes: Mostly a diagnostic-quality gap (no 'why is this never' explanation for dead-code rules) plus a rare template-inference edge case.

clusters.root_cause: Type::Mixed is a single undifferentiated variant with no implicit-vs-explicit distinction, and phpstan-rs has no rule-level (PHPStan level 9+) system at all for this to plug into.
clusters.rust_location: n/a — no rule-level infrastructure exists
clusters.notes: Not just a Type gap — needs a rule-level enforcement system first, which doesn't exist in this project's architecture at all.
prerequisite_clusters: PHPStan rule-level (level 9+) system — out-of-category prerequisite, not present anywhere in phpstan-rs

clusters.root_cause: Grep of checker/*.rs for 'ArrayAccess' finds zero hits — offsetGet/offsetSet/offsetExists/offsetUnset on a class implementing ArrayAccess is never specially checked, and there's no ArrayAccess-aware offset-accessible union type builder (used for $argv/$argc-style precise typing too).
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/expr.rs (index-access expression handling); src/checker/assignment.rs ($argv/$argc typing, lines 361-384)
clusters.notes: ArrayAccess-implementing classes (ORMs, collection libraries) get no offset-type-checking today. Also explains why $argv/$argc are typed as plain Array(Mixed)/Int rather than PHPStan's precise non-empty-list<string>/int<1,max>.

clusters.root_cause: Type::Object(String, Vec<Type>) is a flat 2-tuple carrying only a class name and generic args, with no room for auxiliary per-instance metadata: no enum-case tag (enum instances are plain Objects), no allowedSubTypes/sealed-hierarchy support, and no GMP/SimpleXMLElement/BcMath\Number-specific numeric-coercion special-casing.
clusters.rust_location: src/types.rs Type::Object(String, Vec<Type>)
clusters.notes: Core identity and class-hierarchy subtyping already work well (registry.rs/oop.rs); this cluster is specifically the remaining structural richness beyond hierarchy checks. Overlaps partially with the SubtractableType and ArrayAccess clusters above (ObjectType's subtractedType and ArrayAccess-offset gaps are counted there instead, to avoid double-billing the same fix).

clusters.cluster_name: ConstantScalarType has no unifying value accessor
clusters.root_cause: Literal values (IntLiteral/FloatLiteral/StringLiteral/True/False/Null) are first-class enum variants, but there is no shared isConstantValue()/getValue()/getConstantScalarTypes() accessor — every call site pattern-matches the individual variants directly.
clusters.rust_location: src/types.rs Type enum (literal variants)
clusters.notes: Pure code-quality/DRY gap, not a correctness gap — every call site already handles the individual variants correctly, just redundantly.

clusters.cluster_name: ConstantTypeHelper doesn't fold values into constant-array shapes
clusters.root_cause: Scalar literal-to-type conversion happens correctly at parse time from AST nodes, but there is no array-literal folding into a shaped constant-array type and no object/enum-instance value-to-type conversion path.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/expr.rs (~lines 1472-1490, Literal match)
clusters.notes: Most relevant for reflection-derived default values/attribute args reconstructing an array's shape from a literal value.
prerequisite_clusters: ArrayType has no independent key type / uniform mutation API

clusters.cluster_name: ExponentiateHelper: pow() has no precision machinery
clusters.root_cause: The `**` operator is folded into the exact same arm as Sub/Mul ('Float if either operand is Float, else Int'); no constant-literal pow() computation, no IntegerRangeType-aware exponentiation, no ErrorType gating for non-numeric-string operands, no exponent-0/1 special-casing.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/expr.rs lines 2399-2407 (BinOp arm)
clusters.notes: The coarse fallback shape already matches PHPStan's own worst-case fallback; only the precision refinements are missing, and `**` is a rare operator in most real-world code.

clusters.root_cause: Type::Union is a flat Vec<Type> compared via plain nested iteration (O(n*m)) instead of an identity-keyed hashmap for large finite-valued unions.
clusters.rust_location: src/types.rs lines 840-841 (is_subtype union member iteration)
clusters.notes: Pure performance optimization per PHPStan's own docstring — no correctness difference from the plain scan; only relevant if a corpus surfaces pathologically large string-literal-enum unions as a measured hotspot.

clusters.root_cause: There is no Type::generalize(precision) API; type widening across loop iterations/branches is instead handled ad hoc via union_types (simple branch-merge) and a narrower generalize_by_key_set array-shape helper, without PHPStan's 3-level precision control deciding how much literal detail survives generalization.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/expr.rs union_types (~line 2540), generalize_by_key_set (~line 2625)
clusters.notes: Affects how much precision survives when merging types across loop iterations/branches — a real source of over- or under-widening in loop-heavy code.

clusters.cluster_name: IterableType parsed eagerly instead of modeled as a dedicated type
clusters.root_cause: iterable<V>/iterable<K,V> is parsed directly into Union([Array(V), Traversable-like Object]) at parse time rather than as a dedicated type carrying its own key/value accessors, losing the isSuperTypeOfMixed explicit-vs-implicit distinction.
clusters.rust_location: src/types.rs lines 716-729 ("iterable" parsing)
clusters.notes: Covers the common accepts-a-value case reasonably well via existing Union subtyping; the loss is mostly in dedicated accessor ergonomics rather than correctness.

clusters.cluster_name: Conditional-type / late-resolvable PHPDoc syntax entirely unparsed
clusters.root_cause: docblock.rs deliberately does not parse conditional return types (`($subject is Target ? If : Else)`, documented at ~line 179) or PHPDoc pseudo-types like key-of<T>/value-of<T>/self::CONST-as-type; types.rs has no deferred-resolution (LateResolvableType-style) mechanism at all — template substitution is eager-only, and the existing try_parse_conditional_type (line 307) just unions both branches textually without evaluating the condition per call site.
clusters.rust_location: src/docblock.rs (~line 179); src/types.rs try_parse_conditional_type (line 307) and the Type enum (no late-resolution variant)
clusters.notes: The single biggest coherent missing subsystem in this category by item count. Conditional return types are a common pattern in real stubs and increasingly in user code for is_*()-style predicates; phpstan-rs sidesteps this only for its own hardcoded built-in functions, giving no coverage for user-authored or third-party-stub conditional-return functions.

clusters.root_cause: infer_binary's Eq/NotEq (and comparison) arms unconditionally return plain Type::Bool regardless of operand types — no constant-folding of `==`/`!=` between two literal operands into a known ConstantBooleanType, and no PHP-8-vs-earlier numeric-string comparison semantics.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/expr.rs lines 2362-2372 (BinOp::Eq)
clusters.notes: Blocks flagging/narrowing classic PHP loose-comparison footguns (e.g. `0 == 'foo'`) even when both operands are known literals at analysis time.

clusters.root_cause: `new` on a literal class name is handled correctly, but `new $className()` where $className is a variable (e.g. a class-string<T> parameter) falls straight through to the `_ => Type::Mixed` catch-all instead of resolving to T's object type.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/expr.rs ExprKind::New (~line 1609-1624)
clusters.notes: Common factory/container/DI code pattern (`new $className()` from a class-string parameter) currently loses all type information.

clusters.root_cause: When a class with no `extends` uses `parent`, resolve_pseudo leaves Type::ParentRef unresolved (falls through to ty.clone()) rather than substituting a dedicated 'denies all member access' sentinel; is_subtype separately treats bare ParentRef as assignable to/from any Object, so it doesn't crash but also doesn't flag the illegal usage.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/resolve.rs resolve_pseudo (Type::ParentRef arm, ~line 94)
clusters.notes: Rare edge case (using `parent::` in a class with no parent) that most real code never hits, since it's usually a fatal error PHP itself would catch.

clusters.root_cause: No `object{` token handling anywhere in docblock.rs, types.rs, or the parser — confirmed via grep — so a `@param object{id: int, name: string} $x` annotation is not recognized at all.
clusters.rust_location: src/docblock.rs
clusters.notes: Object shapes are a fairly common modern-PHPDoc pattern for ad hoc config/DTO-like structures; falls back to plain `object` or is silently dropped today.

clusters.cluster_name: RecursionGuard duplicated ad hoc instead of centralized
clusters.root_cause: No single RecursionGuard::run()-style utility exists; each recursive class-hierarchy/template-binding traversal in registry.rs and generics.rs carries its own local HashSet<String> cycle guard.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/generics.rs class_template_bindings_rec (~line 289); src/registry.rs (multiple HashSet guards, e.g. lines 479, 509, 562, 632, 663, 699)
clusters.notes: Functionally covers the same cyclic-hierarchy protection today; the risk is purely forward-looking — a newly-added recursive traversal could forget to add its own guard where a centralized utility would be opt-in-by-wrapping.

clusters.cluster_name: SimultaneousTypeTraverser: template binding has no general dispatch
clusters.root_cause: bind_template_param is a hardcoded, special-purpose parallel-tree-walk that only recurses through Array and ClassString wrappers, with no general dispatch table covering Union/Intersection members or a user generic class's own type arguments the way PHPStan's traverseSimultaneously() does per-Type-subclass.
clusters.rust_location: src/types.rs bind_template_param (line 939)
clusters.notes: Template inference through a union-typed or intersection-typed parameter, or through a user generic class's own type arguments, isn't reconciled today — a real gap for generics-heavy code beyond the simple Array<T>/class-string<T> cases.

clusters.cluster_name: TypeCombinator: no general intersect()/remove(), union_types is a small hand-rolled subset
clusters.root_cause: Intersection values are only ever constructed directly by the type parser for a small fixed set of known accessory shapes — there is no generic intersect()/remove() computed from two arbitrary types; union_types (the union() analog) has exact-equality/Mixed-absorption fast paths and a hard member-count cap falling back to Mixed, but is missing IntegerRangeType merging, ConstantArrayType tagged-union merging, oversized-array generalization, and SubtractableType-aware union/intersect.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/expr.rs union_types (line 2540); src/types.rs (no general intersect() combinator exists)
clusters.notes: Type normalization quality (union()/intersect()/remove()) is one of the most central, load-bearing pieces of any type-checker's engine — most of UnionType's remaining specific gaps (array-op delegation across members, FiniteTypeSet fast paths) trace back to this missing engine rather than to UnionType itself.
prerequisite_clusters: SubtractableType / negative-instanceof narrowing on non-union types absent
ArrayType has no independent key type / uniform mutation API

clusters.cluster_name: No generic recursive Type-tree traverse/map combinator
clusters.root_cause: No fn traverse/map exists over the Type enum — every place that needs to walk into Union/Intersection/Array children (is_subtype, substitute_template, union_types) hand-rolls its own recursive match instead of sharing one traversal abstraction, which is also why BenevolentUnionType's identity-preserving re-wrap-through-transform behavior has no home to live in.

clusters_by_category.not_applicable_summary: 4 items (TemplateStrictMixedType, TemplateTypeArgumentStrategy, TemplateTypeParameterStrategy, TypeProjectionHelper) are correctly marked not_applicable: each depends on PHPStan machinery phpstan-rs doesn't have at all and wouldn't sensibly be bolted on in isolation - a bleeding-edge StrictMixedType distinction, the dual AcceptsResult/CompoundType argument-vs-parameter accepts() strategy pattern, and per-argument variance/wildcard annotation syntax (Collection<covariant T>) that isn't parsed anywhere in the docblock/type parser. Data quality check: all 60 items have specific, differentiated descriptions and file:line-grounded notes (verified AccessoryKind enum at src/types.rs:85-92 has exactly the 6 variants the notes claim and no Lowercase/Uppercase/DecimalIntegerString variants) - no placeholder or invented-looking entries found.
bright_spots: ConstantIntegerType is genuinely 'implemented', not just partial: IntLiteral(i64) has real subtype integration against Type::IntRange (types.rs:799-802), the actual PHPStan-equivalent of IntegerRangeType-aware isSuperTypeOf.

The list-type representation (AccessoryArrayListType) is architecturally faithful, not a shortcut: `list`/`non-empty-list` are modeled as Type::Intersection([Array, Accessory(ArrayList)]) - exactly PHPStan's own internal representation - rather than a flattened synthetic variant.

NonEmptyArrayType is produced through the same real-world idioms PHPStan relies on (!empty()/count()>0/!==[] narrowing in upgrade_array_to_non_empty), so the common case actually works even though the ~dozen array-operation-specific overrides don't.

TemplateMixedType's fallback role is genuinely reproduced: substitute_template's default-to-Mixed and class_template_bindings' unbound-leaves-Mixed both mirror this specific class's job as the safe fallback for an unbound @template, not just a coincidental default.

TemplateTypeScope's core anti-collision purpose is actually solved: substitute_class_templates' class_scope HashSet prevents exactly the same 'two unrelated classes' own same-named T collide' bug that TemplateTypeScope guards against in real PHPStan (the doc comments even cite the same symfony/type-info NullableType<T>/UnionType<T> case) - just via a HashSet instead of a value-object.

GenericObjectType's core representation is pervasive and load-bearing, not a stub: Object(name, type_args) plus check_generic_bounds and class_template_bindings form a real, working generic-object pipeline used throughout the checker, even though variance and cross-hierarchy ancestor resolution are simplified.
