bright_spots: RegexAlternation and RegexGroupList (status: implemented) — reimplemented with a flatter data shape (alternation id/branch-index tuples on each capture group, plus free functions over a slice instead of a dedicated Countable/IteratorAggregate collection) but produce the same tagged-union $matches shapes, confirmed against a live PHP interpreter per surrounding code comments.

FalseyBooleanTypeTrait (status: implemented) — consolidated into one direct filter function (narrow_type_excluding_falsy) rather than a per-type virtual method plus dispatcher, same net narrowing effect with less code.

RegexGroupParser's hand-rolled recursive-descent scanner (status: partial) covers a surprisingly complete subset given it replaces the Hoa\Compiler PCRE grammar entirely: capturing/named/non-capturing groups, alternation, bounded/unbounded quantifiers, POSIX classes, \Q...\E quoted blocks, and lookaround exclusion from literal contribution all work.

ObjectTypeTrait's practical member-resolution path (status: partial) is solid — routed directly through the class registry rather than PHPStan's dummy-reflection scaffolding, covering the everyday hasProperty/getProperty/hasMethod/getMethod cases that matter for most diagnostics.

MaybeObjectTypeTrait's ad hoc leniency (status: partial) achieves the same practical 'assume maybe, don't error' outcome as PHPStan's TrinaryLogic::Maybe for common cases, just via a `_ => Type::Mixed` fallthrough instead of a formal trinary API.
clusters_by_category.not_applicable_summary: 6 items marked not_applicable: ClassNameUsageLocationCreateIdentifierDynamicReturnTypeExtension exists solely for PHPStan's own dogfooding self-analysis of its own source and has no general PHP-analysis meaning to port. The other 5 (NonArrayTypeTrait, NonCallableTypeTrait, NonGeneralizableTypeTrait, NonGenericTypeTrait, NonRemoveableTypeTrait) are pure interface-boilerplate-avoidance stubs that exist only because PHPStan represents each type kind as its own class needing ~20 default no-op method implementations — phpstan-rs's single flat Type enum with match-based dispatch has no structural need for this pattern, so there's no file-shaped equivalent to build. One caveat worth flagging: NonGeneralizableTypeTrait's own notes concede that PHPStan's generalize() (loop-fixpoint type widening for control-flow stabilization) has no counterpart anywhere in phpstan-rs at all — that's a real, if narrow, capability gap hiding behind a not_applicable label because this specific trait-file is simply the wrong place to attach it; it may deserve its own investigation outside this category rather than being treated as fully closed.

Only a few items are genuinely not_applicable, all tied to one theme: PHPStan's technique of invoking a real PHP interpreter/stdlib object (DateInterval, DOMDocument, SimpleXMLElement) at analysis time to validate a literal string has no faithful Rust port, since phpstan-rs embeds no PHP runtime or XML parser (DateIntervalConstructorThrowTypeExtension, DateIntervalCreateFromDateStringThrowTypeExtension, SimpleXMLElementConstructorThrowTypeExtension). A second small group (ArrayCombineFunctionThrowTypeExtension, AssertThrowTypeExtension, VersionCompareFunctionDynamicThrowTypeExtension) is marked not_applicable only because phpstan-rs has zero throw-type subsystem to attach to; these would become ordinary 'missing' items once cluster 2 (throw-type subsystem) is built. ConstantHelper is pure plumbing for the missing ConstantFunctionReturnTypeExtension with no independent behavior, so it isn't counted as its own gap.
bright_spots: RegexArrayShapeMatcher has a substantial from-scratch reimplementation (src/regex_groups.rs + src/checker/expr/preg_shapes.rs) covering single-optional-group and single-alternation tagged unions, PREG_OFFSET_CAPTURE tuples, and PATTERN_ORDER/SET_ORDER/UNMATCHED_AS_NULL flags, verified against live PHP dumpType() per its own comments — far more capable than a bare 'partial' label suggests.

ArrayReduceFunctionReturnTypeExtension (builtin_calls.rs:193) is near-full parity via infer_closure_return_with_param_overrides, correctly binding $carry/$item and resolving the closure's return type.
ArrayReverseFunctionReturnTypeExtension and ArrayValuesFunctionDynamicReturnTypeExtension are effectively fully implemented and comment-verified via dumpType() against real PHPStan output.
PregMatchParameterOutTypeExtension (the $matches by-ref shape assignment) is fully implemented, reusing the same regex-shape engine that backs RegexArrayShapeMatcher.

Closure::bind/bindTo body-rechecking (check_closure_literal_with_this, expr.rs) solves the arguably more valuable half of those extensions — catching invalid property/method access under a rebound $this — even though the extensions' own return-type narrowing is unported.

ArrayMergeFunctionDynamicReturnTypeExtension has a real field-by-field ArrayShape merge (int-key renumbering, string-key overwrite, unsealed-slot union) that is comparable in care to the PHPStan original, not a token stub.

The in_array() strict-literal-array narrowing (Phase 33 Finding 2) and IsArrayFunctionTypeSpecifyingExtension parity, plus the round-18/19 Piwigo-corpus commits (array_column list-ness, version_compare 2-arg int, array_search on list haystacks), show the team is actively closing real-world-driven gaps incrementally rather than only chasing PHPStan's file list.

clusters.root_cause: Type::Array carries only an element type, no separate key type/shape, so any operation whose defining feature is transforming or restricting array KEYS (as opposed to values) cannot be represented precisely.
clusters.rust_location: src/types.rs Type::Array variant; consuming call sites in src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs
clusters.notes: array_flip/array_change_key_case/array_search key precision are common enough idioms that this is worth doing, but it's a real data-model change touching every array-constructing call site, not a single function.

clusters.root_cause: phpstan-rs has no DynamicFunctionThrowTypeExtension-equivalent and no per-call-site exception-type inference feeding an unhandled-exception rule at all.
clusters.rust_location: new module, e.g. src/checker/throws.rs, hooked from src/checker/calls.rs and src/checker/expr.rs
clusters.notes: Whole missing subsystem. json_encode's own JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR bit-detection already exists (reused for return-type false-stripping) so the hardest per-callee logic is partly there; the gap is the consumer pipeline (uncaught-exception checking) itself.

clusters.root_cause: Type enum has plain Int with no min/max range representation, so any extension whose entire value-add is narrowing to a bounded int range degrades to bare int.
clusters.rust_location: src/types.rs Type enum
clusters.notes: IntegerRangeType shows up constantly in real PHPStan output for lengths/counts/offsets; this is one of the highest-leverage structural gaps in the whole category since so many other clusters (dates, strlen, random) are blocked or degraded by it.

clusters.root_cause: AccessoryKind has NonEmptyString/NonFalsyString/LiteralString/NumericString but no case-tracking variants, so any function whose signature depends on preserving/asserting string case cannot be modeled even once the dispatch logic is written.
clusters.rust_location: src/types.rs AccessoryKind enum
clusters.notes: Existing NonEmptyString/NonFalsyString/NumericString infra already covers half of what these functions need; adding the two case variants plus wiring is a moderate, well-scoped batch.

clusters.cluster_name: array_diff/array_intersect family not generalized from array_unique
clusters.root_cause: builtin_calls.rs implements the 'return an ArrayType from arg 0' pattern only for array_unique; the other 15 functions sharing that exact pattern in PHPStan's FUNCTION_NAMES list were never extended to.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs (~line 265, array_unique arm)
clusters.notes: Single class covering 16 functions (array_diff*, array_udiff*, array_intersect*, array_uintersect*); a near copy-paste extension of an existing arm.

clusters.cluster_name: Array-pointer/position accessor functions get no empty-aware narrowing
clusters.root_cause: current/next/prev/reset/end/key/array_key_first/array_key_last/array_first/array_last all need the same 'false-or-null when empty, T|false when uncertain, bare T when non-empty' shape already used elsewhere (e.g. the array_pop pattern), but none of these six-plus functions have a match arm at all.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs
clusters.notes: Pattern is uniform and cheap to replicate across all these functions in one pass.

clusters.cluster_name: array_pop/array_shift's own return value is never computed
clusters.root_cause: calls.rs only updates the by-ref array argument's post-call type (list-ness/element type of what remains); no builtin_calls.rs arm computes the value the call expression itself evaluates to (the popped/shifted element, unioned with null).
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs (new arms), reusing element-type extraction already in src/checker/calls.rs:170
clusters.notes: Very common idiom ($x = array_pop($arr)); the by-ref side of this is already solved, only the expression's own type is missing.

clusters.root_cause: No match arms exist; array_replace could reuse the ArrayShape field-merge logic already built for array_merge (minus renumbering), and array_splice/array_pad could reuse the slice/element-union patterns already used elsewhere in the file.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs
clusters.notes: Straightforward extensions of already-existing sibling logic (array_merge, array_slice).

clusters.root_cause: These function names have zero registry/stub coverage at all (not even a generic signature), a stub-generation gap rather than a missing special case.
clusters.rust_location: src/registry.rs / stub generation (build.rs), src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs
clusters.notes: PHP 8.4-only; low frequency in most current corpora but will grow.

clusters.cluster_name: array_filter/array_find callback-narrowing helper covers only 2 syntactic shapes
clusters.root_cause: narrow_array_element_type_excluding_falsy recognizes only an explicit `=== null`/`!== null` check and an `instanceof` check; it has no general mechanism for re-evaluating an arbitrary boolean closure body via truthy/falsey scope-filtering, and no ARRAY_FILTER_USE_KEY/USE_BOTH mode handling.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs:141-185 (is_null_filter_callback, is_instanceof_filter_callback)
clusters.notes: array_filter is one of the most common higher-order array functions in real PHP; generalizing truthy-narrowing here would meaningfully reduce false positives on filtered-array element types.
prerequisite_clusters: No contextual parameter-type injection into closures passed to builtin higher-order functions

clusters.cluster_name: No contextual parameter-type injection into closures passed to builtin higher-order functions
clusters.root_cause: infer_closure_return_with_param_overrides binds override param types only to compute the OUTER call's own return type in a read-only pass; the closure BODY's own diagnostic-checking pass (ExprKind::Closure/ArrowFn, expr.rs ~1267/1344) always types untyped params as bare Mixed, so bugs inside array_map/array_filter/array_walk/preg_replace_callback callbacks (e.g. calling an undefined method on $item) are never caught.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/expr.rs (Closure/ArrowFn diagnostic arm ~1267/1344; infer_closure_return_with_param_overrides ~2151)
clusters.notes: This is a cross-cutting architectural gap, not a per-function one: fixing it once (plumbing a contextual param-type map into the closure-body check) would raise precision for every builtin that takes a callback, and is a real source of missed bugs today.

clusters.root_cause: Static-call return-type inference has only one ad hoc special case (Closure::bind's body-recheck); there is no general mechanism for callee-specific static-method return-type logic, so Closure::fromCallable/getCurrent, DatePeriod's constructor-arg-driven generics, and PDO::connect's driver-prefix dispatch all fall back to the generic stub.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/expr.rs ExprKind::StaticCall handling (~line 946)
clusters.notes: Closure::bind/bindTo already have the more valuable body-recheck half; this cluster is specifically about the return-type-of-the-call-itself half, which is a smaller but real gap.

clusters.cluster_name: No object-operator-overloading dispatch in binary/unary inference
clusters.root_cause: infer_binary and unary-op inference (src/checker/expr.rs) assume plain numeric operands throughout; there is no hook of any kind for an object operand overloading +,-,*,/,**,%,comparisons the way GMP and BcMath\Number do.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/expr.rs infer_binary (~2338) and its unary-op counterpart
clusters.notes: Narrow, well-defined scope (a class-name-keyed dispatch table covering 2 classes x 2 extensions each) but GMP/BcMath are rarely used in typical application corpora.

clusters.cluster_name: No PHP-runtime/XML simulation for literal-string validation (Date*, DOM, SimpleXML)
clusters.root_cause: PHPStan validates literal date/XML/tag-name strings by actually constructing the real PHP object (DateInterval, DateTime, DOMDocument, SimpleXMLElement) at analysis time and observing whether it throws; phpstan-rs has no embedded PHP runtime or XML parser to replicate this technique.
clusters.rust_location: none — would require a hand-written ISO-8601/relative-date-string parser and/or XML validator as new modules
clusters.notes: Highest-effort, lowest-value cluster in the category: correctness here is a precision nicety (narrower literal types), not a source of missed real bugs, and building a faithful relative-date-string parser purely to match this is a large undertaking for modest payoff.

clusters.root_cause: No static lookup table mapping date()-format characters (d/j/N/w/m/n/t/L/g/G/h/H/i/s/y/Y/...) to precise numeric-range/string types exists; unlike the cluster above, PHPStan's own logic for the common characters is a static switch, not a runtime shell-out, so this is natively buildable.
clusters.rust_location: new helper in src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs or src/types.rs
clusters.notes: Distinct from the DateInterval/DateTime simulation cluster — this one needs no runtime simulation, just a static per-character table.

clusters.cluster_name: No narrowing predicate table entry for is_iterable
clusters.root_cause: narrowing_type_for_predicate (src/checker/narrowing.rs:826-866) has entries for is_string/is_int/is_float/is_bool/is_array/is_countable/is_null/is_object/is_callable/is_resource/is_scalar but is missing is_iterable, despite fitting the exact same single-arg fixed-target-type shape as its neighbors.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/narrowing.rs:826-866
clusters.notes: Trivial one-line table addition, not an architectural gap — easy, high-ratio win.

clusters.cluster_name: Narrowing predicate table can't express multi-arg or argument-derived target types
clusters.root_cause: narrowing_type_for_predicate is a static single-arg-name -> fixed-Type lookup; it has no way to express 'narrow arg[0] to a type derived from arg[1]'s literal value' (is_a/is_subclass_of/class_exists) or narrow based on a second predicate argument at all.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/narrowing.rs
clusters.notes: class_exists/is_a-style narrowing is a common defensive-coding idiom in real PHP; str_contains/strlen truthy-narrowing is also frequent. This is a real architecture upgrade to the narrowing engine, not just new table rows.

clusters.cluster_name: No HasMethodType/HasPropertyType accessory for dynamic-member narrowing
clusters.root_cause: AccessoryKind has no 'this object has dynamic member X' variant, so method_exists()/property_exists()/is_callable([$obj,'method'])-style truthy narrowing (which lets later code call a method PHPStan can't otherwise see declared) has no representation to narrow into; explicitly scoped out per src/checker/tests/narrowing.rs:192-203.
clusters.rust_location: src/types.rs AccessoryKind
clusters.notes: A deliberate, documented scoping decision rather than an oversight; dynamic-method/property idioms are less common in strictly-typed modern PHP but still appear in older/magic-method-heavy code.

clusters.root_cause: phpstan-rs has no AST node or scope-tracked type for a bare constant reference; define()/const declarations are inspected only for unrelated purposes (e.g. yield-containment), never given a tracked type.
clusters.rust_location: src/ast.rs (no ConstFetch node), src/checker (no constant-type scope entry)
clusters.notes: define()-based constants are less common than const class constants (which presumably ARE tracked), limiting real-world impact.

clusters.cluster_name: Locals map not queried to build a variable-name-keyed shaped array
clusters.root_cause: compact() and get_defined_vars() both need to introspect 'every currently-defined local variable name and its type', which the existing Locals struct plausibly supports, but nothing wires that introspection into a ConstantArrayType-shaped return value.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs, using the existing Locals struct
clusters.notes: Reuses existing scope-tracking machinery rather than requiring new infrastructure.

clusters.cluster_name: No polymorphic type-cast dispatch (toString/toInteger/toBoolean/toFloat) on Type
clusters.root_cause: PHPStan's Type interface exposes toString()/toInteger()/toFloat()/toBoolean()/toAbsoluteNumber() cast methods that many extensions delegate to; Type in src/types.rs has no equivalent cast-dispatch methods at all.
clusters.rust_location: src/types.rs impl Type
clusters.notes: strval/intval/boolval/floatval are common enough that this is a reasonable investment; overlaps with the IntegerRangeType cluster for abs()'s toAbsoluteNumber().

clusters.root_cause: Type enum has no benevolent-union variant (a union whose falsy/nullable members are suppressed for Mixed-typed inputs to avoid false-positive complaints), so functions whose PHPStan return type depends on this concept degrade to a plain union or are skipped.
clusters.rust_location: src/types.rs
clusters.notes: MicrotimeFunctionReturnTypeExtension's true/false-literal half is already implemented; this is specifically the Mixed-argument degradation case.

clusters.cluster_name: Hardcoded per-function constant-array-shape tables incomplete or absent
clusters.root_cause: No shared blocker — phpstan-rs already has precedent for this exact technique (curl_getinfo's ~20-entry CURLINFO_* table in builtin_calls.rs); these functions just need the same treatment: a hardcoded shape/lookup table transcribed from the PHP manual.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs (extend curl_getinfo_component_type pattern)
clusters.notes: curl_getinfo already covers the ~20 most-used constants; extending to the full ~75 plus the sibling functions is transcription work, not new architecture.

clusters.root_cause: PHPStan queries the real PHP runtime (hash_algos(), openssl_get_cipher_methods(), mb_list_encodings()) to build valid-value lists at analysis time; phpstan-rs has no live-runtime source and no hardcoded snapshot of these lists either.
clusters.rust_location: new static tables, referenced from src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs
clusters.notes: A hardcoded snapshot table (versioned, updated occasionally) is a reasonable substitute for the live-runtime query and avoidable without XL effort.

clusters.root_cause: No FILTER_VALIDATE_*/FILTER_SANITIZE_* constant-to-type mapping table, no FILTER_NULL_ON_FAILURE/FILTER_REQUIRE_ARRAY/FILTER_FORCE_ARRAY flag logic, and no literal-value coercion rules exist anywhere — a whole self-contained subsystem PHPStan devotes one shared helper plus 3 thin wrappers to.
clusters.rust_location: new module (e.g. src/checker/expr/filter_var.rs), hooked into builtin_calls.rs
clusters.notes: filter_var is common in real-world form/input-handling code (the kind of code the Piwigo corpus work has been targeting); a self-contained, well-scoped subsystem worth prioritizing.

clusters.cluster_name: No Reflection* class/method modeling in registry
clusters.root_cause: registry.rs has zero special-casing for ReflectionClass/ReflectionMethod/ReflectionProperty/ReflectionFunction/ReflectionAttribute — no generic-template tracking, no hasMethod()/hasInstanceProperty()-style introspection hooks for any of them.
clusters.rust_location: src/registry.rs
clusters.notes: Reflection-heavy code is more common in frameworks/DI containers than typical application corpora like Piwigo; lower priority unless targeting framework code.

clusters.root_cause: No PropertiesClassReflectionExtension-equivalent hook exists for magic/dynamic property resolution on specific built-in classes, so SimpleXML's __get-based child-element access resolves as a normal (likely 'undefined property') lookup instead of SimpleXMLElement|null.
clusters.rust_location: src/registry.rs / src/checker/oop.rs
clusters.notes: XML-processing code is a minority case in most modern web-app corpora.

clusters.cluster_name: No enum case backing-value tracking in registry
clusters.root_cause: registry.rs has no getEnumCases()-equivalent with backing values; oop.rs's only enum-case logic checks for duplicate backing-value declarations, not lookup-by-value.
clusters.rust_location: src/registry.rs
clusters.notes: Backed enums are idiomatic in PHP 8.1+ codebases; ::from()/::tryFrom() narrowing to the exact matching case is a meaningful precision win for modern code.

clusters.cluster_name: No per-class method-return-type override table for built-ins
clusters.root_cause: Method-call return-type inference has no per-method extension mechanism keyed on the resolved receiver class for special built-ins like Throwable::getCode() (whose type differs by concrete exception class).
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/expr.rs / src/checker/oop.rs method-call dispatch
clusters.notes: Small, isolated gap; XMLReader is additionally unregistered as a class at all.

clusters.cluster_name: get_class family: late-static-binding lookup and runtime-string mapping tables missing
clusters.root_cause: Only the 1-arg get_class(Object) case is special-cased; there's no late-static-binding equivalent of 'static::class' for the 0-arg forms, and no type-to-runtime-string mapping table for gettype()/get_debug_type().
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs:759
clusters.notes: gettype()/get_class() literal-string narrowing is common in logging, debugging, and type-switch code.

clusters.cluster_name: Default parameter value doesn't influence unbound @template inference
clusters.root_cause: generics.rs's template substitution doesn't consider a method's default parameter value when the corresponding call-site argument is omitted and the template would otherwise be unbound, so it falls back to Mixed instead of unioning with the default's type.
clusters.rust_location: src/generics.rs (substitute_class_templates / method-template binding)
clusters.notes: Narrow generics edge case; the general class-template pipeline already gets the common case (with an explicit 2nd arg) right.

clusters.cluster_name: Truthy-context narrowing only fires for specific top-level AST shapes
clusters.root_cause: apply_narrowing is invoked only for hardcoded shapes (top-level if/while conditions, a bare assert() statement, two literal count()-comparison patterns) rather than a general recursive walk of any truthy-evaluated sub-expression the way PHPStan's TypeSpecifierContext does.
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/stmt.rs; src/checker/narrowing.rs (apply_narrowing, ~112-134)
clusters.notes: This is a general-quality issue for the narrowing engine as a whole, not just these 3 extensions — fixing it would compound with every other narrowing rule in the checker (assert() nested in &&, count($x) in a plain `if (count($x))`, etc. all currently fail to narrow).

clusters.cluster_name: Long tail of scalar builtins with straightforward, unshared native logic
clusters.root_cause: No shared architectural blocker — each just needs a small argument-driven match arm following patterns already established elsewhere in builtin_calls.rs (constant folding, flag-bit checks, version-agnostic simplifications).
clusters.rust_location: src/checker/expr/builtin_calls.rs
clusters.notes: Batched as a roadmap item since each is individually S-effort with no shared blocker; TriggerErrorDynamicReturnTypeExtension's NeverType-for-E_USER_ERROR case is worth prioritizing within this batch since it feeds dead-code/control-flow reasoning downstream.

# phpstan-rs Roadmap: Proposed New Phase Sequence

This document proposes an ordered sequence of phases to move phpstan-rs toward parity with real PHPStan, synthesized from the 15-category audit. Entries marked **[EXPAND EXISTING PHASE N]** map onto an already-open phase from ROADMAP.md's "Open phases" section — these are not new phase numbers, but the audit confirms/grounds their scope and in several cases shows they unlock far more than their current one-paragraph description suggests. Entries marked **[NEW PHASE]** have no existing open-phase counterpart.

Ordering logic: prerequisite/foundational phases first (things many other clusters depend on), then by value÷effort among independent phases.

---

## Tier 0 — Foundational infrastructure (build first; each unlocks many later phases)

### 1. [NEW PHASE] Diagnostic identifier & metadata infrastructure
**Scope.** Give `Diagnostic` (currently `{location, message, span, level}`, `src/checker.rs:71`) a stable per-check identifier, a tip/annotation field, and a fluent builder — the Rust equivalent of `RuleErrorBuilder`. This is what real PHPStan's `@phpstan-ignore <identifier>` matches against, what CI output formats (JSON/checkstyle) want for machine consumption, and what lets a "possibly impure" tip be appended to a constant-condition diagnostic without a second diagnostic.
**Sources.** standalone-infra: *Diagnostic metadata builder (RuleErrorBuilder)*.
**Prerequisite for.** ROADMAP Phase 44 (`@phpstan-ignore`, which explicitly already calls this out as a prerequisite), ROADMAP Phase 16 (CI output formats), the "Possibly-impure tip decoration" cluster below.
**Size.** M.

### 2. [NEW PHASE] Symbol-existence validation pipeline (classes, functions, use-imports, typehints)
**Scope.** `resolve_name_expr` (`src/checker/resolve.rs:39`) unconditionally returns `Type::Object(name, ..)` regardless of whether the class exists — confirmed by reading the function. Build the missing "does this name actually resolve" primitive once, then wire it into every site that currently trusts a name blindly: `use`/`use function`/`use const`/group-use validation, catch-clause types, `extends`/`implements`/`instanceof`/trait-use targets, and — the single highest-value application — parameter/return/property type hints (`resolve_type_hint`, `src/checker/resolve.rs:53`), which today silently accepts a typo'd class name unless that name is *also* used at a `new` or call site elsewhere.
**Sources.** exceptions-api-restricted: *Symbol-existence validation*; classes-traits: *No class-like-name existence+kind validation family*; standalone-infra: *Unified unknown-class usage collection & reporting pipeline*; standalone-checks: *Function/method declaration signature validation*; methods-keywords-debug-pure: *Existing-class validation on declared typehints*; properties-enum-whitespace: *No class-existence validation for property type hints*; functions-generators: *Class-existence validation for type hints*.
**Unlocks.** `ExistingNamesInUseRule`, `ExistingNamesInGroupUseRule`, `CaughtExceptionExistenceRule`, `ExistingClassInClassExtendsRule`, `ExistingClassesInClassImplementsRule`, `ExistingClassesInEnumImplementsRule`, `ExistingClassesInInterfaceExtendsRule`, `ExistingClassInInstanceOfRule`, `ExistingClassInTraitUseRule`, `ExistingClassesInTypehintsRule`, `ExistingClassesInPropertiesRule`, `ExistingClassesInArrowFunctionTypehintsRule`, `ExistingClassesInClosureTypehintsRule`, `ExistingClassesInPropertyHookTypehintsRule`, `ClassNameCheck`/`ClassCaseSensitivityCheck`/`ClassForbiddenNameCheck` (case-sensitivity + leaked-prefix checks fold in cheaply once the lookup exists).
**Prerequisite for.** InstantiationRule's remaining trait/enum-instantiation cases; several ROADMAP Phase 15 items.
**Size.** L. Highest real-world value item in the entire audit — typo'd/missing class references are one of PHPStan's most common catches.

### 3. [EXPAND EXISTING PHASE 38] PHP target-version (PhpVersion) configuration
**Scope.** ROADMAP Phase 38 is already open and already scoped correctly (`php_version: Option<(u8,u8)>`, `config.rs` → CLI → `Project`, following the `strict_mixed_arrays` precedent). This audit found it as a **recurring blocker** across four other categories, which should move it earlier in the sequence than its current position implies: it gates the version-gate half of `FinalConstantRule`, `NativeTypedClassConstantRule`, `ConstantAttributesRule`, `DeprecatedCastRule`, `VoidCastRule`, `BacktickRule`, `UnsetCastRule`, `ArrayUnpackingRule`, `ReadOnlyClassRule`, `ConstantsInTraitsRule`, `InvalidPromotedPropertiesRule`, `NoncapturingCatchRule`, and `ThrowExpressionRule`.
**Sources.** arrays-cast-operators-regex: *PHP target-version subsystem*; classes-traits: *No PHP-target-version concept anywhere*; generics-variables-constants: *PhpVersion / target-PHP-version gating abstraction absent*; methods-keywords-debug-pure notes it too.
**Recommendation.** No new phase — but recommend resequencing it to run early given how many downstream clusters block on it, rather than leaving it deep in the existing list.
**Size.** L (already scoped as L in ROADMAP).

### 4. [EXPAND EXISTING PHASE 37] Attribute (`#[...]`) AST support
**Scope.** ROADMAP Phase 37 is already open and already correctly scoped (real lexer tokens instead of skip, new `Attribute{name,args}` node, checker-side existence/target-validity checking, `#[NoDiscard]`). The audit confirms this is the single most cross-cutting gap in the whole codebase — it independently blocks rule clusters in *six* different audit categories.
**Sources.** exceptions-api-restricted (AttributesCheck via standalone-checks — see below); standalone-checks: *Attribute AST support and semantic validation*; classes-traits: *PHP attribute AST support entirely absent* (corrects a factual error in that category's raw audit data — `attr_groups`/`AttrGroup` do **not** exist anywhere in `ast.rs`/`parser/classes.rs`, re-verified during clustering); properties-enum-whitespace: *No PHP attribute parsing/AST support*; methods-keywords-debug-pure: *Attribute semantics for methods*; functions-generators: *Attribute AST support*; generics-variables-constants: *Attribute AST/validation infrastructure absent*.

## Won't-port / not-applicable, aggregated (for ROADMAP's own record — no phases proposed)

- **PHPStan's own BC-promise and reflection-migration machinery** (`Api/*` family — `ApiClassConstFetchRule`, `ApiMethodCallRule`, etc. — 11 items, plus `GetTemplateTypeRule` and PHP-parser-v4 migration rules): gate on referencing PHPStan's own `PHPStan\*` namespace, meaningless for a Rust rewrite.
- **`Playground/*` family** (11 items — `ArrayDimCastRule`, `FunctionNeverRule`, `NoPhpCodeRule`, `PromoteParameterRule`, etc.): registered only in phpstan.org's separate issue-bot service, confirmed via `conf/*.neon`, never the CLI analyzer.
- **DI/plugin-architecture wrapper classes with zero logic of their own**: `DirectRegistry`/`LazyRegistry`/`Registry`/`Rule` (standalone-infra), `AlwaysUsedClassConstantsExtension`/`AlwaysUsedMethodExtension`, the ~10 `*TypeSpecifyingExtension`+`Registry` pairs and `*ParameterClosureThisExtension`/`ParameterOutTypeExtension` interfaces (core-types) — phpstan-rs has no DI container or plugin model; every check is a hardcoded Rust function, so there is no seam these interfaces would fill.
- **PHP-runtime/XML-shell-out techniques with no faithful Rust port**: `DateIntervalConstructorThrowTypeExtension`, `DateIntervalCreateFromDateStringThrowTypeExtension`, `SimpleXMLElementConstructorThrowTypeExtension` — PHPStan validates these by literally constructing the real PHP object at analysis time; phpstan-rs embeds no PHP runtime. (The *format-table* half of DateTime/date() handling, Tier 5 #39, remains genuinely portable and is scheduled.)
- **Interface-boilerplate-avoidance stubs**: `NonArrayTypeTrait`, `NonCallableTypeTrait`, `NonGeneralizableTypeTrait`, `NonGenericTypeTrait`, `NonRemoveableTypeTrait`, `TypeWithClassName`, `TypeTraverserCallable`, `CompoundType`, `JustNullableTypeTrait` — exist only because PHPStan represents each type kind as its own class needing ~20 default no-op methods; phpstan-rs's flat `Type` enum with match-based dispatch has no structural need for the pattern. **Caveat**: `NonGeneralizableTypeTrait`'s own notes concede PHPStan's `generalize()` (loop-fixpoint type widening for control-flow stabilization) has no counterpart anywhere in phpstan-rs — that's a real, narrow gap hiding behind this not-applicable label and may deserve standalone investigation later (candidate for folding into Tier 1 #11 if a corpus surfaces it).
- **Sealed-hierarchy extension point** (`AllowedSubTypesRule`) — inert even in stock PHPStan without third-party configuration; no natural home in phpstan-rs's architecture. Not scheduled.
- **`ClassNameUsageLocationCreateIdentifierDynamicReturnTypeExtension`** — exists solely for PHPStan's own dogfooding self-analysis; no general-PHP-analysis meaning.
- **`InnerFunctionRule`** — phpstan-rs *intentionally* does the opposite of this rule (it recurses into and checks nested named-function declarations, an explicit in-repo design choice citing the common `function_exists()`-guarded polyfill idiom). Replicating PHPStan's restriction here would be a regression, not a gap.
- **`EnumCaseOutsideEnumRule`** — structurally impossible in phpstan-rs's AST shape (`EnumCase` only ever exists as a field of `EnumDecl.cases`, never a free-floating node).
- **`ReadWritePropertiesExtension`** — third-party DI extension-point interface; no plugin architecture to attach it to.
- **Two structurally-infeasible-without-PHP-or-SQL-parser gaps** already documented in ROADMAP's own "Known limitations" (`strtotime()`'s real-`strtotime()`-call-at-analysis-time technique; raw SQL/DQL column-shape inference) — reconfirmed by this audit, not newly found, not phase-tracked by design.
